**Statutory and Non-Statutory Committees in Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs)**

***Mandatory by regulatory bodies like AICTE, UGC, NAAC, NBA, etc.***

**ABSTRACT**

Committees play a pivotal role in the governance, academic development, administrative efficiency, and overall quality enhancement of Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs). This document provides a comprehensive overview of the Statutory and Non-Statutory Committees that are essential for the structured and effective functioning of HEIs.

**Statutory Committees** are mandated by regulatory bodies such as the University Grants Commission (UGC), All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), and other apex organizations to ensure transparency, accountability, academic integrity, and welfare of all stakeholders. Examples include the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC), Anti-Ragging Committee, Grievance Redressal Committee, Internal Complaint Committee (ICC), and Examination Cell, among others.

**Non-Statutory Committees**, while not legally mandated, are equally vital for promoting academic excellence, innovation, industry interaction, student engagement, alumni relations, and infrastructure development. These include the Research and Development (R&D) Committee, Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC), Alumni Coordination Committee, Library Advisory Committee, and others.

This document outlines the objectives, functions, structure, year planners, best practices, and documentation requirements of each committee. It emphasizes the significance of a robust committee system in ensuring good governance, quality assurance, stakeholder involvement, and continuous institutional improvement aligned with national education policies and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Through the effective constitution and functioning of these committees, HEIs can foster an ecosystem of excellence, inclusivity, innovation, and sustainability, ultimately enhancing their academic reputation and societal impact.

**1. Statutory Committees**

**1.1. Introduction**

Statutory committees play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth functioning of higher education institutions by upholding academic, administrative, and operational integrity. These committees ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, thus contributing to the institution's governance, quality assurance, and continuous improvement. The role of statutory committees in institutions is directly linked to the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) and National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) accreditation frameworks, as these committees are integral to maintaining institutional standards and fulfilling the criteria for both accreditations. Here is a detailed overview of the key statutory committees in engineering colleges and universities, in line with NBA and NAAC accreditation standards

**1.2. Governing Body (GB)**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The Governing Body (GB) is the highest decision-making body of an institution, ensuring overall governance, strategy, and compliance.
>
> • It is responsible for overseeing the institution's adherence to legal and regulatory requirements, institutional policies, and quality standards, including the NBA and NAAC criteria.

**Key Functions:**

> • Policy formulation and implementation: Establishes policies for academic, administrative, and financial operations.
>
> • Financial oversight: Approves the budget, monitors expenditures, and ensures financial accountability.
>
> • Strategic planning: Sets long-term goals for academic excellence and infrastructure development.
>
> • Compliance: Ensures adherence to statutory regulations such as AICTE, UGC, and others.
>
> • Quality assurance: Monitors and ensures the institution meets NBA and NAAC quality standards.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 6 (Governance, Leadership, and Management) and Criterion 7 (Institutional Values and Best Practices) assess the functionality of the governing body in ensuring transparency, accountability, and strategic management.
>
> • NBA Criterion 9 (Institutional Support and Progression) also evaluates the governing body’s role in ensuring that the institution meets its educational objectives.

**1.3. Academic Council**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The Academic Council is responsible for the academic affairs of the institution, including curriculum design, academic policies, and assessment.
>
> • It ensures that the academic programs are relevant, rigorous, and aligned with industry needs.

**Key Functions:**

> • Curriculum Design and Revision: Approves curriculum updates and new programs in alignment with the institution's vision and evolving industry standards.
>
> • Academic Regulations: Develops academic rules, regulations, and policies for examinations, grading, and student progression.
>
> • Research Promotion: Encourages research initiatives and projects within the institution.
>
> • Quality Assurance: Ensures that teaching and learning processes meet NAAC and NBA standards.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 1 (Curricular Aspects) evaluates the role of the Academic Council in designing and delivering curricula that aligns with academic standards and employability.
>
> • NBA Criterion 2 (Teaching-Learning and Evaluation) assesses how the Academic Council ensures effective teaching-learning processes and evaluation practices.

**1.4. Finance Committee**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The Finance Committee is responsible for overseeing the financial health and budgetary management of the institution.

**Key Functions:**

> • Budgeting and Financial Planning: Formulates the annual budget, allocates funds, and monitors the financial status.
>
> • Audit and Compliance: Ensures the institution adheres to financial regulations and statutory compliance (e.g., income tax, GST).
>
> • Funding for Infrastructure and Development: Allocates resources for infrastructure expansion, research projects, and academic programs.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 6 (Governance, Leadership, and Management) evaluates the institution's financial management and resource utilization.
>
> • NBA Criterion 10 (Institutional Support and Financial Resources) looks into the sufficiency and efficiency of financial resources and support for academic and administrative activities.

**1.5. Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) ensures that the institution maintains and enhances its quality standards through internal audits, feedback mechanisms, and continuous improvement practices.

**Key Functions:**

> • Quality Monitoring: Regularly monitors the quality of education, teaching, and learning.
>
> • Feedback Systems: Collects and analyzes feedback from students, faculty, alumni, and industry stakeholders to ensure the continuous improvement of academic and administrative processes.
>
> • Policy Formulation: Develops and implements policies to improve quality in all aspects of the institution.
>
> • Accreditation Preparation: Prepares the institution for accreditation by NAAC and NBA by aligning the quality initiatives with their respective standards.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 1 (Curricular Aspects), Criterion 2 (Teaching-Learning and Evaluation), and Criterion 6 (Governance, Leadership, and Management) assess the role of the IQAC in quality assurance and continuous improvement.
>
> • NBA Criterion 10 (Institutional Support and Financial Resources) evaluates the role of IQAC in creating a culture of quality across the institution.

**1.6. Board of Studies (BoS)**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The Board of Studies is responsible for designing and revising the curriculum for the institution's academic programs.

**Key Functions:**

> • Curriculum Development: Reviews and revises the syllabus, subjects, and courses offered by the institution.
>
> • Industry Collaboration: Ensures that the curriculum meets the demands of the industry and incorporates emerging trends.
>
> • Research and Innovation: Encourages faculty and students to engage in research and innovation through course offerings.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 1 (Curricular Aspects) evaluates how the Board of Studies designs and updates the curriculum.
>
> • NBA Criterion 2 (Teaching-Learning and Evaluation) assesses the role of the BoS in ensuring that the curriculum is aligned with industry needs and pedagogical best practices.

**1.7. Grievance Redressal Committee**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The Grievance Redressal Committee addresses complaints and grievances from students, faculty, and staff, ensuring fair and timely resolution.

**Key Functions:**

> • Addressing Complaints: Resolves grievances related to academics, faculty-student issues, infrastructure, etc.
>
> • Ensuring Fairness: Maintains confidentiality and impartiality during grievance investigations.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 6 (Governance, Leadership, and Management) evaluates the effectiveness of grievance redressal mechanisms.
>
> • NBA Criterion 9 (Institutional Support and Progression) assesses the institution's handling of grievances and its impact on creating a conducive learning environment.

**1.8. Academic and Administrative Audit (AAA) Committee**

**Role and Functions:**

> • The AAA Committee conducts regular audits of the institution's academic and administrative processes to ensure compliance with quality standards and statutory regulations.

**Key Functions:**

> • Audit Reports: Provides feedback on academic performance, student outcomes, and administrative effectiveness.
>
> • Suggestions for Improvement: Offers recommendations for policy improvements, faculty development, and infrastructure needs.

**NAAC/NBA Relevance:**

> • NAAC Criterion 4 (Infrastructure and Learning Resources) and Criterion 6 (Governance, Leadership, and Management) focus on the outcomes of audits and their role in improving institutional practices.
>
> • NBA Criterion 5 (Student Support and Progression) evaluates how the audit process ensures academic and support systems are continuously improved.

**1.9. Conclusion**

Statutory committees such as the Governing Body, Academic Council, Finance Committee, IQAC, Board of Studies, Grievance Redressal Committee, and others are integral to the proper functioning of an institution, ensuring it adheres to statutory guidelines, promotes academic and administrative excellence, and complies with accreditation criteria. These committees play an important role in fulfilling NAAC and NBA standards, driving continuous improvement and fostering a culture of quality.

**2. Non-Statutory Committees**

**2.1. Introduction**

Non-statutory committees are institution-specific, formed to streamline operations, promote institutional effectiveness, and support quality enhancement. While they are not legally mandated like statutory committees, they significantly contribute to governance, academic quality, and accreditation readiness for both NBA and NAAC.

**2.2. Importance in NBA/NAAC Context**

> • NAAC: Non-statutory committees contribute to various criteria like Curricular Aspects, Teaching-Learning, Governance, and Institutional Values.
>
> • NBA: These committees support the Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) process under criteria such as Vision/Mission, Faculty Contributions, Infrastructure, and Student Support.

**2.3. Key Non-Statutory Committees (with Functions & Accreditation Relevance)**

**1. Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee**

> • Function: Offers academic and emotional guidance, redresses student issues, and tracks well-being and progress.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 5 – Student Support & Progression
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 5.1 – Student Support, 6.3 – Faculty Empowerment

**2. Research & Development (R&D) Committee**

> • Function: Promotes research culture, guides proposal submission, monitors funded projects, and encourages publications and patents.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 3 – Research and Innovation
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 3.1 – Resource Mobilization for Research

**3. Industry-Institute Interaction Cell (IIIC)**

> • Function: Builds industry collaboration for internships, guest lectures, MoUs, and placements.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 8 – First Year Academics / Industry Interaction
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 5.2 – Student Progression, 7.1 – Best Practices

**4. Alumni Coordination Committee**

> • Function: Engages alumni in mentoring, networking, guest talks, curriculum feedback, and funding support.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 7 – Continuous Improvement
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 5.3 – Alumni Engagement

**5. Press, Media & Publications Committee**

> • Function: Manages institutional publicity, coordinates press releases, newsletters, magazine publications, and media coverage of events.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 6.5 – Internal Quality Assurance
>
> o General: Enhances stakeholder communication and visibility.

**6. Library Advisory Committee**

> • Function: Recommends procurement of books, journals, digital resources, and ensures availability of academic material.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 4 – Infrastructure and Learning Resources
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 4.2 – Library as a Learning Resource

**7. Entrepreneurship Development Cell (EDC)**

> • Function: Encourages entrepreneurship and start-ups through training, mentoring, and funding guidance.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 3 – Research and Innovation
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 3.3 – Innovation Ecosystem

**8. Women Empowerment & Gender Sensitization Cell**

> • Function: Promotes gender equality, conducts sensitization workshops, and ensures a safe environment.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 7.1.1 – Gender Equity Initiatives

**9. Renewable Energy & Green Campus Committee**

> • Function: Promotes sustainable practices, energy audits, rainwater harvesting, waste management, and solar energy usage.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 7.1 – Institutional Values and Environmental Consciousness

**10. Cultural, Sports & Extracurricular Committee**

> • Function: Organizes events, competitions, and activities to foster all-round student development.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 5 – Student Support
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 5.3 – Student Participation and Activities

**11. Website/ICT/ECAP/IT Infrastructure Committee**

> • Function: Maintains institutional website, manages e-learning platforms, ECAP/LMS tools, and digital communication infrastructure.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 4.3 – IT Infrastructure
>
> o NBA: Criterion 10 – Institutional Support

**12. Transport Committee**

> • Function: Manages transportation facilities for students and staff, ensuring safety and punctuality.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o General: Supports Criterion 5 – Student Support (for accessibility and infrastructure)

**13. Discipline and Anti-Ragging Committee**

> • Function: Ensures code of conduct is followed, monitors discipline, and handles cases of ragging.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 5.1 – Student Support
>
> o NBA: Indirect support to healthy learning environment

**14. Faculty/Staff Grievance Committee**

> • Function: Addresses grievances related to workload, promotions, and workplace environment.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 6.3 – Faculty Empowerment Strategies
>
> o NBA: Criterion 6 – Faculty Contributions

**15. Timetable and Workload Committee**

> • Function: Prepares and optimizes academic schedules, ensuring balanced workload across departments.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o General: Supports academic process and efficient delivery under Criterion 2 – Teaching Learning Process

**16. Curriculum Development & Revision Committee**

> • Function: Periodically revises syllabus, integrates OBE, Bloom’s Taxonomy, and industry needs.
>
> • NBA/NAAC Link:
>
> o NBA: Criterion 1 – Vision, Mission and PEOs
>
> o NAAC: Criterion 1.1 – Curriculum Design and Development
