**3. Governing Body (GB)**

**3.1. Introduction to Governing Body**

The Governing Body (GB) is the apex authority in a Higher Educational Institution (HEI) responsible for overseeing the institution's overall strategic direction, governance, financial management, and academic policy framework. It ensures that the institution fulfills its mission, maintains high standards of education, operates efficiently, and remains compliant with national and regulatory requirements (such as UGC, AICTE, NAAC, NBA guidelines).

**3.2. Objective of Governing Body**

The Governing Body is the apex decision-making authority of the institution. It provides strategic direction, ensures academic and administrative accountability, and oversees financial and infrastructural resources to achieve the institution's mission and vision. It plays a crucial role in ensuring institutional governance—a key component in both NBA and NAAC frameworks.

**3.3. Functions of the Governing Body (GB)**

**1. Strategic Planning and Policy Making**

> • Formulates long-term goals, policies, and strategic plans for institutional development.

**2. Financial Oversight**

> • Approves annual budgets, financial statements, audit reports, and ensures financial sustainability.

**3. Appointment and Evaluation of Leadership**

> • Appoints the Head of Institution (e.g., Principal/Director) and oversees their performance and leadership effectiveness.

**4. Ensuring Statutory Compliance**

> • Ensures that the institution complies with all regulatory requirements of UGC, AICTE, NAAC, NBA, State and Central Governments.

**5. Monitoring Institutional Performance**

> • Reviews academic performance, research output, faculty development, student outcomes, and institutional rankings.

**6. Approval of New Programs and Courses**

> • Approves introduction of new academic programs, centers of excellence, and collaboration initiatives with other institutions and industries.

**7. Infrastructure Development**

> • Approves proposals for construction, expansion, renovation, and upgradation of academic and administrative infrastructure.

**8. Promoting Quality Assurance**

> • Ensures effective functioning of the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) and other quality improvement mechanisms.

**9. Resource Mobilization**

> • Guides efforts in securing grants, donations, endowments, CSR contributions, and other resources to support institutional growth.

**10. Welfare of Students and Staff**

> • Reviews and approves welfare schemes, grievance redressal systems, and safety/security measures for students and employees.

**11. Risk Management and Crisis Response**

> • Establishes protocols for handling institutional risks, emergencies, and crisis management.

**12. Approval of Statutory and Non-Statutory Committees**

> • Constitutes and oversees the effective functioning of various committees required for governance, academics, and operations.

**13. Stakeholder Engagement**

> • Encourages collaboration with alumni, industry, community, and other stakeholders to strengthen the institution's ecosystem.

**14. Review of Institutional Reports**

> • Approves Annual Reports, Audit Reports, AQARs (Annual Quality Assurance Reports), and any documents submitted to external agencies.

**15. Ethical Governance**

> • Ensures transparency, accountability, ethical practices, and upholds the institution's mission, vision, and core values.

**3.4. Composition of Governing Body**

As per AICTE/UGC/University norms, a typical GB includes:

| **Designation**                                        | **Remarks**                                    |
|--------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson (Independent, Educationist/ Industrialist) | Nominated by the management                    |
| Member Secretary (Principal/Director)                  | Ex-officio member                              |
| University Nominee                                     | Senior Academic from affiliating university    |
| AICTE/UGC Nominee (if applicable)                      | External regulatory nominee                    |
| Management Representatives                             | 2-3 members from the sponsoring society/ trust |
| Academic Experts                                       | 1-2 members from academia/industry             |
| Faculty Representatives                                | Senior faculty members (1 or 2)                |
| Industry Expert (Optional)                             | To align academic and industry perspectives    |
| Alumni Representative (Optional)                       | For stakeholder engagement                     |

The GB must meet at least twice a year, and maintain proper minutes and action taken reports.

**3.5. Roles & Responsibilities of Governing Body**

**1. Policy Formulation & Strategic Planning**

> • Approves the institution's vision, mission, and strategic plans.
>
> • Approves new programs, departments, centers of excellence.
>
> • Oversees compliance with statutory and accreditation bodies.

**2. Academic Oversight**

> • Approves academic calendar, faculty recruitment, and curricular reforms.
>
> • Reviews student performance, quality assurance, and placement reports.
>
> • Monitors research, innovation, and extension activities.

**3. Financial Governance**

> • Approves annual budget, financial statements, and audit reports.
>
> • Sanctions major expenditure related to infrastructure and development.
>
> • Ensures financial sustainability and transparency.

**4. Infrastructure Development**

> • Reviews and approves proposals for new buildings, labs, equipment.
>
> • Evaluates resource utilization and upgrades.

**5. Faculty Development & HR Policies**

> • Approves policies for recruitment, promotion, appraisal, and FDPs.
>
> • Encourages faculty welfare and capacity building.

**6. Quality Assurance & Accreditation**

> • Guides NAAC/NBA preparations, IQAC reviews, and feedback mechanisms.
>
> • Promotes a culture of continuous improvement.

**7. Grievance and Compliance Oversight**

> • Ensures fair resolution of grievances, disciplinary issues, and code of conduct adherence.
>
> • Periodically reviews compliance with statutory norms (AICTE, UGC, University).

**3.6. Roles & Responsibilities of Governing Body Members**

**Chairperson (usually President/Chairman)**

Leads and presides over GB meetings. Provides vision, leadership, and guidance for strategic development. Signs major approvals (budgets, MoUs, policies) on behalf of the GB. Represents the institution at official events or external bodies when needed.

**Head of Institution (Principal/Director/Dean)**

Acts as the Secretary of the GB. Prepares agenda. Presents academic, administrative, and financial status reports. Implements GB decisions. Suggests new initiatives and requirements for institutional development.

**Management/Trust/Society Nominees**

Bring institutional and financial perspectives. Contribute to decision-making related to infrastructure, resource mobilization, and expansion. Ensure adherence to the founding vision and mission of the institution.

**Academic Experts (University Nominees/External Educationists)**

Provide academic advice, curriculum enrichment, and quality assurance suggestions. Recommend new programs or collaborations. Ensure alignment with educational policies and accreditation frameworks (NAAC, NBA).

**Industrialists/Employers Nominee**

Advise on industry requirements and trends. Suggest measures for employability enhancement and industry-institute linkages. Support internship, training, placement initiatives.

**Member – Senior Faculty Members**

Represent faculty perspectives. Provide feedback on academic processes, teaching-learning practices. Assist in framing policies regarding faculty development, research activities.

**Finance Officer/Account Officer (Special Invitee)**

Advises on financial matters, budgeting, and resource planning. Prepares financial reports and audit compliance documentation. Ensures transparency and proper utilization of funds.

**Legal Expert (Optional/Special Invitee)**

Guides on legal compliance, regulatory issues. Assists in drafting institutional policies (service rules, contracts, agreements).

**Alumni Representative (Optional Member)**

Brings external perspectives from alumni. Helps strengthen alumni engagement and fundraising activities. Advises on global academic and industry trends.

**Student Representative (Optional, typically in advisory capacity)**

Conveys students' expectations and concerns. Participates in discussions relating to student welfare and campus development.

**Notes:**

> • The specific composition and the powers of the Governing Body depend on the affiliating university's regulations, UGC norms, AICTE requirements, and the institution's statutes.
>
> • In Autonomous Colleges, Governing Body structures are particularly important and must follow UGC guidelines.

**3.7. Relevance to NAAC & NBA**

| **Accreditation** | **Relevant Criteria**                                                                                                                     |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NAAC              | Criterion 6: Governance, Leadership and Management (6.1.1, 6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3); Criterion 7: Institutional Values and Best Practices     |
| NBA               | Criterion 1: Vision, Mission, and Program Educational Objectives; Criterion 10: Governance, Institutional Support and Financial Resources |

**3.8. Key Deliverables / Documents Maintained**

> • Governing Body meeting agendas, minutes, and action taken reports.
>
> • Institutional Strategic Development Plan.
>
> • Approval letters for budget, new courses, infrastructure, and policies.
>
> • Annual Reports presented to the GB.
>
> • Periodic review reports from IQAC, academic council, and other statutory committees.

**3.9. Impact on NBA & NAAC**

| **Area**               | **Impact**                                                                |
|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Strategic Development  | Helps in vision-mission articulation and PO-PEO alignment (NBA)           |
| Effective Leadership   | Assesses leadership involvement in quality initiatives (NAAC Criterion 6) |
| Financial Support      | Shows adequate resource allocation for teaching-learning and R&D          |
| Institutional Values   | Ensures transparency, decentralization, and participative governance      |
| Continuous Improvement | Governing Body reviews feedback-based reforms and quality initiatives     |

**3.10. Interactions with Other Committees**

The Governing Body functions in coordination with:

> • IQAC (Internal Quality Assurance Cell)
>
> • Academic Council / Board of Studies
>
> • Finance Committee
>
> • Research and Development Cell
>
> • Infrastructure and Purchase Committee
>
> • Anti-Ragging, Grievance, Gender Cell, etc.

**3.11. Meeting Frequency**

> • Twice a year (minimum): One at the beginning of the academic year and one post-semester to review outcomes.
>
> • Emergency meetings may be called when required.

**3.12. Annual Action Plan of the Governing Body**

| **Month/Quarter** | **Activity/Agenda**                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| April – May       | Annual Review Meeting; Approval of Annual Budget                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| June              | Strategic Planning Session; Vision & Mission Review                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| July              | Academic Planning Approval; Approval of Admissions Policy                                                                                                                                                                           |
| August            | Faculty Recruitment and Promotion Policies                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| September         | Development Review – Review previous year's performance; Approve budget for the new financial year                                                                                                                                  |
| October           | Mid-Year Progress Review – Update Strategic Plan; Align institutional goals with national policies (e.g., NEP 2020)                                                                                                                 |
| November          | Approve new academic programs/courses; Review and approve student intake and reservation policies                                                                                                                                   |
| December          | Quality Assurance Review – Review staffing needs; Approve recruitment and promotion policies for faculty and staff                                                                                                                  |
| January           | Approve major infrastructure proposals (labs, hostels, digital classrooms); Assess academic, financial, and administrative progress                                                                                                 |
| February          | Research & Innovation Review – Address challenges; Review internal and external audit reports; Ensure regulatory compliances (NAAC, NBA, AICTE, UGC)                                                                                |
| March             | Student and Alumni Engagement Review; Infrastructure – Audit and Compliance Review                                                                                                                                                  |
| Final             | Final Annual Report Preparation; Planning for Next Academic Year – Approve new student welfare schemes; Strengthen alumni engagement and outreach activities; Prepare consolidated Annual Report; Set goals for next academic cycle |

**Key Focus Areas Throughout the Year:**

> • Strategic Leadership and Vision Setting
>
> • Quality Assurance and Academic Excellence
>
> • Financial Accountability and Resource Mobilization
>
> • Infrastructure and Technological Advancements
>
> • Student and Staff Welfare
>
> • Regulatory Compliance
>
> • Promotion of Innovation, Research, and Extension Activities

**Important Note:** Responsible sub-committees for the above activities typically include the Infrastructure SubCommittee, GB Core Members, Finance and Compliance SubCommittee, Chairperson/IQAC Coordinator, R&D Sub-Committee, and the Student Welfare and Alumni Sub-Committee, reporting back to the full Governing Body (Members, Principal, IQAC).

The Annual Action Plan should be flexible enough to accommodate mid-year updates or special initiatives based on institutional needs, government policies, or stakeholder feedback.

**3.13. Powers of the Governing Body**

The Governing Body of the institution shall have the following powers:

**1. Asset Acquisition and Management**

> • To purchase lands, premises, buildings, and vehicles for institutional purposes.

**2. Infrastructure Development**

> • To provide or construct buildings, laboratories, hostels, halls, theatres, and other facilities required for the college.

**3. Financial Investment**

> • To invest the college funds in scheduled banks or any other approved banks/securities.

**4. Employee Association Recognition**

> • To grant or withdraw recognition to associations of college employees and to formulate related procedures.

**5. Determination of Authority Roles**

> • To decide powers, duties, and perquisites of the Principal and Administrative Officer (AO), in addition to what is specified in the regulations.

**6. Student and Staff Welfare**

> • To make provisions for welfare measures such as medical facilities, residential quarters, loans, and advances for students and employees.

**7. Retirement Benefits**

> • To provide retirement benefits as outlined in the Service and Financial Rules of the institution.

**8. Referral to Academic Authorities**

> • To refer matters to the Academic Council, Deans, or Chairpersons of Boards of Studies for reports and recommendations.

**9. Remuneration and Allowances**

> • To prescribe terms and conditions for payment of remuneration, sitting fees, travel allowance (T.A.), daily allowance (D.A.), and other expenses to:
>
> o Members of Authorities
>
> o Members of Committees
>
> o Experts and invitees
>
> o College employees

**10. Examination Related Payments**

> • To fix remuneration, T.A., and D.A. for paper setters, examiners, invigilators, and others involved in examination processes.

**11. Delegation of Powers**

> • To delegate specific powers to the Principal or other officers for matters relating to Administration, Finance, Examinations, or any other activities.

**12. Constitution of Committees**

> • To constitute committees for recommending actions on specific matters, including:
>
> o Grievances Redressal Committee
>
> o Examination Practices Committee
>
> o Appointments and Promotions Committee
>
> o Building Committee
>
> o Any other committees as needed

**13. Appeal Mechanism**

> • To allow any employee or student to appeal against decisions made by college officers within thirty (30) days from the receipt of the decision.

**3.14. Rules of Procedure for Conducting Meetings of the Governing Body (GB)**

The meetings of the Governing Body (GB), convened and chaired by the principal, shall be of the following types:

> • Ordinary Meetings
>
> • Special Meetings
>
> • Requisition Meetings

**1. Ordinary Meetings**

**Frequency:**

Ordinary meetings are generally held once every three months.

**Notice of Meeting:**

> • An advance notice of a minimum of fifteen (15) days shall be given. The notice must:
>
> o Be signed by the Administrative Officer (AO).
>
> o Be accompanied by a detailed agenda prepared under the principal's directions.
>
> o Specify the place, time, and date of the meeting, as fixed by the principal.

**Chairing the Meeting:**

> • The principal chairs the meeting.
>
> • In the absence of the Principal, the Vice Principal chairs it.
>
> • If the Vice Principal is also absent, members present shall elect one among themselves to preside.

**Quorum:**

A quorum of eight (8) members is required as specified in the regulations.

**Agenda Items:**

> • Agenda items are presented in the form of subjects only (not as resolutions).
>
> • GB members may suggest inclusion of additional topics through the AO, who shall seek Principal's approval.

**Table Items:**

> • The principal may place urgent or confidential matters before the GB as table items during the meeting.

**Decision-Making:**

> • Decisions should preferably be made by consensus.
>
> • In case of differences, a majority decision shall prevail.
>
> • The principal has a right to vote and also a casting vote in case of a tie.

**Recording Minutes:**

> • Minutes shall clearly state the subject discussed and the GB's decision.
>
> • Approved minutes, signed by the principal, shall be circulated to members within ten (10) days.

**Approval of Minutes:**

> • If no objections or modification suggestions are received within seven (7) days of receipt, the minutes are deemed approved.
>
> • If objections or suggestions are received:
>
> o The AO will place them before the principal for final decision.
>
> o If objections/suggestions are from the majority of members, the principal may either amend the minutes or place the matter before the next GB meeting for reconsideration.

**3.15. Financial Responsibilities of the Governing Body**

The Governing Body plays a crucial role in ensuring the financial health, transparency, and accountability of the institution. Its key financial responsibilities include:

**1. Financial Soundness and Asset Protection**

> • Ensuring the financial soundness of the institution.
>
> • Safeguarding the institution's assets and resources.

**2. Strategic Financial Oversight**

> • Approving the financial strategy in alignment with the institution's long-term goals while maintaining financial stability.
>
> • Approving annual operating plans and budgets that reflect the institution's strategic plan.

**3. Compliance with Funding Requirements**

> • Ensuring that funds provided by funding agencies are utilized strictly in accordance with the terms and conditions laid out in agreements, contracts, or memoranda.

**4. Delegated Financial Authority**

> • Establishing a clear and quantified scheme of delegated financial authority.
>
> • Ensuring that managers at appropriate levels have defined approval and expenditure limits.

**5. Risk Management and Internal Controls**

> • Ensuring the existence, integrity, and effectiveness of risk management, control, and internal governance systems.
>
> • Monitoring the internal controls through an Audit Committee.

**6. Approval of Financial Statements**

> • Receiving, reviewing, and approving the institution's audited annual accounts.
>
> • Periodically monitoring both capital and operating expenditures to ensure alignment with the approved financial plan.
>
> • Approving any genuine variations from the approved plan.

**7. Delegation to Finance Committee**

> • Detailed monitoring of the institution's financial position, prospects, and expenditure approvals is delegated to a Finance Committee, which reports periodically to the Governing Body.

**8. Audit Procedures**

> • Establishing clear and well-defined procedures for the audit of all financial aspects.
>
> • Appointing independent auditors to conduct annual financial audits.
>
> • Receiving and approving audited financial statements in a timely manner to maintain transparency and accountability.

**3.16. Procurement Responsibilities of the Governing Body**

The Governing Body is responsible for ensuring that the institution maintains a robust, transparent, and efficient procurement system. Their focus is to achieve Value for Money (VFM) from public and institutional funds while upholding quality, fairness, and transparency across all procurement activities.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Internal Controls and Policies**

> • Ensuring that adequate internal procurement policies and procedures are formulated and implemented.
>
> • Guaranteeing that policies and procedures are consistently applied and fully compliant with applicable rules, regulations, and standards.

**2. Transparency and Fairness**

> • Ensuring that procurement processes are open, fair, and transparent, with no entry barriers.
>
> • Guaranteeing that all eligible suppliers, manufacturers, and consultants are given equal opportunity to participate.

**3. Monitoring and Review**

> • Periodically reviewing the functioning of the procurement system to ensure its effectiveness and integrity.
>
> • Receiving regular reports and assessments from internal auditors or designated committees regarding procurement practices.

**4. Risk Management and Reporting**

> • Ensuring that the institution's risk management framework and reporting mechanisms adequately cover: fairness and transparency of procurement processes; achievement of Value for Money (VFM); identification and mitigation of procurement risks.

**5. Conflict of Interest Management**

> • Ensuring that procedures to govern conflicts of interest in procurement are defined, documented, and strictly enforced.
>
> • Such procedures must be incorporated into the institution's Financial Regulations, which require approval from the Governing Body.

**6. Policy Approval**

> • Reviewing and formally approving the Financial Regulations, including procurement rules, ensuring they are comprehensive and up to date.

**3.17. Monitoring Institutional Performance and Quality Assurance Arrangements**

The Governing Body holds the ultimate responsibility for monitoring institutional performance and ensuring that robust quality assurance mechanisms are in place. It oversees that the institution is achieving its mission, vision, and strategic objectives effectively and efficiently.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Performance Measurement**

> • Measuring and monitoring institutional performance through the use of agreed Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that are:
>
> o Realistic
>
> o Challenging
>
> o Aligned with the institution's strategic goals

**2. Benchmarking**

> • Reviewing the institution's performance against peer institutions through structured benchmarking exercises.
>
> • Using benchmarking data to:
>
> o Identify performance gaps
>
> o Set performance improvement targets
>
> o Share and implement best practices

**3. Reporting Mechanism**

> • Requiring the Head of the Institution (e.g., Principal/Director) to report periodically to the Governing Body based on the KPIs established.
>
> • Reports must present both quantitative and qualitative assessments, offering a comprehensive view of institutional achievements and areas for improvement.

**4. Continuous Improvement**

> • Analyzing institutional performance reviews and advising on corrective measures where gaps or deficiencies are identified.
>
> • Providing strategic guidance to drive improvements in academic, research, administrative, and financial performance.

**3.18. Appointment and Performance Review of Managerial and Administrative Positions**

**Role of the Governing Body:**

The Governing Body holds the crucial responsibility for the appointment and performance evaluation of the institution's key managerial and administrative leadership. These actions ensure strong institutional governance, strategic direction, and effective operational management.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Appointment of Leadership Positions**

> • Head of the Institution (e.g., Principal/Director):
>
> o Appointed by the Governing Body based on transparent selection processes.
>
> o Expected to align with the institution's vision, mission, and strategic goals.
>
> • Senior Academic and Administrative Positions:
>
> o The Governing Body appoints key positions including:
>
> o Dean (Academic Affairs)
>
> o Dean (Research and Development)
>
> o Dean (Planning and Development)
>
> o Dean (Student Welfare)
>
> o Controller of Examinations
>
> o Other senior officers as recommended by the Head of the Institution

**2. Performance Monitoring**

> • Regularly reviewing the performance of the Head of Institution against pre-agreed goals and performance indicators.
>
> • Reviewing the performance of Deans and senior administrative officials to ensure:
>
> o Effective academic leadership
>
> o Research and innovation enhancement
>
> o Robust planning and development strategies
>
> o Student welfare and support systems
>
> o Transparent and efficient examination management
>
> • Ensuring that annual performance appraisals are carried out and corrective actions, if necessary, are recommended.

**3. Strategic Alignment**

> • Ensuring that all appointments and reviews are aligned with the institution's strategic development plan.
>
> • Supporting leadership succession planning and capacity building across the institution's administration.

**3.19. Establishment of Human Resources and Employment Policy**

The Governing Body is responsible for establishing comprehensive Human Resources (HR) and Employment Policies that foster institutional growth, ensure compliance with regulations, and promote employee development.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Policy Formulation**

> • Ensures that well-defined Human Resources and Employment Policies are framed, documented, and periodically updated.
>
> • Policies cover key aspects such as:
>
> o Recruitment and selection
>
> o Induction and orientation
>
> o Career progression and promotion
>
> o Professional development and training
>
> o Performance appraisal and feedback mechanisms
>
> o Disciplinary procedures and grievance redressal
>
> o Service rules, retirement, and welfare measures

**2. Implementation and Monitoring**

> • Ensures that appropriate procedures are in place for the implementation, management, and monitoring of HR policies.
>
> • Oversees the transparent and merit-based recruitment of faculty, staff, and administrative personnel.
>
> • Ensures adherence to statutory requirements related to employment, including equal opportunity, diversity, and inclusion.

**3. Human Resources Development**

> • Promotes initiatives for the continuous development of teaching and non-teaching staff through:
>
> o Faculty development programs
>
> o Technical skill enhancement workshops
>
> o Leadership training
>
> o Research and innovation support
>
> • Encourages the creation of a positive working environment that enhances productivity, satisfaction, and institutional loyalty.

**4. Review and Improvement**

> • Conducts periodic reviews of HR policies to ensure relevance and alignment with the institution's strategic objectives.
>
> • Introduces necessary amendments based on feedback, regulatory changes, and evolving best practices.

**3.20. Support for Collaborations between Institution and Academic, Research, and Industry Partners**

The Governing Body plays a pivotal role in creating, supporting, and strengthening collaborations with academic partners, research establishments, and industries of global, national, and local importance. These partnerships help fulfill the mission, vision, and strategic objectives of the institution.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Strategic Facilitation of Collaborations**

> • Encourages partnerships with reputed academic institutions, universities, research organizations, and industry leaders.
>
> • Promotes interdisciplinary research initiatives, student and faculty exchange programs, and joint ventures that enhance academic quality and research output.

**2. Policy and Framework Development**

> • Establishes clear policies and guidelines for forming collaborations and signing MoUs, partnership agreements, or consortia.
>
> • Ensures due diligence is conducted before entering into formal collaboration agreements.

**3. Resource Mobilization and Support**

> • Allocates necessary financial and infrastructural resources to support joint initiatives such as research and innovation projects, skill development programs, industry-relevant curriculum development, and internships and placement programs for students.

**4. Monitoring and Review**

> • Oversees the performance and effectiveness of collaborations.
>
> • Regularly reviews outcomes such as research publications, patents filed, sponsored projects undertaken, and student internships and placements facilitated.
>
> • Takes corrective actions where partnerships do not meet expected goals.

**5. Global Outreach**

> • Promotes international collaborations to ensure that the institution stays aligned with global academic standards and fosters a multicultural learning environment.
>
> • Supports participation in global academic networks, international research conferences, and joint degree programs.

**3.21. Instituting Scholarships, Fellowships, Studentships, Medals, Prizes, and Certificates**

The Governing Body is responsible for formulating the norms and policies regarding the institution of scholarships, fellowships, studentships, medals, prizes, and certificates to encourage academic excellence, research, innovation, leadership, and co-curricular achievements among students.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Norms and Policy Formulation**

> • Establishes clear guidelines and eligibility criteria for instituting scholarships, fellowships, awards, medals, prizes, and certificates.
>
> • Defines the objectives, funding sources (institutional funds, endowments, donations, industry sponsorships), and the selection process.

**2. Recommendations by Academic Council**

> • The Academic Council evaluates proposals based on the norms set by the Governing Body.
>
> • After thorough examination, the Academic Council recommends the awards and scholarships to the Governing Body for approval.

**3. Approval and Institution**

> • The Governing Body reviews and approves the recommendations made by the Academic Council.
>
> • Ensures that the awards align with the institution's mission of promoting academic excellence, innovation, inclusivity, and holistic student development.

**4. Periodic Review**

> • Reviews and updates the policies and criteria periodically to stay relevant to emerging academic and industry trends.
>
> • May introduce new scholarships, fellowships, or awards in response to new academic programs, societal needs, or based on donor/endowment proposals.

**3.22. Approval of Requests for New Programmes of Study Leading to Degrees and/or Diplomas**

The Governing Body plays a critical role in evaluating and approving the institution's requests to launch new academic programs, such as degrees and diplomas. This process ensures that new programs align with the institution's mission, educational goals, and the needs of the student community.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Review of Request**

> • The Academic Body (such as the Academic Council or relevant department) evaluates and reviews proposals for new programs, considering academic, industry, and societal relevance.
>
> • Upon thorough assessment, the Academic Body recommends the proposed program to the Governing Body.

**2. Approval Process**

> • The Governing Body reviews the proposal for the new program based on: academic merit, strategic alignment with the institution's goals, industry and research needs, availability of faculty, infrastructure, and resources, and compliance with regulatory and accreditation requirements.
>
> • The Governing Body approves or rejects the request based on the merits of the proposal.

**3. Monitoring and Evaluation**

> • The Governing Body ensures the successful implementation and sustainability of newly approved programs.
>
> • Regular monitoring mechanisms are put in place to ensure that these programs continue to meet the standards of quality and relevance over time.

**4. Feedback and Revision**

> • The Governing Body may require feedback from students, faculty, and industry partners to evaluate the effectiveness and relevance of the new program.
>
> • If necessary, the Governing Body can recommend revisions to the program or suggest its discontinuation if it no longer serves the institution's strategic objectives.

**3.23. Promotion of Transparency at Every Level**

The Governing Body is committed to ensuring transparency in all institutional operations by establishing mechanisms to provide clear, accessible, and accurate information to all stakeholders, including students, faculty, the general public, and potential employers.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. Information Dissemination**

> • The Governing Body ensures the availability of relevant information to all stakeholders regarding the institution's activities, especially in the areas of:
>
> • Academic performance
>
> • Financial management
>
> • Institutional governance

**2. Annual Report**

> • The Governing Body publishes an Annual Report that provides a comprehensive overview of the institution's academic achievements (including faculty and student performance), research accomplishments, extracurricular activities and sports achievements, and financial statements.
>
> • This report serves as a transparent communication tool to showcase the institution's performance and financial health.

**3. Public Access to Meeting Minutes**

> • The minutes of the Governing Body meetings are made publicly available by being posted on the institution's website. This allows stakeholders to access and review the decisions, discussions, and resolutions made by the Governing Body.

**4. Encouraging Accountability**

> • By promoting transparency, the Governing Body fosters accountability within the institution. Stakeholders can track the institution's progress, identify areas for improvement, and ensure that the institution is fulfilling its mission and commitments.

**5. Engagement with Stakeholders**

> • The Governing Body actively encourages feedback from stakeholders to ensure that the institution remains open and responsive to the needs of its community.

**3.24. Delegation to Chairman**

**Delegated Authority**

The Governing Body may grant the Chairman the authority to act on its behalf in situations that arise between meetings. This delegation of authority allows for the smooth functioning of the institution and ensures timely decision-making when necessary.

**Conditions for Delegation:**

**1. Urgency or Routine Nature:**

> • Delegated actions are typically taken in cases that are urgent or of a routine nature, where waiting for the next scheduled Governing Body meeting would cause unnecessary delays.

**2. Following Established Procedures:**

> • Actions taken under delegated authority must adhere to a set of predefined procedures, ensuring consistency, fairness, and alignment with the institution's overall goals and regulations.

**Notification and Ratification Process:**

> • Notification: After taking any action under delegated authority, the Chairman must inform the member convener about the decision.
>
> • Ratification: The member convener is responsible for bringing the Chairman's action to the notice of the Governing Body at its next meeting.
>
> • Approval: The Governing Body will then ratify or endorse the action taken by the Chairman, ensuring transparency and maintaining accountability for decisions made outside of regular meetings.

**3.25. Frequency, Processes, and Rules for Conduct of Governing Body Meetings**

**Frequency of Meetings:**

> • The Governing Body meetings shall be conducted at least four times in an academic year.

**Process for Conducting Meetings:**

**1. Meeting Scheduling:**

> • In consultation with the Chairman of the Governing Body, the Principal (who is also the Member Secretary) fixes the date, time, venue, and agenda for each meeting.

**2. Notification and Agenda:**

> • The Member Secretary sends the meeting notice along with the agenda to all members and invitees at least two weeks prior to the meeting.
>
> • Pre-agenda notes containing the minutes of the previous meeting and the action taken report on prior resolutions are sent to all members before the meeting.

**3. Agenda and Additional Items:**

> • On the day of the meeting, pre-agenda notes, along with any table agenda (items added with the permission of the Chairman), are provided to all members.
>
> • Any additional matters that need discussion can also be included with the Chairman's approval at the meeting.

**4. Proceedings and Minutes:**

> • The Member Secretary prepares the proceedings, which are then circulated to all members.
>
> • The minutes of the meeting are finalized and approved by the principal (Chairperson).

**5. Decision-Making:**

> • Decisions are ideally made through consensus. If a difference of opinion arises, the decision is made by majority vote.
>
> • The principal has the right to vote and can cast a casting vote in the case of a tie.

**6. Approval of Minutes:**

> • The minutes, as approved by the principal, are sent to each member present at the meeting within 10 days of the meeting.
>
> • If no objections are raised or suggestions made within one week of receipt, the minutes are deemed approved.
>
> • If there are objections or suggestions from a majority of members, the principal will either amend the minutes or place the matter before the Governing Body for reconsideration at the next meeting.

**7. Publication of Minutes:**

> • The minutes of the meetings are made available on the college website, except for content that: contains personal information, is not open to the whole Governing Body for discussion, is commercially sensitive, or is declared as confidential by the Governing Body and marked as "Reserved".

**3.26. Orientation and Development for Governing Body Members**

It is essential for the Chairman of the Governing Body, or the Nomination Committee in coordination with the Member Secretary, to ensure that all members are adequately oriented and prepared for their roles when they take up office. This ensures that they understand the responsibilities they have towards the proper governance of the institution. The orientation process includes:

**Key Elements of the Orientation Process:**

**1. Briefing on Appointment Terms and Responsibilities:**

> • Each new member is briefed on the terms of their appointment.
>
> • The member is made aware of the responsibilities placed on them for effective governance and decision-making.

**2. Documents Provided to New Members:**

> • New members will receive the following documents as part of their orientation: Institution's Governance Document (outlines the governance structure and responsibilities); Institution's Annual Report (overview of activities, progress, and performance over the previous year); Audited Financial Statements & Financial Forecast; Strategic Plan and Strategy Documents (covering learning, teaching, research, widening participation, and estate development); Organizational Structure Notes; Rules and Procedures of the Governing Body.

**3. Induction Program:**

> • A one-day induction program is organized for new members as soon as they are appointed. This program helps them understand their roles and equips them with the necessary knowledge to perform their governance duties effectively.

**4. Continuous Development Opportunities:**

> • Management Development Programs (MDPs) are organized periodically for both new and existing members.
>
> • These programs provide opportunities for ongoing professional development, helping members discharge their individual and collective responsibilities effectively.

**Objective of MDPs:**

> • Enhance leadership and management skills.
>
> • Improve decision-making and problem-solving capabilities.
>
> • Foster understanding of emerging challenges and governance best practices.

**3.27. Performance Review of the Governing Body**

The Governing Body plays a critical role in ensuring the effective governance and strategic direction of the institution. To maintain and enhance its effectiveness, the Governing Body is committed to regular reviews of its performance in meeting the institution's strategic goals and objectives.

**Key Elements of the Performance Review Process:**

**1. Review Frequency:**

> • The effectiveness of the Governing Body is assessed once every five years. This period allows for a thorough evaluation of the institution's progress in achieving its strategic objectives and the overall performance of the governing body.

**2. Criteria for Review:**

> • The performance of the Governing Body is measured against the institution's strategic goals and objectives, ensuring alignment with the institution's vision and mission.
>
> • Committees formed under the Governing Body are also reviewed to assess their contributions toward the institution's goals.

**3. Review Process:**

> • The self-assessment process involves evaluating the actions and decisions made by the Governing Body, as well as the overall governance practices.
>
> • The review process may involve the assessment of structure, effectiveness of decision-making, strategic oversight, and the adequacy of resources allocated to achieve institutional objectives.

**4. Engagement of External Experts:**

> • To ensure objectivity and a comprehensive evaluation, the Governing Body may choose to engage external consultants or independent reviewers.
>
> • These experts help evaluate the effectiveness of not only the Governing Body but also other internal boards and committees that contribute to the functioning of the institution.

**5. Outcomes of the Review:**

> • Based on the review findings, the Governing Body may consider revisions in its structure, processes, or strategies to improve overall effectiveness.
>
> • Adjustments may be made to ensure better alignment with the institution's evolving needs and to address any gaps or weaknesses identified during the review process.

**Importance of the Review:**

> • Continuous Improvement: Regular performance reviews allow the Governing Body to reflect on its own operations and make necessary improvements.
>
> • Strategic Alignment: The review process ensures that the institution's strategic goals remain at the forefront of decision-making and that resources are effectively allocated to meet those goals.
>
> • Transparency and Accountability: The review process enhances accountability, ensuring that the Governing Body operates with transparency and is responsible for its decisions.

**3.28. Regulatory Compliance**

The Governing Body plays a critical role in ensuring that the institution operates within the frameworks established by regulatory bodies and adheres to all relevant statutes, ordinances, and provisions. This commitment to regulatory compliance is essential to maintain the institution's credibility, reputation, and continued eligibility for funding and accreditation.

**Key Responsibilities for Ensuring Compliance:**

**1. Adherence to Regulatory Standards:**

> • The Governing Body ensures the institution complies with various regulatory bodies, such as:
>
> o AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education)
>
> o UGC (University Grants Commission)
>
> o State Government Regulations
>
> o Affiliating University Regulations
>
> • These regulations govern multiple aspects, including curriculum, infrastructure, faculty qualifications, student welfare, and financial management.

**2. Reporting Mechanism:**

> • The Head of the Institution (such as the Principal or CEO) is responsible for providing regular updates and reports to the Governing Body on the institution's compliance status.
>
> • The Governing Body receives these reports periodically to ensure that all compliance requirements are being met and that the institution is in good standing with the regulatory authorities.

**3. Final Decision-Making:**

> • The Governing Body holds the ultimate responsibility for final decisions on matters that are of fundamental concern to the institution, including regulatory compliance.
>
> • These decisions ensure that the institution remains aligned with statutory and legal obligations.

**4. Not-for-Profit Purpose:**

> • The Governing Body ensures that the institution continues to operate as a not-for-profit entity, in line with the legal framework governing educational institutions.
>
> • This means that all revenues generated by the institution are reinvested into the improvement and development of educational resources, infrastructure, and faculty.

**5. Accreditation and Quality Assurance:**

> • The Governing Body also ensures that the institution is accredited by national and international professional bodies, such as the National Board of Accreditation (NBA), NAAC, and others.
>
> • Accreditation is critical for ensuring the institution meets quality standards in teaching, research, student support, and management practices.
>
> • This accreditation assures stakeholders—such as students, faculty, parents, employers, and funding agencies—that the institution delivers a high-quality educational experience.

**Compliance with Statutory and Legal Requirements:**

> • Monitoring and Reporting: Regular monitoring of compliance status is essential to maintain accreditation and avoid penalties or legal issues.
>
> • Periodic Audits: Compliance audits should be conducted periodically to assess adherence to regulatory requirements and to prepare for inspections or audits by external authorities.
>
> • Legal and Ethical Operations: The institution must uphold high standards of legal and ethical behavior, ensuring transparency, fairness, and accountability in all its dealings.

**Importance of Regulatory Compliance:**

> • Institutional Credibility: Compliance ensures that the institution operates within the laws of the land, reinforcing its credibility and trust with external stakeholders.
>
> • Accreditation and Funding: Regulatory compliance is a prerequisite for obtaining and maintaining accreditations and funding from governmental and non-governmental agencies.
>
> • Quality Assurance: Accreditation assures stakeholders that the institution maintains high standards of education and services, contributing to student satisfaction and career success.

**3.29. Minutes of the Governing Body Meetings**

The minutes of all proceedings of each Governing Body meeting play a crucial role in documenting the discussions, decisions, and actions taken during the meeting. These minutes ensure transparency, accountability, and serve as an official record for future reference. Below is an outline of the process for recording and distributing the minutes:

**Procedure for Recording and Distribution of Minutes:**

**1. Recording of Proceedings:**

> • The Administrative Officer (AO) is responsible for recording the minutes of the meeting.
>
> • The AO must document all discussions, decisions, and resolutions clearly and accurately during the meeting.
>
> • The minutes should include the subject matter of each agenda item, the key points of discussion, and the decisions or resolutions made by the Governing Body.

**2. Approval of Minutes:**

> • Once the minutes are recorded, they are signed by the Chairperson of the meeting to confirm their accuracy.
>
> • The Chairperson's signature validates that the minutes reflect the true proceedings of the meeting.

**3. Distribution of Minutes:**

> • The AO, under the direction of the principal, is responsible for sending out the minutes to all members of the Governing Body.
>
> • The minutes should be sent within two weeks after the meeting, ensuring that all members receive the minutes in a timely manner.

**4. Attestation of Minutes:**

> • The minutes are sent to the members duly attested by the AO, ensuring authenticity.
>
> • The minutes must be distributed to all members of the Governing Body for their review.

**5. Review and Objections:**

> • Members of the Governing Body can review the minutes after receiving them and raise any objections or suggest modifications.
>
> • If there are no objections within a week from the date of receipt, the minutes will be considered approved.
>
> • If any objections or suggestions for amendments are raised, the AO will present these to the principal for a final decision.

**6. Finalization:**

> • If necessary, the principal will either approve the amendments or place the matter before the Governing Body in the next meeting for further discussion and final approval.

**7. Publication:**

> • After approval, the minutes of the meeting are made available to the stakeholders, including being published on the institution's website, except for any confidential or reserved content.

**Importance of Proper Minutes:**

> • Record of Decisions: The minutes serve as a formal and legal record of the decisions and actions taken by the Governing Body.
>
> • Transparency and Accountability: Proper documentation ensures transparency and accountability in the decision-making process, as members can refer to past minutes to track progress and review outcomes.
>
> • Future Reference: Minutes act as an important reference for resolving any disputes or clarifying past decisions.

**3.30. Objection to Minutes of the Governing Body Meeting**

The procedure for handling objections to the minutes of a Governing Body meeting is outlined below to ensure that all members have an opportunity to review and raise concerns if needed. Here's how the process works:

**Procedure for Handling Objections to the Minutes:**

**1. Circulation of Minutes:**

> • After the meeting, the Administrative Officer (AO), under the guidance of the principal, sends the draft minutes to all members of the Governing Body.
>
> • The minutes are sent within two weeks of the meeting, and each member is given a chance to review them.

**2. Review Period:**

> • The members are given a period of 10 days from the date of receiving the minutes to review the document and identify any discrepancies or errors.
>
> • Members are encouraged to check for factual inaccuracies or issues with the representation of discussions, decisions, or actions taken during the meeting.

**3. Objections or Suggestions:**

> • If a member has any objections or suggestions regarding the content of the minutes, they must communicate these to the AO within the 10-day period.
>
> • The objections or suggestions could include amendments to the record or clarification of specific points discussed during the meeting.

**4. Deemed Confirmation:**

> • If no objections are raised within 10 days, the minutes are deemed to have been correctly recorded and confirmed by all members of the Governing Body.
>
> • This means the minutes are considered final and accurately reflect the proceedings of the meeting.

**5. Addressing Objections:**

> • If any objections are raised, the AO will review them and bring the matter to the attention of the principal for final decision.
>
> • The Principal will either approve the suggested amendments or address the objections as appropriate.
>
> • If necessary, the issue will be discussed at the next Governing Body meeting for resolution.

**6. Finalization and Publication:**

> • Once any objections have been addressed, and the minutes are finalized, they will be considered approved.
>
> • The approved minutes will be made available to all members, and, in most cases, will be published on the institution's website.

**Importance of this Procedure:**

> • Accountability: This process ensures that all members have an opportunity to correct any errors in the official record.
>
> • Transparency: It establishes clear guidelines for members to raise concerns about how the meeting was recorded, promoting transparency in the decision-making process.
>
> • Efficiency: The 10-day review period allows for prompt action and keeps the meeting documentation current and accurate.

**3.31. Admission of Press and Visitors to Governing Body Meetings**

The policy regarding the admission of Press representatives and Visitors to the meetings of the Governing Body is as follows:

**Guidelines for Admission:**

**1. Prior Permission:**

> • Representatives of the Press and Visitors may be allowed to attend the meetings of the Governing Body only if they have obtained prior permission from the principal.
>
> • This ensures that the attendance of external parties is managed and controlled to maintain the confidentiality and integrity of the meetings.

**2. Discretion of the Principal:**

> • The principal, as the head of the institution, has the discretion to grant or deny permission for the admission of Press representatives and Visitors based on the nature of the meeting.
>
> • For sensitive or confidential discussions, permission may be withheld.

**3. Purpose of Admission:**

> • The Governing Body meetings are typically focused on strategic and operational decisions, and admitting external parties may be appropriate when discussions are meant to be open or when public interest is involved.

**4. Confidentiality and Sensitivity:**

> • In cases where the meeting involves discussions that are confidential or involve sensitive information, the Principal may decide to exclude Press representatives and Visitors.
>
> • The Governing Body is responsible for ensuring that confidential matters are not disclosed to unauthorized persons.

**5. Protocol for Visitors:**

> • Visitors, if allowed, must adhere to the decorum of the meeting and may not actively participate unless specifically invited to do so.

**Implications:**

> • Transparency vs Confidentiality: The policy balances the need for transparency with the need for confidentiality in decision-making processes.
>
> • Controlled Access: It ensures that only those with legitimate interests are present during the proceedings of the Governing Body.

**3.32. Attendance Register at Governing Body Meetings**

To ensure proper documentation and accountability, the following procedure is followed for attendance at Governing Body meetings:

**Procedure for Signing Attendance:**

**1. Sign-in Requirement:**

> • Members of the Governing Body are required to sign the Attendance Register upon arrival at the meeting.
>
> • This must be done before they take their seats at the meeting.

**2. Purpose of the Register:**

> • The Attendance Register serves as an official record of who was present at the meeting.
>
> • It ensures that the Governing Body's meetings are properly documented, and the quorum for decision-making can be confirmed.

**3. Responsibility of Members:**

> • It is the responsibility of each member to ensure they sign the attendance register to confirm their participation in the meeting.
>
> • This helps maintain transparency and accountability for the attendance of members at each meeting.

**4. Location of the Register:**

> • The Register will be kept at the entrance of the meeting room or at a designated location, where members can sign it before proceeding to their seats.

**Implications:**

> • Accountability: The attendance register ensures that the members' participation is formally recorded and monitored.
>
> • Quorum Verification: It helps verify the quorum for the meeting, which is required for making decisions.
>
> • Transparency: The process adds to the overall transparency of the meeting proceedings and confirms the attendance of key decision-makers.

**3.33. Meetings and Quorum of the Governing Body**

**1. Frequency of Meetings:**

> • The Governing Body meetings shall be held at least twice a year. This ensures regular oversight and governance of the institution, addressing important matters and aligning the institution with its strategic goals.

**2. Quorum for Governing Body Meetings:**

> • The quorum for any meeting of the Governing Body is defined as one-third of the total number of members, including the Chairperson.
>
> • This means that for a meeting to be valid and for decisions to be made, at least one-third of the total members (including the Chairperson) must be present.

**Implications of Quorum:**

> • Decision-Making: Without a quorum, the meeting cannot proceed, and any decisions made would not be valid. This ensures that decisions are made with sufficient representation from the Governing Body members.
>
> • Ensuring Participation: The quorum requirement ensures that key decisions are made collectively and that there is adequate representation from all members.

**3.34. Best Practices of the Governing Body**

**Vision and Mission Alignment / Strategic Planning**

Periodically review and update the institution's Vision and Mission. Ensure all policies and programs align with institutional goals. Approve and monitor the Strategic and Perspective Plans. Set measurable targets for academic, research, and infrastructure growth. Conduct regular, well-structured GB meetings with proper minutes and actionable decisions. Establish sub-committees for focused attention (Finance, Academic, Research, etc.).

**Transparency and Accountability**

Ensure transparency in financial operations, recruitment, admissions, and procurement. Publish annual reports and audit statements.

**Academic Excellence Promotion**

Approve policies for curriculum reforms, industry-academia collaborations, internships, and research funding. Encourage autonomy and innovation in academic delivery.

**Quality Assurance**

Support Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) initiatives. Monitor NAAC, NBA, NIRF, and other quality accreditation activities.

**Inclusive Decision-Making**

Include representatives from various stakeholders (faculty, students, alumni, industry experts, society members). Encourage participatory governance.

**Faculty and Staff Welfare**

Frame policies for faculty development (FDPs, promotions, sabbaticals). Introduce welfare schemes for teaching and non-teaching staff.

**Student Development and Welfare**

Approve scholarships, skill development programs, mentorship initiatives, and grievance redressal mechanisms. Promote inclusivity, diversity, and student engagement.

**Resource Mobilization and Infrastructure Development**

Approve plans for infrastructure augmentation. Mobilize funds through alumni engagement, CSR initiatives, research grants, and government schemes.

**Regulatory Compliance**

Ensure the institution's compliance with UGC, AICTE, University, State, and National Education Policy (NEP 2020) requirements.

**Sustainability and Ethics**

Promote sustainable development practices on campus. Ensure ethical practices in all institutional activities. Support Green Campus initiatives.

**Key Message:** The Governing Body should lead the institution with vision, integrity, transparency, innovation, inclusivity, and quality consciousness.

**4. Academic Council (AC)**

**4.1. Objective**

The Academic Council is the highest academic body of an institution and is primarily responsible for the planning, coordination, development, and maintenance of standards of teaching, research, and evaluation. It plays a central role in academic governance and is critical for compliance with NAAC and NBA accreditation standards.

**4.2. Functions of the Academic Council (AC)**

| **Sl. No.** | **Function / Description**                                                                                                                                                        |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1           | Academic Policy Formation: Formulates and recommends academic policies for maintaining standards of teaching, research, and evaluation.                                           |
| 2           | Approval of Curricula and Syllabi: Approves new programs, courses, curriculum revisions, credit structures, and syllabi suggested by Boards of Studies (BoS).                     |
| 3           | Academic Regulations: Frames academic rules, regulations, and procedures (including admission, examination, attendance, promotion, grading, etc.).                                |
| 4           | Academic Program Development: Initiates, evaluates, and approves new academic programs, value-added courses, interdisciplinary courses, and skill development initiatives.        |
| 5           | Examination and Evaluation: Supervises policies related to the conduct of examinations, evaluation systems, moderation, results declaration, and award of degrees.                |
| 6           | Research Promotion: Encourages and monitors research activities, policies related to Ph.D./M.Phil programs, and faculty/student research projects.                                |
| 7           | Student Support and Welfare: Recommends academic support programs such as mentoring, bridge courses, internships, student research projects, and scholarships.                    |
| 8           | Approval of Academic Calendar: Reviews and finalizes the Academic Calendar including the schedule for admissions, classes, exams, vacations, and co-curricular activities.        |
| 9           | Affiliation and Accreditation Support: Supports efforts towards maintaining or improving accreditation (NAAC, NBA) and affiliation standards with regulatory bodies (AICTE, UGC). |
| 10          | Faculty Development and Training: Recommends strategies for faculty development, orientation programs, workshops, and training related to academic excellence.                    |
| 11          | Quality Assurance: Ensures continual academic quality enhancement by working closely with the IQAC (Internal Quality Assurance Cell).                                             |

| **Sl. No.** | **Function / Description**                                                                                                                                           |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 12          | Collaborations: Reviews and approves academic collaborations, MoUs with industries, universities, and international bodies for exchange programs and joint research. |
| 13          | Advisory Role to Governing Body: Advises the Governing Body on academic matters requiring their approval or support.                                                 |
| 14          | Grievance Redressal (Academic): Looks into academic grievances of students and faculty and recommends redressal measures.                                            |
| 15          | Annual Academic Report Review: Reviews the annual academic performance report and suggests future academic improvements.                                             |

The Academic Council serves as the highest academic authority within the institution and plays a pivotal role in ensuring academic excellence, innovation, and regulatory compliance.

**4.3. Composition of Academic Council**

According to UGC/AICTE/University norms, a typical Academic Council includes:

| **Designation**                               | **Remarks**                                    |
|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Principal/Director (Chairperson)              | Ex-officio                                     |
| All Heads of Departments (HoDs)               | Members                                        |
| Senior Faculty Members                        | Nominated by Chairperson                       |
| University Nominees                           | Academic experts from affiliating university   |
| External Subject Experts                      | From industry or reputed academic institutions |
| Controller of Examinations (if applicable)    | Member                                         |
| IQAC Coordinator (optional)                   | Member                                         |
| Student and Alumni Representatives (optional) | For feedback-based academic improvements       |

Meetings: At least twice a year (pre-semester and post-semester review)

**4.4. Roles and Responsibilities of Academic Council**

**1. Academic Planning and Curriculum Design**

> • Review and approve new programs/courses.
>
> • Suggest and implement curriculum revisions to meet industry standards.
>
> • Approve course structures, credit systems, electives, etc.

**2. Teaching-Learning Processes**

> • Monitor and improve teaching methodologies and learning outcomes.
>
> • Encourage the adoption of ICT tools, e-learning, and flipped classrooms.
>
> • Approve guidelines for student-centric teaching strategies.

**3. Assessment and Evaluation**

> • Approve systems for internal and external assessments.
>
> • Formulate and review grading policies and examination systems.
>
> • Oversee question paper setting, moderation, and result approval.

**4. Academic Calendar and Scheduling**

> • Finalize and approve the academic calendar for each semester/year.
>
> • Synchronize institutional events and examination schedules.

**5. Faculty Development and Research**

> • Promote Faculty Development Programs (FDPs) and MOOCs.
>
> • Review research initiatives, publication policies, and resource allocations.
>
> • Approve short-term training programs, workshops, and conferences.

**6. Accreditation and Quality Assurance**

> • Support and review preparations for NAAC, NBA, NIRF, IQAC initiatives.
>
> • Recommend academic quality enhancement measures based on feedback.
>
> • Approve guidelines for CO-PO mapping, rubrics, and OBA (Outcome-Based Assessment).

**4.5. Roles and Responsibilities of Academic Council (AC) Members**

**1. Chairperson**

Lead the AC in all meetings and activities. Ensure that the academic policies and programs are in line with institutional goals and regulatory requirements. Approve the final academic agenda and ensure the execution of decisions. Act as a mediator between AC and the governing body.

**2. Vice-Chairperson**

Assist the Chairperson in all activities. In the absence of the Chairperson, take over the responsibilities of the Chair. Help in coordinating academic activities, such as curriculum revisions and examination policies.

**3. Secretary**

Record and maintain minutes of all meetings and decisions of the AC. Communicate decisions and action points from AC meetings to concerned departments. Organize and manage meetings of the AC. Ensure proper documentation and filing of all academic-related reports.

**4. Member (Faculty)**

Represent faculty interests and provide input on academic policies, syllabi, and course structures. Actively participate in discussions on curriculum development and suggest improvements. Provide feedback on the teaching-learning process and evaluate the effectiveness of existing programs.

**5. Member (Department Heads)**

Provide department-specific insights on curriculum development, faculty performance, and student academic progress. Collaborate with other departments to propose interdisciplinary programs and initiatives. Advocate for department needs in terms of resources, faculty, and infrastructure.

**6. Member (Dean of Faculty)**

Ensure coordination between departments and alignment with institutional academic goals. Oversee faculty development programs, academic research activities, and curriculum reforms. Monitor academic quality and ensure the institution meets national and international standards.

**7. Member (Registrar)**

Ensure that the decisions of the AC are in line with university regulations and statutory requirements. Serve as a bridge between the administration and academic council for ensuring smooth implementation of academic policies. Provide academic data related to admissions, enrollment, and performance reports.

**8. Member (Student Representative)**

Represent student perspectives on curriculum and teaching methods. Provide feedback on student needs and grievances related to academics. Suggest improvements for student engagement, extracurricular activities, and learning experiences.

**9. Member (External Expert)**

Bring industry insights and best practices to the council. Provide objective feedback on academic offerings and suggest new trends in the academic landscape. Ensure that the curriculum is aligned with industry standards and future job market demands.

**10. Member (Specialized Faculty)**

Offer expertise in specific academic areas such as technology, engineering, business, etc. Help in developing specialized programs and courses that meet the evolving needs of the academic environment. Provide academic leadership in their respective domains and assist with research initiatives.

**Key Functions of the Academic Council (AC) Members:**

> • Collaboration: The members work together to ensure that the academic programs are in line with institutional objectives and regulatory standards.
>
> • Curriculum Development: Members contribute to the creation, revision, and approval of the curriculum to ensure it remains relevant, comprehensive, and up-to-date.
>
> • Student-Focused Initiatives: The student representative plays a key role in ensuring that the academic environment caters to student needs.
>
> • Monitoring Academic Standards: Members ensure that the academic offerings are of high quality and align with national/international standards.
>
> • Policy Making: The AC members play a significant role in formulating academic policies, including examination systems, grading structures, and degree conferrals.
>
> • Research and Innovation: They foster a culture of research, innovation, and interdisciplinary learning through policy recommendations.

**4.6. Powers of the Academic Council**

The Academic Council is entrusted with the overall supervision and regulation of the academic affairs of the college. It shall exercise the following powers:

**1. Academic Supervision and Leadership:** The Academic Council shall exercise general supervision over the academic policies of the college and provide leadership in enhancing the standards and quality of education and research.

**2. Consideration of the Annual Report:** The Academic Council shall have the authority to examine and consider the Annual Report presented by the Principal or Governing Body.

**3. Delegation and Committee Formation:** The Academic Council may constitute Committees and delegate powers to such Committees or the Principal for executing functions in accordance with the UGC Regulations and the College Rules.

**4. Meetings:** The Academic Council shall convene at least two meetings annually, one of which shall be an Annual Meeting held before 31st March, during which the Annual Report of the previous academic year shall be presented.

**5. Standing Committee:** The Academic Council shall appoint a Standing Committee from among its members. When the Academic Council is not in session, the Standing Committee may meet as required and discharge all functions and powers of the Academic Council, subject to ratification in the subsequent Academic Council meeting.

**6. Consultation with Faculties and Boards of Studies:** The Academic Council has the authority to seek opinions, feedback, or recommendations from any Faculty or Board of Studies on matters of academic importance.

**7. Regulations and Procedures:** The procedures for conducting meetings of the Academic Council and its Standing Committee shall be governed by the UGC Regulations and the internal rules of the college.

**8. Rule-Making Authority:** The Academic Council shall have the power to frame detailed rules and guidelines concerning the design, implementation, and revision of all academic programs of the college.

**4.7. Documents Maintained**

> • Academic Council meeting agenda, minutes, and action taken reports (ATR)
>
> • Curriculum structure documents with revision history
>
> • Academic policies: Attendance, internal evaluation, make-up exams
>
> • Feedback reports and resulting academic reforms
>
> • NAAC/NBA self-study inputs (CO-PO mapping, PEOs, outcomes)

**4.8. Interaction with Other Bodies**

> • IQAC (for quality initiatives and academic feedback analysis)
>
> • Board of Studies (BoS) – Recommends syllabi/course changes to AC
>
> • Examination Cell – Aligns with assessment policies
>
> • Research and Development Committee – For research-integrated curriculum

**4.9. Best Practices for Academic Council (NAAC/NBA-focused)**

> • Include external experts from IITs/NITs/industry.
>
> • Collect and review course feedback from students and alumni.
>
> • Establish sub-committees under AC for curriculum development, OBE, and innovations.
>
> • Publish curriculum and regulation documents on the institutional website.
>
> • Encourage departments to map COs with POs and PEOs and document improvements based on performance.

**4.10. Impact on Accreditation**

| **Criteria**               | **How Academic Council Supports It**                                            |
|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NAAC - Criterion 1         | Enables curriculum enrichment, revision, and flexibility                        |
| NAAC - Criterion 2         | Promotes fair and transparent assessment and student performance evaluation     |
| NBA - Curriculum Relevance | Facilitates industry-academia alignment via updated course structures           |
| NBA - Governance           | Demonstrates structured academic decision-making with stakeholder participation |
| Continuous Improvement     | Ensures systematic review and reform based on feedback and performance metrics  |

**4.11. Relevance to NAAC & NBA**

| **Accreditation Body** | **Relevant Criteria**                                                                                                                                                            |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NAAC                   | Criterion 1: Curricular Aspects (1.1.1, 1.2.1, 1.3.2); Criterion 2: Teaching-Learning and Evaluation (2.6.1, 2.6.2); Criterion 6: Governance, Leadership and Management          |
| NBA                    | Criterion 1: Vision, Mission, and PEOs; Criterion 2: Program Curriculum and Teaching-Learning Processes; Criterion 10: Governance, Institutional Support and Financial Resources |

**4.12. Meeting Frequency**

> • Twice per academic year (mandatory)
>
> • Additional meetings as per need for urgent academic policy decisions

| September                               | Syllabus Gap Analysis and Industry Consultation Review; Ensure curriculum-industry alignment and relevance                                    |
| October                                 | Review of Feedback from Students, Alumni, Employers; use feedback for mid-year course corrections                                             |
| November                                | Academic Performance Analysis (Mid-Semester Review); Monitor academic progress and identify support needed                                    |
| December                                | Review of Research, Consultancy, and Innovation Initiatives; Strengthen academic research culture                                             |
| January                                 | Preparation for External Accreditations / Regulatory Inspections; Ensure compliance with NAAC, NBA, UGC, AICTE guidelines                     |
| 2nd Academic Council Meeting (February) | Approval of New Courses, Minor Changes in Regulations; Approve academic changes for next academic year                                        |
| March                                   | Examination Continuous Review Reforms; Assessment Review / Methods; Ensure effective evaluation systems                                       |

**Additional Standing Activities Throughout the Year:**

> • Approval of Curriculum for Autonomous Programs
>
> • Monitoring Implementation of Outcome-Based Education (OBE)
>
> • Coordination for MOUs, Academic Collaborations, Student Exchange Programs
>
> • Review of Student Grievances related to academics
>
> • Digital Education and ICT Integration Initiatives
>
> • Enhancement of Academic Policies and Examination Reforms

**4.14. Chairperson of the Meeting – Academic Council**

The principal shall preside over all meetings of the Academic Council. In the absence of the Principal, the Vice Principal or Dean Academics shall chair the meeting.
