If none of the above are available, the Academic Council shall elect a Chairperson from among its members to preside over that particular meeting.

**4.15. Notice of the Meeting – Academic Council**

The Principal's Office, under the direction of the principal, shall issue a notice of the meeting at least fifteen (15) days in advance of the scheduled date.

**4.16. Dispatch of Final Agenda Paper – Academic Council**

The Principal's Office (PO) shall, under the direction of the Principal, prepare the final agenda paper and dispatch a copy to each member of the Academic Council not less than four (4) days prior to the date of the meeting.

**4.17. Seating of Members – Academic Council**

The members of the Academic Council shall be seated in such order as may be determined by the principal.

**4.18. Order of Business – Academic Council**

At every meeting of the Academic Council, the order of business shall be as follows:

> • a. Business brought forward by the Governing Body, if any;
>
> • b. Business brought forward by the principal;
>
> • c. Business brought forward by the Faculties and the Boards of Studies; and
>
> • d. Business brought forward by members of the Academic Council in the form of motions.

**4.19. How to Move Motions – Academic Council**

Every motion at a meeting of the Academic Council shall:

> • Be affirmative in form;
>
> • Be moved and seconded at the meeting; otherwise, it shall be deemed to have been dropped.

**Exception:** Motions placed before the Academic Council by the Governing Body or by the Principal on behalf of any of the College Authorities shall not require a seconder.

**4.20. Order of Amendments – Academic Council**

> • 1. The order in which amendments to resolutions are to be moved shall be determined by the Chairperson of the meeting.
>
> • 2. When the debate on an amendment is concluded, the Chairperson shall state: “It has been moved,” and shall clearly state the original motion; then add, “Since then, it has been moved by way of amendment,” and shall clearly state the proposed amendment.

**4.21. Not More than one Resolution and one Amendment at a Time**

This clause ensures orderly conduct of Academic Council meetings by limiting the discussion to one resolution and one amendment at a time. It promotes clarity and structured debate by:

> • Allowing only one resolution and one amendment at a time: This prevents confusion and overlapping discussions.
>
> • Treating a carried amendment as a new, substantive motion: Once amended, the resolution is re-stated and treated as the main motion.
>
> • Permitting further amendments to the amended motion: These must be relevant to the new version of the motion.
>
> • Final voting: After all permissible amendments are resolved, a vote is taken on the final, amended motion.

**4.22. Withdrawals of motions at the meeting**

This clause establishes rules for withdrawing motions or amendments during Academic Council meetings:

> • **Unanimous consent required:** A motion or amendment can only be withdrawn if *all members present* agree to it. This prevents arbitrary or unilateral withdrawal.
>
> • Amendment precedence: If an amendment has been proposed, the original resolution cannot be withdrawn until the amendment has been discussed and decided upon. This ensures that contributions already made to the debate are respected.

**4.23. Ruling out of order a motion**

This rule grants the Chairperson the authority to rule a motion out of order—meaning it can be dismissed or excluded from consideration—at any point before the vote is taken during Academic Council proceedings. This typically applies when:

> • The motion violates procedural rules.
>
> • It is irrelevant or inappropriate to the agenda.
>
> • It contradicts previous decisions or college regulations.

The Chairperson's decision in such matters is usually final, unless provisions allow for an appeal.

**4.24. Motion for appointment of a committee**

A motion for the appointment of a committee during an Academic Council meeting can be introduced at any time, provided it does not interrupt a speaker currently holding the floor.

**Key Provisions:**

> • Purpose clarity: The motion must clearly specify the objective for which the committee is being formed.
>
> • Membership details: It must also list the names of the proposed members and identify the convener.
>
> • Amendments allowed: Amendments can be moved to:
>
> o Expand or limit the committee's scope, or
>
> o Modify the matter referred to the committee

**4.25. Speeches at Academic Council Meetings – Guidelines**

A member is permitted to speak only when a formal question (motion/resolution) is before the house, or when moving or seconding a motion, *except in the following cases*:

> • a) Point of Order – When addressing a procedural error or breach of rules.
>
> • b) Personal Explanation – To clarify a personal matter or misinterpretation.
>
> • c) Special Permission of the Chair – When permitted by the Chairperson to make a formal statement.

**Additional Rule:**

> • A member may speak before moving a motion to explain its context but must stick to the subject/question, and end the speech by formally moving the motion.

**4.26. Rules on Frequency of Speeches at Academic Council Meetings**

**1. Single Speech Rule:** A member may not speak more than once on the same question, unless otherwise permitted.

**2. Restriction on Amendment Participation:** A member who has already spoken on the main motion cannot move or second an amendment to it during the same debate. However, they may still speak on the amendment if it is moved and seconded by others, and debate is allowed.

**3. Special Permission Statements:** A member may make a statement related to the ongoing debate if granted special permission by the Chair.

**4.27. Conditions for the right of Reply for mover**

**1. When the Right of Reply is Granted:** The mover of a resolution is entitled to a right of reply when:

> • The Chairperson has confirmed that no other member, who is entitled to speak, wishes to address the meeting.
>
> • The mover may reply to the entire debate.

**2. No Further Speeches After Reply:** Once the mover has made their reply, no other member shall be allowed to speak on the question.

**Duration of Speeches:**

> • General Limit: No speech shall exceed five minutes in duration.
>
> • Exception for Mover: The mover of a resolution or amendment may speak for a longer period, but only if permitted by the Chairperson.

**4.28. Order of Speeches**

The member who first rises to speak at the conclusion of a speech has the right to be heard. In case of more than one member rising simultaneously, the Chairperson shall decide who is to speak first.

**4.29. Personal Explanation**

A Member, who complains that his speech has been misunderstood or that his conduct or character has been impugned in the debate, may be allowed to make a personal explanation. Such personal explanation may be offered while another member is speaking, only if the Chairperson permits.

**4.30. Point of Order**

Any member may call the Chairperson's attention to a point of order even while another member is speaking, but he/she shall confine himself/herself to a statement of the point of order and shall not make a speech on such point of order.

**4.31. Motion to be put to Vote**

When a debate on a motion is concluded or if there is no debate, the Chairperson shall put the question to voting.

**4.32. Decision on questions**

In the Academic Council meetings, all questions are decided by a majority vote of the members who are present and voting.

> • The Chairperson is entitled to vote on any question.
>
> • If there is a tie (i.e., an equal number of votes for and against the motion), the Chairperson has a casting vote. This means the Chairperson can cast an additional vote to break the tie and make a final decision on the motion.

**4.33. Manner of taking Vote/Poll**

The manner of taking a vote or poll on any motion in the Academic Council meeting is determined at the discretion of the Chairperson. This means the Chairperson has the flexibility to decide how the voting process will be conducted, which could include methods such as:

> • Voice vote (members say "aye" or "no"),
>
> • Show of hands,
>
> • Electronic voting, or any other method deemed appropriate by the Chairperson for ensuring a fair and transparent process.

**4.34. Powers of Chairperson**

The Powers of the Chairperson are as follows:

> • 1. Sole Judge on Points of Order: The Chairperson has the exclusive authority to make decisions on any point of order during the meeting.
>
> • 2. Calling Members to Order: The Chairperson may call any member to order if they are not adhering to the rules of the meeting or speaking out of turn.
>
> • 3. Enforcing Decisions: The Chairperson has the authority to enforce their decisions on all points of order, ensuring that the meeting runs smoothly and according to the rules.
>
> • 4. Right to Interrupt: If the Chairperson rises to speak, any member who is speaking or offering to speak must immediately stop and sit down. This ensures the Chairperson has the floor and can manage the proceedings.

**4.35. Powers of Chairperson to Maintain order**

The Powers of the Chairperson to Maintain Order are outlined as follows:

> • 1. Authority to Direct Withdrawal: The Chairperson has the power to direct any member whose conduct is considered grossly disorderly to immediately withdraw from the meeting.
>
> • 2. Special Motion: This action can only be carried out if a special motion is presented and approved by the majority of the members present at the meeting.
>
> • 3. Immediate Action: Once the majority has approved the motion, the member whose conduct is in question must withdraw immediately from the meeting.
>
> • 4. Exclusion for the Remainder of the Meeting: Any member who is ordered to withdraw is required to absent themselves for the rest of the day's meeting, ensuring the disruption does not continue.

**4.36. Powers of Chairperson to Suspend or Adjourn sittings**

The Powers of the Chairperson to Suspend or Adjourn Sittings are as follows:

> • 1. Suspension or Adjournment due to Grave Disorder: The Chairperson has the authority to suspend or adjourn the meeting if there is grave disorder during the proceedings. This ensures that the meeting can be brought to an immediate halt to restore order.
>
> • 2. Specified Time for Resumption: If the meeting is adjourned, the Chairperson will specify the time when the meeting will resume, providing clarity on when the proceedings will continue.

**4.37. Minutes of the Academic Council meetings**

The Minutes of the Academic Council meetings are managed as follows:

> • 1. Recording of Proceedings: The PO (Principal's Office) is responsible for recording the minutes of all proceedings during each meeting of the Academic Council.
>
> • 2. Signature of Chairperson: Once the minutes are recorded, they must be signed by the Chairperson of the meeting to authenticate them.
>
> • 3. Distribution of Minutes: The PO, under the direction of the principal, is responsible for sending a copy of the minutes to each member of the Academic Council. This must be done within two weeks after the meeting.
>
> • 4. Attestation: The copy of the minutes sent to the members must be duly attested by the PO, ensuring that the minutes are official and verified.

**4.38. Objection to Minutes**

Objection to Minutes is handled as follows:

> • 1. Timeframe for Objection: Any member who was present at the meeting has 10 days from the sending of the minutes to raise any objections regarding the correctness of the minutes.
>
> • 2. Deemed Confirmation: If no exception or objection is raised within the 10-day period, the minutes will be deemed to have been correctly recorded and confirmed by all the members of the Academic Council.

**4.39. Procedure to Decide the objections**

Procedure to Decide the Objections to the minutes is as follows:

> • 1. Raising Objections: If a member takes exception to the minutes within the 10-day period, the member must submit a letter to the Principal Office. This letter should clearly specify the points that need correction in the minutes.
>
> • 2. Principal's Decision: The Principal will then take the final decision on the matter. The principal has the authority to either approve or make the necessary corrections to the minutes.
>
> • 3. Clarifications if Necessary: If the Principal believes that the minutes address an important issue requiring action, the principal may seek clarification from the concerned member(s) or other members present at the meeting. This clarification may be sought either by direct contact or by circulation. Based on the feedback, the principal will proceed accordingly with the necessary action or corrections.

**4.40. Admission of Press and Visitors**

Admission of Press and Visitors to meetings of the Academic Council:

> • Representatives of the Press and Visitors may be allowed to attend meetings of the Academic Council.
>
> • However, their admission is subject to obtaining prior permission from the principal.

**4.41. Attendance Register at meetings**

Members of the Academic Council attending a meeting are required to sign an attendance register. This should be done before they occupy their places in the meeting.

**4.42. Best Practices for Academic Council**

**1. Clear Vision and Mission Alignment**

Ensure that the decisions of the Academic Council align with the institution's long-term academic goals and vision. Regularly revisit and update the academic strategies to keep pace with changing academic, research, and industry needs.

**2. Inclusive Decision Making**

Encourage a participative approach by involving members from diverse backgrounds (faculty, students, industry experts, etc.) in curriculum development, policy formulation, and academic planning. This inclusiveness ensures that all perspectives are considered.

**3. Regular Feedback Mechanisms**

Implement systematic methods for gathering feedback from students, faculty, and alumni regarding the curriculum, teaching methodologies, and academic support systems. Use this feedback to continuously improve academic offerings.

**4. Dynamic Curriculum Review**

Review and update the curriculum periodically to ensure it is relevant, forward-looking, and aligned with industry trends, emerging technologies, and international standards. Encourage flexibility in the curriculum to accommodate evolving needs.

**5. Professional Development**

Regularly organize faculty development programs, workshops, and training sessions that focus on innovative teaching methods, research skills, and academic leadership. This helps improve the quality of education and supports faculty members in their professional growth.

**6. Focus on Interdisciplinary Learning**

Promote interdisciplinary programs and collaborative courses that allow students to gain knowledge and skills across different fields of study. Encourage faculty to work together on developing these programs, fostering a holistic educational environment.

**7. Student-Centric Approach**

Ensure that the academic programs are student-centered and provide opportunities for personalized learning, mentorship, and student involvement in research and innovation activities. Introduce student representatives in the council to voice student concerns and suggestions.

**8. Use of Technology in Education**

Integrate technology-driven solutions into academic planning, such as e-learning platforms, digital libraries, and online assessment tools. Ensure that faculty and students are equipped with the necessary skills and resources to adapt to modern educational tools.

**9. Transparent Communication**

Foster open and transparent communication between all members of the Academic Council and other stakeholders. Share meeting minutes, decisions, and action points with the academic community, ensuring accountability and inclusivity.

**10. Data-Driven Decision Making**

Use data analytics and research-based evidence to support decision-making. Regularly collect and analyze data on student performance, feedback, faculty assessments, and academic outcomes to inform curriculum changes and improvements.

**11. Quality Assurance and Accreditation**

Ensure that academic programs comply with national and international accreditation standards. Regularly monitor and audit academic processes to maintain high standards of teaching, learning, and research.

**12. Research and Innovation Support**

Encourage faculty and students to engage in research and innovation activities by offering research grants, organizing conferences, and creating research centers within the institution. Establish collaborations with industry partners to facilitate knowledge transfer and practical applications.

**13. Academic Integrity and Ethics**

Establish and uphold a strong academic integrity policy, including guidelines for plagiarism prevention, honor codes, and ethical research practices. Ensure that these standards are communicated clearly and followed by all members of the academic community.

**14. Annual Academic Review**

Conduct an annual review of the institution's academic performance, including a detailed analysis of the curriculum, faculty performance, student outcomes, and research contributions. Based on the review, make necessary adjustments and set new academic goals for the next year.

**15. Promotion of Extracurricular and Co-curricular Activities**

Encourage the integration of extracurricular and co-curricular activities within the academic structure, recognizing their value in the holistic development of students. Support student clubs, societies, and competitions as a part of the learning experience.

**Summary of Best Practices:**

> • Focus on alignment with the institution's vision and mission.
>
> • Involve all stakeholders in the decision-making process.
>
> • Adapt to emerging trends by continuously reviewing and updating curricula.
>
> • Use technology to enhance teaching, learning, and administrative processes.
>
> • Ensure transparency and accountability in all academic affairs.
>
> • Foster an environment that encourages research, innovation, and student engagement.

**5. Board of Studies (BoS)**

**5.1. Introduction**

The Board of Studies (BoS) is the fundamental academic body in a department of an engineering college or university that formulates and updates the curriculum, syllabi, and academic regulations. It plays a pivotal role in ensuring the academic quality and relevance of the programs offered, in alignment with the Outcome-Based Education (OBE) model promoted by NBA and quality benchmarks defined by NAAC.

**5.2. Functions of the Board of Studies (BoS)**

**1. Curriculum Development:**

> • Design and develop the curriculum for various programs and courses offered by the institution.
>
> • Define the course content, objectives, learning outcomes, and the structure of the program.
>
> • Review and propose changes or additions to the curriculum to ensure it is up-to-date with current trends in academia, industry, and research.

**2. Course Content Review and Approval:**

> • Review and approve the syllabus for each course in consultation with subject experts.
>
> • Ensure the syllabus is aligned with academic standards, institutional goals, and market demands.
>
> • Approve the number of credits allocated to each course and the assessment methods (e.g., assignments, examinations, projects).

**3. Program and Course Evaluation:**

> • Regularly evaluate the effectiveness and relevance of existing programs and courses.
>
> • Identify areas for improvement or revision in the curriculum to meet educational and industry requirements.
>
> • Review feedback from students, alumni, faculty, and industry experts to assess the effectiveness of the academic programs.

**4. Innovative Teaching Methods:**

> • Suggest and encourage the adoption of innovative teaching methods and technologies that enhance learning outcomes.
>
> • Ensure that teaching practices are student-centered, inclusive, and promote critical thinking and problem-solving.
>
> • Recommend the use of digital tools, e-learning platforms, and interactive learning methods to improve engagement and learning efficiency.

**5. Skill Development:**

> • Ensure that the curriculum incorporates necessary skill development activities, including soft skills, communication, and industry-specific technical skills.
>
> • Align courses with the competencies required by the industry and society.
>
> • Promote interdisciplinary learning to ensure that students acquire a broad skill set.

**6. Assessment Methods and Evaluation:**

> • Define and recommend evaluation techniques for courses and programs, such as formative assessments, summative assessments, practical exams, and projects.
>
> • Ensure that assessment methods are fair, transparent, and aligned with course objectives.
>
> • Regularly review and update the examination policies to meet academic standards.

**7. Interdisciplinary and Collaborative Programs:**

> • Encourage the development of interdisciplinary programs that promote holistic learning.
>
> • Collaborate with other departments or institutions to create joint programs that offer broader perspectives and enhance learning outcomes.

**8. Academic Policy Recommendations:**

> • Formulate and recommend academic policies regarding curriculum design, grading systems, teaching-learning processes, and student assessments.
>
> • Propose changes or updates to academic rules and regulations in consultation with the academic council.

**9. Feedback Mechanism:**

> • Collect and analyze feedback from stakeholders (students, faculty, alumni, and employers) to understand the effectiveness of the curriculum and identify areas for improvement.
>
> • Use the feedback to make informed decisions about curriculum changes or enhancements.

**10. Approval of New Programs and Courses:**

> • Evaluate the necessity and feasibility of introducing new programs or courses based on emerging academic and industry trends.
>
> • Approve the introduction of new academic programs or modifications to existing ones after reviewing their academic and practical relevance.

**11. Integration with Industry Needs:**

> • Ensure that the curriculum aligns with industry needs and technological advancements.
>
> • Facilitate industry involvement in curriculum design, guest lectures, workshops, and internships.
>
> • Promote partnerships with industry to enhance the employability of graduates.

**12. Regulatory Compliance:**

> • Ensure that the curriculum adheres to the guidelines set by regulatory bodies like UGC, AICTE, or other relevant accrediting bodies.
>
> • Keep the academic programs compliant with national and international standards for higher education.

**13. Faculty Development:**

> • Suggest and implement faculty development programs to enhance teaching capabilities, research skills, and the overall academic environment.
>
> • Recommend training programs for faculty to stay updated on the latest developments in their respective fields.

**14. Research and Development:**

> • Encourage the inclusion of research components in the curriculum, where appropriate.
>
> • Promote academic research and integrate it into the teaching-learning process.
>
> • Ensure that students are encouraged to participate in research projects, conferences, and academic collaborations.

**15. Review of Existing Regulations:**

> • Periodically review and revise the academic regulations to ensure they are current and relevant to the institution's goals.
>
> • Approve modifications to regulations concerning admission, examinations, evaluation, and academic progression.

**5.3. Constitution of BoS**

Each department constitutes its own BoS, chaired by the Head of the Department (HoD). Members usually include:

| **Category**                | **Representation**                                              |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson                 | Head of the Department (HoD)                                    |
| Internal Faculty Members    | Senior faculty members of the department                        |
| Subject Experts             | Two experts from outside the college/university (academia)      |
| Industry Representative     | One expert from industry/technical organization                 |
| Alumni                      | One alumnus from the program                                    |
| University Nominee          | Nominee appointed by the affiliating university (if applicable) |
| Special Invitees (Optional) | External experts, MoU partners, professional body members       |

**5.4. Key Responsibilities of the BoS**

**1. Curriculum Development & Revision:**

> • Design, review, and revise syllabus and course structures periodically based on current trends, technological advancements, and stakeholder inputs.
>
> • Ensure alignment with Outcome-Based Education (OBE) framework – COs, POs, PSOs mapping and attainment levels.
>
> • Include industry-relevant topics, MOOCs, value-added courses, and multidisciplinary electives.

**2. Regulation Framing:**

> • Draft academic regulations regarding course credits, grading systems, internships, minor/major degrees, and project evaluation.

**3. Stakeholder Feedback Integration:**

> • Analyze feedback from students, alumni, employers, faculty, and industry to inform curriculum decisions.

**4. Academic Innovation:**

> • Recommend incorporation of emerging technologies, interdisciplinary learning, research components, and entrepreneurship elements.

**5. Assessment Reforms:**

> • Propose examination schemes (internal/external), continuous evaluation methods, and Bloom's Taxonomy-based question paper designs.

**6. Validation of Course Outcomes:**

> • Ensure well-defined and measurable Course Outcomes (COs) and their mapping with Program Outcomes (POs).

**7. Recommendations to Academic Council**

> • Forward curriculum and policy proposals to the Academic Council for final approval.

**5.5. Responsibilities of the BoS member wise**

**1. Chairperson (Head of the BoS)**

> • Curriculum Oversight: Ensure the curriculum is aligned with institutional goals and national standards.
>
> • Leadership: Provide overall direction and leadership to the BoS in terms of academic planning and decision-making.
>
> • Decision-Making: Lead discussions on the introduction of new courses, amendments to existing courses, and new academic programs.
>
> • Strategic Planning: Oversee the long-term academic strategy of the department/program.
>
> • Implementation of Recommendations: Ensure that the decisions of the BoS are implemented in a timely manner.
>
> • Quality Assurance: Monitor the implementation of academic standards and quality assurance mechanisms.

**2. Faculty Members (Subject Experts)**

> • Curriculum Development: Contribute subject-specific knowledge for the development and review of curricula.
>
> • Course Design: Participate in the design of course content, learning outcomes, and teaching methodologies.
>
> • Feedback and Suggestions: Provide feedback on existing programs and suggest improvements based on industry trends, academic research, and student needs.
>
> • Evaluation Standards: Recommend evaluation methods and assessment criteria for courses and programs.
>
> • Continuous Improvement: Regularly review courses and programs to ensure they are upto-date and relevant.

**3. Industry Representatives (If applicable)**

> • Curriculum Alignment with Industry Needs: Ensure that the curriculum meets current industry requirements and prepares students with the necessary skills.
>
> • Expert Opinions: Provide insights on emerging industry trends, technologies, and practices that should be integrated into the curriculum.
>
> • Networking: Facilitate collaboration between the institution and industry for internships, training, and placement opportunities.
>
> • Evaluation Feedback: Provide input on the employability of graduates and how the curriculum can be improved to meet industry standards.

**4. Alumni Representatives (If applicable)**

> • Program Evaluation: Provide feedback on how well the curriculum prepared them for their professional careers and offer suggestions for improvement.
>
> • Bridge Between Academia and Industry: Share real-world insights to ensure that programs reflect both academic rigor and practical applicability.
>
> • Mentorship Opportunities: Offer mentorship to current students and advise on the introduction of new programs or skill sets that would be beneficial.

**5. Student Representatives (If applicable)**

> • Student Needs: Represent the views and concerns of the student body, including academic needs, course structure, and assessment methods.
>
> • Feedback: Provide feedback from the student perspective on curriculum delivery, course content, and teaching methodologies.
>
> • Course Improvement Suggestions: Highlight areas where students feel more focus or enhancement is required within courses or academic programs.

**6. Academic Coordinator or Program Head**

> • Academic Program Coordination: Oversee the coordination of specific academic programs and ensure they align with the overall vision and goals of the institution.
>
> • Monitoring Performance: Track the performance of courses, student satisfaction, and academic results to identify areas for improvement.
>
> • Administrative Support: Provide administrative support to the BoS and ensure smooth communication between the committee, faculty, and students.
>
> • Implementation of Changes: Ensure that the changes or decisions made by the BoS are implemented at the departmental level.

**7. Registrar (If applicable)**

> • Policy Enforcement: Ensure that the academic policies approved by the BoS are communicated and followed across the institution.
>
> • Data Management: Maintain records of BoS meetings, decisions, and course details.
>
> • Compliance: Ensure compliance with regulatory bodies, accreditation standards, and institutional guidelines.

**5.6. BoS and NBA Criteria Alignment**

| **NBA Criterion**                          | **BoS Role**                                                                               |
|--------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 1 – Vision, Mission, PEOs        | Ensures curriculum aligns with institutional vision and PEOs.                              |
| Criterion 2 – Curriculum Design and Review | Drives curriculum revision based on OBE, industry trends, and stakeholder feedback.        |
| Criterion 3 – Teaching-Learning Process    | Updates syllabus to incorporate active learning strategies, FDPs, and pedagogy.            |
| Criterion 5 – Faculty Contributions        | Encourages syllabus design through collaboration, innovation, and knowledge dissemination. |

**5.7. BoS and NAAC Criterion Alignment**

| **NAAC Criterion**                                  | **BoS Role**                                                                           |
|-----------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 1 – Curricular Aspects                    | Designs and reviews curriculum to ensure relevance and inclusivity.                    |
| Criterion 2 – Teaching-Learning & Evaluation        | Sets up effective assessment patterns, academic flexibility, and OBE-aligned syllabus. |
| Criterion 7 – Institutional Values & Best Practices | Integrates ethics, environment, gender, human values into course content.              |

**5.8. Frequency of Meetings**

> • Minimum: Twice a year (once before odd and even semesters).
>
> • Additional meetings: As needed for urgent academic matters or curriculum reforms.

**5.9. Sample Outcomes of a BoS Meeting**

> • Approval of a new elective on Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare.
>
> • Introduction of Value-Added Course on Data Science with Python.
>
> • Modification of laboratory syllabus for Digital Electronics Lab.
>
> • Recommendation to include project-based learning (PBL) component in core subjects.
>
> • Integration of MOOCs (SWAYAM/NPTEL) into credit-based learning.

**5.10. Documentation Required**

> • Meeting Agenda and Notice
>
> • Attendance Sheets
>
> • Minutes of the Meeting (MoM)
>
> • Action Taken Report (ATR)
>
> • Syllabus Booklet / Curriculum Copy
>
> • Stakeholder Feedback Analysis Report
>
> • CO-PO Mapping and Attainment Reports

**5.11. Year Planner: Board of Studies (BoS)**

| **Month** | **Activity/Task**                                                                                             |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| June      | 1st BoS Meeting – Review of existing curriculum and syllabus; Identification of gaps and areas of improvement |
| July      | Collection of Feedback from Stakeholders (Students, Alumni, Industry Experts)                                 |
| August    | Propose Add-on / Certificate / Value-Added Courses                                                            |
| September | Mapping of Curriculum to Emerging Trends and SDGs                                                             |
| October   | Review of Course Outcomes (COs) and Program Outcomes (POs) Mapping                                            |
| November  | Propose new electives and interdisciplinary subjects                                                          |
| December  | Industry Consultation for Curriculum Validation                                                               |
| January   | Preparation of Revised Syllabi / Curriculum Documents                                                         |
| February  | 2nd BoS Meeting – Approval of new/revised curriculum and syllabi                                              |
| March     | Workshop/Seminar on Curriculum Design for Faculty                                                             |
| April     | Review of Academic Progress and Result Analysis                                                               |
| May       | Planning for Next Academic Year BoS Activities                                                                |

**Standing Activities Throughout the Year:**

> • Purpose/Objective – Start the academic year by assessing curriculum relevance; Officially approve changes for the next academic year; Build capacity of faculty on curriculum innovation; Analyze student performance and suggest academic strategies; Gather insights for curriculum enhancement; Enrich curriculum with skill-based learning; Set agenda for upcoming academic year; Update curriculum in line with new technologies, societal needs; Ensure alignment with Outcome-Based Education (OBE) goals; Diversify academic options for students; Validate and fine-tune curriculum with industry feedback; Draft syllabus revisions based on all reviews
>
> • Continuous Curriculum Review based on Industry 4.0 requirements
>
> • Conducting Guest Lectures and Expert Talks for content enhancement
>
> • Promoting Interdisciplinary and Multidisciplinary Learning
>
> • Integration of MOOCs, SWAYAM, NPTEL courses into syllabus
>
> • Periodic Workshops for Faculty on New Pedagogical Techniques

**5.12. Board of Studies (BoS) – Mapping to NEP 2020**

**Objective:**

To align the roles and responsibilities of the Board of Studies (BoS) with the principles and directives of the National Education Policy 2020, thereby promoting academic excellence, flexibility, and relevance in curriculum design and delivery.

**BoS Roles Aligned with NEP 2020 Themes**

| **NEP 2020 Theme**                                 | **BoS Function / Mapping**                                                                                                           |
|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Multidisciplinary & Holistic Education             | BoS incorporates courses from various disciplines (e.g., open electives, value-added courses) to foster holistic development.        |
| Academic Flexibility                               | BoS structures UG/PG programs with exit options, credit transfers, and internships in line with NEP's flexible curricular framework. |
| Employability & Skill Development                  | BoS integrates industry-relevant, skill-based and vocational courses to ensure graduates are job-ready.                              |
| Integration of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS)      | Courses include modules or electives that promote Indian knowledge systems, languages, arts, and ethics.                             |
| Research & Inquiry-based Learning (Undergraduate)  | BoS designs curriculum with research projects, minor projects, and inquiry-based learning, even at the UG level.                     |
| Assessment Reforms                                 | BoS ensures that evaluation includes formative assessments, rubrics, and project-based learning as per NEP recommendations.          |
| Digital Learning Technology Use                    | Approval of MOOCs / Online Courses; BoS includes SWAYAM/NPTEL MOOCs as part of curriculum for blended and self-paced learning.       |
| Holistic Development (Life Skills and Soft Skills) | Courses related to communication, ethics, leadership, and emotional intelligence are embedded in the curriculum.                     |
| Stakeholder Consultation (Industry/Alumni)         | BoS invites alumni, employers, and external Stakeholder experts to participate in curriculum design and revision.                    |
| Relevance and Upgradation                          | BoS ensures that the curriculum remains updated, relevant, and aligned with global and national trends.                              |

**BoS Recommendations in line with NEP 2020**

1\. Adopt Academic Bank of Credits (ABC): Encourage credit transfer and accumulation through recognized digital platforms.

2\. Promote Interdisciplinary Courses: Enable combinations across science, humanities, arts, and engineering.

3\. Implement Multiple Entry-Exit Framework (MEES): Design certificate/diploma/degree pathways.

4\. Encourage Project-based and Experiential Learning: Embed real-world problem-solving into coursework.

5\. Inclusion of Environmental and Sustainable Development Courses: Promote responsible citizenship.

6\. Align Outcomes with NHEQF (National Higher Education Qualification Framework): Structure POs and COs to map with NEP's graduate attributes.

**5.13. Best Practices for Board of Studies (BoS)**

| **S.No** | **Best Practice**                                     | **Description**                                                                                                                                                      |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Stakeholder-Inclusive Curriculum Design               | Involve students, alumni, industry experts, and academic peers to gather feedback and ensure the curriculum meets academic and industry expectations.                |
| 2        | Regular Curriculum Updation                           | Conduct curriculum reviews every year (not just at mandated intervals) to incorporate latest trends, technologies, and research findings.                            |
| 3        | Integration of Emerging Fields                        | Introduce electives and modules on AI, Data Science, Blockchain, Sustainable Development, and other emerging areas.                                                  |
| 4        | Outcome-Based Education (OBE) Focus                   | Map all Courses Outcomes (COs) to Program Outcomes (POs) and ensure continuous monitoring and assessment.                                                            |
| 5        | Industry-Academia Collaboration                       | Engage industry professionals in BoS meetings to validate curriculum relevance and suggest real-world applications.                                                  |
| 6        | Interdisciplinary and Multidisciplinary Approach      | Design courses that cross traditional academic boundaries, promoting holistic education and innovation.                                                              |
| 7        | Inclusion of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship   | Integrate skill enhancement modules, internships, live projects, and entrepreneurship development programs into the curriculum.                                      |
| 8        | Encouragement of MOOCs/NPTEL/SWAYAM                   | Recognize and credit online courses to broaden learning opportunities for students and faculty.                                                                      |
| 9        | Use of Technology in Curriculum Delivery              | Encourage the use of Learning Management Systems (LMS), blended learning models, and e-resources in teaching.                                                        |
| 10       | Curriculum Alignment to National and Global Standards | Align syllabi with NEP-2020 guidelines, National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF), SDGs, and global accreditation norms like Washington Accord.                  |
| 11       | Periodic Faculty Workshops                            | Conduct workshops on “Curriculum Design & Development,” “OBE,” and “Innovative Pedagogy” to continuously upgrade faculty capabilities.                               |
| 12       | Student-Centric Course Content                        | Introduce flexibility through Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS), interdisciplinary minors, and open electives.                                                       |
| 13       | Focus on Research and Innovation                      | Include project-based learning, research internships, and dissertation components to cultivate a research mindset early.                                             |
| 14       | Sustainability and Ethics Modules                     | Embed topics on ethics, environmental sustainability, and social responsibility across disciplines.                                                                  |
| 15       | Transparent Documentation                             | Maintain clear records of BoS meetings, stakeholder feedback reports, curriculum revision documents, and approval workflows for easy auditing and quality assurance. |

**6. Finance Committee**

**6.1. Introduction**

The Finance Committee is a statutory body responsible for overseeing and guiding the financial planning, budgeting, monitoring, and utilization of resources in an engineering college or university. It plays a key role in ensuring fiscal accountability, resource optimization, and financial transparency — all of which are crucial for accreditation under NBA and NAAC.

**6.2. Key Objectives of the Finance Committee**

**1. Budget Planning and Allocation:**

> o Develop, review, and approve the institution's annual budget.
>
> o Ensure that financial resources are allocated in alignment with the institution's educational and operational goals.
>
> o Provide recommendations for funding various departments, activities, and capital expenditures.

**2. Financial Oversight:**

> o Monitor the institution's income and expenditure, ensuring that it is within the approved budget.
>
> o Oversee the allocation and management of resources across departments and projects.
>
> o Ensure the institution's financial performance aligns with its objectives.

**3. Revenue Generation:**

> o Identify and propose sources of revenue, such as grants, donations, tuition fees, and other financial avenues.
>
> o Recommend measures for optimizing income generation while ensuring affordability and sustainability.

**4. Cost Control and Efficiency:**

> o Identify areas for cost savings and operational efficiency.
>
> o Monitor financial reports to ensure proper utilization of funds and prevent wastage.
>
> o Implement strategies to reduce costs while maintaining high standards of education and services.

**5. Compliance with Regulations:**

> o Ensure that the institution's financial operations comply with governmental regulations and accreditation standards.
>
> o Oversee audits and ensure adherence to financial policies and procedures.

**6. Investment Planning:**

> o Guide the institution on safe and profitable investment options for its funds.
>
> o Recommend policies for managing investments, ensuring financial growth without undue risk.

**7. Financial Transparency:**

> o Promote transparency in all financial dealings.
>
> o Ensure that financial reports and decisions are communicated effectively to stakeholders, including faculty, students, and governing bodies.

**8. Sustainable Financial Management:**

> o Develop long-term financial strategies for growth, ensuring financial sustainability.
>
> o Plan for future infrastructure development, technological upgrades, and academic growth through sound financial management.

**9. Monitor Financial Health:**

> o Regularly review financial reports to assess the institution's financial health and identify areas for improvement.
>
> o Make recommendations to improve financial stability and ensure that the institution's financial resources support its strategic objectives.

**10. Ensure Accountability:**

> o Hold faculty and administrative departments accountable for the proper utilization of allocated budgets.
>
> o Establish clear financial management guidelines and ensure adherence across all levels of the institution.

**6.3. Composition of Finance Committee**

| **Designation**                          | **Role**                                   |
|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson (Usually Principal/Director) | Heads the Committee                        |
| Management Representative                | Nominee of the Governing Body              |
| Senior Faculty Member                    | From the Academic Council/Dean (Academics) |
| Finance Officer/Bursar                   | Handles accounts and financial reporting   |
| UGC/University Nominee (if applicable)   | Oversight and policy compliance            |
| External Auditor/Advisor (optional)      | Provides financial prudence (invitee)      |

**6.4. Functions of Finance Committee**

| **S.No** | **Function**                                 | **Description**                                                                                                                                       |
|----------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Budget Preparation and Review                | Formulate, recommend, and review the annual budget of the institution covering both recurring and non-recurring expenditures.                         |
| 2        | Approval of Expenditure                      | Scrutinize and approve major financial expenditures, ensuring proper allocation of resources for academic, administrative, and infrastructural needs. |
| 3        | Monitoring Financial Position                | Regularly monitor the financial health of the institution through audits, balance sheets, and financial reports.                                      |
| 4        | Resource Mobilization                        | Suggest strategies for resource generation such as fundraising, grants, donations, alumni contributions, and consultancy projects.                    |
| 5        | Fund Allocation for Research and Development | Allocate funds for promoting research activities, innovation, and faculty development programs.                                                       |
| 6        | Infrastructure Development Support           | Recommend budgets for new building construction, renovation, and campus infrastructure enhancement.                                                   |
| 7        | Scholarships and Financial Aid               | Approve financial aid, scholarships, and fee concessions for deserving students based on merit and economic criteria.                                 |
| 8        | Financial Compliance                         | Ensure all financial practices are in compliance with government regulations, UGC/AICTE norms, and statutory auditing requirements.                   |
| 9        | Monitoring Sponsored and Funded Projects     | Track and report financial activities related to sponsored research projects and government-funded schemes.                                           |
| 10       | Review of Fee Structure                      | Recommend revisions in tuition fees and other charges for various academic programs based on affordability and sustainability.                        |
| 11       | Vendor and Purchase Approval                 | Oversee and approve large procurement proposals and vendor selections to ensure transparency and cost-efficiency.                                     |
| 12       | Internal Audit and Risk Management           | Recommend periodic internal audits, suggest improvements, and mitigate financial risks.                                                               |
| 13       | Annual Reporting                             | Present the institution's financial statements, utilization certificates, and audit reports to the Governing Body for approval.                       |
| 14       | Financial Support Planning                   | Provide financial advice for strategic initiatives like starting new programs, collaborations, or major projects.                                     |

**6.5. Roles and Responsibilities of the Finance Committee**

**Chairperson (Usually the Head of the Institution/Principal)**

> • Preside over all Finance Committee meetings.
>
> • Ensure that financial planning aligns with the institution's strategic goals.
>
> • Approve the agenda and proposals before presenting to Governing Body.
>
> • Act as the link between Finance Committee and the Governing Body.

**Finance Officer / Accounts Officer**

> • Present detailed budgets, income & expenditure statements, audit reports.
>
> • Assist in financial planning, projections, and forecasting.
>
> • Scrutinize and approve proposals for major capital and operational expenditures.
>
> • Ensure expenses are within the approved budget limits.
>
> • Prioritize projects based on institutional needs and funding availability.
>
> • Monitor the management of institutional funds including grants, endowments, donations, and revenues.
>
> • Ensure timely utilization and reporting of funds received from various sources.

**Committee Member Roles and Responsibilities**

> • Senior Faculty Representative, Administrative Officer / Registrar, External Financial Expert / Auditor (if any), Management Representative / Trust/Board Member (for Private Institutions), Student Representative (optional, if included).
>
> • Compliance Officer: Ensure adherence to statutory financial regulations, UGC/AICTE guidelines, and government norms.
>
> • Resource Allocator: Oversee that auditing standards are maintained; address audit observations and implement corrective measures.
>
> • Fee Structure Recommender: Recommend fund allocation to academic departments, research projects, student welfare, infrastructure, and innovations; allocate financial resources for staff development and quality improvement initiatives.
>
> • Monitoring Authority: Review and suggest revisions to tuition fees, hostel fees, transport fees, and other charges periodically; maintain affordability while ensuring institutional financial sustainability.
>
> • Strategic Support Partner: Monitor financial performance through quarterly and annual reports; conduct internal audits and ensure financial transparency; analyze financial risks and recommend mitigation strategies.
>
> • Facilitator for Financial Aid and Scholarships: Provide financial inputs during major decisions like expansion projects, collaborations, or launch of new academic programs; support planning for infrastructure development, ICT upgrades, and research enhancement.
>
> • Vendor Management and Procurement Advisor: Oversee the distribution of scholarships, fellowships, and financial aid to students; ensure transparency and fairness in the selection process; approve major procurement plans; ensure procurement follows due process, tender norms, and achieves cost efficiency.

**6.6. Member-wise Roles and Responsibilities of the Finance Committee**

> • Monitors and allocates budget for research activities and innovations.
>
> • Allocates financial resources for lab upgrades, academic reforms.
>
> • Approves purchases of equipment, ICT tools, and technical resources.
>
> • Ensures sustainability and faculty development through appropriate funding (Criterion 7: Institutional Support).

**6.7. Alignment with NAAC and NBA Accreditation**

| **Accreditation Body & Criterion**                       | **Finance Committee's Contribution**                                        |
|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NAAC Criterion 6: Governance, Leadership & Management    | Supports efficient financial management and autonomy in resource planning.  |
| NAAC Criterion 4: Infrastructure & Learning Resources    | Ensures funds for infrastructure development and maintenance.               |
| NAAC Criterion 3: Research, Innovation & Extension       | Monitors and allocates budget for research activities and innovations.      |
| NAAC Criterion 2: Program Curriculum & Teaching-Learning | Allocates financial resources for lab upgrades, academic reforms.           |
| NAAC Criterion 6: Facilities & Technical Support         | Approves purchases of equipment, ICT tools, and technical resources.        |
| NBA Criterion 7: Institutional Support                   | Ensures sustainability and faculty development through appropriate funding. |

**6.8. Frequency of Meetings**

> • Minimum: Twice a year (before start and end of financial year)
>
> • Special Meetings: As and when required for urgent approvals or financial reviews

**6.9. Documentation Required**

> • Annual Budget Plan
>
> • Minutes of Finance Committee Meetings
>
> • Utilization Certificates
>
> • Audit Reports (Internal & External)
>
> • Expenditure Statements
>
> • Records of Fund Allocations to Departments/Projects

**6.10. Sample Agenda Items**

1\. Approval of Annual Budget

2\. Review of Expenditure vs Budget

3\. Approval of New Capital Expenditure

4\. Discussion on Audit Findings and Compliance

5\. Allocation of R&D/Project Funds

6\. Review of Fee Structures/Financial Aid Proposals

**6.11. Key Documents Maintained by the Finance Committee**

> • **Annual Budget Reports:** Detailed breakdown of the annual income and expenditures, including specific allocations for departments, staff salaries, operational costs, etc.
>
> • **Quarterly/Annual Financial Reports:** Financial statements, including profit and loss, balance sheet, and cash flow statements.
>
> • **Audit Reports:** Reports from internal and external auditors highlighting the institution's financial health and compliance with regulations.
>
> • **Revenue and Expense Analysis:** Detailed reports showing income generation (from tuition, grants, and donations) and expense analysis (salaries, infrastructure, etc.).
>
> • **Investment Reports:** Documentation of all institutional investments, including risk assessments and returns.
>
> • **Grants and Donations Records:** Documentation on any government or non-government funding or donations received by the institution.
>
> • **Capital Expenditure Proposals:** Detailed proposals for infrastructure, technology, and development expenditure, with cost-benefit analysis.

**6.12. Meeting Documentation**

> • **Meeting Agendas:** Documented agendas for each finance committee meeting, including discussion points and key decisions.
>
> • **Minutes of Meetings:** Written records of each meeting, including decisions made, action items, and responsibilities assigned.
>
> • **Follow-up Actions:** A record of actions and resolutions from the previous meetings, ensuring that tasks are completed on time.

**6.13. Finance Committee Reporting**

> • **To the Governing Body:** The Finance Committee should provide periodic reports to the institution's Governing Body or Board of Trustees, summarizing the institution's financial position, challenges, and opportunities.
>
> • **To the Faculty and Staff:** Annual financial reports should be shared with faculty and staff to ensure transparency.
>
> • **To Regulatory Bodies:** Reports required by government bodies or accrediting organizations (e.g., NAAC, UGC) should be prepared and submitted as per guidelines.

**6.14. Periodicity of Finance Committee Meetings**

> • **Quarterly:** Regular quarterly meetings to review financial performance and make necessary adjustments to the budget or financial strategies.
>
> • **Annually:** Annual budget planning and review meeting, including detailed discussions on long-term financial strategies, capital expenditures, and major financial decisions.
>
> • **Special Meetings:** As necessary, for urgent financial matters like unexpected expenses, grants, or major investments.

**6.15. Accountability Guidelines for the Finance Committee**

**1. Reporting to the Governing Body:**

> • The Finance Committee is responsible for **regularly reporting** its discussions and recommendations to the **Governing Body**. This is achieved by maintaining **detailed meeting minutes** and providing comprehensive financial reports that outline the key financial decisions, budgets, and forecasts.
>
> • These reports should ensure that the Governing Body is **well-informed** of the institution's financial health and any potential risks or issues that could affect its stability.

**2. Independent Review of Financial Matters:**

> • The Finance Committee is empowered to conduct independent reviews of financial matters without management present, if necessary. This ensures **objectivity** and **transparency** in the review process, especially when evaluating sensitive financial topics, such as audits, budgets, or discrepancies.

**3. Interaction with the Board Chair:**

> • The Chair of the Finance Committee must maintain clear communication with the Board Chair about any significant financial issues, challenges, or decisions requiring the board's attention. This allows the board chair to be well-prepared for discussions in Governing Body meetings and ensures timely action on financial matters.

**4. Communication with the CEO/President:**

> • The Board Chair should keep the CEO/President informed about financial matters and any potential concerns raised by the Finance Committee. This helps maintain a transparent and consistent flow of information at all levels of leadership.

**5. Conflict of Interest in Financial Decisions:**

> • The Finance Committee is responsible for identifying and managing conflicts of **interest** among committee members or staff involved in financial decisions. If a conflict is identified, the committee may request the affected individual to **recuse themselves** from discussions or decision-making related to that matter to ensure impartiality and the integrity of financial processes.

**6. Ensuring Financial Compliance:**

> • The committee must ensure that the institution's financial activities comply with relevant laws, regulations, and **accreditation standards**. This includes reviewing financial audits, overseeing financial controls, and ensuring the integrity of financial
>
> • The Finance Committee should also **oversee risk management processes**, ensuring that potential financial risks (e.g., cash flow issues, regulatory noncompliance, fraud risks) are adequately mitigated.

**7. Approval of Financial Plans:**

> • The Finance Committee is tasked with **approving financial strategies**, **annual budgets**, and long-term financial forecasts. All financial decisions should align with the institution's strategic objectives and ensure the effective use of resources.
>
> • The committee is also responsible for monitoring and adjusting the **institution's financial performance** against the approved budget and making recommendations for any necessary adjustments.

**8. Oversight of Internal Controls and Audits:**

> • The committee ensures that **adequate internal controls** are in place to safeguard the institution's assets and ensure compliance with financial regulations. This includes overseeing the **internal audit processes** and ensuring that external audits are conducted appropriately and issues are resolved.
>
> • The Finance Committee is responsible for reviewing audit findings and ensuring that any **financial discrepancies or concerns** are addressed promptly.

**9. Transparency and Communication with Stakeholders:**

> • The Finance Committee ensures that there is **transparency** in the financial decision-making process, particularly with regard to budgeting, fundraising, and use of institutional funds. It should make the necessary financial information available to relevant stakeholders, such as faculty, staff, students, and donors, where appropriate.

**10. Regular Review of Financial Performance:**

> • The committee must regularly monitor and review the institution's financial performance in relation to the approved budget and long-term financial goals. The Finance Committee is responsible for reporting significant variances and proposing corrective actions when necessary.

**6.16. Budgeting and Control-Based Policies**

**1. Advance Budget Notifications:**

> • The Finance Committee shall notify the financial budgets for the academic year, which must be made available to the departments six months ahead of the start of the academic year. This early notification ensures that all departments can plan and manage their finances effectively in line with institutional goals.

**2. Budget Submission Process for Organizational Units:**

> • Each organizational unit (e.g., departments, research centers) requiring financial resources to meet their operational, maintenance, and development expenses must submit a comprehensive financial plan five months before the academic year starts.
>
> • The plan should outline:
>
> o Operational Expenditure: Costs for consumables.
>
> o Maintenance Expenditure: Costs for upkeep and servicing of physical infrastructure.
>
> o Development Expenditure (Capital Expenditure): Costs for expansion, upgrades, or infrastructure improvements.
>
> • The plan should include detailed descriptions of the physical resources required, with proper specifications for each item.

**3. Financial Estimates for Resources:**

> • The Estimate Committee is tasked with preparing financial estimates for the required physical resources based on the submitted plans, ensuring that they align with budgetary constraints.

**4. Procurement Proposals:**

> • Organizational units requiring the purchase of goods or services must submit a procurement proposal to the Finance Officer. The Finance Officer is responsible for:
>
> o Verifying that the proposal is in line with the approved budgetary provisions.
>
> o Confirming the availability of funds.
>
> o Submitting recommendations to the Finance Committee for scrutiny.
>
> • The Finance Committee will review the proposal and, after due consideration, seek approval from the Chairman.
>
> • Once approved, the proposal is forwarded to the Finance Officer, the In-charge Purchase, and the respective organizational unit to proceed with the procurement process.

**5. Procurement Process:**

> • The In-charge Purchase shall follow the standard procurement procedures to ensure that purchases are made in an efficient, transparent, and cost-effective manner. The Central Stores will manage the distribution of procured items, providing the necessary goods to the respective organizational units through an issue note.

**6. Construction and Infrastructure Procurement:**

> • For construction projects, the In-charge Construction will prepare a detailed engineering proposal outlining the necessary materials and services required for the project.
>
> • This proposal is submitted to the Finance Officer, who verifies the proposal with reference to budgetary provisions. The verified proposal is then forwarded to the Finance Committee, which seeks approval from the President.
>
> • After receiving approval, the proposal is sent back to the Estimate Committee and Finance Officer for further processing.

**7. Expenditure Control:**

> • All expenditure must strictly align with the approved budget. Any expenditure related to the purchase of goods, services, or conducting activities requires prior approval from the Principal/Chairman.
>
> • The institution reserves the right to re-appropriate the budgeted expenditure as necessary, based on utility, necessity, or for other unforeseen reasons. This ensures financial flexibility and adaptability to changing circumstances during the academic year.
>
> • Preparing the Budget Estimates for the next financial year and the Revised Estimates for the current year.
>
> • Submitting these documents to the Board of Management (BOM) through the Finance Committee.

**6. Specific Duties (Budget Oversight role):**

> • Budget Oversight: Ensure that the limits set in the budget for both recurring and non-recurring expenditure are adhered to, and that funds are only used for their designated purposes, subject to the Finance Rules of the institution.
>
> • Monitoring Unspent Balances: Keep track of any unspent balances under various budget heads and bring them to the notice of the principal.
>
> • Bank Balances and Investments: Regularly monitor the college's bank balances and investment status and report them to the principal.
>
> • Revenue Collection: Oversee the progress of revenue collection and recommend effective methods to avoid delays or errors.
>
> • Audit: Ensure that the college's accounts are audited regularly as per the Board of Management's prescribed procedure. The Audit Report and any audit objections must be presented to the BOM along with appropriate explanations.
>
> • Addressing Financial Irregularities: Investigate unauthorized expenditure or other financial irregularities, demand explanations from employees responsible, and recommend disciplinary action if needed.
>
> • Information Requests: Request financial information or returns from any office or department deemed necessary for carrying out the Finance Officer's duties.
>
> • No Dues Certificates: Issue “No Dues Certificates” to employees being relieved or retiring after verifying their financial status.

**7. Receipt Issuance:**

> • The receipts issued by the Finance Officer or any employee authorized by the principal for payments made to the college shall be valid proof of the transaction and shall serve as a sufficient discharge for the payment.

**8. Other Functions:**

> • The Finance Officer may perform other functions as assigned by the Governing Body, the Principal, or as specified in the Rules or Regulations of the institution.

**6.17. Powers and Duties of the Finance Officer**

**1. Appointment and Eligibility:**

> • The Finance Officer (F.O.) shall be appointed according to the provisions of the institution's regulations. The salary and allowances of the Finance Officer will be determined by the Governing Body.

**2. Interim Appointment:**

> • In the event that the office of the Finance Officer is vacant, the duties of the Finance Officer will be performed by an Administrative Officer appointed by the principal.

**3. Accounting Responsibilities:**

> • The Finance Officer is responsible for maintaining the accounts of the college and providing advice on all matters related to income and expenditure.

**4. Secretary to the Finance Committee:**

> • The Finance Officer serves as the Secretary of the Finance Committee, facilitating the smooth operation and reporting of the committee's activities.

**5. Preparation of Accounts and Budget Estimates:**

> • The Finance Officer is responsible for preparing the Annual Accounts for the previous year.

**9. Financial Authority:**

> • The Finance Officer has the authority to pass bills and issue cheques for payments on behalf of the college. In the absence of the Finance Officer, this responsibility is delegated to the Administrative Officer (AO) or any other designated officer, who may also have the power to pass bills and sign cheques.

**6.18. Fee Payments by Students**

**1. Payment Deadline:**

> • All students are required to pay their tuition and other fees in full within one month from the beginning of each academic year.

**2. Delayed or Part Payments:**

> • Delayed payments or part payments must be approved by the principal. If no approval is obtained, the fee payment will be considered as unpaid.
>
> • The principal may permit delayed or part payments for a maximum period of 15 days only. After this period, fees will be considered overdue.

**3. Non-Refundable Fees:**

> • Fees, once paid, cannot be refunded or adjusted in any manner for reasons such as:
>
> o Discontinuation of studies
>
> o Detention
>
> o Approved leave
>
> o Any other similar reason.

**4. Annual Payment:**

> • Fees paid by the students will be considered for the entire academic year and cannot be adjusted or refunded for any specific semester.

**5. Additional Fees:**

> • Extra Training Fees: Students shall pay separately for any extra training provided that enhances the skills required by the industry.
>
> • Transport Charges and Hostel Fees: These will be paid separately in addition to tuition fees and any fees for extra training.
>
> • Caution Deposit: Students are required to pay a caution deposit. This deposit will be refunded when the student leaves the college, after deducting charges for:
>
> o ID card
>
> o Industrial Visits
>
> o Alumni membership
>
> o Souvenir charges
>
> o Any outstanding dues in college labs.

**6.19. Funds from Donators**

**1. Purpose of Donations:**

> • Donations can be collected for various purposes, including but not limited to:
>
> o Research Funding: Supporting research projects and academic initiatives.
>
> o Infrastructure Development: Enhancing and expanding the physical infrastructure of the institution.
>
> o Development of Amenities: Improving facilities such as libraries, labs, sports facilities, and student welfare programs.
>
> o Scholarships: Funding scholarships to support deserving students financially and encourage academic excellence.

**2. Donation Management:**

> • All donations must be properly documented, specifying the purpose for which the funds are intended.
>
> • A transparent system should be in place to manage and allocate donations in accordance with the specified objectives.

**3. Acknowledgement of Donations:**

> • Donors should receive proper acknowledgment for their contributions, including receipts and recognition in relevant institutional communications (annual reports, websites, etc.).
>
> • Special appreciation or recognition can be given to major donors, including naming rights for certain facilities or scholarships.

**4. Utilization of Funds:**

> • Donations will be strictly utilized for the designated purposes as agreed upon by the institution and the donors.
>
> • The institution should ensure proper auditing of the funds to ensure transparency and accountability in their use.

**6.20. Funds from External Organizations**

**1. Approach to External Funding Sources:**

> • External organizations such as the World Bank, AICTE, UGC, DST, CSIR and other government or international bodies are critical sources for securing financial support for the institution's growth and development.
>
> • The institution will initiate formal applications and proposals to these organizations for obtaining funds dedicated to specific projects and needs.

**2. Specialized Infrastructure Projects:**

> • Excellence Centers: The funds may be sought to establish or upgrade centers of excellence in specialized fields such as research, innovation, or specific academic disciplines.
>
> • Laboratories and Research Facilities: Donations or grants can be requested to set up state-of-the-art laboratories, research centers, and facilities for practical learning.

**3. Application Process:**

> • Proposal Development: The institution must prepare detailed project proposals highlighting the need for the specific infrastructure, expected outcomes, budget estimates, and timelines.
>
> • Documentation and Compliance: All required documentation, including institutional accreditations, financial statements, and compliance with regulatory guidelines, must be submitted as part of the application.
>
> • Monitoring and Reporting: Once funds are received, the institution is obligated to report regularly on the utilization of funds and progress of the infrastructure projects. External organizations may require periodic audits and assessments to ensure transparency.

**4. Specific Uses of Funds:**

> • Laboratories and Equipment: Funds can be allocated to upgrade or develop laboratories with the latest equipment, which can enhance students' hands-on learning experiences and facilitate research.
>
> • Faculty Development: Some external funds may also be directed towards faculty training and development programs.
>
> • Technological Advancements: Funding can also be aimed at introducing advanced technologies in teaching, learning, and research, such as digital classrooms, elearning platforms, and specialized software.

**5. Sustainability and Long-Term Goals:**

> • Funds must be utilized not just for immediate needs, but also with a focus on sustainable growth, ensuring that the infrastructure or programs funded continue to benefit the institution in the long term.
>
> • Clear plans for maintenance and operational sustainability should be outlined when applying for external funding.

**6.21. Policies Related to Payments**

**1. Supporting Documentation for Payments:**

> • Invoices and Bills: Every payment made must be accompanied by valid invoices or bills that detail the nature of the goods/services rendered.
>
> • Purchase Orders (PO) / Work Orders: Invoices and bills must reference the corresponding Purchase Orders (PO) or Work Orders, ensuring that the payment corresponds to an authorized request.
>
> • Financial Approval: All payments must be backed by prior financial approval, confirming that the expenditure is within the allocated budget.

**2. Payment Processing Workflow:**

> • Department Heads (HoDs): HoDs initiate the payment request by reviewing and verifying the need for the payment and ensuring that the supporting documentation (invoice, bill, PO/Work Order) is complete and accurate.
>
> • Finance Officer's Vetting: The Finance Officer then vets the payment request to ensure that it aligns with the approved budget and there are no discrepancies. They also check the financial aspects for compliance with institutional policies and procedures.
>
> • Finance Committee Recommendation: Once vetted by the Finance Officer, the payment request is recommended by the Finance Committee for further approval, ensuring that the expenditure aligns with strategic financial goals.
>
> • Approval by Chairman/Principal: The final approval for the payment is granted by the Chairman or Principal, ensuring that the payment is within institutional guidelines and priorities.

**3. Payment Process Flow:**

> • The payment must follow a clear and documented approval process to maintain financial accountability and transparency.
>
> • Regular audits may be conducted to ensure compliance with these processes.

**4. Exceptions and Delays:**

> • Exception Handling: Any deviations from the standard payment process (e.g., delayed payments or part payments) must be formally requested and approved by the Principal.
>
> • Delayed Payments: Any delays or part payments beyond the stipulated time will require special approval from the principal, who may allow an extension up to a maximum of 15 days.

**5. Audit and Compliance:**

> • Payments are subject to both internal and external audits to ensure that financial resources are utilized in accordance with the institution's policies, and the funds are appropriately allocated for their intended purpose.

**6. Communication and Documentation:**

> • The Finance Officer is responsible for maintaining accurate records of all payment transactions and ensuring the proper documentation (invoices, bills, PO/Work Orders) is stored for audit purposes.

**6.22. Policies on Advances**

**1. Advances to Suppliers or Service Organizations:**

> • Conditions for Payment: Advances can only be paid to suppliers or service organizations if the terms are explicitly mentioned in the service contract or purchase orders.
>
> • Bank Guarantees Requirement: Any advance paid to suppliers or service organizations must be secured against bank guarantees, ensuring that the institution's funds are protected.

**2. Advances to Employees:**

> • Employee Advances: Employees can request advances for specific purposes (such as travel, project-related expenses, etc.), but they must obtain approval from the President prior to drawing such advances.
>
> • Approval Process: The President must authorize the payment of advances, ensuring that the requested advance is for legitimate and authorized purposes.

**3. Outstanding Advances Monitoring:**

> • Monthly Statement Submission: The Finance Officer is responsible for submitting a monthly statement of all outstanding advances to the President. This allows the institution to monitor the status of advances and take any necessary corrective actions.
>
> • Corrective Actions: The President reviews the statement and may take corrective actions if there are unutilized or unaccounted advances, ensuring that funds are being used properly.

**4. Settlement of Advances:**

> • Timely Settlement: Any advances drawn for approved expenditure must be settled within two weeks of being issued. If the advance is not settled within this period, it is considered overdue.
>
> • Salary Deduction: Advances that are not settled within the stipulated period will be deducted from the salary of the employee who received the advance, without any further intimation. This serves as a corrective measure to ensure timely settlement.

**5. Audit and Compliance:**

> • Advances are subject to regular audit checks to ensure that they are being issued for legitimate reasons and settled in a timely manner.
>
> • The Finance Officer will also ensure that all advances are properly recorded and monitored to avoid financial discrepancies.

**6. Documentation and Transparency:**

> • Proper documentation for each advance (including the purpose, approval, amount, and terms) must be maintained. This ensures transparency and accountability in the issuance and settlement of advances.

**6.23. Construction-Related Payments Policy**
