>
> • Conducting regular Satisfaction Surveys (student, faculty, employer).

**8. Planning & Development Board/Committee**

**8.1. Introduction**

The Planning and Development Committee (P&D Committee) is a strategic body constituted in engineering and higher education institutions to drive institutional growth, policy formulation, infrastructure expansion, and quality enhancement. It acts as an advisory and executive body that supports long-term and short-term institutional goals, ensuring alignment with NAAC criteria and NBA program-level expectations.

**8.2. Objectives**

> • To prepare strategic and development plans aligned with the Vision and Mission of the institution.
>
> • To assess academic, administrative, financial, and infrastructural needs of the institution.
>
> • To monitor the implementation of policies, infrastructural projects, and academic initiatives.
>
> • To align institutional planning with quality benchmarks of NAAC and NBA.
>
> • To promote sustainable and inclusive growth through informed planning and resource mobilization.

**8.3. Composition of the Committee**

| **Designation**                           | **Role**                                               |
|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| Principal / Director (Chairperson)        | Leads the committee and finalizes proposals            |
| Vice Principal / Dean (Academic/Admin)    | Coordinates academic & administrative perspectives     |
| Senior Faculty Members (HODs/Professors)  | Provide academic insight and program development input |
| IQAC Coordinator                          | Advises on financial feasibility and budgeting         |
| Finance Officer / Accounts In-charge      | Provides planning input for physical infrastructure    |
| Estate Officer / Infrastructure Head      | Offers external and futuristic perspective             |
| Alumni/Industry/Management Representative | Assists with logistics and documentation               |
| Administrative Officer                    | Ensures quality alignment with NAAC/NBA standards      |

**8.4. Functions of the Planning & Development Board/Committee**

| **Sl.No** | **Function**                        | **Description**                                                                                                                  |
|-----------|-------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1         | Strategic Planning                  | Formulate long-term and short-term development plans aligned with the institution's vision and mission.                          |
| 2         | Infrastructure Development          | Identify needs for new infrastructure, renovation, modernization, and expansion projects.                                        |
| 3         | Academic Planning                   | Support academic growth through the introduction of new programs, courses, research centers, and collaborations.                 |
| 4         | Resource Mobilization               | Plan for financial resources including government grants, private sponsorships, industry partnerships, and alumni contributions. |
| 5         | Budgeting Support                   | Recommend major development projects and their budgetary needs to the Finance Committee and Governing Body.                      |
| 6         | Monitoring and Evaluation           | Track the progress of ongoing development projects and evaluate their outcomes.                                                  |
| 7         | Policy Development                  | Frame policies related to institutional growth, including quality assurance, green initiatives, and innovation policies.         |
| 8         | Stakeholder Engagement              | Engage with students, faculty, alumni, industry, and community stakeholders for input on development plans.                      |
| 9         | Collaboration and MoUs              | Promote national and international collaborations for academic and research development.                                         |
| 10        | Sustainability Initiatives          | Integrate sustainable and eco-friendly practices into planning and development projects.                                         |
| 11        | Accreditation and Ranking Readiness | Plan developmental activities to improve institutional rankings and meet accreditation requirements.                             |
| 12        | Reporting and Documentation         | Prepare and submit regular reports on planning and development activities to the Governing Body.                                 |

**8.5. Roles and Responsibilities of Planning & Development Board/Committee**

**Chairperson (usually Principal/Director)**

> • Lead strategic planning and development activities.
>
> • Approve agendas and chair meetings.
>
> • Represent the institution's vision and mission in development initiatives.
>
> • Communicate proposals to Governing Body for approval.

**Dean/Head of Planning & Development**

> • Draft detailed development plans.
>
> • Prepare infrastructure, academic, and research expansion proposals.
>
> • Coordinate between departments for gathering development requirements.
>
> • Monitor project progress.

**Faculty Representatives**

> • Identify departmental infrastructure and academic needs.
>
> • Propose research and innovation facilities.
>
> • Support policy formulation related to academic development.

**Finance Officer**

> • Assist in preparing financial estimates for development projects.
>
> • Analyze budgetary impact and funding sources.
>
> • Recommend resource mobilization strategies.

**Administrative Officer**

> • Manage administrative approvals and clearances for development projects.
>
> • Maintain implementation and documentation related to project progress and reporting.

**Industry/External Experts (if applicable)**

> • Provide insights on industry trends for future-readiness.
>
> • Suggest collaborations and resource mobilization through CSR or other channels.

**Student/Alumni Representatives (optional)**

> • Provide feedback on infrastructure, academic, and extracurricular needs.
>
> • Suggest alumni-supported initiatives for institutional development.

**Member Secretary Roles and Responsibilities**

> • Organize meetings, circulate notices, prepare minutes.
>
> • Keep records of all proposals, action items, and approvals.
>
> • Facilitate communication between stakeholders.

**General Responsibilities of the Planning & Development Board:**

> • Conduct need assessments periodically.
>
> • Draft strategic and master plans (5-year plans, Vision 2030 plans, etc.).
>
> • Prioritize projects based on institutional goals.
>
> • Coordinate with external agencies for grants and approvals.
>
> • Ensure compliance with regulatory bodies (like UGC, AICTE, NAAC, NBA guidelines).
>
> • Promote sustainability and innovation in development projects.

**8.10. Best Practices for Planning & Development Committee**

The Planning & Development Committee (PDC) plays a critical role in the long-term success of an institution. It ensures that the vision, mission, and strategic goals of the institution are met through thoughtful planning, resource allocation, and continuous evaluation. Below are some best practices that can be adopted by the Planning & Development Committee to enhance institutional growth and development:

**1. Strategic Planning and Vision Alignment**

> • **Clear Vision and Mission Alignment:** Ensure that all institutional plans align with the long-term vision and mission of the institution. This involves periodic reviews to ensure that goals remain relevant.
>
> • **Comprehensive Planning:** Develop long-term and short-term plans that address academic, administrative, infrastructural, and financial growth.
>
> • **Stakeholder Involvement:** Involve key stakeholders—faculty, students, alumni, industry partners, and governing bodies—in the planning process to gather diverse perspectives and align objectives.

**2. Data-Driven Decision Making**

> • **Evidence-Based Planning:** Base decisions on data and research, such as student performance data, financial reports, faculty feedback, and industry trends. This ensures that plans are realistic, measurable, and achievable.
>
> • **SWOT Analysis:** Regularly conduct SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analyses to assess institutional performance and identify areas for improvement.
>
> • **Annual Performance Reviews:** Implement a systematic review of performance indicators (academic, financial, infrastructure) to measure progress toward strategic goals.

**3. Infrastructure Development and Management**

> • **Sustainable Infrastructure Planning:** Develop a roadmap for the sustainable development of the institution's infrastructure, including classrooms, laboratories, sports facilities, hostels, and libraries.
>
> • **Technology Integration:** Plan for the integration of new technologies and digital tools to enhance teaching, learning, and administrative efficiency.
>
> • **Maintenance Plans:** Establish preventive maintenance and periodic review of institutional infrastructure to avoid sudden breakdowns or inefficiencies.

**4. Budgeting and Resource Allocation**

> • **Transparent Budgeting:** Develop a transparent budgeting process where resources are allocated based on institutional priorities. Ensure that resources are optimally utilized.
>
> • **Resource Optimization:** Implement strategies to optimize the use of resources, reduce waste, and maximize the impact of every expenditure.
>
> • **Grant and Fund Acquisition:** Actively seek funding through government schemes, private donors, and industry partnerships to supplement the institution's budget.

**5. Faculty and Staff Development**

> • **Professional Development Programs:** Plan and implement continuous professional development (CPD) programs for faculty and staff to enhance their skills and knowledge.
>
> • **Succession Planning:** Create a succession plan to ensure the institution has a pipeline of qualified individuals for leadership roles, minimizing disruptions due to retirements or resignations.
>
> • **Work-Life Balance Initiatives:** Introduce programs that promote the well-being of staff and faculty, such as wellness programs, flexible work schedules, and counseling support.

**6. Student-Centric Initiatives**

> • **Student Support Systems:** Develop and maintain robust student support systems, including academic counseling, mental health support, and career services.
>
> • **Involvement in Decision-Making:** Engage students in decision-making processes, particularly regarding changes to the curriculum, extracurricular activities, and student services.
>
> • **Student Feedback Integration:** Regularly collect and integrate student feedback into the planning process to improve the learning environment and overall student experience.

**7. Innovation and Research**

> • **Encourage Research and Innovation:** Develop a strategy to promote research and innovation within the institution by encouraging faculty and students to participate in research projects, conferences, and publications.
>
> • **Collaborative Partnerships:** Foster partnerships with industry, research organizations, and other institutions to promote collaborative research and share knowledge.
>
> • **Establish Innovation Hubs:** Set up dedicated spaces for innovation, such as incubators or research labs, to support students and faculty in their entrepreneurial and research activities.

**8. Regular Monitoring and Evaluation**

> • **Progress Monitoring:** Regularly monitor the progress of strategic plans and initiatives through set timelines, periodic reviews, and measurable KPIs (Key Performance Indicators).
>
> • **Periodic Reports:** Publish and present regular reports on institutional progress, financial health, and academic performance to stakeholders, ensuring transparency and accountability.
>
> • **Benchmarking Against Best Practices:** Compare institutional practices with those of leading institutions to ensure continuous improvement and maintain competitiveness.

**9. Accreditation and Quality Assurance**

> • **Accreditation Compliance:** Ensure that the institution is compliant with accreditation standards, and consistently work towards achieving or maintaining quality certifications.
>
> • **Internal Quality Reviews:** Implement internal audits and reviews to evaluate the institution's operations, processes, and outcomes, making necessary adjustments based on findings.
>
> • **Continuous Improvement:** Develop mechanisms for continual improvement based on internal and external evaluations, ensuring the institution maintains high academic standards and operational excellence.

**10. Alumni and Industry Engagement**

> • **Active Alumni Network:** Build and maintain a robust alumni network that can support the institution in various ways, including donations, mentoring, internships, and placement assistance.
>
> • **Industry Collaborations:** Strengthen industry-academia partnerships for internships, placements, joint research, and knowledge exchange programs.
>
> • **Alumni Feedback:** Regularly engage alumni to get feedback on their academic experiences and how the institution can further improve in preparing students for the workforce.

**11. Environmental Sustainability**

> • **Sustainability Planning:** Incorporate environmental sustainability into institutional planning, including energy-efficient buildings, waste management, and green campuses.
>
> • **Green Initiatives:** Promote green initiatives such as tree planting, water conservation, and waste segregation to reduce the institution's carbon footprint.
>
> • **Sustainable Practices in Academics:** Integrate sustainability themes into the curriculum, encouraging students to think about environmental challenges and solutions.

**12. Community Engagement**

> • **Social Responsibility Programs:** Plan and implement community outreach programs that allow students and staff to give back to society, such as blood donation drives, health camps, and educational support for underprivileged communities.
>
> • **Public-Private Partnerships:** Collaborate with governmental and non-governmental organizations for community development initiatives, such as skill-building workshops or vocational training.
>
> • **Volunteering and CSR Initiatives:** Encourage students and faculty to participate in corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiatives by partnering with industry organizations and local communities.

**8.11. Conclusion**

By following these best practices, the Planning & Development Committee can ensure that the institution operates efficiently, stays aligned with its long-term goals, and responds effectively to changes in the educational landscape. These practices help build a strong foundation for academic excellence, sustainability, and community engagement, leading to the overall growth and success of the institution.

**9. Admission Committee**

**9.1. Introduction**

The Admission Committee is a core institutional body responsible for managing, regulating, and overseeing the student admission process. It ensures transparency, adherence to regulatory norms, and fair access to academic programs in accordance with statutory and accreditation standards. Its effective functioning reflects the institution's commitment to inclusiveness, quality, and equity in higher education.

**9.2. Objectives**

> • To facilitate fair, transparent, and merit-based admission processes.
>
> • To comply with the guidelines of regulatory bodies like AICTE, UGC, APSCHE, DTE, and University norms etc.
>
> • To ensure reservation policies and admission quotas are implemented correctly.
>
> • To monitor and document admission statistics for internal quality assurance and external audits (NBA/NAAC).
>
> • To promote diversity and inclusiveness in student intake.

**9.3. Composition of the Committee**

| **Designation**                                   | **Role**                                                            |
|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Principal / Director (Chairperson)                | Supervises the overall admission process                            |
| Admission Coordinator (Convener)                  | Coordinates day-to-day admission activities                         |
| HoDs (of various departments)                     | Guide department-specific admissions                                |
| Senior Faculty Representatives                    | Assist in counseling and document verification                      |
| Administrative Officer                            | Handles records, verifications, and government compliance           |
| Accounts Officer                                  | Assists in fee structure, scholarships, and financial documentation |
| Examination Section Representative                | Ensures academic eligibility and document scrutiny                  |
| SC/ST/OBC/Minority Cell Representative            | Ensures reservation norms are followed                              |
| Parent/Alumni/Industry Representatives (optional) | Encourage transparency and external observation                     |

**9.4. Functions of Admission Committee**

| **Sl.No** | **Function**                           | **Description**                                                                                                                       |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1         | Formulate Admission Policy             | Design and periodically review policies in alignment with university/AICTE/UGC norms.                                                 |
| 2         | Publicize Admission Notifications      | Ensure timely dissemination of course-wise admission information through official portals, print media, and social platforms.         |
| 3         | Manage Application Process             | Oversee the collection, verification, and processing of application forms, documents, and fee payments.                               |
| 4         | Conduct Counseling and Orientation     | Guide applicants regarding course selection, eligibility, career opportunities, and institutional facilities.                         |
| 5         | Monitor Reservation & Quota Compliance | Ensure adherence to reservation norms (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PH/NRI/Management quota etc.) as per government and affiliating body guidelines. |
| 6         | Prepare and Publish Merit Lists        | Generate and release course-specific merit or rank lists based on qualifying criteria, entrance scores, or other benchmarks.          |
| 7         | Facilitate Allotment & Admissions      | Supervise the final seat allotment and admission of selected candidates, including waitlisted ones.                                   |
| 8         | Coordinate with Regulatory Bodies      | Liaise with affiliating university, AICTE/UGC, and government agencies for compliance and reporting.                                  |
| 9         | Maintain Admission Records             | Ensure secure documentation and digital storage of student data, admission forms, and supporting certificates.                        |
| 10        | Address Admission Grievances           | Provide a platform for addressing admission-related issues or appeals in a transparent and time-bound manner.                         |

**9.5. Roles & Responsibilities**

**Before Admission**

> • Prepare and publicize the Prospectus/Information Brochure and program offerings.
>
> • Display eligibility criteria, intake capacity, fee structure, and admission schedule.
>
> • Conduct awareness and outreach programs, particularly in rural and underserved areas.
>
> • Set up online/offline admission portals for efficient data handling.
>
> • Coordinate with government portals (e.g., AP EAMCET, JoSAA, DASA, NRI, Management quota).

**During Admission**

> • Verify original documents (marksheets, transfer certificate, caste certificate, etc.).
>
> • Ensure adherence to reservation policy, lateral entry, and special quotas.
>
> • Coordinate with Academic and Finance departments for smooth student onboarding.
>
> • Assist with provisional admission and scholarship/fee reimbursement processes.

**After Admission**

> • Prepare detailed Admission Reports: category-wise, branch-wise, gender-wise, and region-wise.
>
> • Submit admission data to IQAC, University, State Council, and accreditation bodies.
>
> • Maintain a student admission register (soft & hard copies).
>
> • Monitor diversity metrics and inclusion practices.
>
> • Collect feedback from newly admitted students and parents for further improvement.

**10. Internal Complaint Committee (ICC)**

**10.1. Introduction**

The Internal Complaint Committee (ICC) is a statutory body mandated by the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition, and Redressal) Act, 2013, and UGC regulations. It is mandatory for all higher education institutions to establish an ICC to address issues related to sexual harassment and gender-based discrimination on campus.

The existence and effective functioning of ICC contribute to the Institutional Values and Best Practices criterion in NAAC and ensure compliance with ethical and safe practices, also supporting NBA's vision for student and faculty welfare.

**10.2. Objectives**

> • To ensure a safe and secure environment for women students, faculty, and staff.
>
> • To implement the provisions of the POSH Act, 2013 in letter and spirit.
>
> • To provide a confidential and neutral platform for redressing complaints.
>
> • To conduct awareness campaigns about gender sensitization and respectful behavior.
>
> • To promote a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual harassment.

**10.3. Composition of ICC**

As per UGC & AICTE guidelines:

| **Position**                        | **Eligibility**                                                 |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Presiding Officer (Chairperson)     | Senior woman faculty member (preferably at least 10 years' exp) |
| 2 Faculty Members                   | Experience in social work/legal knowledge                       |
| 1 Non-teaching Staff Representative | Woman employee preferred                                        |
| 1 Student Representative            | From UG/PG/Research (based on case type)                        |
| 1 External Member                   | NGO or legal expert in women's rights                           |

*At least 50% of the ICC members must be women.*

**10.4. Functions of the Internal Complaint Committee (ICC)**

**1. Receive Complaints:**

> o The ICC is responsible for receiving complaints related to any form of harassment, discrimination, or any other misconduct, including sexual harassment, caste discrimination, or any violation of the institution's code of conduct.
>
> o The committee provides a confidential and safe platform for individuals to report incidents without fear of retaliation.

**2. Investigation of Complaints:**

> o The ICC conducts a thorough and impartial investigation into the complaints received.
>
> o The committee gathers evidence, interviews witnesses, and ensures that all parties involved are heard.
>
> o The committee adheres to a fair and transparent process while handling complaints.

**3. Maintain Confidentiality:**

> o Ensures confidentiality throughout the process of complaint handling, protecting the identity of the complainant and the accused to the extent possible.
>
> o Prevents any disclosure of information that could lead to retaliation against the complainant or any other party involved.

**4. Resolution of Complaints:**

> o After investigation, the ICC recommends appropriate actions based on the severity and nature of the complaint.
>
> o Actions may include counseling, warnings, suspension, or other disciplinary measures.
>
> o The committee ensures that the resolution respects the rights of both the complainant and the accused, aiming for a fair and just outcome.

**5. Awareness and Education:**

> o Organizes awareness programs, workshops, and seminars to educate students, staff, and faculty about their rights and responsibilities.
>
> o Promotes awareness regarding issues such as sexual harassment, gender equality, and anti-discrimination policies within the institution.
>
> o Ensures that all individuals within the institution understand the procedure for filing complaints and the importance of creating a respectful and safe environment.

**6. Monitoring the Implementation of Policies:**

> o The ICC ensures that the institution's policies related to harassment, discrimination, and misconduct are being effectively implemented and followed.
>
> o It monitors whether the decisions taken by the committee are being properly executed and that corrective actions are followed.

**7. Periodic Review of Policies:**

> o The committee reviews existing policies and practices related to complaints and grievances to ensure they are relevant, comprehensive, and in alignment with legal standards.
>
> o It recommends updates or changes to institutional policies based on emerging needs, trends, and the legal landscape.

**8. Conflict Resolution:**

> o The committee may help mediate conflicts and disputes between students, faculty, and staff in a constructive and non-confrontational manner.
>
> o It aims to resolve conflicts through dialogue, mutual understanding, and mediation before the situation escalates.

**9. Report Submission:**

> o The ICC prepares periodic reports regarding the complaints received, their resolution, and the outcomes.
>
> o It submits these reports to the appropriate authorities, including the administration, to ensure accountability and transparency.

**10. Support and Counseling:**

> o The committee provides necessary support to complainants, including counseling services and guidance throughout the process.
>
> o It may recommend external resources for counseling or legal assistance if required.

**11. Follow-Up:**

> o The committee follows up on the status of complaints to ensure that the actions and decisions taken are effective and that no further issues arise.
>
> o It ensures that the complainant is satisfied with the resolution and that no retaliation occurs.

**12. Preventive Measures:**

> o The ICC works proactively to create a safe and inclusive environment by identifying and mitigating potential risks or sources of harassment or discrimination.
>
> o It suggests preventive measures such as awareness campaigns and policy reforms to reduce incidents of harassment or discrimination in the future.

**10.5. Roles & Responsibilities**

**Complaint Redressal**

> • Receive, investigate, and resolve complaints of sexual harassment.
>
> • Ensure confidentiality and impartiality throughout the process.
>
> • Submit findings to the Head of Institution for disciplinary action if required.

**Preventive Measures**

> • Conduct gender sensitization programs, workshops, and seminars.
>
> • Display anti-harassment policies prominently on campus.
>
> • Collaborate with Women Empowerment Cell and HR/Student Affairs for awareness initiatives.

**Documentation & Reporting**

> • Maintain a register of complaints (with due confidentiality).
>
> • Submit annual reports to the affiliating University, AICTE, and UGC as required.
>
> • Document proactive activities to show prevention initiatives.

**10.6. Contribution to NAAC Criteria**

| **NAAC Criterion**                                   | **Contribution of ICC**                                                           |
|------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 1: Curricular Aspects                      | Integrates gender studies, ethics, and sensitization through value-added programs |
| Criterion 5: Student Support and Progression         | Ensures psychological safety and grievance redressal for women students           |
| Criterion 6: Governance, Leadership and Management   | Reflects institutional transparency and accountability                            |
| Criterion 7: Institutional Values and Best Practices | Promotes gender equity and safe campus initiatives                                |

**10.7. Contribution to NBA Criteria**

| **NBA Criterion**                         | **Contribution of ICC**                                                        |
|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 6: Faculty Contributions        | Supports faculty well-being and ethical teaching environment                   |
| Criterion 8: First-Year Induction Program | Sensitization on anti-ragging, gender rights, and safety included in induction |
| Criterion 10: Student Support Systems     | Provides a structured support mechanism for female students and staff          |

**10.8. Mandatory Compliance**

According to AICTE/UGC regulations, each HEI must:

> • Constitute an Internal Complaint Committee (ICC).
>
> • Display names, roles, and contact details of ICC members on the institution's website.
>
> • Conduct minimum 2 awareness sessions per academic year.
>
> • Submit Annual Reports indicating:
>
> o Number of complaints received/resolved.
>
> o Preventive actions and sensitization sessions held.

| **Activity**                                        | **Frequency**         |
|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| ICC Meetings & Hearings                             | Quarterly / As needed |
| Awareness Programs / Gender Sensitization Workshops | Bi-annual             |
| Submission of Compliance Report to UGC/AICTE        | Annual                |

**10.11. Events / Activities Organized by Internal Complaint Committee**

**1. Awareness Programs and Workshops**

> • **Objective:** To educate students, staff, and faculty about their rights, the anti-harassment policies, and how to file a complaint.
>
> • **Topics Covered:** Sexual harassment, discrimination, gender equality, workplace harassment, consent, understanding the law, etc.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students, faculty, and staff members.
>
> • **Method:** Guest lectures by legal experts, HR professionals, or social activists, and interactive workshops that discuss various types of harassment and how to prevent them.

**2. Orientation Programs**

> • **Objective:** To inform new students, faculty, and staff about the institution's anti-harassment policies and the role of the ICC.
>
> • **Topics Covered:** ICC's roles, procedures for reporting harassment, creating a respectful and safe environment, the importance of gender equality, etc.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Freshers, new faculty, and staff.
>
> • **Method:** Presentations, pamphlets, and online modules.

**3. Gender Sensitization Programs**

> • **Objective:** To foster a respectful and inclusive environment by addressing issues of gender bias, discrimination, and promoting equality.
>
> • **Topics Covered:** Gender stereotypes, unconscious bias, harassment, gender-based violence, creating a supportive environment for all genders.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students, faculty, and staff.
>
> • **Method:** Panel discussions, workshops, and screenings of relevant documentaries or films.

**4. Campaigns Against Harassment and Discrimination**

> • **Objective:** To raise awareness about harassment and encourage reporting and prevention.
>
> • **Activities:**
>
> o Posters and banners displaying key messages about anti-harassment.
>
> o Social media campaigns.
>
> o Signature campaigns to show commitment to a harassment-free institution.
>
> • **Target Audience:** General campus population.
>
> • **Method:** Distribution of materials, social media posts, and organizing events such as rallies or group discussions.

**5. Interactive Sessions and Seminars**

> • **Objective:** To provide a platform for discussion on issues related to workplace harassment, gender discrimination, and legal rights.
>
> • **Topics Covered:** Legal aspects of harassment, the role of the ICC, and creating a safe environment.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students, faculty, and staff.
>
> • **Method:** Inviting experts such as lawyers, counselors, and social activists for seminars and discussions.

**6. Orientation on Legal Rights and Reporting Mechanisms**

> • **Objective:** To inform students and staff about their legal rights and the procedures to report complaints related to harassment and discrimination.
>
> • **Topics Covered:** The Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH) Act, rights of employees and students, reporting mechanisms, how to approach ICC, confidentiality, and protection from retaliation.
>
> • **Target Audience:** All members of the institution.
>
> • **Method:** Legal expert talks, distribution of handouts, and online modules.

**7. Counseling and Support Sessions**

> • **Objective:** To provide emotional and psychological support to those who have been affected by harassment or discrimination.
>
> • **Activities:**
>
> o One-on-one counseling sessions.
>
> o Support groups for victims of harassment.
>
> o Providing information on external help (e.g., legal support, helplines).
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students, staff, or anyone in need of assistance.
>
> • **Method:** Confidential one-on-one sessions or group therapy.

**8. Panel Discussions and Debates**

> • **Objective:** To foster critical thinking and open discussions about harassment, discrimination, and creating a respectful institutional culture.
>
> • **Topics Covered:** Gender equality, workplace culture, understanding harassment, women's empowerment, etc.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students and faculty.
>
> • **Method:** Organizing panel discussions with faculty, students, and external experts or debates where students can express their views on related topics.

**9. International Day Celebrations**

> • **Objective:** To mark significant global days such as International Women's Day, Anti-Harassment Day, Human Rights Day, or International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women with events that emphasize the importance of respect, safety, and equality.
>
> • **Activities:**
>
> o Guest lectures or webinars.
>
> o Interactive quizzes or competitions on related topics.
>
> o Cultural programs or exhibitions to raise awareness about the importance of equality and safety.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students and staff.
>
> • **Method:** Special events, workshops, and media campaigns.

**10. Conflict Resolution Sessions**

> • **Objective:** To mediate conflicts between students, faculty, or staff and to help resolve any issues before they escalate.
>
> • **Method:**
>
> o Mediation and counseling sessions.
>
> o Open forums where issues can be raised and resolved in a neutral setting.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Students, staff, or faculty members involved in disputes.

**11. Annual Reports and Evaluation**

> • **Objective:** To evaluate the functioning of the ICC and its activities, and assess the impact of its programs on creating a safe environment.
>
> • **Activities:**
>
> o Gathering feedback from students and staff about the effectiveness of ICC's initiatives.
>
> o Publishing annual reports on the number of cases handled, resolutions, and awareness programs conducted.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Administration, faculty, and staff.
>
> • **Method:** Surveys, feedback forms, and presentations.

**12. Celebration of Key Milestones**

> • **Objective:** To celebrate the achievements and positive changes brought about by the ICC in improving the institutional culture.
>
> • **Activities:**
>
> o Celebrations of the success stories from the year, such as successfully resolving cases or launching effective awareness campaigns.
>
> o Recognizing the efforts of individuals or groups who have contributed to the success of anti-harassment initiatives.
>
> • **Target Audience:** Entire institution community.
>
> • **Method:** Ceremony, awards, or recognition events.

**10.13. Explanation of Key Activities**

> • **Orientation for New Students/Staff (January):** Provides an introduction to the ICC's role, and the procedures for filing complaints, and ensures that all members understand the policies related to harassment and discrimination.
>
> • **Gender Sensitization Workshop (February):** Conducted to foster awareness and create sensitivity around gender issues, to prevent gender-based discrimination and harassment.
>
> • **International Women's Day Celebration (March):** A special event to celebrate and acknowledge the contribution of women while promoting respect for gender equality.
>
> • **Anti-Harassment Campaign (May):** A campaign designed to engage the entire campus through posters, digital campaigns, and outreach to ensure that everyone understands their rights and the institution's stance on harassment.
>
> • **Counseling & Mental Health Support Sessions (June):** The ICC provides access to counseling services for anyone who has experienced harassment or discrimination, ensuring emotional and psychological support.
>
> • **Conflict Resolution & Mediation Training (July):** Focused on providing skills to mediate and resolve disputes amicably, preventing conflicts from escalating into harassment complaints.
>
> • **Student Feedback & Grievance Collection (September):** A mechanism for gathering anonymous feedback to understand the issues faced by students and to ensure that their grievances are being addressed effectively.
>
> • **Annual Review and Report (December):** A reflective activity that allows the ICC to evaluate the impact of its activities, look at areas for improvement, and share key outcomes and reports with the administration.

**10.14. Documentation for the Internal Complaint Committee (ICC)**

**1. Complaint Handling Forms**

> • **Complaint Form for Students/Staff:**
>
> o A standard form to be filled by complainants for reporting incidents of harassment, discrimination, or any other form of misconduct.
>
> o Should include basic details of the complainant, nature of the complaint, date and place of occurrence, and any witnesses.
>
> • **Follow-up Form:**
>
> o A form to track the progress of the complaint from initial receipt to final resolution.
>
> o Includes updates on actions taken, meetings held, and decisions made.

**2. Confidentiality and Privacy Agreements**

> • **Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) for ICC Members:**
>
> o A document that ensures all ICC members adhere to strict confidentiality while handling complaints.
>
> o Covers details like non-disclosure of complainant's identity, details of the investigation, and final outcomes.
>
> • **Confidentiality Agreement for Complainants:**
>
> o Provides assurance to the complainant that all personal and case-related information will be kept confidential.

**3. Case Record Files**

> • **Complaint Case Files:**
>
> o Each case should have its own file that includes all details about the complaint, investigation, hearings, and final outcomes.
>
> o Should also include any written communications with the complainant and respondent, investigation reports, and the committee's final decision.
>
> • **Case Log Sheet:**
>
> o A summary sheet to track all complaints received, including case numbers, dates, status, and resolution timelines.

**4. Investigative Reports**

> • **Preliminary Investigation Report:**
>
> o A report documenting the initial findings of the investigation, including interviews, evidence collected, and analysis.
>
> • **Final Investigation Report:**
>
> o A detailed report of the investigation process, findings, and recommendations. This should also include evidence, analysis, and witness statements.
>
> • **Action Taken Report:**
>
> o A report documenting the actions taken after the investigation, including disciplinary measures or remedial actions implemented.

**5. Minutes of Meetings**

> • **ICC Meetings Minutes:**
>
> o Detailed minutes of each meeting held by the ICC, including discussions, decisions made, and follow-up actions.
>
> o Should capture the attendance, agenda, resolutions passed, and any pending actions.

**6. Policy Documents**

> • **Anti-Harassment/Anti-Discrimination Policy:**
>
> o The official policy document outlining the institution's commitment to preventing harassment and discrimination, as well as the process for handling complaints.
>
> • **Code of Conduct for Students and Staff:**
>
> o A document outlining acceptable behavior for both students and staff, with clear guidelines on harassment, misconduct, and the consequences of violations.
>
> • **ICC Standard Operating Procedure (SOP):**
>
> o A clear and concise document outlining the step-by-step process that the ICC follows from receiving a complaint to resolving the case.
>
> o Includes guidelines for investigation, hearing, and follow-up actions.

**7. Awareness Materials**

> • **Brochures/Booklets for Awareness:**
>
> o Printed or digital materials explaining the complaint process, rights of complainants, and how to file complaints.
>
> o Should also include the details of the committee members and the steps taken to protect complainants' privacy.
>
> • **Posters/Flyers for Awareness:**
>
> o Displayed in various parts of the institution (hostels, common areas, offices) to raise awareness about harassment policies, complaint filing procedures, and resources for support.

**8. Communication Logs**

> • **Complaint Acknowledgment Receipt:**
>
> o A receipt confirming that the complaint has been received by the ICC, including a complaint reference number and the next steps in the process.
>
> • **Communication with Complainant and Respondent:**
>
> o Copies of all letters, emails, or other forms of communication sent to or received from the complainant and respondent during the investigation process.

**9. Reports and Review Documents**

> • **Annual Report on Complaints:**
>
> o An annual summary report of all complaints received during the year, including types of complaints, resolutions, and any patterns identified.
>
> • **Feedback Forms from Complainants:**
>
> o A form for complainants to provide feedback on the grievance handling process, which can help improve future processes.

**10. Training and Sensitization Documents**

> • **Training Materials for ICC Members:**
>
> o Presentation slides, handouts, or other materials used to train ICC members on handling complaints, legal guidelines, confidentiality, and sensitivity in investigations.
>
> • **Sensitization and Awareness Session Record:**
>
> o Documentation of awareness programs, including attendance, topics covered, and any evaluations or surveys taken by participants.

**11. External Documentation**

> • **Referral Documents to External Authorities:**
>
> o Documents related to cases referred to external authorities, such as police or legal bodies, if the case exceeds the institution's jurisdiction.
>
> • **Legal Documentation:**
>
> o Any documents related to legal action taken as a result of the complaint, including court notices, legal correspondence, or official statements.

**12. Policy Reviews and Updates**

> • **Review and Revision Logs:**
>
> o Records of any changes made to institutional policies regarding complaints, harassment, or discrimination, including the dates of revision and details of changes.
>
> • **Evaluation Reports on ICC Effectiveness:**
>
> o Periodic reports evaluating the effectiveness of the ICC in handling complaints, identifying gaps, and making recommendations for improvements.

**10.15. Best Practices of Internal Complaint Committee (ICC)**

**1. Clear and Transparent Grievance Redressal Process:**

> o Ensure that the procedure for filing complaints is clear, accessible, and well-communicated to all students and staff.
>
> o Regularly update the institution's website, noticeboards, and other communication channels to guide individuals on how to file complaints.

**2. Awareness and Sensitization Campaigns:**

> o Conduct continuous awareness campaigns, workshops, and seminars to educate students, staff, and faculty about the institution's anti-harassment policies, legal rights, and procedures.
>
> o Promote gender sensitization and respect for diversity through programs that target both students and employees.

**3. Confidentiality and Anonymity:**

> o Ensure strict confidentiality and protect the identities of complainants and witnesses during investigations.
>
> o Provide anonymous channels for complaints, such as online forms or dedicated email addresses, to encourage individuals to report incidents without fear of retaliation.

**4. Prompt Action and Timely Resolution:**

> o Maintain a commitment to resolving complaints in a timely manner, as per the guidelines set by the institution and statutory regulations.
>
> o Ensure that there is no delay in investigating complaints, providing support to victims, and taking appropriate action against perpetrators.

**5. Training and Capacity Building:**

> o Regularly train ICC members, faculty, staff, and students on how to identify harassment, how to handle complaints, and the importance of a zero-tolerance policy for harassment.
>
> o Organize capacity-building sessions on legal aspects of harassment, dispute resolution, and counseling skills for ICC members.

**6. Inclusive and Non-Discriminatory Approach:**

> o Ensure that the ICC handles complaints with an inclusive approach, taking into account the diverse backgrounds, identities, and experiences of the individuals involved.
>
> o The committee should be trained to address intersectionality (e.g., gender, caste, race, disability, etc.) in complaints.

**7. Support Mechanisms for Complainants:**

> o Provide psychological counseling, legal support, and guidance for complainants to help them recover from harassment incidents and navigate through the grievance process.
>
> o Create support groups or offer mentorship programs to help victims cope with the emotional and social aspects of their experiences.

**8. Regular Monitoring and Feedback:**

> o Regularly monitor the implementation of anti-harassment policies and seek feedback from the institution's stakeholders (students, faculty, staff) about the effectiveness of the ICC.
>
> o Use surveys, focus group discussions, or other methods to gauge the effectiveness of ICC's work and identify areas for improvement.

**9. Comprehensive Record-Keeping and Documentation:**

> o Maintain detailed and systematic records of all complaints, investigations, and resolutions. These records should be kept confidential but should be available for institutional audits and reviews as required.
>
> o Ensure that all steps of the complaint handling process are well-documented, including the timeline, communication with parties, and outcomes.

**10. Regular Reporting and Transparency:**

> o The ICC should submit regular reports (quarterly/annually) to the administration regarding the number of complaints, types of issues reported, actions taken, and the outcomes.
>
> o Share the overall trends (anonymized) with the institutional community to reinforce the message of transparency and accountability.

**11. Collaboration with External Experts and Organizations:**

> o Collaborate with legal experts, external counselors, and organizations that specialize in harassment prevention and support. This enhances the expertise of the ICC and provides an additional layer of support for complainants.
>
> o Invite guest speakers, trainers, and other professionals to conduct workshops and build awareness on sensitive issues.

**12. Zero Tolerance Policy:**

> o Establish and communicate a zero-tolerance policy towards all forms of harassment, bullying, and discrimination within the institution.
>
> o Ensure that the committee enforces consequences for those found guilty of misconduct, with appropriate measures in place for both staff and students.

**13. Encourage Reporting through Multiple Platforms:**

> o Make the complaint mechanism easily accessible by providing multiple platforms for reporting, such as an online portal, email, or physical drop-box.
>
> o Create awareness about the availability of these platforms to ensure that students and staff feel comfortable reporting incidents when they arise.

**14. Gender-Sensitive and Trauma-Informed Approach:**

> o Approach complaints with a gender-sensitive and trauma-informed mindset, understanding the psychological impact on the complainant.
>
> o Train all members of the ICC to handle complaints with empathy, patience, and respect for the dignity of the individual.

**15. Empower Students and Staff:**

> o Empower students and staff members with the knowledge of their rights and responsibilities in preventing harassment and ensuring a safe campus.
>
> o Create a culture where individuals feel responsible for maintaining a respectful and safe environment for all.
>
> • Integration with Women Empowerment Cell and Student Grievance Cell.
>
> • Use of online complaint portals with secure login and complaint tracking.
>
> • Collaboration with local NGOs for expert training sessions.
>
> • Display of Code of Conduct in classrooms and public spaces.

**11. Academic and Administrative Audit (AAA) Committee**

**11.1. Introduction**

The Academic and Administrative Audit (AAA) is a systematic internal and external review process to evaluate the effectiveness, quality, and integrity of academic processes and administrative functions in an institution. The AAA Committee ensures that the institution aligns with its vision, mission, and quality benchmarks set by NAAC, NBA, UGC, and other regulatory/accrediting agencies.

**11.2. Objectives of the AAA Committee**

> • To monitor and assess the academic and administrative performance of departments and institutional units.
>
> • To identify strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement.
>
> • To promote a culture of quality enhancement, transparency, and accountability.
>
> • To provide recommendations for academic reforms, governance, and resource optimization.
>
> • To ensure compliance with NAAC/NBA accreditation criteria, UGC regulations, and institutional quality standards.

**11.3. Composition of the AAA Committee**

| **Role**                    | **Profile**                                                 |
|-----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson                 | Senior academic leader (Principal / External academician)   |
| Internal Members            | Deans, IQAC Coordinator, Senior Faculty from various Depts. |
| External Experts (Optional) | Eminent academicians/administrators from other institutions |
| NAAC/NBA Coordinators       | Ex-officio Members for documentation and process compliance |

*In large universities/autonomous institutions, external experts are mandatory.*

**11.4. Scope of the Audit**

**1. Academic Audit**

> • Curriculum design & revision aligned with Outcome-Based Education (OBE)
>
> • Academic delivery, teaching-learning process
>
> • Assessment and evaluation mechanisms
>
> • Faculty quality and research output
>
> • Student feedback & mentoring systems
>
> • Academic calendar adherence
>
> • CO-PO-PSO attainment
>
> • Industry-academia collaborations, FDPs, internships
>
> • Student performance and pass-out rates

**2. Administrative Audit**

> • Governance structure & policy implementation
>
> • HR practices and faculty deployment
>
> • Admission, examination, and student support systems
>
> • Infrastructure and resource management
>
> • ICT usage in administration
>
> • Financial and procurement procedures
>
> • Documentation, file management, and compliance
>
> • Stakeholder grievance mechanisms

**11.5. Key Functions of the AAA Committee**

> • Prepare and circulate audit schedules & formats
>
> • Collect and review departmental data, records, and evidence
>
> • Conduct site visits, interact with faculty, staff, and students
>
> • Evaluate compliance with NAAC/NBA criteria
>
> • Provide detailed observations and score-based reports
>
> • Submit recommendations and actionable points to the Principal/IQAC
>
> • Follow up on implementation of suggestions

**11.6. Frequency of Audit**

| **Type of Audit**       | **Frequency**                        |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Internal Academic Audit | Once every Semester                  |
| External Academic Audit | Once in 1 or 2 years (as per policy) |
| Administrative Audit    | Annually or Biennially               |

**11.7. Deliverables of the AAA Committee**

> • Academic Audit Report (Department-wise)
>
> • Administrative Audit Report
>
> • Consolidated Institutional Audit Report
>
> • SWOT Analysis (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats)
>
> • Action Taken Reports (ATRs) on previous audit observations
>
> • Recommendations for quality enhancement

**11.8. Contribution to NAAC Criteria**

| **NAAC Criterion**                   | **How AAA Contributes**                                                 |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 1: Curricular Aspects      | Evaluates curriculum planning and revision aligned with OBE             |
| Criterion 2: Teaching-Learning       | Assesses faculty quality, pedagogy, learning outcomes                   |
| Criterion 3: Research and Innovation | Tracks research output, consultancy, and MoUs                           |
| Criterion 4: Infrastructure          | Assesses utilization and adequacy of physical and ICT infrastructure    |
| Criterion 6: Governance              | Reviews administrative practices, leadership, and decentralization      |
| Criterion 7: Best Practices          | Highlights innovations, inclusivity, and quality improvement mechanisms |

**11.9. Contribution to NBA Criteria**

| **NBA Criterion**                      | **Relevant Aspects Evaluated by AAA**                                   |
|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 1: Vision, Mission           | Ensures alignment between department-level and institutional objectives |
| Criterion 2: Program Outcomes          | Reviews attainment of COs, POs, PSOs through audits                     |
| Criterion 5: Faculty Contributions     | Evaluates faculty qualifications, performance, and FDP participation    |
| Criterion 8: Institutional Improvement | Monitors quality enhancement through systematic feedback and actions    |
| Criterion 10: Institutional Support    | Assesses resource availability and administrative efficiency            |

**11.10. Documentation Required for AAA**

> • Department-wise Self-Assessment Report (SAR)
>
> • Teaching plans, CO-PO mappings, question paper analysis
>
> • Faculty portfolios, FDP records
>
> • Student feedback summaries
>
> • Exam results and progression data
>
> • Administrative policy files and procedure manuals
>
> • Budget and procurement records
>
> • IQAC meeting minutes and reports

**11.10.1. Essential Documents Maintained by the Committee**

**1. Audit Framework and Guidelines**

> • **Audit Framework Document:** A comprehensive document that outlines the scope, objectives, and methodology for conducting academic and administrative audits.
>
> • **Audit Guidelines:** Clear guidelines to standardize the audit process, ensuring consistency and objectivity across all departments and administrative functions.

**2. Audit Schedule/Plan**

> • **Annual Audit Calendar:** A schedule for when audits will take place for each department and administrative unit, including deadlines and milestones.
>
> • **Audit Timetable:** Specific timelines for auditing each academic and administrative area (e.g., semester-wise or annual audit schedules).

**3. Academic Audit Reports**

> • **Department-wise Academic Audit Reports:** Detailed reports for each department, covering the review of teaching quality, student performance, curriculum adherence, faculty qualifications, and learning resources.
>
> • **Course-wise Feedback Reports:** Feedback collected from students regarding the quality of courses, teaching methods, and resource availability.
>
> • **Faculty Evaluation Records:** Records of faculty performance, including teaching evaluations, research output, and professional development.

**4. Administrative Audit Reports**

> • **Administrative Unit Reports:** Reports detailing the operations of various administrative departments (e.g., finance, HR, student services), including compliance with policies, procedures, and efficient use of resources.
>
> • **Resource Utilization Reports:** Documents that show how effectively the institution's financial, human, and infrastructural resources are being used.
>
> • **Compliance Reports:** Reports on the compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements (e.g., UGC, AICTE, accreditation bodies).

**5. Audit Feedback Forms**

> • **Student Feedback Forms:** Surveys or questionnaires that collect feedback from students on academic matters, teaching effectiveness, and learning outcomes.
>
> • **Faculty Feedback Forms:** Evaluations from faculty regarding administrative support, infrastructure, and resource availability.
>
> • **Administrative Staff Feedback Forms:** Surveys that collect feedback from non-academic staff about administrative processes, communication, and resource management.

**6. Audit Action Plans and Recommendations**

> • **Action Plan Documents:** Plans developed post-audit, detailing steps to improve areas of concern identified during the audit process.
>
> • **Recommendations from the Audit Team:** Written suggestions or corrective actions recommended by the audit team, with timelines for implementation.

**7. Corrective Action Reports**

> • **Post-Audit Reports:** Documents showing the implementation of corrective actions and improvements based on audit findings.
>
> • **Follow-up Reports:** Regular reports detailing the progress made in implementing the recommended changes and improvements.

**8. Institutional Self-Assessment Documents**

> • **Self-Assessment Reports:** Reports generated by various academic and administrative departments before the audit to identify their strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement.
>
> • **SWOT Analysis Reports:** Reports created to assess the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats of academic and administrative processes.

**9. Accreditation and Compliance Documents**

> • **Accreditation Reports:** Documents related to institutional accreditation processes, including assessments by agencies like NAAC, NBA, or UGC.
>
> • **Compliance Records:** Documentation of adherence to various external guidelines, such as government regulations, academic standards, and accreditation requirements.

**10. Audit Review Meeting Minutes**

> • **Audit Review Meetings:** Minutes from meetings where audit findings, progress on corrective actions, and future plans are discussed by the audit committee and other stakeholders.
>
> • **Board or Committee Review Reports:** Reports presented to the governing body or academic council after the audit, summarizing the key findings and necessary actions.

**11. Stakeholder Communication Documents**

> • **Communication with Stakeholders:** Letters, emails, or official communications informing stakeholders (faculty, students, and staff) about audit processes, findings, and the need for improvement.
>
> • **Stakeholder Engagement Reports:** Documents that record the involvement of stakeholders (such as faculty, students, and staff) in the audit process, including meetings, workshops, and feedback sessions.

**12. Audit Records and Data**

> • **Raw Data from Audits:** Raw data or evidence collected during the audits (e.g., student performance records, faculty teaching evaluations, financial records).
>
> • **Audit Checklists:** Standardized checklists used by auditors to ensure that all relevant areas of academic and administrative performance are evaluated.

**13. Audit Committee Reports**

> • **Audit Committee Annual Reports:** A yearly summary report from the audit committee that provides an overview of the audit activities conducted throughout the year, including major findings, challenges, and recommendations for the next period.

**14. Continuous Improvement Records**

> • **Quality Improvement Plans:** Documents showing how the audit findings are being integrated into the institution's broader quality assurance and improvement strategies.
>
> • **Best Practices Records:** Documentation of best practices identified during audits, which can be replicated across departments and administrative units.

**15. Policy and Procedure Documents**

> • **Audit Policy Documents:** Institutional policies that outline the purpose, scope, and procedures for conducting audits in both academic and administrative areas.
>
> • **Audit Procedures Manual:** A step-by-step guide on how to conduct audits, including roles and responsibilities, tools, and techniques used during the audit process.

>
> • **Action Plans:** These plans outline corrective measures and enhancements based on audit results, ensuring that findings are implemented effectively.
>
