>
> • **Continuous Improvement:** Regular reviews and audits contribute to the culture of continuous improvement within the institution.

**11.12. Best Practices for the Academic and Administrative Audit (AAA) Committee**

**1. Regular and Systematic Audits**

> • **Frequency:** Ensure that both academic and administrative audits are conducted regularly—ideally once a year, but at least once every two years to assess both areas comprehensively.
>
> • **Scope:** Maintain a clear distinction between the academic audit (focused on teaching, learning, student performance, and faculty development) and the administrative audit (focused on infrastructure, financial management, and policy compliance).

**2. Well-Defined Criteria and Framework**

> • **Standardized Audit Criteria:** Develop and maintain standardized audit tools that are aligned with national and international accreditation standards (such as NAAC, NBA).
>
> • **Clear Guidelines:** Prepare detailed guidelines for auditors to ensure consistency in the evaluation process and that they assess all relevant components comprehensively.

**3. Use of Technology and Data Analytics**

> • **Digital Auditing:** Use digital platforms and tools for auditing processes to ensure accurate data collection, analysis, and reporting.
>
> • **Data-Driven Insights:** Incorporate data analytics to identify trends, gaps, and areas requiring improvement. This can help in making evidence-based decisions for improvement.

**4. Transparency in Processes**

> • **Open Communication:** Maintain transparency during audits by ensuring that all departments, units, and stakeholders are informed well in advance about the audit procedures.
>
> • **Documentation and Reporting:** Ensure that all audit reports are clear, structured, and accessible to relevant stakeholders, including faculty, administration, and governing bodies.

**5. Feedback Mechanism**

> • **Stakeholder Involvement:** Involve all key stakeholders, such as faculty members, administrative staff, and students, in the audit process by gathering feedback through surveys and discussions.
>
> • **Post-Audit Review:** After the audit, review the findings with all stakeholders and establish clear action plans to address identified issues.

**6. Development of Action Plans**

> • **Action Plan Creation:** For every audit finding, develop a corrective or improvement plan with specific goals, timelines, and resources required.
>
> • **Follow-Up:** Ensure that the action plans are regularly followed up on to track the implementation and impact of changes.

**7. Continuous Improvement**

> • **Benchmarking:** Compare the institution's performance with similar institutions or national standards to gauge its relative standing.
>
> • **Continuous Professional Development (CPD):** Use audit findings to identify areas where faculty and staff need further training and development.

**8. Performance Review and Self-Assessment**

> • **Self-Assessment:** Encourage departments and administrative units to conduct internal self-assessments before the audit to identify their strengths and weaknesses.
>
> • **Peer Reviews:** Involve peer departments or external experts for an objective evaluation.

**9. Ensuring Compliance**

> • **Regulatory Compliance:** Regularly ensure that all academic and administrative activities comply with statutory and regulatory requirements such as UGC guidelines, accreditation requirements, and government policies.

**10. Management of Resources**

> • **Resource Utilization:** Ensure that the audit evaluates the effective utilization of institutional resources, including finances, human resources, and infrastructure, and suggests improvements.

**11. Capacity Building for Auditors**

> • **Training Auditors:** Provide regular training to auditors on the latest audit methodologies, standards, and tools to ensure the effectiveness of audits.

**12. Involvement of External Experts**

> • **External Audit Experts:** Occasionally invite external auditors or experts to assess the institution's practices. Their independent perspective helps ensure objectivity and credibility.

**13. Alignment with Institutional Goals**

> • **Strategic Alignment:** Ensure that audit outcomes are aligned with the long-term vision and mission of the institution, especially in areas of quality assurance, student outcomes, and resource optimization.

**14. Reporting and Documentation**

> • **Audit Reports:** Maintain comprehensive and well-documented audit reports that include observations, recommendations, and action plans. The reports should be reviewed by senior management and shared with the relevant committees for decision-making.

**15. Enhancing Institutional Reputation**

> • **Promoting Best Practices:** Share successful audit outcomes and best practices in institutional meetings, newsletters, or on institutional websites to highlight continuous improvement efforts.

**11.13. Conclusion**

The Academic and Administrative Audit (AAA) Committee plays a vital role in maintaining institutional accountability and continuous improvement. By incorporating these best practices, HEIs can ensure that they meet accreditation standards, improve teaching and learning outcomes, streamline administrative operations, and foster a culture of excellence and transparency.

**12. Faculty/Staff Grievance Committee**

**12.1. Introduction**

The Faculty/Staff Grievance Committee is a formal mechanism established in higher educational institutions to provide a transparent, fair, and structured process for redressal of grievances raised by teaching and non-teaching staff. It ensures a healthy work environment, promotes institutional ethics, and supports continuous quality improvement—critical for achieving NAAC and NBA quality benchmarks.

**12.2. Objectives**

> • To provide a responsive and accessible platform for faculty and staff to address professional or administrative grievances.
>
> • To ensure grievances are resolved in a timely, just, and non-discriminatory manner.
>
> • To promote institutional transparency, harmony, and well-being.
>
> • To comply with statutory guidelines from NAAC/NBA/UGC/AICTE regarding staff welfare and grievance redressal mechanisms.

**12.3. Composition of the Committee**

| **Designation**            | **Role**                                      |
|----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson                | Principal or Dean                             |
| Member Secretary           | HR Head or Senior Faculty Member              |
| Members (Teaching Staff)   | 2-3 faculty members from various departments  |
| Members (Non-Teaching)     | 1-2 non-teaching staff representatives        |
| External Member (Optional) | Legal advisor or HR expert (in serious cases) |

*Gender balance and representation from different staff categories are encouraged.*

**12.4. Roles and Responsibilities**

*1. Grievance Redressal Mechanism*

> • Receive written complaints or concerns from faculty and staff.
>
> • Acknowledge grievances formally and maintain records confidentially.
>
> • Scrutinize and verify the grievance before initiating further action.

*2. Initial Review & Assessment*

> • Conduct preliminary investigation to assess the nature and seriousness of the complaint.
>
> • Identify whether the issue can be resolved informally or requires formal proceedings.

*3. Conducting Hearings*

> • Arrange meetings with the complainant, respondent (if any), and witnesses (if needed).
>
> • Ensure a fair and unbiased environment for both parties to present their points.

*4. Resolution & Recommendation*

> • Recommend necessary corrective actions, counseling, or mediation as appropriate.
>
> • Forward serious matters to higher authorities (e.g., Principal or Management) for final decision.

*5. Policy and Compliance Oversight*

> • Ensure that the grievance handling process complies with institutional policies and labor laws.
>
> • Periodically review institutional grievance policies for faculty/staff and suggest improvements.

*6. Reporting and Documentation*

> • Maintain proper documentation of all grievance records, proceedings, and resolutions.
>
> • Submit periodic reports (quarterly/bi-annually) to the Principal/HR/Management.

*7. Follow-Up*

> • Ensure the resolution measures are implemented effectively.
>
> • Follow up with the complainant to ensure satisfaction with the outcome.

*8. Awareness and Support*

> • Educate faculty and staff about grievance redressal mechanisms through circulars or meetings.
>
> • Offer emotional support and guidance during grievance handling.

**12.5. Faculty/Staff Grievance Committee – Member-Wise Roles & Responsibilities**

**1. Chairperson (Senior Faculty Member/Professor)**

> • **Role:** Provides overall leadership and guidance to the committee.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Ensures that grievance handling is fair, transparent, and timely.
>
> o Leads the meetings and hearings of the grievance committee.
>
> o Makes final recommendations or escalates the matter to higher authorities when necessary.
>
> o Oversees the entire grievance redressal process and ensures that appropriate resolutions are provided.
>
> o Acts as the main point of contact for any concerns or queries related to the grievance process.

**2. Member (Head of Department – Non-Involved Department)**

> • **Role:** Brings departmental and academic perspectives to the grievance resolution process.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Participates in hearings and contributes to resolving grievances.
>
> o Ensures that decisions taken are in line with institutional policies and regulations.
>
> o Offers insights into departmental or academic issues that may have led to the grievance.
>
> o Supports the Chairperson in implementing fair and unbiased resolutions.
>
> o Provides confidential advice and mediation where required.

**3. Member (Senior Administrative Officer)**

> • **Role:** Provides administrative oversight and ensures that the grievance process is compliant with institutional and legal standards.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Assists in verifying the facts and circumstances surrounding the grievance.
>
> o Ensures all institutional policies and procedures are adhered to during the grievance process.
>
> o Helps manage confidential records and documentation.
>
> o Works closely with HR and other departments to resolve administrative or procedural issues.
>
> o Facilitates communication between the committee and other institutional bodies.

**4. Member Secretary (HR/Establishment Officer)**

> • **Role:** Responsible for the smooth administrative functioning of the grievance committee.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Manages all documentation, including grievance records, meeting minutes, and follow-up reports.
>
> o Coordinates the scheduling of meetings and hearings.
>
> o Communicates decisions and outcomes to the complainant and the respondent.
>
> o Acts as the liaison between the grievance committee and other departments or individuals involved in the process.
>
> o Ensures that the grievance redressal process is initiated and completed within the prescribed timelines.
>
> o Maintains confidentiality and professionalism throughout the grievance process.

**5. External Member (Optional)**

> • **Role:** Provides an objective and unbiased perspective in cases requiring external mediation.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Offers an independent viewpoint during committee meetings and hearings.
>
> o Assists in ensuring that the grievance process is fair and equitable.
>
> o Can act as an advisor in complex or sensitive cases, ensuring neutrality in decision-making.
>
> o Helps bring an external perspective on organizational practices or policies that may need improvement.

**Note:**

> • The committee is expected to maintain confidentiality, integrity, and fairness in all its proceedings.
>
> • Regular reviews and training for committee members are necessary to keep them updated on legal and institutional norms.

**12.6. Types of Grievances Addressed**

**Faculty:**

> • Workload distribution and teaching assignments
>
> • Research recognition and funding issues
>
> • Promotion and appraisal-related concerns
>
> • Resource and infrastructure inadequacies
>
> • Interpersonal conflicts and unfair treatment

**Non-Teaching Staff:**

> • Duty allocation and overtime concerns
>
> • Salary, leave, and service conditions
>
> • Workplace safety and harassment
>
> • Transfer or job responsibility issues
>
> • Delay in service benefits, pension, or PF

**12.7. Grievance Redressal Process**

**Step 1: Submission of Grievance**

> • Faculty/staff submits a written application or uses an online grievance portal or suggestion box.
>
> • The grievance must include all relevant details and documents.

**Step 2: Initial Screening**

> • The committee screens the grievance for validity and assigns a file number.

**Step 3: Inquiry and Hearing**

> • The committee conducts a confidential inquiry, seeks clarification from involved parties, and documents proceedings.
>
> • A formal hearing may be conducted if necessary.

**Step 4: Resolution and Recommendations**

> • A decision is communicated to the aggrieved party within 7-15 working days.
>
> • Corrective actions, mediation, or escalation (to higher authorities/legal cell) are taken based on the case.

**Step 5: Follow-Up**

> • The case is closed with a signed report and follow-up is ensured for implementation of recommendations.

**12.8. Mode of Submitting the Grievance**

> • Offline: Submission through a sealed envelope to the committee chairperson.
>
> • Online: Institutional ERP portal, dedicated grievance redressal form, or institutional email.
>
> • Anonymous Submissions: May be reviewed but are generally not processed unless containing serious and verifiable allegations.

**12.9. Consequences of Non-Compliance**

| **Stakeholder**   | **Consequences**                                                             |
|-------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Institution       | Delays in resolution due to lack of formal process adherence                 |
| Committee Members | Disciplinary action for non-responsiveness or biased behavior                |
| Stakeholder       | Adverse comments during NAAC/NBA peer review, drop in morale, and reputation |

**12.10. Corrective Actions for Non-Compliance**

> • Re-training and sensitization programs for staff and committee members
>
> • Policy strengthening and clear documentation
>
> • Formal warnings, reassignment, or disciplinary action (if justified)

**12.11. Role in NAAC Accreditation**

| **NAAC Criteria**                                   | **Relevance of Faculty/Staff Grievance Committee**                     |
|-----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 6 – Governance, Leadership & Management   | Demonstrates organizational ethics, fair treatment, and support        |
| Criterion 7 – Institutional Values & Best Practices | Promotes a healthy and motivating work culture for faculty development |

**12.12. Role in NBA Accreditation**

| **NBA Criterion**                    | **Relevance of Faculty/Staff Grievance Committee**               |
|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 10 – Institutional Support | Evidence of welfare and grievance redressal mechanisms for staff |
| Criterion 9 – Faculty Contributions  | Inclusive and supportive work environment policies               |

**12.13. Documentation Required**

> • Constitution of the Grievance Committee
>
> • Policy document/manual on grievance handling
>
> • Minutes of grievance meetings (with confidentiality preserved)
>
> • Action Taken Reports (ATRs)
>
> • Faculty/staff feedback on grievance redressal satisfaction

**12.14. Best Practices**

> • Confidential grievance drop box and digital portal
>
> • Annual grievance review reports
>
> • Grievance awareness workshops for all employees
>
> • Anonymous satisfaction surveys to improve the redressal system

**13. Sports & Games Committee**

**13.1. Introduction**

The Sports & Games Committee in colleges plays a crucial role in promoting physical education, fitness, and overall student well-being. From the perspective of NBA (National Board of Accreditation) and NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council), this committee contributes significantly to the Holistic Development of students, which is an important criterion in both accreditation processes.

**13.2. Objectives of the Sports & Games Committee**

> • To promote physical fitness, mental well-being, and team spirit among students.
>
> • To plan, organize, and supervise sports and recreational activities (indoor and outdoor).
>
> • To foster discipline, leadership, and a sense of fair play.
>
> • To identify and nurture sports talent among students.
>
> • To promote inter-college and intra-college competitions.

**13.3. Functions of the Sports & Games Committee**

The Sports & Games Committee is constituted to foster a culture of physical fitness, teamwork, and sportsmanship among students. It is responsible for promoting and coordinating sports activities throughout the academic year.

| **Function No.** | **Function**                                                                                                                            |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | To encourage students to actively participate in organizing and conducting various sports and games within the college.                 |
| F2               | To motivate students to represent the college in inter-collegiate, university, state, and national-level sports and games competitions. |
| F3               | To inculcate the spirit of sportsmanship, discipline, and teamwork among the students.                                                  |
| F4               | To promote awareness about the benefits of regular physical exercise for maintaining good physical and mental health.                   |
| F5               | To address and resolve issues or grievances related to sports and games within the campus.                                              |
| F6               | To prepare an annual sports event planner in consultation with student representatives and management.                                  |
| F7               | To organize inter-collegiate tournaments and an annual sports fest to showcase and celebrate student talent in sports.                  |

**13.4. Core Roles & Responsibilities**

**1. Planning & Coordination**

> • Prepare and maintain an annual sports calendar (intra- and inter-collegiate events).
>
> • Coordinate sports activities during college fests, annual day, and other celebrations.
>
> • Plan training and coaching sessions for students in various sports disciplines.

**2. Infrastructure and Equipment**

> • Ensure proper maintenance of sports grounds, courts, gymnasium, and indoor game facilities.
>
> • Procure, maintain, and inventory sports equipment and kits.
>
> • Recommend upgrades or development of sports infrastructure as needed.

**3. Student Participation & Development**

> • Identify and encourage talented students to participate in inter-college, university, and state/national level competitions.
>
> • Conduct trials and select students for college teams.
>
> • Provide guidance and motivation to students interested in physical education and competitive sports.

**4. Event Organization**

> • Organize intra-departmental and inter-departmental competitions.
>
> • Conduct Annual Sports Meet and prize distribution ceremonies.
>
> • Ensure fair play and discipline during all events.

**5. Collaboration**

> • Liaise with external sports organizations, coaches, and physical education trainers.
>
> • Coordinate with affiliated university for zonal/university-level tournaments.

**6. Record Keeping & Reporting**

> • Maintain attendance and performance records of student athletes.
>
> • Document event results, achievements, and sports activity reports for IQAC/NAAC/University.
>
> • Prepare budget proposals and utilization reports for sports activities.

**7. Health and Safety**

> • Ensure availability of first aid during events and regular training sessions.
>
> • Educate students on injury prevention and physical well-being.

**13.5. Member-wise Roles**

| **S.No** | **Designation**                            | **Responsibilities**                                                                   |
|----------|--------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Chairperson (Principal/Director)           | Overall supervision and approval of sports programs and policies.                      |
| 2        | Physical Director / Sports In-charge       | Day-to-day execution of sports activities, coaching, event organization.               |
| 3        | Faculty Coordinators (One from each dept.) | Motivate student participation and support logistics during events.                    |
| 4        | Student Representatives                    | Represent student interests, encourage peer participation, and assist in coordination. |
| 5        | Administrative Staff                       | Manage logistics, procurements, and maintain sports infrastructure and records.        |

**13.6. Events / Activities Organized by Sports & Games Committee**

| **Sl.No** | **Name of the Event/Activity**                             | **Objective**                                                                                            | **Participants**               |
|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| 1         | Annual Sports Meet                                         | To promote physical fitness and competitive spirit among students                                        | All Students                   |
| 2         | Inter-Departmental Tournaments (Cricket, Volleyball, etc.) | To encourage team spirit and healthy competition                                                         | Students (all departments)     |
| 3         | Yoga and Wellness Workshop                                 | To promote mental health and well-being through yoga                                                     | Students & Faculty             |
| 4         | Zonal/Inter-Collegiate Sports Participation                | To provide opportunities to represent the college at external events                                     | Selected Student Teams         |

| 6         | Fitness and Gym Awareness Session                          | To raise awareness about fitness resources available on campus; to foster healthy bonding through sports | All Students                   |
| 7         | Faculty vs Students Friendly Matches                       | To foster healthy bonding through sports                                                                 | Faculty & Students             |
| 8         | Table Tennis / Chess / Carrom Indoor Games Fest            | To promote indoor games and brain engagement                                                             | UG/PG Students                 |
| 9         | Women's Sports Day                                         | To encourage active participation of girl students in sports                                             | Female Students                |
| 10        | Independence Day / Republic Day Sports Events              | To celebrate national days with sporting spirit                                                          | Students & Staff               |

**13.7. Indirect Attainment Calculation for Sports & Games Committee**

**Purpose:** To assess how sports and games activities contribute to the achievement of Program Outcomes (POs) such as team spirit, ethics, leadership, and well-being — usually mapped to POs like PO6, PO7, PO8, PO9, PO10.

**Step-by-Step Indirect Attainment Process:**

***Step 1: Define Tool Rubrics***

Create assessment tools (rubrics) based on participation and performance. For example:

| **Parameter**               | **Level 1** | **Level 2** | **Level 3**      | **Tool** |
|-----------------------------|-------------|-------------|------------------|----------|
| No. of Participants         | \< 100      | 100 – 300   | \> 300           | \-       |
| No. of Events Organized     | \< 3        | 3 – 4       | ≥ 5              | \-       |
| Awards/Recognitions         | None        | 1 – 2       | ≥ 3              | \-       |
| Team/Leadership Involvement | \< 3 teams  | 3 – 4 teams | ≥ 5 teams formed | \-       |

***Step 2: Collect Activity Data***

Example activity-wise data:

| **Activity Name**                   | **T1**  | **T2** | **T3**  | **T4**   |
|-------------------------------------|---------|--------|---------|----------|
| Annual Sports Meet                  | 3       | 3      | 2       | 3        |
| Inter-College Volleyball Tournament | 2       | 2      | 3       | 3        |
| Yoga & Wellness Workshop            | 2       | 1      | \-      | \-       |
| Health Awareness Run                | 3       | 2      | \-      | 2        |
| Total                               | 10      | 8      | 5       | 8        |
| **Average Attainment Level**        | **2.5** | **2**  | **2.5** | **2.66** |

***Step 3: Map Functions to POs***

Example:

| **Function**                    | **PO6 (Health & Safety)** | **PO7 (Environment)** | **PO9 (Teamwork)** | **PO10 (Communication)** |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|
| F1: Annual Sports Meet          | 3                         | 2                     | 3                  | 2                        |
| F2: Wellness Workshop           | 3                         | 3                     | 2                  | 1                        |
| F3: Team Sports (e.g., cricket) | 2                         | 2                     | 3                  | 3                        |
| F4: Awareness Activities        | 2                         | 3                     | 2                  | 3                        |
| **Average Attainment Level**    | **2.5**                   | **2.5**               | **2.5**            | **2.25**                 |

***Step 4: Calculate Final Indirect PO Attainment***

| **PO** | **Average Attainment Level (Indirect)** |
|--------|-----------------------------------------|
| PO6    | 2.5                                     |
| PO7    | 2.5                                     |
| PO9    | 2.5                                     |
| PO10   | 2.25                                    |

You can normalize this with direct attainment (if available), usually in a 70:30 or 60:40 ratio (Direct: Indirect).

**Summary Format:**

> • Total Activities Considered: 4
>
> • Overall Average Attainment: T1: 2.5, T2: 2, T3: 2.5, T4: 2.66
>
> • Final PO Attainment (Indirect): PO6: 2.5, PO7: 2.5, PO9: 2.5, PO10: 2.25

**13.8. Relevance to NBA Accreditation**

In NBA's SAR (Self-Assessment Report), Sports & Games contribute to:

> o Provision for extracurricular and co-curricular activities.
>
> o Development of soft skills, leadership, and teamwork through sports.

**Criterion 7: Continuous Improvement**

> o Evidence of holistic student development is considered in evaluating overall institutional effectiveness.

**13.18. Best Practices of the Sports & Games Committee**

**1. Inclusive and Diverse Sports Programs**

> o Offer a variety of sports activities catering to students of all interests and skill levels.
>
> o Ensure equal opportunities for all genders, backgrounds, and abilities.
>
> o Organize intra-departmental and inter-departmental sports competitions to encourage participation from every student.

**2. Regular and Effective Scheduling**

> o Maintain a well-structured sports calendar, balancing academic schedules with sports events to avoid clashes.
>
> o Schedule training sessions and practice times well in advance, providing students ample time to prepare for competitions.
>
> o Consider incorporating flexible timings for student-athletes to balance sports with academic commitments.

**3. Student Engagement and Involvement**

> o Encourage student leadership by involving them in the organization and management of sports events and activities.
>
> o Create student-run sports clubs or teams, fostering a sense of responsibility and ownership.
>
> o Organize regular feedback sessions with students to improve sports activities based on their preferences and needs.

**4. Qualified Coaches and Trainers**

> o Hire professional coaches and trainers who are qualified and experienced in their respective sports.
>
> o Regular training programs should be designed for both beginners and advanced players, ensuring continuous improvement.
>
> o Encourage coaches to adopt a holistic approach, focusing not only on skills but also on fitness, mental well-being, and team-building.

**5. Sports Infrastructure and Facilities**

> o Ensure that the sports facilities (fields, courts, gymnasiums, etc.) are well-maintained and up to the required standards.
>
> o Regularly assess and upgrade sports equipment to ensure safety and effectiveness for all users.
>
> o Organize regular cleanliness and maintenance drives to keep the sports facilities in top condition.

**6. Annual Sports Events and Tournaments**

> o Host annual sports events such as annual athletic meets, inter-college tournaments, and sports fests to promote a competitive and vibrant sports culture.
>
> o Organize intra-college tournaments and competitions, with clear guidelines and fair play standards.
>
> o Foster school spirit by ensuring strong participation from all departments and faculties.

**7. Promotion of Health and Fitness Culture**

> o Promote the importance of physical fitness, encouraging students to engage in regular exercise and fitness activities, beyond competitive sports.
>
> o Collaborate with health and wellness departments to provide health check-ups, fitness assessments, and injury prevention workshops for students.
>
> o Implement wellness programs such as yoga, meditation, and stress-relief activities as part of overall student well-being.

**8. Inter-Institutional Collaborations**

> o Foster partnerships with other universities, colleges, or sports clubs for friendly competitions and exposure to a wider range of athletic activities.
>
> o Encourage participation in regional, state, or national-level sports competitions, giving students a chance to showcase their talents.
>
> o Organize workshops and sports clinics in collaboration with experienced athletes or sports organizations.

**9. Awards and Recognition**

> o Recognize and reward outstanding athletes and teams with certificates, trophies, and other incentives for motivation.
>
> o Celebrate achievements through award ceremonies, including sportsmanship and fair play awards, in addition to performance-based recognition.
>
> o Develop a culture of excellence by ensuring consistent and comprehensive recognition for sports achievements.

**10. Mental Health and Sports Psychology Support**

> o Offer counseling services for athletes to support their mental well-being, including stress management and coping strategies.
>
> o Promote sports psychology workshops to help athletes enhance their performance and overcome psychological barriers.
>
> o Create a support system for students facing performance anxiety or burnout, helping them balance academics and sports.

**11. Sustainability in Sports Activities**

> o Encourage eco-friendly practices during sports events, such as reducing plastic usage, recycling materials, and promoting green initiatives.
>
> o Organize campaigns that educate students on the importance of sustainability, especially in relation to large-scale events.

**12. Integration with Academics**

> o Align sports programs with academic calendars to ensure students' academic commitments are not impacted.
>
> o Recognize outstanding athletes through scholarship programs or other academic incentives for those excelling in sports.
>
> o Develop academic partnerships to offer credit for athletic training and performance courses.

**13.19. Conclusion**

These best practices will help create an inclusive, vibrant, and well-managed sports culture within the institution, fostering the development of students both academically and physically. By ensuring that sports activities are accessible, well-supported, and integrated into the overall student experience, the Sports & Games Committee can make a significant contribution to student wellness and achievement.

**14. Examinations Committee**

**14.1. Introduction**

The Examinations Committee is a statutory body responsible for the smooth conduct of internal and external examinations, ensuring transparency, integrity, and academic standards. It plays a key role in academic assessment, record-keeping, and policy formulation in compliance with university regulations.

**14.2. Objectives of the Examination Committee**

> • To plan, organize, and monitor all internal assessments, university exams, and other evaluation activities.
>
> • To ensure fair conduct of exams and timely declaration of results.
>
> • To liaise with the affiliating university regarding examination-related matters.

**14.3. Functions of the Examination Committee**

| **Function No.** | **Function**                                                                                                          |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | To coordinate with the affiliating university for scheduling semester end exams and maintaining exam protocols.       |
| F2               | To plan and conduct Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE) such as Mid Exams, Assignments, Quizzes, and Lab Tests.      |
| F3               | To ensure the preparation and timely submission of internal marks, attendance, and practical marks to the university. |
| F4               | To oversee preparation of seating arrangements, invigilation duty charts, and exam time tables.                       |
| F5               | To ensure secure printing, handling, and storage of question papers for internal exams.                               |
| F6               | To monitor malpractices and take disciplinary action as per university norms.                                         |
| F7               | To analyze exam results and suggest academic improvements based on student performance data.                          |
| F8               | To conduct makeup or improvement exams and maintain records of absentees or detained students.                        |
| F9               | To ensure documentation and maintenance of all examination records for audit and accreditation purposes.              |

**14.4. Composition of the Examination Committee**

| **Designation**                                  | **Role**                   |
|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| Principal / Dean (Academics)                     | Chairman                   |
| Controller of Examinations / Exam Cell In-Charge | Coordinator                |
| HoDs of all Departments                          | Members                    |
| Senior Faculty from Each Department              | Members                    |
| Office Superintendent / Admin Officer            | Logistics & Record Keeping |
| Supporting Technical Staff                       | Exam Cell Assistance       |

**14.5. Examination Committee – Roles and Responsibilities**

**Primary Objective**

To ensure the smooth, fair, and transparent conduct of all examinations (internal assessments, practicals, university exams) in accordance with institutional and affiliating university norms.

**Core Responsibilities:**

**1. Planning and Scheduling**

> • Prepare the internal and external exam schedule/calendar (Mid Exams, Practical Exams, Semester End Exams).
>
> • Coordinate with departments to collect subject-wise question paper requirements.
>
> • Notify faculty and students about exam dates, venues, and rules well in advance.

**2. Question Paper Management**

> • Ensure timely collection of question papers from faculty (for internal exams).
>
> • Verify that question papers adhere to the prescribed syllabus and format.
>
> • Maintain strict confidentiality in handling question papers.

**3. Conduct of Examinations**

> • Arrange seating plans, invigilator duty lists, and exam halls with necessary arrangements.
>
> • Ensure that examination rooms are properly supervised and follow anti-cheating protocols.
>
> • Monitor the attendance of students and invigilators during exams.

**4. Coordination with University**

> • Liaise with the affiliating university regarding university exams, hall tickets, marks entry portals, and circulars.
>
> • Ensure timely communication of university instructions to stakeholders.

**5. Assessment and Result Processing**

> • Coordinate internal answer script evaluations and marks entry.
>
> • Submit internal marks, practical marks, and attendance as per university formats.
>
> • Maintain records of all evaluations and exam-related documentation.

**6. Grievance Redressal**

> • Address exam-related grievances of students and staff (e.g., marks discrepancy, hall ticket issues).
>
> • Recommend revaluation or rechecking as per norms where necessary.

**7. Malpractice Handling**

> • Identify and report cases of unfair practices.
>
> • Convene malpractice committee meetings to recommend disciplinary actions.

**8. Documentation and Reporting**

> • Maintain proper records of:
>
> o Internal and external marks
>
> o Question papers and answer scripts
>
> o Attendance registers during exams
>
> • Submit reports to the academic council/principal periodically.

**9. Continuous Improvement**

> • Analyze examination results to identify trends and suggest improvements.
>
> • Collect feedback from students and staff to enhance examination processes.

**14.6. Examination Committee – Member-Wise Roles & Responsibilities**

| **S.No** | **Designation**                              | **Role**                                                                                                                                                    |
|----------|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Principal / Director                         | Acts as the Chairperson of the Examination Committee; Oversees all exam activities; Approves exam schedules, reports, and policy decisions.                 |

| 9        | Support Staff / Attenders                    | Distribute and collect question/answer booklets; Set up exam halls and maintain cleanliness and orderliness.                                                |

>

>

**14.13. Best Practices of the Examination Committee**

**1.**

**2. Clear Communication of Examination Policies:**

> o Ensure that all stakeholders (students, faculty, and staff) are informed about the examination policies, schedules, and procedures well in advance.
>
> o Use multiple communication channels such as emails, notice boards, and the institution's website for announcements.

**3. Timely Preparation of Examination Schedules:**

> o Develop and publish the examination timetable early to give students and faculty adequate time to prepare.
>
> o Avoid overlapping exam schedules, and consider student workloads to minimize conflicts.

**4. Transparent Evaluation Process:**

> o Establish clear and transparent grading criteria for each exam and communicate these to both students and faculty.
>
> o Encourage faculty to use rubrics or detailed marking schemes to enhance transparency in grading.

**5. Efficient Use of Technology:**

> o Implement online examination systems (for internal assessments or regular exams) to facilitate easier administration, grading, and feedback.
>
> o Ensure that the technology used for exams is secure and reliable, preventing cheating and technical issues.
>
> o Adopt e-valuation for quicker and more accurate result compilation.

**6. Effective Monitoring During Exams:**

> o Ensure proper invigilation procedures to maintain the integrity of exams. This includes proper training of invigilators and adherence to exam hall rules.
>
> o Use CCTV cameras or other surveillance tools to monitor exam halls, if applicable.
>
> o Implement strict measures against malpractice, including a fair process for handling cases of cheating or unethical behavior.

**7. Comprehensive Feedback Mechanism:**

> o Collect feedback from students and faculty regarding the examination process, including ease of access, clarity of instructions, and overall exam conduct.
>
> o Use this feedback to identify areas for improvement and implement changes in the next cycle.

**8. Accessibility and Fairness:**

> o Ensure that examination facilities are accessible to all students, including those with special needs or disabilities.
>
> o Provide accommodations where needed (e.g., extra time, specific arrangements for students with disabilities) to ensure fairness in the assessment process.

**9. Efficient Result Processing and Declaration:**

> o Maintain a well-organized system for the collection and evaluation of examination papers.
>
> o Declare results promptly, ensuring that there is sufficient time for revaluation or addressing student queries.
>
> o Provide students with a clear mechanism for applying for re-evaluation or reviewing their answers.

**10. Confidentiality and Security:**

> o Ensure that examination papers, answer sheets, and student information are kept confidential.
>
> o Secure exam papers by limiting access to only authorized personnel before the examination.
>
> o Establish protocols for handling and storing sensitive examination materials.

**11. Training and Capacity Building for Faculty:**

> o Regularly conduct training sessions for faculty members on assessment methods, evaluation tools, and the use of technology in exams.
>
> o Encourage faculty to design fair and varied assessment strategies to test students' knowledge and skills comprehensively.

**12. Regular Review and Audits of the Examination Process:**

> o Conduct periodic reviews of the examination process to ensure that it is meeting academic and administrative goals.
>
> o Perform internal audits of the examination system to identify any inefficiencies, and take corrective actions where necessary.

**13. Use of Alternative Assessment Methods:**

> o In addition to traditional exams, consider incorporating alternative assessment methods such as project work, group presentations, and online quizzes.
>
> o Encourage innovative ways to assess student learning and reduce over-reliance on written exams.

**14. Post-Examination Analysis:**

> o After each examination, analyze student performance to identify any patterns or areas that may require adjustments in teaching or assessment methods.
>
> o Use performance data to inform future curriculum planning and teaching strategies.

**15. Handling Special Cases (e.g., Absentees, Medical Reasons):**

> o Develop clear policies for handling absentee students or those who cannot appear for exams due to medical or personal reasons.
>
> o Allow for make-up exams or provide alternative assessment methods for such cases.

**16. Ethical Standards and Academic Integrity:**

> o Promote and enforce ethical standards within the examination process.
>
> o Take appropriate action against students or faculty involved in any unethical practices, ensuring fairness and transparency throughout.

**15. Placement and Training, Career Guidance Committee**

**15.1. Introduction**

The Placement and Training Cell (PTC) and Career Guidance Cell (CGC) are critical support units in an engineering institution that prepare students for employment, higher education, and entrepreneurship. These cells work to bridge the gap between academics and industry requirements while nurturing students' career readiness.

**15.2. Objectives**

> • To prepare students for campus placements, competitive exams, and entrepreneurial ventures.
>
> • To develop students' soft skills, technical skills, and industry awareness.
>
> • To facilitate internships, industrial visits, and interaction with industry experts.
>
> • To offer career counseling and mentorship for academic and professional development.

**15.3. Functions of the Placement and Training, Career Guidance Cell**

| **Function No.** | **Function Description**                                                                                            |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | To coordinate campus recruitment activities with national and multinational companies.                              |
| F2               | To organize training programs on aptitude, reasoning, group discussion, interview skills, resume building, etc.     |
| F3               | To establish and maintain linkages with industries for internships, training, and placements.                       |
| F4               | To conduct career guidance programs on higher studies (GATE, GRE, TOEFL), public sector jobs, and entrepreneurship. |
| F5               | To collaborate with alumni and industry mentors to guide students on career paths.                                  |
| F6               | To maintain and regularly update the placement database and analyze trends for improvement.                         |
| F7               | To facilitate industrial visits, internships, and MoUs with corporate and government bodies.                        |
| F8               | To provide special guidance for students from underprivileged backgrounds to improve employability.                 |

**15.4. Organizational Structure**

| **Designation**                        | **Responsibility**              |
|----------------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Principal / Director                   | Strategic oversight             |
| Placement Officer / Training In-Charge | Coordination and implementation |
| Faculty Coordinators (Dept-wise)       | Department-level liaison        |
| Student Placement Coordinators         | Student interface and support   |
| Alumni/Industry Advisors (optional)    | Mentorship and industry connect |

**15.5. Roles & Responsibilities of Placement and Training, Career Guidance Committee**

**1. Placement and Training Functions**

> • **Establish Industry Linkages:** Collaborate with industries, companies, and corporate sectors to facilitate campus placements and internships.
>
> • **Campus Recruitment Drives:** Organize on-campus and off-campus recruitment drives in coordination with HR teams of companies.
>
> • **Skill Development Programs:** Conduct training in aptitude, reasoning, communication, group discussions, and interview skills.
>
> • **Pre-placement Preparation:** Arrange mock interviews, resume writing workshops, and personality development sessions.
>
> • **Internship Opportunities:** Facilitate summer/winter internships for students in reputed organizations.
>
> • **Alumni Connect:** Leverage alumni network to mentor students and assist in securing employment or internship opportunities.

**2. Career Guidance and Counseling**

> • **Career Awareness Sessions:** Organize seminars/webinars on diverse career options - higher education, civil services, entrepreneurship, etc.
>
> • **One-on-One Counseling:** Provide individual counseling to students to guide them in career decision-making based on their interests and aptitude.
>
> • **Competitive Exam Preparation Support:** Guide students in preparing for exams like GATE, GRE, GMAT, CAT, IELTS, TOEFL, etc.
>
> • **Higher Education Support:** Assist with applications, SOP preparation, recommendation letters, and choosing universities for PG studies.

**3. Coordination and Documentation**

> • **Maintain Placement Records:** Keep a systematic record of placement statistics, offers received, company visits, and training programs.
>
> • **Feedback Mechanism:** Collect feedback from recruiters and students for continuous improvement in training and placement strategies.
>
> • **Communication Bridge:** Serve as a bridge between students, faculty, and companies to ensure effective communication.

**4. Committee-Level Responsibilities**

> • **Strategic Planning:** Formulate policies and annual action plans to enhance placement performance and career readiness.
>
> • **Stakeholder Engagement:** Involve departments, faculty, parents, and alumni in initiatives for career development.
>
> • **Monitoring & Reporting:** Submit regular progress reports to the institution's leadership and accreditation committees.

**15.6. Placement and Training, Career Guidance Committee – Member-wise Roles & Responsibilities**

**1. Chairperson (Head of the Institution / Principal)**

> • Provides strategic direction and institutional support for placement and training activities.
>
> • Approves budgets, policies, and MoUs related to placement and career guidance.
>
> • Monitors the effectiveness and overall impact of the committee.
>
> • Chairs review meetings and oversees collaboration with industry stakeholders.

**2. Placement & Training Officer / Coordinator**

> • Acts as the main liaison between students, companies, and departments.
>
> • Coordinates campus recruitment drives and training programs.
>
> • Maintains placement data, student interest forms, and feedback.
>
> • Engages with companies for internship and job opportunities.
>
> • Prepares placement reports and submits them to relevant authorities.

**3. Career Guidance Faculty In-charge**

> • Organizes workshops and expert talks on career paths, higher education, civil services, etc.
>
> • Provides counseling to students regarding career options and goal setting.
>
> • Facilitates sessions on resume building, personal branding, and interview techniques.
>
> • Coordinates with alumni for mentoring and career talks.

**4. Department Placement Coordinators (Faculty)**

> • Identify and shortlist eligible students from their respective departments.
>
> • Ensure student participation in pre-placement training sessions.
>
> • Serve as points of contact between students and the placement office.
>
> • Support in resume verification, communication with students, and tracking interest.

**5. Technical Support / Administrative Staff**

> • Manage logistics during placement drives (hall arrangements, IDs, notices).
>
> • Maintain digital records of training sessions and student attendance.
>
> • Support online test arrangements, student registration, and company requirements.
>
> • Assist with documentation and report preparation.

**6. Student Placement Representatives**

> • Act as peer leaders and communication links between students and faculty coordinators.
>
> • Help in organizing student participation in training, drives, and talks.
>
> • Share feedback and placement updates from the student body.

>

**15.8. Rubric for Assessment – Placement & Training, Career Guidance (CRT Tool)**

| **Tool Code** | **Assessment Parameter**                     | **Level 3**     | **Level 2**      | **Level 1**     |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------|------------------|-----------------|
| T1            | Number of student enrollments in CRT Program | \> 300 students | 100-300 students | \< 100 students |
| T2            | Number of trainers involved/trained          | ≥ 4 trainers    | 2-3 trainers     | \< 1 trainer    |
| T3            | Number of students actually trained          | \> 300 students | 100-299 students | \< 99 students  |
| T4            | Number of Career Counseling Sessions         | ≥ 3 sessions    | 1-2 sessions     | \< 1 session    |
| T5            | Number of Company-Specific Training Sessions | ≥ 4 sessions    | 2-3 sessions     | \< 1 session    |
| T6            | Number of Practice/Mock Tests Conducted      | ≥ 5 tests       | 2-3 tests        | \< 1 test       |

For each academic year or program, evaluate the performance based on these six tools (T1-T6). Assign the level for each tool, and then calculate the average attainment level:

> • Level 3: High performance
>
> • Level 2: Moderate performance
>
> • Level 1: Needs improvement

**15.9. Example: PO Attainment Level Table – Placement and Training, Career Guidance Committee**

| **Function**         | **PO1** | **PO2** | **PO5** | **PO6** | **PO7** | **PO8** | **PO9/PO10** |
|----------------------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|--------------|
| F1                   | 3       | 3       | 3       | 3       |         |         |              |
| F2                   | 3       | 3       |         |         |         |         |              |
| F3                   | 2       | 2       | 2       |         |         |         |              |
| F4                   | 3       | 3       |         |         |         |         |              |
| F5                   | 3       | 3       | 3       |         |         |         |              |
| F6                   | 3       | 3       | 3       | 3       | 3       |         |              |
| **Attainment Level** | **3**   | **3**   | **2.6** | **2.6** | **2.6** | **3**   | **3**        |

**Notes:**

> • Blank cells indicate no significant contribution to that PO by the function.
>
> • Attainment levels are calculated based on the average contribution across all functions mapped to a specific PO.

**Activity-wise Attainment Table**

| **Sl.No** | **Name of the Activity**                    | **T1 (Students Enrolled)** | **T2 (Trainers Trained)** | **T3-T6** |
|-----------|---------------------------------------------|----------------------------|---------------------------|-----------|
| 1         | Aptitude & Communication Skills             | 3                          | 3                         | 3         |

**Average / Attainment → 2.5 → Level 2**

**Notes:**

> • 2.5 → Level 2
>
> • 2.25 → Level 2
>
> • The individual T1–T6 scores are based on the rubric levels (1 to 3) as per actual performance.
>
> • Final attainment level is calculated by taking the average across all activities for each tool and converting that into Level 1 / 2 / 3 based on the scale:
>
> o \> 2.5 = Level 3,
>
> o 1.5 – 2.5 = Level 2,
>
> o \< 1.5 = Level 1

**16. Central Library & Information/ Library Advisory Committee**

**16.1. Purpose**

The Central Library & Information Committee is responsible for overseeing the effective management, development, and utilization of the library and its resources. It ensures the library supports academic and research needs, meets quality benchmarks, and aligns with NBA Criteria 4 & 7 and NAAC Criteria 4.2 & 4.3.

**16.2. Composition of the Committee**

| **Designation**                                 | **Role**         |
|-------------------------------------------------|------------------|
| Principal / Dean                                | Chairperson      |
| Librarian                                       | Member Secretary |
| Senior Faculty Members (1 from each department) | Members          |
| IT Support Staff                                | Member           |
| Student Representatives (UG & PG)               | Members          |
| Research Coordinator (if applicable)            | Member           |

**16.3. Objectives**

> • To strengthen library services in line with academic and research objectives.
>
> • To provide strategic direction and recommend policies for development.
>
> • To ensure access to high-quality learning resources (print and digital).
>
> • To monitor library budget utilization and procurement of learning materials.
>
> • To encourage use of ICT and e-resources in teaching and learning.

**16.4. Functions of the Committee**

| **Function No.** | **Function**                                                                                                               |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | Review and recommend purchase of books, journals, magazines, and digital resources.                                        |
| F2               | Plan and evaluate library automation and digital library initiatives.                                                      |
| F3               | Facilitate training and orientation programs for students and faculty on library usage.                                    |
| F4               | Ensure availability of e-journals, e-books, and subscription databases like IEEE, JGate, ScienceDirect, DELNET, NPTEL etc. |
| F5               | Monitor library usage data and feedback to improve services.                                                               |
| F6               | Coordinate with departments for curriculum-aligned resource procurement.                                                   |
| F7               | Implement open access and institutional repository policies for research papers and thesis.                                |
| F8               | Maintain discipline, cleanliness, and academic ambiance in the library.                                                    |
| F9               | Ensure compliance with quality parameters laid out by NBA & NAAC for library infrastructure and services.                  |

**16.5. Facilities and Support Provided by the Library Advisory Committee (LAC)**

| **S.No** | **Facility / Support**                   | **Description**                                                                                                                                              |
|----------|------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Collection Development                   | Recommends procurement of textbooks, reference books, journals, e-resources, and other learning materials based on curriculum needs and faculty suggestions. |
| 2        | Digital Library and E-Resources Access   | Ensures access to e-journals, e-books, databases (e.g., IEEE, Springer, ScienceDirect, NPTEL), and digital repositories.                                     |
| 3        | Budget Allocation & Utilization          | Advises on budget planning and optimal utilization of library funds for print and digital resources.                                                         |
| 4        | Library Infrastructure Improvement       | Suggests enhancements like reading halls, air conditioning, digital access points, Wi-Fi zones, ergonomic seating, and lighting.                             |
| 5        | Automation & Library Management Software | Oversees implementation and updating of Library Management Systems (e.g., KOHA, SOUL) for cataloging, circulation, and inventory.                            |
| 6        | User Orientation and Awareness Programs  | Organizes training for students/faculty on using OPAC, e-resources, plagiarism checking tools, and referencing software.                                     |
| 7        | Book Bank & Lending Facilities           | Recommends and maintains book banks for economically disadvantaged students; improves issue-return policies.                                                 |
| 8        | Feedback Mechanism & Grievance Redressal | Collects feedback from users and addresses grievances related to library services, environment, or accessibility.                                            |
| 9        | Policy Framing & Guidelines              | Frames and reviews library usage policies (membership, borrowing limits, timings, conduct, etc.).                                                            |
| 10       | Support for Research and Publication     | Facilitates access to research tools (Scopus, Turnitin), thesis repository, and assists with referencing and citation tools.                                 |
| 11       | Coordination with Departments            | Coordinates with academic departments to align resources with course requirements and new program launches.                                                  |

**16.6. Roles and Responsibilities of the Library Advisory Committee (LAC)**

The Library Advisory Committee (LAC) acts as a bridge between the library administration and the academic community. Its primary purpose is to support the effective development, functioning, and modernization of library resources and services to meet the academic and research needs of faculty, students, and staff.

**1. Planning & Development**

> • Advise on long-term development plans for library infrastructure, services, and resource acquisition.
>
> • Assist in formulating policies for effective library governance, including circulation rules, membership, working hours, and code of conduct.

**2. Budgeting & Resource Allocation**

> • Recommend annual budget requirements based on academic and research priorities.
>
> • Monitor and review expenditure on books, journals, e-resources, and digital tools.
>
> • Ensure equitable distribution of funds across departments for academic resources.

**3. Collection Development**

> • Assess and approve the procurement of textbooks, reference books, periodicals, and e-resources.
>
> • Encourage departments to submit recommendations based on curriculum and research needs.
>
> • Review weeding out policies for outdated or less-used materials.

**4. Digital Access and Modernization**

> • Promote the use of digital tools like institutional repositories, OPAC, and remote access portals.
>
> • Recommend subscriptions to national/international databases (e.g., INFLIBNET, DELNET, IEEE, Scopus).
>
> • Facilitate library automation through modern Library Management Software (e.g., KOHA, SOUL).

**5. User Support and Capacity Building**

> • Organize orientation programs, workshops, and seminars on effective library usage.
>
> • Promote awareness about plagiarism detection tools, citation management software, and research databases.
>
> • Evaluate user feedback and suggest improvements in services and facilities.

**6. Infrastructure & Accessibility**

> • Recommend improvements in physical infrastructure (seating, lighting, Wi-Fi, computer terminals).
>
> • Ensure inclusive access for differently-abled users through assistive technologies and special provisions.

**7. Monitoring and Review**

> • Conduct regular reviews of library performance and usage metrics.
>
> • Provide recommendations for service enhancement and report findings to academic councils or institutional heads.
>
> • Encourage feedback mechanisms for continuous improvement.

**8. Policy Framing and Compliance**

> • Help draft and periodically review library policies and procedures.
>
> • Ensure that the library complies with institutional, accreditation, and regulatory standards (NAAC, NBA, UGC).

**16.9. Library Advisory Committee (LAC) – Tool Rubric for Assessment**

> • **T1: Beneficiaries from Library (Visitors)**
>
> • **T2: Book Circulation, Reading Space & Digital Library Usage**
>
> • **T3: Student/Faculty Participation in E-Learning (e.g., NPTEL, SWAYAM)**
>
> • **T4: No. of Awards/Certifications Received**

| **Tool** | **Level 3**                    | **Level 2**                                       | **Level 1**                 |
|----------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| T1       | \> 500                         | Between 200 – 500                                 | \< 200                      |
| T2       | \> 200 (Gold / Elite + Silver) | Between 100 – 199 (Elite / Successful Completion) | \< 100 (Participation Only) |
| T3       | \> 100                         | Between 50 – 99                                   | \< 49                       |

**How to Use This Rubric:**

> • Collect data for each tool (T1-T4) for a given period (e.g., semester/year).
>
> • Compare the actual data to the rubric levels.
>
> • Assign a Level (1 to 3) for each tool based on thresholds.
>
> • Compute overall attainment by averaging the levels across all tools.

**16.18. Best Practices of Central Library & Information/ Library Advisory Committee**

| **Best Practice**                                  | **Description**                                                                                                                                              |
|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Regular User Feedback & Surveys                    | Conduct regular feedback surveys to gauge user satisfaction and identify areas for improvement in library services.                                          |
| Collaborative Budgeting & Resource Planning        | Engage faculty, students, and library staff in the budgeting process to ensure that resources meet academic needs.                                           |
| Annual Resource Review                             | Perform an annual review of library resources, including books, journals, and digital content, to keep it current.                                           |
| Digital Resource Integration                       | Promote the use of e-journals, e-books, and digital databases to ensure easy access to resources for all students and faculty.                               |
| Library Orientation Programs                       | Organize orientation programs at the beginning of each semester for new students and faculty, introducing them to library services and resources.            |
| Themed Library Weeks (e.g., National Library Week) | Celebrate library-related events such as National Library Week with workshops, lectures, and interactive sessions to raise awareness.                        |
| Research Skills Workshops                          | Regularly organize workshops on research skills, reference management, and academic writing to enhance the academic experience.                              |
| Integration with Academic Curriculum               | Align library resources and services with the institution's academic curriculum to support faculty and student needs.                                        |
| Innovative Library Technologies                    | Invest in modern library technologies (e.g., RFID, digital catalogs, online databases) to enhance efficiency and user experience.                            |
| Collaborations with Research Committees            | Collaborate with academic departments, research and development committees, and faculty to support research activities through access to relevant resources. |
| Staff Development Programs                         | Ensure that library staff undergoes continuous training on the latest trends in information management and library services.                                 |
| Promotion of Open Access Resources                 | Encourage the use and promotion of open-access journals and databases to ensure students and faculty have unrestricted access to scholarly content.          |
| Sustainability Initiatives                         | Adopt sustainable practices in library operations, such as reducing paper usage, promoting digital resources, and recycling materials.                       |
| Inclusive and Accessible Resources                 | Ensure that the library is inclusive by providing resources that cater to the needs of differently-abled students (e.g., audio books, screen readers, etc.). |
| Promote Library as a Knowledge Hub                 | Create a culture where the library is not just a place to borrow books but a central hub for knowledge sharing, learning, and innovation.                    |

**17. Ethics / Innovation / IPR Committee**

**17.1. Purpose**

To foster ethical academic conduct, promote innovation and entrepreneurship, and educate stakeholders on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR). The committee ensures that institutions are compliant with NBA Criteria 8 & 10 and NAAC Criteria 3.3, 3.4, 5.1.4 & 7.1.10.

**17.2. Composition of the Committee**

| **Designation**                                     | **Role**        |
|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| Principal / Dean                                    | Chairperson     |
| Innovation Coordinator / IIC Convener               | Coordinator     |
| Senior Faculty Members from each Department         | Members         |
| Industry/Startup Mentor                             | External Member |
| IPR Cell Coordinator / Legal Expert (if applicable) | Member          |
| Faculty Advisor – Entrepreneurship Development Cell | Member          |
| Student Representatives (UG/PG)                     | Members         |

**17.3. Objectives**

> • To ensure integrity in research, projects, and academic work.
>
> • To sensitize students and faculty on ethics, plagiarism, and academic honesty.
>
> • To encourage innovation and guide students in converting ideas into prototypes/products.
>
> • To promote awareness and training on IPR filing, patents, copyrights, and trademarks.
>
> • To support startups and entrepreneurial initiatives through incubation or mentoring.

**17.4. Functions of the Committee**

| **Function No.** | **Function**                                                                                                                          |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | Conduct workshops/seminars on academic and research ethics, including plagiarism awareness.                                           |
| F2               | Organize innovation challenges, hackathons, and idea-thons at institutional level.                                                    |
| F3               | Coordinate with Institution's Innovation Council (IIC) for Ministry of Education's Innovation Ranking (ARIIA).                        |
| F4               | Guide students in converting project ideas into PoC/Prototypes under schemes like Smart India Hackathon (SIH), Toycathon, YUKTI, etc. |
| F5               | Conduct IPR awareness programs with legal or patent experts.                                                                          |
| F6               | Assist in filing and tracking patents, copyrights, and design registrations.                                                          |
| F7               | Frame code of conduct related to academic ethics and ensure compliance.                                                               |
| F8               | Publish institutional guidelines on research ethics and IPR policy.                                                                   |
| F9               | Collaborate with startups, industries, and innovation hubs for internships or funding.                                                |

**17.5. Ethics/Innovation/IPR Committee – Roles and Responsibilities**

**1. Chairperson (Senior Faculty or Head of Department)**

> • **Role:** Oversee and guide the committee in its responsibilities.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Provide leadership and strategic direction to the committee.
>
> o Ensure that the committee's activities align with the institutional policies and ethical standards.
>
> o Approve recommendations related to innovation and intellectual property rights (IPR) matters.
>
> o Represent the committee in discussions with external bodies such as research councils, regulatory agencies, and industry partners.
>
> o Facilitate the development of policies and frameworks to promote ethical practices in research, innovation, and IPR.
>
> o Monitor the implementation of decisions and actions within the scope of ethics, innovation, and IPR.

**2. Faculty Members (Research and Innovation Experts)**

> • **Role:** Provide expertise in research, innovation, and the application of ethical standards.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Guide and advise students and faculty on ethical conduct in research and innovation.
>
> o Develop programs and workshops to raise awareness of ethical issues, intellectual property, and innovation practices.
>
> o Review research proposals, projects, and innovations to ensure they meet ethical standards.
>
> o Advise on the protection of intellectual property (patents, copyrights, trademarks) and guide on filing for patents and copyrights.
>
> o Assist in the formulation of policies related to academic integrity, plagiarism, and ethical research practices.
>
> o Promote an innovation-driven culture by identifying opportunities for faculty and students to commercialize their research outcomes.

**3. Intellectual Property Experts (External Members/Advisors)**

> • **Role:** Offer specialized guidance on intellectual property management and innovation strategies.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Provide expert advice on matters related to patents, trademarks, copyrights, and other intellectual property rights.
>
> o Help in the identification and protection of innovative ideas and technologies developed within the institution.
>
> o Advise faculty and students on the legal implications of innovation and intellectual property.
>
> o Assist in patent filing processes and navigating IP laws.
>
> o Organize awareness programs and workshops related to IPR and its importance for innovation.
>
> o Facilitate connections with legal professionals and IP firms to help with the commercialization of innovative technologies.

**4. Industry Experts/Innovation Leaders**

> • **Role:** Support the committee by bringing industry perspectives and expertise in driving innovation.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Share insights into market trends and emerging technologies to guide institutional innovation efforts.
>
> o Mentor students and faculty in transforming innovative ideas into viable commercial products or services.
>
> o Facilitate partnerships with industry for research and innovation projects.
>
> o Assist in identifying opportunities for startups or collaborations between the institution and industry partners.
>
> o Help in creating an entrepreneurial ecosystem that fosters innovation and IPR management.

**5. Student Representatives (Student Entrepreneurs/Volunteers)**

> • **Role:** Act as a liaison between the committee and the student body to represent student interests in ethics, innovation, and IPR matters.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Share feedback from the student body regarding the ethical standards of research and innovation.
>
> o Help organize student-centered events, such as innovation challenges or hackathons.
>
> o Participate in workshops, seminars, and training programs related to ethics and intellectual property.
>
> o Promote ethical behavior in student research and innovation activities.
>
> o Advocate for greater awareness of IPR among students, encouraging them to protect their ideas.

**6. Administrative Support (Administrative Officer/Coordinator)**

> • **Role:** Manage logistical and organizational aspects of the committee's activities.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Coordinate meetings, events, and initiatives organized by the committee.
>
> o Maintain records of ethical reviews, innovation projects, and IPR activities.
>
> o Assist in preparing documentation for patent filings, project proposals, and other innovation-related matters.
>
> o Ensure that the committee's activities comply with legal and institutional guidelines.
>
> o Provide administrative support for awareness programs, workshops, and seminars related to ethics, innovation, and IPR.
>
> o Facilitate communication between the committee and external bodies, such as IP offices, patent lawyers, and regulatory authorities.

**7. External Advisors (Legal Experts/Patent Attorneys)**

> • **Role:** Offer legal expertise related to IPR matters and ethical issues.
>
> • **Responsibilities:**
>
> o Provide legal advice on the protection of intellectual property, including patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets.
>
> o Guide on the legalities involved in the commercialization of innovations and technologies.
>
> o Assist in ensuring compliance with national and international IPR laws.
>
> o Advise on resolving conflicts related to ethical issues in research and innovation.
>
> o Help navigate legal frameworks related to collaborative research, partnerships, and commercialization of ideas.

**Additional Key Responsibilities for All Members:**

> • **Ethical Compliance:** Ensure that all research and innovation activities comply with ethical standards, including adherence to ethical research guidelines, avoiding plagiarism, and respecting participants' rights.
>
> • **Innovation Promotion:** Foster a culture of creativity and innovation among students and faculty, identifying opportunities to turn research into practical, marketable solutions.
>
> • **Intellectual Property Protection:** Guide students and faculty in identifying, protecting, and commercializing their intellectual property through patents, copyrights, and trademarks.
>
> • **Awareness Building:** Organize workshops, training sessions, and awareness programs related to ethics in research, innovation, and intellectual property management.
>
> • **Collaboration and Networking:** Collaborate with external agencies, legal experts, and industry partners to facilitate innovation and IP protection.

**Note:**

> • The roles and responsibilities outlined above may vary depending on the institution's specific goals, the scope of the committee's activities, and the areas of research and innovation they prioritize.
>
> • Members are expected to work collaboratively to ensure the successful integration of ethical practices, innovation support, and IP management within the academic environment.
