***Key Events / Activities:***

**1. Orientation for New Members:** This event ensures that all new students are introduced to the available professional societies and the opportunities for involvement.

**2. Workshops & Skill Development:** Regular workshops focus on upskilling students in technical and soft skills. These workshops might cover areas like coding, project management, public speaking, leadership, etc.

**3. Industry Visits:** These visits give students a chance to understand the practical applications of their studies, interact with industry professionals, and build connections.

**4. Networking Events & Alumni Interactions:** These events create opportunities for students to network with alumni and professionals, gain career insights, and potentially secure internships or job opportunities.

**5. Competitions and Hackathons:** Competitions between societies encourage teamwork, creativity, and problem-solving skills. Hackathons, in particular, promote innovation and technical prowess.

**6. Annual Society Exhibition & Paper Presentations:** This event allows students to showcase the projects they've worked on over the year, encouraging a culture of research and innovation.

**7. Professional Development Week:** This week-long event includes a series of seminars, workshops, and guest lectures designed to enhance students' career development and industry readiness.

**8. Collaborations with External Organizations:** Building partnerships with external professional bodies and organizations can bring new resources, opportunities, and events to the societies.

**9. Annual Professional Societies Conference:** An end-of-year conference where all societies present their achievements and plan for the next academic year.

***Impact of Professional Societies Coordination Committee Activities:***

> • **Student Engagement:** These activities provide students with multiple platforms to engage with their peers, industry professionals, and alumni.
>
> • **Skill Enhancement:** The workshops and training programs help students enhance their technical, leadership, and interpersonal skills, preparing them for the workforce.
>
> • **Industry Exposure:** Industry visits, internships, and networking events provide invaluable exposure to students, helping them build a professional network before they graduate.
>
> • **Research and Innovation:** Through competitions, conferences, and paper presentations, the committee encourages students to engage in research and innovative thinking.
>
> • **Community Building:** The coordination between various professional societies fosters a sense of community, collaboration, and teamwork among students from diverse disciplines.

**22.13. Best Practices – Professional Societies Coordination Committee**

**1. Institutional Membership Drives**

> • Facilitate student and faculty memberships in reputed societies like IEEE, ISTE, CSI, IE(I), ACM, IETE, etc.
>
> • Offer subsidized group memberships to increase participation.

**2. Regular Technical Events**

> • Organize guest lectures, workshops, seminars, hackathons, webinars, and FDPs in collaboration with professional bodies.
>
> • Events aligned with emerging technologies, industry trends, and national/international days like Engineers Day, Innovation Day, etc.

**3. Interdisciplinary Collaboration**

> • Encourage cross-departmental participation in events and competitions, promoting interdisciplinary learning and teamwork.

**4. Mentoring and Guidance**

> • Assign faculty mentors to guide students in preparing technical papers, participating in competitions, and conferences hosted by professional societies.

**5. Collaboration with Industry**

> • Collaborate with industry experts, alumni, and society representatives to ensure knowledge exchange and networking.

**6. Participation in National-Level Events**

> • Motivate students to take part in national and international tech fests, conferences, paper presentations, and student chapters of professional bodies.

**7. Recognition and Rewards**

> • Recognize and honor students/faculty who actively participate in society events or publish papers in professional forums.

**8. Student Chapters**

> • Establish and maintain active student chapters of key societies with regular meetings, leadership roles, and annual reporting.

**9. Digital Engagement**

> • Use social media and institutional websites to promote events, publish outcomes, and showcase achievements related to professional societies.

**10. Annual Review and Planning**

> • Maintain a yearly planner of activities, review previous outcomes, and prepare strategies to expand reach and quality of programs.

**23. Timetable and Workload Committee**

**23.1. Objective**

To ensure the effective planning, preparation, implementation, and monitoring of academic timetables for smooth conduct of the academic process in alignment with the curriculum, faculty availability, infrastructure, and regulatory guidelines of NBA and NAAC.

**23.2. Timetable and Workload Committee Composition**

| **Role**            | **Designation**                          |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson         | Head of the Institution / Dean Academics |
| Convenor            | Time Table Coordinator (Faculty)         |
| Member              | One Faculty Member from each Department  |
| Supporting Member   | Administrative Office Staff              |
| Invitee (as needed) | Examination Cell Representative          |

**23.3. Functions of the Timetable and Workload Committee (Function Nos. F1–F10)**

| **Function No.** | **Description**                                                           |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | Collect workload and course offerings from departments for each semester. |
| F2               | Allocate classrooms, labs, and other resources optimally.                 |
| F3               | Prepare department-wise and master timetables with no conflicts.          |
| F4               | Integrate value-added courses, remedial sessions, bridge courses, etc.    |
| F5               | Coordinate with the Exam Cell to factor in assessment dates.              |
| F6               | Display and disseminate timetables to all stakeholders in advance.        |
| F7               | Incorporate provisions for co-curricular/extra-curricular activities.     |
| F8               | Modify and reissue timetables in case of contingencies or disruptions.    |
| F9               | Maintain records of timetables, changes, and meeting minutes for audits.  |
| F10              | Assist in NBA/NAAC-related documentation related to academic planning.    |

**23.4. Roles & Responsibilities of Timetable and Workload Committee**

***General Responsibilities:***

> • Allot subjects to the faculty based on specialization, preferences, and workload balance.
>
> • Ensure effective use of lecture halls, labs, and other resources.
>
> • Avoid scheduling overlaps and maintain equitable teaching distribution.

***Coordinator Responsibilities:***

> • Ensure timetable conflicts are avoided.
>
> • Provide finalized timetables to all departments and stakeholders.
>
> • Coordinate dissemination through notice boards, emails, and portals.
>
> • Support committee members and facilitate smooth operation of scheduling.

***Member Responsibilities:***

> • Draft and finalize class and faculty-wise timetables.
>
> • Collect and verify course load, specialization, and subject preferences.
>
> • Post timetables on classroom notice boards and digital platforms.
>
> • Resolve faculty-level scheduling conflicts collaboratively.

|----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|

| **S.No** | **Activities**                                                   | **Responsibility**        | **Target Dates/Days**                      |

| 4        | Receiving service courses from relevant departments              | HoDs                      | Two weeks before semester starts           |

**23.6. Detailed Procedure of Timetable and Workload Committee**

**1. Data Collection**

> • Teaching load data and subject preferences collected from faculty.
>
> • Inputs from Academic Committee and Exam Cell incorporated.

**2. Timetable Drafting**

> • Class timetables and lab schedules prepared in consultation with the departments.

> • Check for overlaps and assign rooms/labs accordingly.

**3. Validation**

> • Provisional timetable reviewed by HoDs and committee.
>
> • Corrections or adjustments made based on feedback.

**4. Finalization**

> • Final timetables for classes and individual faculty circulated and displayed.
>
> • Digital copy shared via institutional ERP / email.

**5. Monitoring & Updating**

> • Timetables reviewed periodically for adjustments (e.g., electives, mentoring).
>
> • Committee addresses any clash or need-based changes during the semester.

**23.11. Best Practices of Timetable and Workload Committee**

**Best Practices of Timetable and Workload Committee**

| **Advance Planning and Scheduling**           | Prepare and finalize the academic timetable well before the start of each semester to allow students and faculty adequate time for preparation.                            |
|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Faculty-Centric Workload Distribution**     | Distribute workload fairly based on faculty specialization, experience, and preferences, ensuring optimal teaching quality and faculty satisfaction.                       |
| **Automation Tools Usage**                    | Utilize digital tools and software (e.g., ERP systems, Timetable Management Software) for timetable generation to minimize errors and save time.                           |
| **Student-Centric Timetabling**               | Design student-friendly schedules by avoiding long gaps between classes, ensuring balanced distribution of difficult subjects, and considering transport and hostel needs. |
| **Flexibility and Adaptability**              | Maintain flexibility to quickly adjust timetables in unexpected events such as faculty leave, guest lectures, or emergency holidays.                                       |
| **Department-wise Coordination Meetings**     | Regularly coordinate with department heads and faculty representatives to gather inputs and address challenges while drafting the timetable.                               |
| **Special Slots for Value-Added Courses**     | Reserve slots in the timetable for activities like skill development courses, seminars, workshops, co-curricular activities, and mentoring sessions.                       |
| **Monitoring and Feedback Mechanism**         | Collect feedback from faculty and students about the effectiveness of the timetable and workload management and use it for continuous improvement.                         |
| **Transparent Communication**                 | Ensure the timetable and workload are communicated well in advance and are displayed prominently (both physically on notice boards and digitally).                         |
| **Compliance with Regulatory Norms**          | Ensure that the workload distribution and timetable adhere to AICTE/UGC/University norms regarding working hours, contact periods, and academic credits.                   |
| **Emergency Response Plan**                   | Develop a backup plan for sudden faculty absence to minimize disruption to academic activities.                                                                            |
| **Balanced Academic and Administrative Load** | While scheduling, balance administrative responsibilities, activities assigned to faculty, teaching duties with guidance, and research/project work.                       |
| **Continuous Review and Updates**             | Conduct periodic reviews of the timetable implementation to ensure smooth functioning throughout the semester and make necessary corrections proactively.                  |

> • Use of ERP / Timetable Management Software
>
> • Rotation of lab slots to ensure optimal usage
>
> • Integration of slot system to accommodate electives and open courses
>
> • Communication of timetables via website/email/student portal
>
> • Separate planning for Value-Added Programs (VAPs) and Remedial Classes

**24. Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee**

**24.1. Objective**

The Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee (SCM-GRC) is designed to provide students with guidance, mentorship, and a platform to express grievances in a safe and supportive environment. The committee focuses on enhancing the emotional well-being, academic performance, and overall personal development of students by fostering positive student-teacher relationships, addressing academic and non-academic issues, and resolving grievances in an unbiased manner. This committee is an essential part of the college's efforts to maintain a healthy learning atmosphere and promote student welfare, while also aligning with NBA and NAAC criteria on student support services.

**24.2. Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee Composition**

| **Designation**         | **Role**                                         |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson             | Principal / Dean (Academic)                      |
| Members                 | HoDs, Faculty Mentors                            |
| Student Representatives | Non-Voting Members (1–2 students per department) |
| Counselors              | Professional Counsellor(s)                       |
| Grievance Officer       | Designated Faculty Member                        |
| Support Staff           | Administrative Assistance                        |

**24.3. Functions of the Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee**

| **Function No.** | **Function Description**                                                                                                                 |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | To appoint faculty members as mentors for each student to offer personalized academic and career guidance.                               |
| F2               | To conduct regular meetings between mentors and mentees for discussing academic progress and personal development.                       |
| F3               | To offer a platform for students to lodge grievances related to academic, non-academic, or administrative issues.                        |
| F4               | To resolve student grievances in a fair and timely manner, ensuring transparency in the redressal process.                               |
| F5               | To maintain confidentiality in all counseling and grievance redressal matters.                                                           |
| F6               | To organize workshops, seminars, and awareness programs focusing on mental health, stress management, and career counseling.             |
| F7               | To provide regular feedback mechanisms for students and faculty to evaluate the effectiveness of the counseling and grievance processes. |
| F8               | To provide academic and emotional counseling services to students, addressing stress, personal, and academic concerns.                   |
| F9               | To create an inclusive and welcoming atmosphere that encourages students to express concerns without fear of retaliation.                |

**24.4. Roles & Responsibilities of Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee**

***Chairperson:***

> • Oversee the operations of the committee and ensure its objectives align with institutional policies.
>
> • Chair regular committee meetings and provide guidance on decision-making.

***Committee Members:***

> • Serve as mentors and provide counseling for academic and personal issues.
>
> • Address specific grievances as they arise and escalate unresolved issues to higher authorities if necessary.
>
> • Ensure that grievances are addressed promptly and transparently.

***Counselors:***

> • Offer professional counseling services to students facing academic or personal difficulties.
>
> • Conduct individual or group counseling sessions as needed.
>
> • Maintain records of counseling sessions and follow up on student progress.

***Grievance Officer:***

> • Serve as the primary point of contact for students wishing to file grievances.
>
> • Investigate and resolve grievances, ensuring a fair and unbiased process.
>
> • Keep detailed records of complaints and their resolution for reporting purposes.

***Student Representatives:***

> • Act as a liaison between students and the committee.
>
> • Provide input from the student body regarding the effectiveness of the counseling and grievance processes.
>
> • Assist in organizing events and spreading awareness about the committee's services.

**24.5. Procedure for Grievance Redressal**

| **S.No** | **Activity**                                   | **Responsible Entity**                           | **Timeline**           |
|----------|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| 1        | Submission of Grievance by Student             | Student (via email, online portal, or in person) | As required            |
| 2        | Acknowledgment of Grievance                    | Grievance Officer/Committee                      | Within 24 hours        |
| 3        | Preliminary Investigation of the Grievance     | Grievance Officer/Committee                      | Within 7 working days  |
| 4        | Resolution and Communication of Outcome        | Committee Members/Principal                      | Within 15 working days |
| 5        | Feedback and Follow-Up                         | Grievance Officer                                | Within 7 working days  |
| 6        | Final Reporting and Documentation for NAAC/NBA | Committee Members                                | End of each semester   |

**24.6. Grievance Redressal Procedure**

**1. Filing the Grievance:** Students can file grievances related to any academic, non-academic, or personal issues through an online portal, email, or directly with the Grievance Officer.

**2. Acknowledgment:** Upon receipt of the grievance, the officer acknowledges the complaint within 24 hours and assures the student of timely resolution.

**3. Investigation:** The Grievance Officer or Committee investigates the issue by gathering all relevant information and ensuring fair consideration of all parties involved.

**4. Resolution:** Based on the investigation, the committee provides a fair resolution. If necessary, the issue may be escalated to senior management for further review.

**5. Communication of Outcome:** The student is informed about the outcome and the resolution in writing. In case of dissatisfaction, the student may appeal to the higher authority.

**6. Feedback Mechanism:** Post-resolution, feedback is sought from the student to evaluate the effectiveness of the grievance redressal process.

**24.7. NBA/NAAC Contribution**

| **Aspect**                    | **Contribution**                                                                                                |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Student Support Services      | Strengthens support structures under NAAC Criterion 5.1 and NBA Criterion 4.                                    |
| Academic Guidance & Mentoring | Contributes to NAAC Criterion 2.6 and NBA Criterion 5.4 by providing mentoring.                                 |
| Grievance Redressal Mechanism | Ensures compliance with NAAC Criterion 5.2 by addressing student grievances promptly.                           |
| Mental Health Awareness       | Supports NAAC Criterion 3.2 by promoting mental well-being and career counseling, holistic student development. |

**24.8. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

| **Metric**                                                             | **Target**        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| Percentage of students attending counseling sessions                   | ≥ 75%             |
| Average time taken for grievance resolution                            | ≤ 10 working days |
| Number of workshops/seminars on mental health, stress management, etc. | ≥ 3 per year      |
| Student satisfaction with grievance resolution process                 | ≥ 80%             |

**24.9. Documents Maintained by the Committee**

> • Student Grievance Records (with resolution details)
>
> • Counseling Session Logs
>
> • Feedback Forms and Impact Assessments
>
> • Report of Committee Meetings
>
> • Annual Reports for NAAC & NBA

**24.10. Meeting Schedule**

> • Regular Meetings: Monthly or as required to review ongoing grievances and counseling cases.
>
> • Emergency Meetings: Held on an ad-hoc basis if urgent issues arise.

**24.11. Mode of Submitting the Grievance**

Students can submit their grievances through the following modes:

**1. Online Portal:** The college maintains an online grievance redressal portal where students can submit their grievances by filling in an online form. The portal allows students to track the progress of their grievance in real-time.

**2. Email:** Students can send an email to the dedicated grievance redressal address (e.g., grievance@college.edu). The email should contain a clear description of the issue, along with any supporting documents or evidence.

**3. Physical Submission:** Students can submit their grievances in writing by filling out the grievance form available at the Students' Counselling Office or the Grievance Redressal Section. The form can be handed over to the Grievance Officer or a designated committee member.

**4. Suggestion/Complaint Box:** A suggestion/complaint box is placed in common areas such as the library, canteen, and hostels, where students can anonymously submit their grievances. These grievances are periodically checked by the committee.

**5. Direct Interaction:** Students can directly approach the Grievance Officer or a committee member in person for an initial discussion. If the issue requires formal documentation, the officer will guide the student on how to submit the grievance.

**6. Social Media Platforms:** Some institutions allow students to submit their grievances via the official college social media platforms (Facebook, Twitter, etc.). These submissions are monitored by the Grievance Redressal Committee to ensure proper attention is given.

**24.12. Procedure for Grievance Submission**

**1. Online Portal Submission:**

> • Student logs into the portal using their student credentials.
>
> • Selects the category of the grievance (academic, non-academic, personal).
>
> • Provides a detailed description of the issue.
>
> • Uploads relevant attachments (e.g., documents, screenshots).
>
> • Submits the grievance and receives an acknowledgment receipt via email.

**2. Email Submission:**

> • Student writes a clear and concise email, stating the grievance and supporting evidence (if applicable).
>
> • The email is addressed to the official grievance redressal address.
>
> • A confirmation reply is sent within 24 hours to acknowledge receipt.

**3. Physical Submission:**

> • Student fills out a grievance form available in the grievance office.
>
> • The form is submitted to the Grievance Officer, who acknowledges it with a receipt.
>
> • The grievance is logged and assigned a tracking number.

**4. Suggestion/Complaint Box:**

> • Student writes their grievance on a piece of paper and places it in the grievance box.
>
> • The Grievance Officer checks the box regularly and records all submitted grievances for follow-up.

**5. Direct Interaction:**

> • Student meets with the Grievance Officer or committee member in person to discuss the issue.
>
> • The grievance is documented during the meeting, and a resolution process is initiated.

**24.13. Consequences of Non-Compliance**

The Grievance Redressal Committee ensures that the processes for submitting and addressing grievances are adhered to by all stakeholders in the institution. Failure to comply with the grievance submission, investigation, or resolution procedures can lead to the following consequences:

***For Students:***

**1. Delayed Resolution:**

> • Failure to follow the proper channels for grievance submission (e.g., using the correct submission forms or platforms) may result in delayed responses or resolution. The grievance may not be processed promptly.

**2. Dismissal of Grievance:**

> • If a grievance is submitted anonymously without following the institution's official grievance procedure, it may be dismissed without investigation, as the institution cannot hold responsible parties accountable or clarify any issues.

**3. Miscommunication and Confusion:**

> • Submitting grievances without clear details, such as lacking proper documentation or leaving out crucial information, can cause confusion and hinder effective investigation or action.

***For Faculty and Staff:***

**1. Failure to Acknowledge Grievances:**

> • If faculty or staff fail to acknowledge grievances in a timely manner, they could be subject to internal disciplinary action. This includes failing to maintain a proper record of grievances or not adhering to the expected timelines for redressal.

**2. Neglect of Responsibilities:**

> • Faculty or staff members who are responsible for investigating or addressing grievances (e.g., department heads, grievance officers) may face warnings, suspension, or other penalties for neglecting their duties, which includes ignoring, delaying, or mishandling the grievance process.

***For Administration/Management:***

**1. Legal Consequences:**

> • Non-compliance with grievance redressal procedures may result in legal implications, especially if a grievance involves harassment, discrimination, or other serious issues that fall under the purview of legal requirements or institutional regulations.

**2. Damage to Institutional Reputation:**

> • Delays in grievance resolution, mishandling of sensitive issues, or non-compliance with grievance redressal procedures can lead to negative publicity, reduced trust in the institution, and a poor reputation among students, faculty, and external stakeholders.

**3. Non-Compliance Penalties:**

> • Failure to adhere to the grievance redressal policy may lead to formal inquiries or investigations. The administration may be required to justify their non-compliance to accrediting bodies like NAAC and NBA, affecting the institution's accreditation and funding.

**4. Loss of Accreditation Points:**

> • For NBA/NAAC evaluations, failure to demonstrate effective grievance redressal processes can lead to a reduction in the score, which may adversely affect the institution's accreditation status and reputation in the higher education community.

**24.14. Corrective Actions for Non-Compliance**

**1. Review and Retraining:**

> • Re-training of involved individuals, including faculty, staff, and administration, on the grievance handling process and the importance of compliance with established procedures.

**2. Strengthening Procedures:**

> • The institution may revise its grievance handling process to make it more robust and transparent, ensuring that all stakeholders understand their roles and responsibilities.

**3. Formal Warnings and Disciplinary Action:**

> • For individuals found to be non-compliant, formal warnings will be issued, and further disciplinary actions may follow depending on the severity of the non-compliance.

**4. Public Disclosure:**

> • Instances of non-compliance may be documented in official reports, which may be shared with students, faculty, and other stakeholders as a means to improve the institution's accountability and transparency.

**24.15. Internal Assessment related grievances**

Three tier mechanism is set up to resolve the internal assessment related grievance: Firstly, the grievance will be brought to the notice of the concerned course teacher. Secondly, in case if the grievance is not resolved/unaddressed, same can be escalated to the Class Teacher/Mentor. Finally, if the grievance still persists, the same shall be referred to the Student Grievance Redressal Committee. In the process of redressal of the grievance, the interest of the aggrieved student shall be considered and as much as possible efforts shall made to resolve the grievance within 7 days by the Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee.

| February  | Mentoring Follow-Up Sessions — Evaluate and assess the progress of mentoring relationships and provide support as needed. (Mentoring Committee)                                                                                       |
| March     | Annual Grievance Redressal Feedback Collection — Collect feedback from students regarding the effectiveness of grievance redressal mechanisms. (Grievance Redressal Committee)                                                        |
| March     | Workshop on Building Emotional Resilience — Provide a workshop to help students build emotional resilience and cope with challenges. (Counselling Committee)                                                                          |
| April     | Pre-Examination Counselling Sessions — Offer pre-examination counselling and stress relief sessions for students. (Counselling Committee)                                                                                             |
| April     | Review of Counselling & Mentoring System — Review and assess the effectiveness of the mentoring and counselling system for improvements. (Counselling & Mentoring Committee)                                                          |
| May       | Feedback Collection on Student Well-being — Collect feedback on how students are managing their academic load, mental health, and overall well-being. (Counselling Committee)                                                         |
| May       | Grievance Handling Session — Address unresolved grievances and provide necessary action or follow-up. (Grievance Redressal Committee)                                                                                                 |
| June      | Post-Exam Counselling & Support — Offer post-examination support and counselling, especially for students facing academic setbacks. (Counselling Committee)                                                                           |
| June      | Mentor-Mentee Feedback Session — Collect feedback from both mentors and mentees to improve the mentoring system. (Mentoring Committee)                                                                                                |

**24.17. Events / Activities Organized by Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee**

The Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee plays a crucial role in addressing students' concerns and providing guidance and support. Below are the key events and activities organized by the committee to foster student well-being, mental health, academic success, and grievance resolution.

1\. **Student Orientation on Counselling and Grievance Mechanism**

> **Purpose:** To introduce new students to the counselling services, grievance redressal systems, and mental health resources available on campus.
>
> **Timing:** During the first week of the academic year.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Introduction to the committee's functions.
>
> o Sharing information on how to access counselling services.
>
> o Awareness of grievance redressal mechanisms.

2\. **Individual and Group Counselling Sessions**

> **Purpose:** To provide one-on-one or group support for students dealing with academic, personal, or emotional challenges.
>
> **Timing:** Throughout the academic year.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Regularly scheduled one-on-one counselling sessions.
>
> o Group therapy or support groups for students with similar concerns (e.g., stress, time management, etc.).

3\. **Mentoring Sessions**

> **Purpose:** To provide guidance and support to students, particularly first-year students, by pairing them with senior mentors who offer academic and emotional support.
>
> **Timing:** Throughout the academic year.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Pairing of senior students (mentors) with juniors (mentees).
>
> o Regular check-ins to track student progress, provide academic guidance, and discuss personal challenges.

4\. **Mental Health Awareness Campaign**

> **Purpose:** To raise awareness about mental health, reduce stigma, and promote healthy coping mechanisms.
>
> **Timing:** Mental Health Awareness Week (Typically in October).
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Workshops on stress management, coping mechanisms, and emotional wellbeing.
>
> o Campus-wide awareness campaigns using posters, pamphlets, and social media.
>
> o Collaboration with external mental health professionals for seminars or webinars.

5\. **Stress Management and Study Skills Workshops**

> **Purpose:** To help students manage academic stress and improve their study habits and techniques.
>
> **Timing:** Before major exams and mid-semester.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Workshops on time management, effective study techniques, and overcoming exam anxiety.
>
> o Interactive sessions on mindfulness, relaxation exercises, and stress relief strategies.

6\. **Grievance Redressal Sessions**

> **Purpose:** To address and resolve student grievances, ensuring a transparent and fair process.
>
> **Timing:** As required, based on grievances raised by students.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Open forums or individual grievance sessions where students can express concerns.
>
> o Resolution of academic, administrative, or personal grievances in a confidential manner.
>
> o Follow-up actions to ensure the grievance is resolved satisfactorily.

7\. **Workshop on Emotional Intelligence and Self-Development**

> **Purpose:** To help students improve their emotional intelligence, self-awareness, and interpersonal skills.
>
> **Timing:** Once a semester.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Sessions focusing on building emotional intelligence, empathy, and communication skills.
>
> o Activities designed to enhance self-awareness and self-regulation.

8\. **Post-Examination Counselling Sessions**

> **Purpose:** To support students who may experience anxiety, disappointment, or mental strain due to exam results.
>
> **Timing:** After the announcement of major exam results.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o One-on-one counselling sessions for students needing emotional support.
>
> o Guidance on academic planning and career options if results are unsatisfactory.
>
> o Sessions on handling failure and setting new academic goals.

9\. **Annual Mental Health Day**

> **Purpose:** To create a platform for promoting mental health awareness, self-care, and building a supportive environment for students.
>
> **Timing:** Annually (typically in May).
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Guest lectures, workshops, and interactive sessions focused on mental health.
>
> o Distribution of mental health resources and stress-relief kits.
>
> o Activities such as group meditation, yoga, or creative expression (art, music, etc.) to reduce stress.

10\. **Career Counselling and Guidance Sessions**

> **Purpose:** To provide students with guidance on career choices, job opportunities, and professional development.
>
> **Timing:** Mid-year and end of academic year.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Workshops on resume building, interview preparation, and job market trends.
>
> o One-on-one career counselling for final-year students.
>
> o Seminars on career development from industry experts.

11\. **Annual Feedback and Survey Collection**

> **Purpose:** To assess the effectiveness of the counselling, mentoring, and grievance redressal systems, and gather student feedback for improvements.
>
> **Timing:** End of each semester.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Collection of feedback from students regarding their experiences with the counselling services.
>
> o Survey on the effectiveness of grievance redressal procedures.
>
> o Use feedback to modify and enhance services based on student needs.

12\. **Pre-Examination Stress Relief and Counselling**

> **Purpose:** To help students manage stress before final exams through various activities and support services.
>
> **Timing:** One or two weeks before exams.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Group counselling sessions on managing exam stress.
>
> o Relaxation techniques such as deep breathing, meditation, and progressive muscle relaxation.
>
> o Peer support groups to help students with exam-related anxiety.

**24.18. Best Practices of the Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee**

The Students Counselling, Mentoring & Grievance Redressal Committee plays a vital role in enhancing student well-being, academic success, and ensuring a healthy academic environment. Below are the best practices that can be implemented by this committee to improve its effectiveness and ensure the comprehensive support of students:

1\. **Regular Awareness Campaigns**

> **Practice:** Organize regular awareness campaigns to ensure students are fully informed about the counselling, mentoring, and grievance redressal services available to them.
>
> **Impact:** Increased student participation and awareness regarding available support systems.
>
> **Method:** Use various platforms such as posters, emails, orientation sessions, and social media to raise awareness.

2\. **Personalized Counselling Services**

> **Practice:** Offer one-on-one counselling services tailored to the individual needs of students, focusing on both personal and academic challenges.
>
> **Impact:** Addressing specific student concerns and providing customized support.
>
> **Method:** Conduct regular individual sessions with students to provide guidance on emotional well-being, stress management, career planning, and personal issues.

3\. **Mentorship Programs for New Students**

> **Practice:** Implement a structured mentorship program for first-year students where they are paired with senior mentors to guide them through academic and social challenges.
>
> **Impact:** Early intervention in students' academic and emotional difficulties, promoting a supportive environment.
>
> **Method:** Assign mentors to a group of first-year students and ensure regular interactions for guidance on study habits, social integration, and stress management.

4\. **Online Counselling and Support**

> **Practice:** Provide online counselling services and virtual support platforms to cater to students who cannot attend in-person sessions due to geographic or personal constraints.
>
> **Impact:** Broader accessibility of services, especially during times when students are unable to meet in person.
>
> **Method:** Implement virtual counselling platforms and email-based support systems, ensuring that students can reach out remotely.

5\. **Confidentiality and Safe Space**

> **Practice:** Maintain strict confidentiality in all counselling and grievance redressal processes to foster trust and openness among students.
>
> **Impact:** Encourages students to share concerns without fear of judgment or breach of privacy.
>
> **Method:** Establish clear guidelines and assurances for confidentiality in all interactions with students.

6\. **Regular Grievance Redressal Mechanisms**

> **Practice:** Ensure a well-established, transparent grievance redressal system that allows students to easily file and follow up on complaints.
>
> **Impact:** Students feel heard and respected, knowing that their issues will be addressed in a timely manner.
>
> **Method:** Set up an online platform or grievance box where students can file complaints anonymously, if preferred, and ensure a fixed timeline for addressing grievances.

7\. **Stress Management and Wellness Workshops**

> **Practice:** Organize workshops and seminars on stress management, time management, mental health awareness, and overall wellness.
>
> **Impact:** Empowering students with the tools to cope with academic pressure and mental health challenges.
>
> **Method:** Invite expert speakers, conduct interactive sessions, and offer practical techniques for dealing with stress, anxiety, and academic pressure.

8\. **Peer Support Systems**

> **Practice:** Foster peer support networks where students can engage with and support each other, especially during high-stress periods like exams.
>
> **Impact:** Peer networks can be a source of comfort, encouragement, and help students feel less isolated.
>
> **Method:** Create student-led groups or clubs that facilitate peer support and enable students to share experiences and coping strategies.

9\. **Regular Feedback Mechanisms**

> **Practice:** Implement regular feedback mechanisms (surveys, focus groups, or one-on-one meetings) to gauge the effectiveness of counselling, mentoring, and grievance redressal processes.
>
> **Impact:** Helps identify areas of improvement and ensures that services remain relevant to students' needs.
>
> **Method:** Distribute online surveys or conduct informal discussions with students to collect their feedback on the effectiveness of services.

10\. **Career and Academic Guidance**

> **Practice:** Provide career counselling and academic support to guide students on course selection, career pathways, job preparation, and higher education options.
>
> **Impact:** Supports students in making informed decisions about their academic and professional future.
>
> **Method:** Organize career fairs, one-on-one career counselling sessions, and workshops on resume building and interview preparation.

11\. **Multi-Disciplinary Support**

> **Practice:** Collaborate with faculty, administrative staff, and external professionals to provide a multi-disciplinary support system that addresses diverse student concerns (academic, personal, financial, etc.).
>
> **Impact:** Holistic support for students, ensuring they have access to a variety of resources.
>
> **Method:** Hold regular meetings with academic and administrative teams to address cross-functional issues and provide a comprehensive support network.

12\. **Timely Intervention in Critical Situations**

> **Practice:** Intervene in a timely manner when students show signs of significant distress, academic struggle, or behavioral changes.
>
> **Impact:** Early intervention can prevent further complications and help students recover or get back on track.
>
> **Method:** Monitor students who are showing signs of distress, engage with them proactively, and refer them to appropriate services (e.g., academic support, medical services, or psychological help).

13\. **Promoting Self-Care and Mental Health Awareness**

> **Practice:** Encourage students to practice self-care and adopt a proactive approach to mental health, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a healthy work-life balance.
>
> **Impact:** Promotes a culture of self-care and reduces the stigma around seeking mental health support.
>
> **Method:** Create initiatives such as self-care tips, mental health days, and awareness campaigns about the importance of mental well-being.

14\. **Crisis Intervention and Counseling**

> **Practice:** Provide immediate support and intervention for students facing crises such as loss of a loved one, financial hardship, or severe academic or personal stress.
>
> **Impact:** Ensures that students feel supported during their most challenging moments.
>
> **Method:** Establish emergency counseling services and clear protocols for dealing with crises in a compassionate and timely manner.

15\. **Collaboration with External Experts**

> **Practice:** Collaborate with external mental health professionals, career counsellors, or wellness coaches to provide additional expertise and services.
>
> **Impact:** Brings in specialized knowledge and diverse resources to support students more effectively.
>
> **Method:** Invite guest speakers or hire external professionals to conduct workshops, webinars, or one-on-one counselling sessions.

**25. Press, Media and Publications Committee**

**25.1. Introduction**

The Press, Media, and Publications Committee (PMPC) in Engineering Colleges plays a vital role in enhancing the institution's visibility, promoting its achievements, and ensuring proper communication through various media channels. This committee is an integral part of an institution's strategic outreach, ensuring alignment with NBA (National Board of Accreditation) and NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council) standards.  
Here's a detailed overview of the Press, Media, and Publications Committee (PMPC) and its relevance to NBA and NAAC:

**25.2. Objective of PMPC**

**1. Enhance Visibility:**

> • To increase the visibility of the institution's achievements, events, programs, and faculty/student research outcomes.

**2. Effective Communication:**

> • To ensure effective and transparent communication with students, faculty, parents, and the external community.

**3. Media Relations:**

> • To build strong relationships with local, national, and international media houses.

**4. Publications and Documentation:**

> • To publish newsletters, brochures, magazines, annual reports, and other documents for promoting academic, co-curricular, and extra-curricular activities.

**5. Promote Research and Innovation:**

> • To publicize research activities, innovations, and collaborations with industries and other institutions.

**25.3. Committee Composition**

| **Designation**             | **Role**                                                                                |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson                 | Director/Principal or Senior Faculty                                                    |
| Members                     | Faculty Members, Communication Experts, Marketing and Branding Team                     |
| Student Representatives     | To assist in content creation and manage social media platforms                         |
| Media Liaisons              | Faculty or External Experts responsible for maintaining relationships with media houses |
| External Members (optional) | Professionals from PR agencies or Media outlets for professional guidance               |

**25.4. Key Functions of PMPC (Function Nos. F1–F8)**

| **Function No.** | **Function Description**                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| F1               | Media Coordination: Establish and maintain relationships with media outlets and journalists. Coordinate with print, digital, and electronic media for coverage of college events, faculty achievements, student accomplishments, etc. |
| F2               | Publication of College Newsletter/Magazines: Regularly publish and distribute newsletters, magazines, or e-bulletins to update students, faculty, alumni, and parents about college activities.                                       |
| F3               | Event Coverage: Organize media coverage for key events such as academic fests, workshops, industry collaborations, guest lectures, and conferences.                                                                                   |
| F4               | Press Releases: Write and issue press releases to highlight significant milestones such as faculty research, student achievements, institutional progress, etc.                                                                       |
| F5               | Social Media Management: Manage the institution's social media profiles, ensure timely updates on platforms like Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, and Instagram.                                                                          |
| F6               | Brand Building: Develop and implement strategies to enhance the college's brand image through consistent media presence and targeted publications.                                                                                    |
| F7               | Documenting Institutional Achievements: Maintain records of publications, media coverage, and other outreach efforts for reference during NBA/NAAC assessments.                                                                       |
| F8               | Community Engagement: Ensure the institution's activities, such as outreach programs, community service, and partnerships with industries, are well-covered in media and publications.                                                |

**25.5. Roles and Responsibilities of Press, Media, and Publications Committee**

The Press, Media, and Publications Committee in an educational institution plays a crucial role in maintaining the public image of the institution, ensuring effective communication both within and outside the campus, and promoting the activities and achievements of the institution. Here are the detailed roles and responsibilities of the committee:

***Media Relations Management***

> **Responsibility:** Establish and maintain positive relationships with media outlets (newspapers, television, radio, online platforms).
>
> **Role:** Act as the primary liaison between the institution and the media to ensure that accurate and timely information is shared.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Responding to media queries.
>
> o Distributing press releases.
>
> o Coordinating interviews with faculty, staff, and students for media coverage.

***Issuing Press Releases and Newsletters***

> **Responsibility:** Draft, review, and distribute press releases and newsletters to inform the public about the institution's events, achievements, initiatives, and other relevant information.
>
> **Role:** Ensure that all communications reflect the institution's values, mission, and accomplishments.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Writing and distributing press releases for events, collaborations, awards, etc.
>
> o Creating periodic newsletters with institutional updates.

***Event Coverage and Reporting***

> **Responsibility:** Provide media coverage for all significant events, programs, seminars, and workshops conducted by the institution.
>
> **Role:** Ensure that all major events are well-documented and publicized, both on-campus and in external media.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Coordinating with event organizers for media coverage.
>
> o Writing reports/articles on events for publication in institutional media or external outlets.
>
> o Taking photographs and videos during events for documentation and future promotion.

***Social Media Management***

> **Responsibility:** Manage and regularly update the institution's social media profiles (e.g., Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn).
>
> **Role:** Ensure that the institution's presence on social media is active, engaging, and reflective of its values.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Creating and posting content related to events, announcements, achievements, and campus life.
>
> o Engaging with students, faculty, alumni, and the public through interactive posts.
>
> o Managing responses and comments from followers to maintain a positive image.

***Publication of Institutional Magazine/Journal***

> **Responsibility:** Oversee the publication of institutional magazines, journals, or other periodicals that showcase student work, faculty research, and institutional achievements.
>
> **Role:** Highlight the academic, cultural, and extracurricular activities of the institution in a professional publication.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Editing and reviewing articles, papers, and features for publication.
>
> o Coordinating with departments for content contributions.
>
> o Organizing periodic releases of institutional publications.

***Developing and Managing Content for Institutional Website***

> **Responsibility:** Ensure the institution's website remains up-to-date with relevant news, publications, announcements, and updates.
>
> **Role:** Provide fresh, engaging, and relevant content for the website to keep the institution's digital presence strong and informative.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Writing and publishing news articles, event updates, and academic information on the website.
>
> o Coordinating with departments to ensure that the website content is accurate and regularly updated.

***Internal Communication***

> **Responsibility:** Ensure clear communication within the institution regarding activities, events, and important information.
>
> **Role:** Foster transparency and ensure that all stakeholders, including students, faculty, and staff, are well-informed.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Sending regular updates via email, posters, or announcements.
>
> o Managing internal newsletters or bulletins for faculty, staff, and students.

***Crisis Communication***

> **Responsibility:** Handle communication during crises, controversies, or emergencies in the institution.
>
> **Role:** Provide accurate and timely information to the media and public during critical situations to maintain the institution's reputation.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Preparing and issuing official statements and responses.
>
> o Coordinating media briefings and interviews during emergencies.
>
> o Managing the narrative around sensitive issues.

***Promoting Student and Faculty Achievements***

> **Responsibility:** Promote the academic, research, and extracurricular achievements of students and faculty members.
>
> **Role:** Recognize and publicize accomplishments to enhance the institution's prestige and encourage a culture of excellence.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Highlighting awards, research publications, conferences, and competitions in media and publications.
>
> o Interviewing faculty members and students to feature their stories and achievements in institutional materials.

***Collaborating with External Stakeholders***

> **Responsibility:** Collaborate with alumni, industry partners, and other educational institutions for mutual promotion and recognition.
>
> **Role:** Build partnerships and create opportunities for the institution through external communication.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Coordinating joint publications, promotional events, and interviews with external stakeholders.
>
> o Developing content for newsletters, websites, and press releases about collaborations and partnerships.

***Archiving and Documenting Media and Publications***

> **Responsibility:** Maintain an archive of all media coverage, publications, press releases, and newsletters.
>
> **Role:** Keep a record of the institution's public communications for future reference and documentation.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Collecting and cataloging all articles, publications, and media coverage about the institution.
>
> o Maintaining a media database for future reference and reports.

***Organizing Media Training for Faculty/Staff***

> **Responsibility:** Provide media training for faculty and staff members who may represent the institution in public forums or interviews.
>
> **Role:** Prepare staff and faculty to effectively communicate with the media.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Organizing media handling workshops.
>
> o Providing guidelines for interviews, press conferences, and public appearances.

**25.6. Meeting Schedule**

> • **Frequency:** Quarterly meetings to discuss media strategies, upcoming events, and dissemination plans.
>
> • **Ad-hoc meetings:** Additional meetings can be scheduled based on the release of major events or publication deadlines.

**25.7. Documentation & Reporting for NBA/NAAC**

PMPC plays a crucial role in fulfilling the requirements for NBA/NAAC accreditation under the following criteria:

> • **NBA Criterion 5 (Student Support and Progression):** Publicity of student achievements, participation in co-curricular activities, industry partnerships, and innovation can enhance the institution's score.
>
> • **NAAC Criterion 7 (Institutional Values and Best Practices):** Documentation and publication of institutional best practices, sustainability efforts, and the impact of community outreach activities improve the institutional score.

**25.8. Documentation Managed by PMPC**

> • Annual reports on media engagement and publications
>
> • Event-wise media coverage and publications
>
> • Press releases issued
>
> • Social media reports (reach, engagement, and impact)
>
> • Feedback reports on publication effectiveness

**25.9. NBA/NAAC Contribution**

| **Aspect**                                   | **Contribution to NBA/NAAC**                                                                                                                                            |
|----------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Co-Curricular and Extracurricular Activities | Enhances visibility of student involvement, promoting institutional values (NAAC Criterion 5.2).                                                                        |
| Research and Innovation                      | Showcases research outputs and innovations, contributing to NBA Criterion 3 (Industry Interaction) and NAAC Criterion 3.3 (Research & Innovation).                      |
| Public Engagement                            | Improves the institution's engagement with the external community, aligning with NAAC Criterion 5.1 (Institutional Values and Best Practices).                          |
| Documentation for SSR/AQAR                   | Ensures all media publications and event records are available for NBA/NAAC review during SSR (Self-Study Report) or AQAR (Annual Quality Assurance Report) submission. |

**25.10. Sample Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

| **Metric**                          | **Target**                                          |
|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Number of Publications per Year     | ≥ 5 (e.g., magazines, research papers, newsletters) |
| Social Media Engagement (Monthly)   | ≥ 1000 interactions (likes, shares, comments)       |
| Number of Media Coverage per Year   | ≥ 20 articles/reports                               |
| Number of Events Covered by Media   | ≥ 10 (conferences, fests, etc.)                     |
| Industry Partnership Press Releases | ≥ 3 per year                                        |

**25.11. Year Planner: Press, Media and Publications Committee**

| **Month** | **Activity/Task (Responsible Party)**                                                                  |
|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| January   | Publish New Year Message via media and social platforms. (Committee Chair, PR Team)                    |
| February  | Press coverage for Annual Sports Meet / Festivals. (Event Coordinator, Media Coordinator)              |
| March     | Collect and compile department-wise academic achievements for newsletter. (Department Representatives) |
| April     | Publish Institution's Quarterly Newsletter (Jan–Mar). (Editorial Team)                                 |
| May       | Plan and design Annual Magazine content. (Editorial Team, Student Editors)                             |
| June      | Archive media coverage of Semester-End Events. (Media Archivist)                                       |
| July      | Press release on Admission Drives / Orientation. (PR Team, Admissions Cell)                            |
| August    | Social media campaigns for Independence Day events. (Social Media Coordinator)                         |
| September | Publish Institution's Quarterly Newsletter (Apr–Jun). (Editorial Team)                                 |
| October   | Organize Media Skills Workshop for Faculty/Students. (Workshop Coordinator)                            |
| November  | Press coverage for Cultural Fests / Technical Symposiums. (Event PR Coordinator)                       |
| December  | Publish Annual Magazine & Year-End Highlights Report. (Editorial Team)                                 |

**Continuous Activities Throughout the Year:**

> • Event-wise Press Releases before and after major programs.
>
> • Maintain regular updates on institutional website and social media.
>
> • Collect student, faculty, and institutional achievements monthly.
>
> • Maintain and update media contacts database.
>
> • Archive press cuttings, video coverage, and publications digitally.

**25.12. Best Practices of Press, Media, and Publications Committee**

| **S.No** | **Best Practice Details**                                                                                                                            |
|----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Timely and Accurate Communication: Ensure news/events are reported promptly with factual accuracy to the media.                                      |
| 2        | Maintaining a Contact Directory: Maintain updated contact lists of local, regional, and national media outlets for quick communication.              |
| 3        | Pre-Event and Post-Event Publicity: Issue press releases before and after major events to maximize visibility.                                       |
| 4        | Centralized Content Review Mechanism: Establish a review process for all publications (newsletters, magazines, reports) for quality and consistency. |
| 5        | Use of Official Templates and Branding: Maintain uniformity by using institution-approved templates for all media communications.                    |
| 6        | Archiving Media Coverage: Systematic documentation and archiving of all newspaper articles, TV clips, and online mentions about the institution.     |
| 7        | In-House Newsletter and Annual Magazine: Publish a quarterly newsletter and an annual magazine showcasing achievements and activities.               |
| 8        | Media Training for Faculty and Students: Organize workshops on media interaction, public speaking, and writing press releases.                       |
| 9        | Digital and Social Media Presence: Actively manage official social media handles (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter) with regular updates.      |
| 10       | Celebrating Achievements: Highlight faculty, staff, and student achievements in internal and external publications.                                  |
| 11       | Proactive Crisis Communication Strategy: Be prepared with a communication plan in case of emergencies or negative media coverage.                    |
| 12       | Collaboration with Academic Departments: Regularly collect news-worthy updates and success stories from all departments.                             |
| 13       | Creative Content Development: Develop videos, infographics, and blog posts along with traditional press releases.                                    |
| 14       | Monthly Media Reports: Prepare and submit monthly reports on media engagement and coverage.                                                          |
| 15       | Encouraging Student Participation: Involve students (media clubs) in writing, photography, editing, and designing institutional publications.        |

***Note:** Following these practices helps in enhancing the brand image of the institution, building trust with stakeholders, and creating a positive public perception.*

**25.13. Conclusion**

The Press, Media, and Publications Committee ensures effective communication, visibility, and documentation of institutional activities that support NBA/NAAC accreditation. By maintaining a consistent and transparent approach to media relations and publications, the committee strengthens the institution's standing in national and international academic circles while aligning with accreditation guidelines.

**26. Alumni Coordination Committee**

**26.1. Introduction**

The Alumni Coordination Committee (ACC) in an Engineering College plays a critical role in maintaining strong ties between the institution and its alumni. The committee works towards engaging alumni, strengthening the alumni network, and leveraging alumni resources for the benefit of the institution. The committee's activities are pivotal in achieving and maintaining accreditation standards set by NBA (National Board of Accreditation) and NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council).

**26.2. Objective of the Alumni Coordination Committee**

**1. Engagement and Networking:**

> • Facilitate continuous interaction between the institution and its alumni for mutual benefit. Encourage alumni to actively participate in college events, conferences, and guest lectures.

**2. Support for Development:**

> • Engage alumni in supporting the institution's development through donations, mentorship, internships, guest lectures, and collaborative projects.

**3. Strengthening Institutional Reputation:**

> • Alumni serve as ambassadors for the college. By fostering strong relationships, alumni can help raise the institution's visibility and reputation.

**4. Feedback Mechanism:**

> • Collect feedback from alumni on the quality of education, curriculum, and the institution's overall impact on their career development. This feedback helps in improving academic offerings, aligning with industry trends, and ensuring a better learning environment.

**5. Industry-Academia Collaboration:**

> • Leverage alumni working in various industries to enhance collaboration, create internship and placement opportunities for students, and organize industrial visits.

**26.3. Committee Composition**

| **Role/Designation**    | **Responsibilities**                                                 |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson             | Senior Faculty Member / Director of Alumni Affairs                   |
| Faculty Coordinators    | Faculty members from each department                                 |
| Alumni Representatives  | Elected representatives from various alumni batches                  |
| Student Representatives | To assist with alumni-related events and activities                  |
| Administrative Staff    | To manage logistics, record keeping, and communication               |
| External Advisors       | Industry mentors, former alumni, or other professionals for guidance |

**26.4. Key Functions of the Alumni Coordination Committee (Function Nos. A1–A8)**

| **Function No.** | **Function Description**                                                                                                                                                                           |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| A1               | Alumni Database Management: Maintain an up-to-date database of alumni, including contact details, professional achievements, and career progression.                                               |
| A2               | Alumni Events & Reunions: Organize regular alumni meets, reunions, and virtual gatherings to foster connections between alumni and the institution.                                                |
| A3               | Alumni Contribution to Curriculum Design: Seek feedback and inputs from alumni to make curriculum updates relevant to current industry trends.                                                     |
| A4               | Career Guidance & Mentoring: Engage alumni in mentoring current students by offering career advice, internships, and job placements.                                                               |
| A5               | Alumni Contributions (Donations, Endowments): Encourage alumni to contribute financially to the college's development through donations or setting up scholarships and endowments.                 |
| A6               | Collaborative Projects: Foster collaboration between alumni and faculty for research and innovation.                                                                                               |
| A7               | Alumni Placement Support: Develop a network of alumni in key industries for placement support and internships for current students.                                                                |
| A8               | Alumni Communication: Establish regular communication channels (newsletters, emails, webinars) to update alumni about the institution's progress, achievements, and opportunities for involvement. |

**26.5. Meeting Schedule**

> • **Frequency:** Quarterly meetings (minimum) to plan and review activities.
>
> • **Ad-hoc meetings:** Additional meetings may be scheduled to plan specific events like reunions or guest lectures.
>
> • **Annual Meeting:** A formal annual meeting with all alumni, featuring discussions on future collaborations, feedback collection, and institutional growth.

**26.6. Documentation & Reporting for NBA/NAAC**

The ACC plays a significant role in supporting NAAC and NBA accreditation criteria by documenting the institution's relationship with alumni and their contributions to the college's academic and extra-curricular activities.
