**26.14. Conclusion**

The Alumni Coordination Committee (ACC) is a pivotal committee that helps bridge the gap between the institution and its former students. Through active alumni engagement, mentorship programs, and feedback loops, the ACC plays a significant role in improving academic offerings, student support systems, and industry collaborations. By aligning its operations with the accreditation standards of NBA and NAAC, the committee ensures that the institution continues to develop and maintain its high standards in education and industry relevance.

**27. Research and Development Committee**

**27.1. Introduction**

The Research and Development (R&D) Committee in an engineering college is a pivotal body that oversees, encourages, and ensures that the research activities of the institution align with its academic and strategic goals. The committee plays an essential role in maintaining and enhancing the college's position in national and international research landscapes. This committee is crucial for fulfilling the requirements set by the National Board of Accreditation (NBA) and the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC), contributing significantly to the overall academic and institutional development.

**27.2. Objective of the Research and Development Committee (R&D)**

**1. Promotion of Research Activities:**

> • To promote and foster a research-oriented culture within the institution among faculty and students.

**2. Aligning with Institutional Goals:**

> • To ensure that research aligns with the institution's mission and vision, contributing to advancements in education, innovation, and industry collaboration.

**3. Support for Faculty and Student Research:**

> • To provide guidance and resources to faculty and students for pursuing research in cutting-edge areas of technology, innovation, and science.

**4. Enhancing Industry-Academia Collaboration:**

> • To build connections with industry leaders, research organizations, and other academic institutions for collaborative research.

**5. Publications and Patents:**

> • Encourage faculty and students to publish their work in reputed journals and conferences and secure patents for innovations.

**6. Monitoring and Reporting:**

> • To monitor the quality and impact of the research carried out within the institution and report it in the form of documentation required for NBA/NAAC accreditation.

**27.3. Committee Composition**

| **Role/Designation**    | **Responsibilities**                                                  |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson             | Senior Faculty Member / Dean of R&D                                   |
| Co-Chairperson          | Head of Research in the institution                                   |
| Faculty Representatives | Faculty members from each department with research experience         |
| Student Representatives | Research-oriented student leaders and representatives                 |
| R&D Coordinator         | Faculty member responsible for coordinating day-to-day R&D activities |
| External Experts        | Industry professionals or academic researchers for expert guidance    |
| Administrative Support  | Managing logistics, records, and communication for R&D activities     |

**27.4. Key Functions of the R&D Committee (Function Nos. R1–R8)**

| **Function No.** | **Function Description**                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| R1               | Promoting Research Culture: Foster a culture of innovation, research, and critical thinking among students and faculty.                                        |
| R2               | Identifying Research Areas: Identify emerging research areas that align with industry needs and future technological trends.                                   |
| R3               | Research Funding: Identify and secure funding opportunities for research from government bodies, industry sponsors, and international organizations.           |
| R4               | Research Collaboration: Facilitate collaborations with national and international academic and research institutions, as well as industry players.             |
| R5               | Monitoring Research Quality: Ensure that the research conducted meets national and international standards of quality and impact.                              |
| R6               | Promoting Publications: Encourage faculty and students to publish research in high-impact journals and present at national and international conferences.      |
| R7               | Incentivizing Research Outputs: Recognize and reward significant contributions to research, including publications, patents, and collaborative projects.       |
| R8               | Research Infrastructure: Ensure adequate infrastructure, such as laboratories, equipment, and digital resources, are available to support research activities. |

**27.5. Roles and Responsibilities of the R&D Committee**

***1. Research Planning and Strategy Development***

> • **Develop Research Strategy:** Formulate long-term and short-term strategies for enhancing the research culture within the institution.
>
> • **Set Research Priorities:** Identify and prioritize key research areas that align with the institution's vision and industry trends.
>
> • **Promote Interdisciplinary Research:** Encourage interdisciplinary research collaborations among different departments and faculties to address complex challenges.

***2. Support for Research Projects***

> • **Guide and Support Faculty/Students:** Provide assistance and resources to faculty and students to design and develop research projects.
>
> • **Funding for Research:** Facilitate the identification and acquisition of research grants from government agencies, industry partners, and private organizations.
>
> • **Research Proposal Evaluation:** Assist in the review and evaluation of research proposals to ensure their feasibility, originality, and alignment with institutional objectives.

***3. Organizing Research Events and Activities***

> • **Organize Research Seminars, Workshops, and Conferences:** Host events to promote research activities, present findings, and encourage collaboration with external experts.
>
> • **Research Competitions and Challenges:** Organize competitions or challenges to encourage students and faculty to engage in innovative and applied research.
>
> • **Collaboration with Industry:** Foster partnerships between faculty/students and industry for applied research, internships, and industrial visits.

***4. Research Dissemination***

> • **Encourage Publication:** Encourage faculty and students to publish their research findings in high-impact journals, conferences, and other reputable platforms.
>
> • **Facilitate Networking:** Support networking opportunities at national and international conferences, symposiums, and research events.
>
> • **Promote Patents and Innovations:** Advocate for patent filing and intellectual property rights (IPR) processes to protect and commercialize innovative research outcomes.

***5. Mentorship and Capacity Building***

> • **Provide Research Training:** Organize workshops, training sessions, and seminars to improve the research skills of faculty and students, such as research methodologies, data analysis, and writing research papers.
>
> • **Encourage Collaboration:** Create a collaborative environment by encouraging faculty members and students to engage in joint research activities across departments and with external institutions.

***6. Monitoring and Evaluation of Research Activities***

> • **Research Progress Monitoring:** Regularly track and evaluate the progress of ongoing research projects and publications to ensure timely completion and quality.
>
> • **Assess Research Impact:** Evaluate the impact of research activities on the academic community, society, and industry, including citations, patents, and commercial applications.
>
> • **Research Performance Reviews:** Monitor and review the research performance of faculty and students, ensuring alignment with institutional goals and quality standards.

***7. Research Infrastructure and Resources***

> • **Ensure Availability of Research Facilities:** Ensure that faculty and students have access to the necessary infrastructure, labs, equipment, and resources required for research.
>
> • **Promote Access to Databases:** Ensure that researchers have access to databases, journals, e-books, and other essential research resources.
>
> • **Maintain Research Equipment:** Oversee the upkeep and availability of research equipment, ensuring they meet the needs of ongoing research.

***8. Collaboration with External Stakeholders***

> • **Engage with Industry Partners:** Develop partnerships with industries, research organizations, and other institutions to enhance the scope and quality of research.
>
> • **Collaborate with Government Bodies:** Build collaborations with government bodies, funding agencies, and regulatory authorities to support research initiatives.
>
> • **Institutional Networking:** Facilitate the institution's participation in national and international research collaborations and alliances.

***9. Promotion of Innovation***

> • **Support Innovation Initiatives:** Foster a culture of innovation by encouraging students and faculty to engage in projects that lead to tangible products, prototypes, or solutions.
>
> • **Encourage Entrepreneurial Research:** Promote the commercialization of research ideas through entrepreneurship and start-up ventures, including incubation support.

***10. Policy Development and Compliance***

> • **Research Ethics and Integrity:** Develop and enforce policies that ensure research integrity, ethics, and compliance with regulations, such as plagiarism policies and ethical research practices.
>
> • **Intellectual Property Rights (IPR):** Create and implement guidelines on intellectual property rights, including patenting, copyrights, and commercialization of research outputs.
>
> • **Ensure Legal Compliance:** Ensure that all research activities comply with legal requirements, institutional policies, and ethical standards.

***11. Reporting and Documentation***

> • **Maintain Research Documentation:** Keep proper records of research projects, publications, grants, collaborations, and patents, ensuring that documentation is accurate and up-to-date.
>
> • **Annual Research Reports:** Prepare and submit annual reports highlighting the institution's research activities, achievements, and future goals to the administration and other stakeholders.

**27.6. Meeting Schedule**

> • **Frequency:** Quarterly meetings (minimum) to plan and review research progress, fund allocations, and outcomes.
>
> • **Special Meetings:** Held when a specific research initiative, collaboration, or funding opportunity arises.
>
> • **Annual Review:** An annual review of the institution's research output and future directions, aligning with NBA and NAAC criteria.

**27.7. Documentation & Reporting for NBA/NAAC**

The R&D committee plays a significant role in maintaining the research standards of the institution and is key to NAAC and NBA accreditation. The documentation of research activities is essential for both accreditation processes, as they help assess the institution's innovation, research impact, and its contribution to society and industry.

**27.8. Documentation Managed by the R&D Committee**

***1. Research Policy Documents***

> • **Institutional Research Policy:** Defines the institution's approach to research, including objectives, funding mechanisms, and collaboration strategies.
>
> • **Research Ethics Policy:** Outlines ethical guidelines and standards for conducting research, ensuring integrity and adherence to ethical practices.
>
> • **Intellectual Property (IP) Policy:** Specifies the procedures for managing, protecting, and commercializing intellectual property created through research.

***2. Research Proposal Documents***

> • **Research Project Proposals:** Documents submitted by faculty or researchers for approval, including project objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes.
>
> • **Research Funding Applications:** Forms and documents for seeking external funding, including grants, scholarships, or government funding.
>
> • **Research Grants Approval Documents:** Official approval or rejection letters from funding agencies, along with any associated conditions or guidelines.
>
> • **Detailed Project Reports (DPRs):** Comprehensive reports on the progress of research projects, including results, challenges, and financial utilization.

***3. Research and Development Records***

> • **Research Progress Reports:** Periodic reports submitted by research teams, detailing milestones, results, and challenges faced during the research.
>
> • **Research Activity Logs:** A record of ongoing research activities, meetings, and decision-making processes.
>
> • **Publications and Research Output Records:** Documents containing records of publications, papers, books, or patents resulting from the institution's research.
>
> • **Conference and Workshop Proceedings:** Documentation of any research-related events organized by the institution, including conferences, seminars, and workshops.

***4. Research Fund Management Documents***

> • **Budget Allocation Documents:** Documents outlining the financial resources allocated to various research projects and their expenditure.
>
> • **Expense Reports:** Detailed records of how research funds were utilized, including receipts, invoices, and financial statements.
>
> • **Audits and Financial Statements:** Reports on the auditing of research funds, showing how funds were allocated and whether they were spent according to the approved budget.
>
> • **Disbursement Records:** Documents detailing the disbursement of research funds to individual researchers, research groups, or departments.

***5. Intellectual Property (IP) Documents***

> • **Patent Applications:** Documents related to the submission of patent applications based on research outcomes.
>
> • **IP Licensing Agreements:** Legal agreements between the institution and external parties for the commercialization or licensing of intellectual property.
>
> • **Copyright Registrations:** Documents regarding the registration of copyrights for research-based work such as papers, software, and creative works.
>
> • **Confidentiality Agreements:** Legal documents signed to protect the intellectual property and confidential information shared during research collaborations.

***6. Research Ethics and Compliance Documents***

> • **Ethics Approval Forms:** Documents that ensure research projects comply with institutional and governmental ethical guidelines, particularly for human or animal research.
>
> • **Informed Consent Forms:** Forms ensuring that participants in research studies understand the nature of the research and voluntarily agree to participate.
>
> • **Conflict of Interest Declarations:** Documents where researchers disclose any potential conflicts of interest that may affect their objectivity or research outcomes.
>
> • **Safety and Risk Assessment Documents:** Records related to the safety protocols and risk assessments for laboratory-based research, especially involving hazardous materials or equipment.

***7. Collaboration and Partnership Documents***

> • **Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs):** Agreements between the institution and external entities (such as industries, universities, or research bodies) for collaboration in research.
>
> • **Partnership and Collaboration Agreements:** Legal contracts that outline the terms of cooperation between the institution and external research partners.
>
> • **Industry Partnership Agreements:** Documents that outline the terms of cooperation for research and development with industrial partners, including commercialization and technology transfer.

***8. Faculty and Student Research Documentation***

> • **Researcher Profiles:** Documenting the research interests, publications, and achievements of faculty members and research scholars.
>
> • **Student Research Projects:** Reports and proposals related to student research projects, including undergraduate and postgraduate thesis work.
>
> • **Research Mentorship Records:** Documentation of mentoring arrangements between faculty and student researchers, detailing guidance and feedback provided throughout the research process.

***9. Research Training and Capacity Building Records***

> • **Training Program Materials:** Documents related to the organization and execution of research capacity-building workshops, seminars, and training programs.
>
> • **Certificates of Participation:** Proof of attendance and successful completion of training programs, workshops, and research skill development courses.

***10. Research Impact and Outcome Reports***

> • **Annual Research Reports:** Comprehensive reports summarizing the research activities, outputs, and impact of the institution over a given academic year.
>
> • **Research Impact Assessment:** Documents measuring the outcomes and societal impact of completed research projects, including citations, patents, products, and community benefits.
>
> • **Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):** Metrics used to assess the effectiveness and productivity of research activities in the institution.

***11. Research Review and Evaluation Documents***

> • **Peer Review Records:** Documentation of peer reviews for research proposals, publications, and research projects.
>
> • **Research Evaluation Forms:** Feedback forms and evaluation reports used to assess the quality, relevance, and potential impact of ongoing research projects.
>
> • **Project Completion Reports:** Final reports submitted upon the completion of research projects, detailing outcomes, findings, and recommendations for future research.

***12. Research Awards and Recognition Documents***

> • **Award Nominations and Certificates:** Documents related to nominations and awards for outstanding research contributions.
>
> • **Research Fellowships:** Records of research fellowships awarded to faculty, students, and research associates, including eligibility criteria and application processes.

**27.9. Roles and Responsibilities of the R&D Committee (Member-wise)**

***1. Chairperson of the R&D Committee***

> • **Overall Leadership and Guidance:** Provide leadership to the committee, ensuring the formulation and implementation of the institution's research strategy.
>
> • **Strategic Planning:** Lead the development of long-term and short-term research goals, strategies, and priorities.
>
> • **Policy Formulation:** Oversee the development of policies related to research funding, ethics, intellectual property, and compliance.
>
> • **Monitoring and Evaluation:** Ensure that research projects are aligned with institutional goals, are monitored effectively, and the progress is evaluated periodically.
>
> • **External Representation:** Represent the institution in external forums, conferences, and research collaborations with other institutions, industries, and research bodies.
>
> • **Approval of Research Proposals:** Oversee the approval process of major research projects and funding.

***2. Convener/Coordinator of the R&D Committee***

> • **Coordination and Management:** Act as the primary point of communication between the committee members and institutional stakeholders.
>
> • **Administrative Oversight:** Organize and facilitate committee meetings, ensure timely submission of reports, and ensure all documentation is well maintained.
>
> • **Implementation of Decisions:** Ensure that the decisions and recommendations of the committee are implemented effectively.
>
> • **Support to Researchers:** Assist faculty and students with administrative support for research proposals, including the collection of required documents and submissions to funding agencies.
>
> • **Data Collection and Reporting:** Collect data on ongoing research projects and prepare detailed reports for the committee, the administration, and external stakeholders.

***3. Faculty Members (Faculty in Charge of Research)***

> • **Research Guidance:** Provide technical expertise and mentorship to faculty and students involved in research projects.
>
> • **Monitoring Research Progress:** Ensure that ongoing research projects are progressing according to the timeline, quality, and objectives set.
>
> • **Research Proposal Writing:** Assist faculty and students in writing and submitting research proposals for external funding.
>
> • **Encourage Publications:** Motivate and support faculty and students to publish their research in reputed journals and conferences.
>
> • **Dissemination of Research Findings:** Organize seminars, workshops, and conferences to disseminate research findings and foster collaboration.
>
> • **Promote Interdisciplinary Research:** Encourage and facilitate collaboration across disciplines to solve real-world challenges.

***4. Member (Research Funding Expert)***

> • **Identification of Funding Sources:** Identify potential funding sources for research, including government bodies, industries, private foundations, and international agencies.
>
> • **Assistance in Funding Applications:** Assist in writing and submitting applications for research funding and grants.
>
> • **Tracking of Research Funds:** Monitor the utilization of research grants, ensuring that funds are used efficiently and according to the project's requirements.
>
> • **Financial Reporting:** Maintain financial documentation and report on the use of funds to the committee and relevant authorities.

***5. Member (Intellectual Property and Innovation Expert)***

> • **Intellectual Property Protection:** Guide researchers in the identification, protection, and commercialization of intellectual property (IP) arising from research projects.
>
> • **Patents and Licensing:** Facilitate the filing of patents, copyrights, and trademarks and the licensing of innovations to industry partners.
>
> • **Collaboration with Industry:** Promote collaboration between faculty members, students, and industry for joint research and commercialization of IP.
>
> • **Support Innovation:** Foster a culture of innovation by guiding the translation of research outcomes into viable products or services.

***6. Member (External Relations/Industry Liaison)***

> • **Industry Collaboration:** Establish and nurture relationships with industry partners to support applied research and provide students with opportunities for internships, industry visits, and hands-on projects.
>
> • **Collaborative Research:** Facilitate partnerships with industry for joint research projects, funded research, and technology transfer.
>
> • **Networking and Partnerships:** Represent the institution at national and international research forums, conferences, and industry events.
>
> • **Commercialization of Research:** Work with external stakeholders to commercialize promising research outcomes and innovations.

***7. Member (Student Representative)***

> • **Voice of the Students:** Represent the interests and concerns of students involved in research activities to the committee.
>
> • **Support for Student Research:** Encourage and assist students in taking part in research opportunities, guiding them in the research process and proposal writing.
>
> • **Organize Student Research Events:** Help organize student-centric research activities such as research colloquiums, student conferences, and research competitions.
>
> • **Promote Student Innovation:** Encourage student participation in innovation and entrepreneurial activities, including startup ideas and commercialization of student-led research.

***8. Member (Library and Resources Expert)***

> • **Resource Management:** Ensure that the institution's library and online resources are well-equipped and accessible for research purposes.
>
> • **Access to Databases:** Ensure researchers have access to a wide range of research databases, journals, and other academic resources required for high-quality research.
>
> • **Knowledge Sharing:** Encourage the use of open-source tools, research repositories, and academic networks for research dissemination.

***9. Member (Research Ethics and Compliance Officer)***

> • **Ensure Ethical Research Practices:** Develop and monitor the implementation of ethical guidelines for research, including human and animal rights, safety regulations, and environmental considerations.
>
> • **Review of Research Proposals:** Review research proposals for compliance with ethical guidelines, ensuring integrity in research methods, data collection, and analysis.
>
> • **Training on Research Ethics:** Organize workshops and training for faculty and students on ethical research practices, data privacy, and plagiarism.

***10. Member (Technical Support/Infrastructure Support)***

> • **Support Research Infrastructure:** Ensure that the necessary technical infrastructure, such as labs, equipment, and software, is available for research activities.
>
> • **Maintenance of Research Facilities:** Oversee the maintenance of research equipment and ensure its availability for faculty and students.
>
> • **Technology Integration:** Implement technology solutions that support data analysis, simulation, and visualization in research projects.

**27.13. Indirect Attainment Calculation for R&D Committee**

Indirect attainment refers to the assessment of how well the objectives of the Research and Development (R&D) Committee have been achieved, but through indirect or secondary means. This can be measured by evaluating the activities and results that indirectly reflect the success of the committee's actions. Below are steps to calculate the indirect attainment of the R&D Committee:

***Indirect Attainment Calculation Framework***

1\. **Define R&D Committee Objectives**

> o Promote research excellence among faculty and students.
>
> o Encourage interdisciplinary collaboration.
>
> o Secure external funding for research.
>
> o Enhance research quality through infrastructure and facilities.
>
> o Foster a culture of innovation and entrepreneurship.

2\. **Key Indicators for Indirect Attainment**

> o **Research Publications:** Number and quality of publications in reputed journals/conferences.
>
> o **Research Funding:** Total external funding received through grants, industry collaborations, and other sources.
>
> o **Patents/Intellectual Property (IP):** Number of patents filed or granted.
>
> o **Collaborations:** Number of collaborations with external institutions, industries, and international research bodies.
>
> o **Research Impact:** Number of citations, research-led innovations, or commercialized products.
>
> o **Research Infrastructure:** Improvement in research infrastructure (new labs, equipment, and resources).
>
> o **Awards/Recognitions:** Recognition of faculty and students for outstanding research achievements (research awards, fellowships, etc.).
>
> o **Participation in Research Events:** Number of research workshops, seminars, and conferences organized and attended.

3\. **Calculation Method for Indirect Attainment**

The indirect attainment can be calculated based on a scoring system for each key indicator. The scores represent the extent to which the committee's goals are achieved, even though these are indirectly linked to the committee's actions. Below is an example of how each key indicator could be quantified:

| **Indicator**                    | **Measurement**                                                                               | **Weight** | **Score (0-5)** | **Attainment (%)** |
|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|-----------------|--------------------|
| Research Publications            | Number of papers published in indexed journals/conferences.                                   | 20%        | 4               | 80%                |
| Research Funding                 | Total amount of external funding secured (e.g., grants, industry support).                    | 15%        | 3               | 45%                |
| Patents/IP                       | Number of patents filed or intellectual properties created.                                   | 10%        | 2               | 20%                |
| Collaborations                   | Number of collaborations with industry, other institutions, or international bodies.          | 15%        | 5               | 75%                |
| Research Infrastructure          | Enhancement in research facilities (e.g., labs, equipment).                                   | 10%        | 3               | 30%                |
| Awards/Recognitions              | Number of research-related awards or recognitions received by faculty or students.            | 10%        | 4               | 40%                |
| Participation in Research Events | Number of research seminars, workshops, and conferences held or attended by faculty/students. | 10%        | 3               | 30%                |
| Research Impact                  | Citations, innovation impact, or commercialization.                                           | 10%        | 4               | 40%                |

4\. **Total Indirect Attainment Calculation**

The total indirect attainment is calculated by multiplying the weight of each indicator by the score achieved and summing these results:

**Total Attainment (%) = ∑ (Weight × Score)**

For the example above:

Total Attainment (%) = (0.20×4) + (0.15×3) + (0.10×2) + (0.15×5) + (0.10×3) + (0.10×4) + (0.10×3) + (0.10×4) = 80 + 45 + 20 + 75 + 30 + 40 + 30 + 40 = 360%

**Total Indirect Attainment = 360% (out of a maximum of 400%).**

5\. **Interpretation of Results**

> o If the total indirect attainment percentage is above 75%, it indicates that the R&D Committee's efforts are highly effective in achieving its objectives through indirect means.
>
> o If the total indirect attainment is below 50%, it may indicate a need for improvement in key areas such as funding, collaborations, or research infrastructure.

***Example Calculation Breakdown***

In the above example, the R&D Committee has scored high in areas like Research Publications and Collaborations, but moderate or lower scores in areas such as Patents/IP and Research Infrastructure. This suggests that while the committee is effective in encouraging research and collaborations, there may be opportunities for growth in areas like intellectual property management or infrastructure enhancement.

This framework helps the committee assess its indirect impact and make data-driven decisions for improvement.

**27.16. Best Practices for an R&D Committee**

The Research and Development (R&D) Committee plays a pivotal role in promoting innovation, fostering research culture, and ensuring the sustainability and growth of research initiatives within an institution. Here are some Best Practices for an R&D Committee that can help ensure effective research management, collaboration, and innovation:

***1. Clear Research Strategy and Vision***

> • **Establish a Clear Research Policy:** Formulate and implement a clear research policy that outlines the vision, goals, and priorities of the institution's research activities.
>
> • **Align with National/Global Trends:** Ensure that the institution's research strategies align with national research priorities and global research trends in various fields.
>
> • **Periodic Strategic Review:** Conduct regular reviews of the research strategy to keep it updated with the latest advancements and emerging trends.

***2. Foster Collaborative Research***

> • **Interdisciplinary Collaboration:** Encourage research collaboration across departments and disciplines within the institution to foster innovation and address complex societal issues.
>
> • **Industry Partnerships:** Build strong partnerships with industry stakeholders to ensure that research outcomes are aligned with real-world challenges and can lead to commercial products, patents, or industry-based solutions.
>
> • **International Collaborations:** Foster research collaborations with international institutions to enhance the quality of research and encourage cross-border innovation.

***3. Support for Researchers***

> • **Seed Funding and Grants:** Provide seed funding, research grants, and fellowships to faculty members and students to kick-start new research initiatives and projects.
>
> • **Capacity Building:** Organize workshops, seminars, and training programs to enhance the research capabilities of faculty and students, particularly in areas such as grant writing, research methodology, and data analysis.
>
> • **Mentorship Programs:** Establish mentorship programs where experienced researchers guide and mentor young faculty members and PhD scholars.

***4. Promote Intellectual Property (IP) Management***

> • **IP Awareness and Training:** Conduct regular workshops on intellectual property rights (IPRs), patents, copyrights, and their significance in academic research.
>
> • **Patent Filing and Commercialization:** Encourage researchers to file patents for innovative solutions developed during their research and help them navigate the commercialization process.
>
> • **IP Support and Legal Assistance:** Provide institutional support for IP management, including legal advice on patent filing, copyright registration, and trademarking.

***5. Encourage Research Dissemination***

> • **Publications and Conferences:** Encourage faculty and students to publish their research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present them at national and international conferences.
>
> • **Institutional Repository:** Establish an open-access institutional repository to store and disseminate research papers, theses, and project reports generated by the institution's faculty and students.
>
> • **Collaborative Journals and Conferences:** Promote and organize conferences, symposia, and webinars to disseminate research findings, attract industry participation, and create networking opportunities.

***6. Data Management and Research Infrastructure***

> • **Provide Robust Research Infrastructure:** Ensure that the institution provides state-of-the-art research facilities, laboratories, and equipment for conducting high-quality research.
>
> • **Research Data Management:** Implement effective data management strategies to store, protect, and organize research data. Ensure compliance with ethical standards for data handling and privacy.
>
> • **Access to Digital Resources:** Provide access to a wide range of digital resources such as journals, e-books, databases, and research tools to support researchers in their work.

***7. Transparent Research Funding and Resource Allocation***

> • **Transparent Funding Process:** Implement transparent processes for research funding applications, evaluation, and disbursement. Ensure that the process is fair and based on merit.
>
> • **Effective Budget Monitoring:** Regularly monitor and evaluate the expenditure on research projects to ensure that funds are being utilized appropriately.
>
> • **Research Fund Sustainability:** Actively seek external research funding from government bodies, industry, and international agencies to ensure sustainable research support.

***8. Ethical Research Practices***

> • **Ethics Committees:** Set up an ethics committee to review and approve research proposals, especially those involving human subjects, animals, or sensitive data.
>
> • **Promote Ethical Research:** Foster a culture of ethical research by providing guidelines on integrity, avoiding plagiarism, and adhering to ethical standards in research.
>
> • **Confidentiality Agreements:** Implement confidentiality and non-disclosure agreements when dealing with sensitive information or proprietary research.

***9. Performance Evaluation and Impact Assessment***

> • **Regular Review of Research Projects:** Conduct periodic reviews of ongoing research projects to assess progress, outcomes, and impact.
>
> • **KPIs for Research Productivity:** Set clear Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to assess research productivity, such as the number of publications, patents, funded projects, and collaborations.
>
> • **Impact Assessment:** Evaluate the societal and industrial impact of the research conducted by the institution, including its contribution to solving real-world problems and addressing societal needs.

***10. Foster a Culture of Innovation***

> • **Encourage Entrepreneurial Thinking:** Promote an entrepreneurial mindset among researchers by offering support for research commercialization, startups, and spin-offs.
>
> • **Hackathons and Innovation Challenges:** Organize hackathons, innovation challenges, and ideation workshops to encourage students and faculty to think creatively and solve real-world problems.
>
> • **Innovation Cells:** Set up innovation cells or research incubators to support the commercialization of research outputs, providing mentorship, seed funding, and business development assistance.

***11. Recognition and Reward Systems***

> • **Award Research Excellence:** Set up awards and recognition programs for outstanding research contributions, including best publication awards, research fellowships, and innovation awards.
>
> • **Career Development Opportunities:** Provide career advancement opportunities for researchers through promotion tracks, sabbaticals, and funding for international collaborations.

***12. Community Engagement and Outreach***

> • **Community-Centric Research:** Encourage research that addresses local or global challenges, such as sustainability, healthcare, education, and poverty alleviation.
>
> • **Public Outreach:** Organize public seminars, webinars, and exhibitions to showcase the research being conducted and to engage the community with the institution's research outcomes.
>
> • **Research for Societal Development:** Align research projects with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to contribute to global societal development.

**27.17. Conclusion**

The Research and Development Committee is at the heart of any institution striving for excellence in higher education. By promoting research, innovation, and industry collaboration, the committee significantly contributes to the academic growth and visibility of the institution. It ensures that the institution remains aligned with the requirements of accrediting bodies like NBA and NAAC, improving its research output, quality, and overall institutional effectiveness. By focusing on faculty and student development, securing funding, and fostering international collaborations, the committee directly impacts the institution's ability to provide high-quality education and maintain its accreditation status.

**28. Website/ICT/ECAP/IT INFRASTRUCTURE /Self (or) e-learning Committee**

**28.1. Objective**

This committee ensures the development, maintenance, and effective use of the institution's digital infrastructure to support teaching-learning, administration, communication, and self-learning. It plays a key role in enhancing digital literacy, supporting blended learning models, maintaining online academic records, and ensuring seamless access to e-resources.

**28.2. Scope of the Committee**

> • Maintenance and regular updating of the institutional website
>
> • Implementation and monitoring of ICT-enabled teaching-learning practices
>
> • Administration and user support for ECAP (ERP/Academic Management Systems)
>
> • Overseeing IT infrastructure across the campus including labs, network, and digital classrooms
>
> • Promotion of e-learning tools, MOOCs (NPTEL, SWAYAM, Coursera, etc.), and LMS platforms (Moodle, Google Classroom)
>
> • Ensuring data security, backups, and policy compliance
>
> • Supporting documentation and evidence preparation for NBA and NAAC

**28.3. Committee Composition**

| **Role**                    | **Responsibility**                                                                |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Chairperson                 | Senior faculty/HoD/Dean in charge of Digital Learning or ICT                      |
| Technical Coordinator       | IT support officer or System Administrator                                        |
| Web Administrator           | Person responsible for updating and maintaining the institutional website         |
| Faculty Members (Dept-wise) | Represent each department for ICT and digital learning support                    |
| LMS/MOOCs Coordinators      | Faculty guiding and monitoring SWAYAM/NPTEL/Coursera enrollment and certification |
| Student Representatives     | Collect feedback and help bridge the digital gap among peers                      |

**28.4. Functions & Responsibilities**

1\. **Website Management**

> o Maintain an up-to-date institutional website containing:
>
> o Vision, Mission, PEOs, POs, COs
>
> o Faculty and staff profiles
>
> o Academic calendar, schedules, notices
>
> o NBA/NAAC mandatory disclosures and reports
>
> o Publish minutes of meetings, policies, placement details, and student achievements
>
> o Ensure mobile responsiveness and accessibility

2\. **ICT Enablement**

> o Equip classrooms with smart boards, projectors, and internet access
>
> o Provide training on the use of digital tools: Zoom, MS Teams, Google Meet, etc.
>
> o Promote ICT-based evaluation tools like online quizzes, forms, LMS-based assessments

3\. **ERP System**

> o Maintain and manage platforms like ECAP (Educational & Curriculum Automation Platform), or any ERP software used for:
>
> o Attendance monitoring
>
> o Internal marks, assignments
>
> o Faculty workload, time table
>
> o Student progression and alumni records
>
> o Support administrative automation

4\. **e-Learning and Self-Learning**

> o Promote enrollment and completion of MOOCs (NPTEL/SWAYAM/Coursera)
>
> o Monitor progress and issue certificates
>
> o Encourage flipped classroom models and blended learning approaches
>
> o Facilitate access to digital libraries like DELNET, NDLI, IEEE, etc.

5\. **IT Infrastructure Management**

> o Maintain the computer labs, network infrastructure, servers, Wi-Fi, firewall, CCTV
>
> o Ensure proper licensing of software and security of institutional data
>
> o Conduct regular audits of IT assets

**28.5. Support for NBA and NAAC Documentation**

**Maintain:**

> • CO-PO Mapping via ECAP or LMS
>
> • ICT-enhanced lesson plans
>
> • List of online certification courses completed
>
> • Usage analytics of LMS and MOOCs
>
> • Online records of attendance, marks, academic calendar

**28.6. Meeting Frequency**

> • At least once every semester
>
> • Additional meetings before NBA/NAAC peer visits
>
> • Special meetings for infrastructure upgrades or digital issues

**28.7. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

| **KPI**                      | **Target/Benchmark**                                           |
|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| Website Update Frequency     | At least bi-weekly updates                                     |
| Smart Classrooms ICT-enabled | ≥ 80% of classrooms                                            |

A strong Website & ICT system not only supports academics but also boosts the institution's image, rankings, and accreditation outcomes.

> • Implementation of Digital Feedback System through ERP

>

**28.13. Conclusion**

The Website/ICT/ECAP/IT Infrastructure/Self or e-Learning Committee plays a pivotal role in transforming a traditional campus into a digitally competent institution. Its efforts are critical for demonstrating digital readiness, enhancing teaching-learning quality, enabling transparency in operations, and fulfilling accreditation benchmarks for NBA and NAAC. A strong digital infrastructure not only supports academic excellence but also strengthens institutional branding and stakeholder satisfaction.

**29. Transport Committee**

**29.1. Objective**

The **Transport Committee** is constituted to ensure safe, efficient, and timely transportation services for students, faculty, and staff. It manages the operations, maintenance, scheduling, grievance handling, and continual improvement of institutional transport services. Its functioning supports inclusivity, punctuality, and overall student support services.

**29.2. Scope of the Committee**

> • Oversee the planning, operation, and logistics of the institution's transport services.
>
> • Ensure the safety and comfort of commuting students and staff.
>
> • Maintain a regular schedule of buses covering various locations.
>
> • Address transportation-related grievances.
>
> • Ensure compliance with transport-related regulatory norms and safety standards.

**29.3. Functions of the Transport Committee**

1\. **Transport Planning & Management**

> o Plan and schedule bus routes and timings to ensure safe and timely transportation of students and staff.

2\. **Vehicle Allocation**

> o Allocate buses for regular commutes, special academic events, field visits, industrial tours, and examinations.

3\. **Supervision of Vehicle Maintenance**

> o Monitor the regular servicing, repair, and fitness certification of all institutional vehicles.

4\. **Driver Coordination**

> o Supervise the duties and punctuality of drivers and support staff; ensure their adherence to safety standards.

5\. **Compliance with Safety Norms**

> o Ensure compliance with road safety rules, insurance regulations, and RTO guidelines.

6\. **Emergency Management**

> o Coordinate emergency response mechanisms in case of breakdowns, accidents, or natural calamities.

7\. **Student/Staff Communication**

> o Act as a liaison between the transport users (students/staff) and the administration for addressing concerns or requests.

8\. **Transport Fee Regulation (if applicable)**

> o Recommend or revise transport fees in consultation with management and ensure transparent fee collection.

9\. **Monitoring Transport Discipline**

> o Enforce discipline and decorum in the use of transport facilities; handle misuse or misconduct.

10\. **Feedback and Improvement**

> o Conduct surveys or feedback drives to improve service quality and address user grievances.

11\. **Record Maintenance**

> o Maintain updated records of bus usage, driver logs, fuel consumption, repairs, and expenses.

12\. **Special Event Planning**

> o Make transport arrangements for extracurricular activities, competitions, fests, and placement drives.

**29.4. Composition of the Transport Committee**

| **Designation**               | **Role** |
|-------------------------------|----------|
| Principal / Dean              | Chair    |
| Transport Officer / In-Charge | Member   |
| Senior Faculty Members        | Member   |
| Admin/HR Representative       | Member   |
| Driver Representative         | Member   |
| Student Representatives       | Member   |

**29.5. Responsibilities**

| **Role**                      | **Responsibility**                           |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| Principal / Dean (Chair)      | Overall policy decisions, final approvals    |
| Transport Officer / In-Charge | Daily coordination and operations            |
| Senior Faculty Members        | Represent academic needs and class schedules |
| Admin/HR Representative       | Coordination of staff transportation         |
| Driver Representative         | Operational and route-level insights         |
| Student Representatives       | Feedback and grievance representation        |

1\. **Route Planning & Scheduling**

> o Plan optimal bus routes and timings to cover maximum student/staff residences.
>
> o Align transport schedules with academic calendars and exam timetables.
>
> o Modify routes based on student population changes or safety concerns.

2\. **Safety & Compliance**

> o Ensure that all institutional vehicles comply with government safety norms, insurance, and emissions regulations.
>
> o Install CCTV, GPS, speed governors, and first-aid kits in buses.
>
> o Periodic safety audits and training for drivers and transport staff.

3\. **Maintenance & Monitoring**

> o Maintain logbooks for each vehicle.
>
> o Schedule regular preventive maintenance, emission checks, and cleanliness.
>
> o Maintain fuel usage records and cost optimization strategies.

4\. **Grievance Redressal**

> o Provide a channel (suggestion box, Google Form, ECAP, or email) to report issues related to:
>
> o Bus delays
>
> o Misconduct or safety concerns
>
> o Overcrowding or breakdowns
>
> o Conduct investigations and take timely corrective action.

**29.6. Support for Events & Emergencies**

> • Arrange transportation for:
>
> o Industrial visits
>
> o Sports and cultural events
>
> o Campus recruitment drives
>
> o Emergency evacuations or medical needs

**29.7. Digital Integration**

> • Use ERP or mobile app for:
>
> o Bus tracking and alerts
>
> o Route and schedule updates
>
> o Student transport registration and pass issuance

**29.8. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

| **Indicator**                  | **Target**                        |
|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Student Transport Satisfaction | ≥ 90% (via feedback survey)       |
| Route Optimization             | Yearly review and reconfiguration |
| Bus Breakdown Frequency        | \< 1 breakdown/month per bus      |
| Accident-Free Operation        | Zero-accident target annually     |
| Emergency Preparedness Drills  | At least one drill per semester   |

**29.9. Contribution to NBA Criteria**

| **NBA Criterion**                                | **Transport Committee Role**                                |
|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| NBA Criterion 2 – Teaching-Learning Process      | Ensures timely access to classes and labs                   |
| NBA Criterion 6 – Facilities & Technical Support | Contributes to physical facility and support infrastructure |
| NBA Criterion 8 – First-Year Students            | Reduces stress for freshers commuting from far-off places   |

**29.10. Contribution to NAAC Criteria**

**29.12. Documentation Maintained by Transport Committee**

1\. **Transport Request Forms:**

> o Forms submitted by departments, faculty, or students to request transportation services for events, field trips, or other academic-related activities.

2\. **Vehicle Maintenance Logs:**

> o Detailed records of vehicle inspections, repairs, servicing, and parts replacements. This includes dates of service, issues identified, actions taken, and costs incurred.

3\. **Driver Logs:**

> o Logs maintained for each driver, including work hours, routes driven, and any incidents or special observations during the transport.

4\. **Fleet Inventory List:**

> o An inventory list that includes all vehicles in the transport fleet with details like make, model, year of manufacture, registration numbers, and the status of each vehicle.

5\. **Fuel Consumption Records:**

> o Records of fuel used by each vehicle, including the date, mileage, and fuel consumption for monitoring and analysis of operational costs.

6\. **Vehicle Insurance Documents:**

> o Copies of insurance policies for each vehicle in the fleet, along with renewal dates and insurance coverage details.

7\. **Transport Budget Records:**

> o Documents detailing the annual budget allocation for transport services, expenses incurred, and any adjustments made throughout the year.

8\. **Student and Staff Transport Feedback:**

> o Feedback forms or surveys collected from students, staff, and faculty regarding the transport services, to ensure quality improvement and satisfaction.

9\. **Accident and Incident Reports:**

> o Documentation of any accidents or incidents involving the transport fleet, including details of the event, the investigation, actions taken, and follow-up procedures.

10\. **Transport Policies and Procedures:**

> o Official documents outlining the guidelines, rules, and procedures for using the transport services, including codes of conduct for drivers, safety measures, and emergency protocols.

11\. **Transport Service Contracts:**

> o Contracts and agreements with third-party vendors, if applicable, for services such as vehicle rentals, drivers, or outsourced maintenance.

12\. **Monthly and Annual Transport Reports:**

> o Monthly performance and service reports, including statistics like the number of trips, fuel consumption, feedback analysis, and other relevant data. Annual reports summarizing the year's transport activities, budget, and performance evaluation.

13\. **Transport Service Usage Records:**

> o Logs of transport service requests, including details of the trip (e.g., destination, date, participants, purpose) and the vehicle assigned.

14\. **Training and Certification Records:**

> o Documentation related to driver training programs, including attendance records, course content, and certifications earned.

15\. **Safety Inspection Checklists:**

> o Checklists used for regular safety inspections of vehicles, covering areas such as tires, brakes, lights, engine, and emergency equipment.

16\. **Student and Faculty Transport Allocation Records:**

> o Records indicating how transport services are allocated to students, faculty, and staff, with details on routes, timings, and special requests.

17\. **Government Regulations and Compliance Documents:**

> o Documents ensuring that the transport services are compliant with local, state, or national laws and regulations related to public transport, road safety, and environmental standards.

18\. **Emergency Response Plans:**

> o Documentation of emergency protocols in case of an accident or breakdown, including contact information, steps to follow, and safety procedures.

**29.13. Events / Activities Organized by Transport Committee**

| **S.No** | **Event/Activity**                             | **Purpose/Description**                                                                     |
|----------|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Transport Schedule Planning                    | Periodic planning of bus routes, timings, and stoppages to accommodate student/staff needs. |
| 2        | Transport Orientation for Freshers             | Introduction to bus facilities, rules, ID verification, and route details.                  |

>

>
> • **Safety Focus:** Regular drills and awareness campaigns to ensure safety standards are met.

**29.15. Best Practices of Transport Committee**

1\. **Regular Vehicle Maintenance and Inspection:**

> o Schedule regular maintenance checks for all vehicles in the fleet to ensure they are in safe operating condition. Conduct safety inspections periodically and keep detailed records of repairs and servicing.
>
> o Implement a preventive maintenance program to address potential issues before they arise, reducing the likelihood of breakdowns.

2\. **Clear and Transparent Transport Policies:**

> o Develop and communicate clear transport policies for students, faculty, and staff, including usage rules, booking procedures, and guidelines for behavior on the bus.
>
> o Ensure transparency in how transport resources are allocated and prioritize safety, efficiency, and fairness.

3\. **Driver Training and Certification:**

> o Provide ongoing training programs for drivers on safe driving practices, road safety laws, and customer service.
>
> o Ensure drivers are certified and comply with health checks, and that they are trained to handle emergency situations and basic first aid.

4\. **Efficient Scheduling and Route Management:**

> o Optimize vehicle routes to ensure efficient time management, reduce delays, and minimize fuel consumption.
>
> o Ensure that transport services meet the needs of both academic activities and extra-curricular events. Use scheduling software or apps for effective route planning and monitoring.

5\. **Student and Staff Feedback Collection:**

> o Regularly gather feedback from students and staff regarding transport services to identify areas for improvement. Implement regular surveys or conduct informal sessions for suggestions.
>
> o Address concerns such as punctuality, safety, and comfort promptly.

6\. **Emergency Response Planning:**

> o Develop a well-documented emergency response plan for accidents or breakdowns, which includes clear protocols for both drivers and passengers.
>
> o Ensure that first-aid kits and necessary emergency tools are available in all vehicles.

7\. **Eco-friendly Practices:**

> o Promote sustainability by adopting eco-friendly practices like using fuel-efficient vehicles, maintaining proper tire pressure to reduce fuel consumption, and exploring the use of electric vehicles or hybrid buses where feasible.
>
> o Implement green driving techniques such as avoiding idling and smooth acceleration to reduce emissions.

8\. **Timely Communication and Updates:**

> o Maintain effective communication with all users of the transport system regarding scheduling, route changes, or any unexpected delays. Utilize SMS notifications, emails, or a dedicated mobile app for real-time updates.
>
> o Have a 24/7 contact system for emergency communication or for resolving issues related to transport services.

9\. **Safety and Security Protocols:**

> o Establish and enforce strict safety standards, including seatbelts, driver training, and vehicle inspections, to ensure that the transport system is safe for all users.
>
> o Provide security staff for high-demand routes during peak hours or special events to ensure the safety of passengers and prevent incidents.

10\. **Usage Monitoring and Data Analysis:**

> o Utilize data analytics to track transport usage patterns, fuel consumption, and vehicle performance. This information can help the committee optimize operations and make data-driven decisions.
>
> o Keep a detailed log of transport activities and make regular assessments to identify cost-saving opportunities, such as reducing underutilized routes or combining trips.

11\. **Collaboration with Local Authorities:**

> o Maintain a good working relationship with local transportation authorities to ensure compliance with regulations and to address road safety issues promptly.
>
> o Work with law enforcement to ensure the safe travel of passengers and to prevent accidents on the road.

12\. **Innovative Technology Integration:**

> o Implement smart technology solutions like GPS tracking, vehicle booking systems, and traffic monitoring tools to enhance the overall efficiency of the transport system.
>
> o Consider creating an online portal or app for students and staff to book transport services, view schedules, track vehicles in real-time, and provide feedback.

13\. **Cultural Sensitivity and Inclusivity:**

> o Ensure that the transport system accommodates the needs of diverse student populations, including students with disabilities. Provide wheelchair-accessible vehicles and other supportive services as needed.
>
> o Organize awareness programs that emphasize respectful behavior towards fellow passengers, creating an inclusive and respectful environment for all.

14\. **Sustainability and Environmental Impact:**

> o Adopt practices that minimize the environmental impact of transport services, such as carpooling for faculty and staff, fuel-efficient vehicle fleets, and sustainable vehicle disposal practices.
>
> o Work towards creating low-emission transport options, such as electric buses, to align with environmental goals.

15\. **Promoting Transport as a Shared Resource:**

> o Encourage students and staff to use the transport system in a shared manner, where feasible, to reduce the overall demand for individual transport and decrease the number of vehicles on campus.
>
> o Explore options such as carpooling or shuttle services to reduce congestion and minimize costs.

**29.16. Conclusion**

The Transport Committee plays a crucial role in enhancing the physical access of students and staff to institutional services. It is instrumental in demonstrating student-friendly infrastructure under NBA and NAAC accreditation. A well-functioning transport system not only improves attendance and punctuality but also supports the safety and overall well-being of the campus community.

**30. Renewable Energy Committee**

**30.1. Objective**

The Renewable Energy Committee is formed to initiate, monitor, and promote sustainable energy practices on campus by integrating renewable energy systems such as solar, wind, and biogas. It also encourages research, awareness, and training in green energy practices among students and staff.

This committee plays a pivotal role in fostering institutional commitment toward environmental sustainability—a key focus of NAAC and NBA.

**30.2. Scope of the Committee**

> • Assess energy consumption and promote the adoption of renewable sources.
>
> • Plan and implement renewable energy installations.
>
> • Monitor energy usage, savings, and carbon footprint reduction.
>
> • Educate and involve students and faculty in sustainability projects.
>
> • Collaborate with government and non-government organizations for renewable energy initiatives.

**30.3. Composition of the Committee**

| **Designation**                 | **Role**    |
|---------------------------------|-------------|
| Principal / Dean                | Chairperson |
| Faculty Members (Energy/EEE/ME) | Member      |
| Estate / Infrastructure Manager | Member      |
| Student Representatives         | Member      |
| External Expert (optional)      | Member      |

**30.4. Functions & Responsibilities**

1\. **Energy Audit and Monitoring**

> o Conduct baseline energy audits of institutional consumption.
>
> o Identify areas where energy efficiency can be improved.
>
> o Monitor renewable energy production and usage.

2\. **Project Planning and Implementation**

> o Install solar panels on rooftops, street lighting, water heating systems, etc.
>
> o Explore wind, biogas, or hybrid systems based on feasibility.
>
> o Liaise with vendors, state renewable energy corporations, and utility boards.

3\. **Awareness and Outreach**

> o Conduct workshops, seminars, and exhibitions on renewable energy.
>
> o Organize student-led awareness campaigns on energy conservation.
>
> o Celebrate National Energy Conservation Day and Earth Day with events.

4\. **Student Projects & Research Support**

> o Encourage students to take up renewable energy-based projects.
>
> o Provide mentorship and support for grant proposals (e.g., AICTE, DST).
>
> o Maintain documentation for use in project-based learning and innovation contests.

5\. **Policy Compliance and Reporting**

> o Ensure alignment with state/central policies on energy efficiency.
>
> o Prepare reports for NBA/NAAC, including power savings and sustainability metrics.
>
> o Maintain documentation such as solar power generation logs, maintenance schedules, etc.
