**30.12. Renewable Energy Committee mapping to SDG**

The Renewable Energy Committee in a higher educational institution plays a vital role in promoting sustainability, energy efficiency, and environmental responsibility. Its actions directly contribute to the achievement of various Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) set by the United Nations. Below is a mapping of the committee's initiatives to the relevant SDGs:

1\. **SDG 7: Affordable and Clean Energy**

> **Objective:** Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all.
>
> **Mapping:** The Renewable Energy Committee's installation of solar panels, wind turbines, and other renewable energy systems directly supports SDG 7. Their efforts in promoting energy efficiency and the use of renewable energy sources help the institution reduce its dependence on non-renewable sources and contribute to cleaner energy production.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Installation of solar power systems on campus.
>
> o Use of solar water heating systems.
>
> o Organizing workshops on renewable energy technologies.

2\. **SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure**

> **Objective:** Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization, and foster innovation.
>
> **Mapping:** The committee's work in integrating renewable energy technologies into campus infrastructure contributes to this SDG. By supporting innovation in renewable energy systems and infrastructure, such as smart grids and energy-efficient buildings, the committee encourages sustainable industrial practices and technological advancements.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Encouraging sustainable building designs with energy-efficient systems.
>
> o Collaboration with industry partners for innovation in renewable energy.

3\. **SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production**

> **Objective:** Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns.
>
> **Mapping:** The Renewable Energy Committee helps achieve SDG 12 by promoting energy conservation, reducing waste, and advocating for sustainable energy use on campus. Their efforts in reducing the carbon footprint and adopting circular economy principles align with responsible consumption practices.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Implementation of energy-saving practices on campus.
>
> o Encouraging recycling and reducing energy waste through awareness campaigns.

4\. **SDG 13: Climate Action**

> **Objective:** Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.
>
> **Mapping:** The committee's core mission is directly aligned with SDG 13, as renewable energy adoption helps mitigate climate change by reducing carbon emissions. Their actions in transitioning to clean energy sources reduce the institution's overall greenhouse gas emissions and set an example for other institutions.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Installation of solar panels and wind turbines to reduce CO2 emissions.
>
> o Promoting green energy solutions and climate change awareness among students and faculty.
>
> o Organizing events and campaigns to highlight the importance of renewable energy in climate change mitigation.

5\. **SDG 4: Quality Education**

> **Objective:** Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.
>
> **Mapping:** Through educational programs, awareness campaigns, and research initiatives on renewable energy, the committee supports SDG 4 by incorporating sustainability and energy literacy into the academic curriculum. This equips students with the knowledge and skills required for a green economy.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Integrating renewable energy concepts into academic programs and research.
>
> o Offering training sessions and workshops on renewable energy technologies.

6\. **SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities**

> **Objective:** Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable.
>
> **Mapping:** The committee's work in promoting renewable energy on campus aligns with SDG 11 by creating a more sustainable and resilient campus. Through projects like smart energy management systems and sustainable building designs, the committee contributes to the long-term sustainability of the institution's infrastructure.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Development of sustainable energy infrastructure on campus.
>
> o Promoting green transportation options like electric vehicle charging stations.

7\. **SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals**

> **Objective:** Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development.
>
> **Mapping:** The Renewable Energy Committee fosters partnerships with local governments, industry leaders, and experts in the renewable energy sector to advance the institution's sustainability goals. These collaborations ensure that the institution stays aligned with global sustainable development targets and facilitates the exchange of knowledge and resources.
>
> **Activities:**
>
> o Partnering with industry stakeholders for renewable energy research and projects.
>
> o Collaboration with local authorities and organizations to enhance campus sustainability.

**30.13. Best Practices of the Renewable Energy Committee**

The Renewable Energy Committee in an institution plays a key role in promoting sustainability, reducing the carbon footprint, and fostering an eco-friendly environment on campus. Here are some best practices that the committee can follow to achieve these objectives effectively:

1\. **Conducting Energy Audits**

> **Best Practice:** Regularly conduct comprehensive energy audits of campus buildings and facilities.
>
> **Purpose:** Identify areas of high energy consumption and pinpoint opportunities for energy conservation.
>
> **Action:** Work with experts to assess energy usage patterns, recommend improvements, and track progress.

2\. **Installation of Renewable Energy Systems**

> **Best Practice:** Advocate for and oversee the installation of renewable energy systems such as solar panels, wind turbines, and geothermal systems.
>
> **Purpose:** Reduce reliance on non-renewable energy sources and contribute to the institution's sustainability goals.
>
> **Action:** Ensure that renewable systems are installed in key areas of the campus, including rooftops, parking areas, and open spaces.

3\. **Awareness and Education Programs**

> **Best Practice:** Organize awareness campaigns, workshops, and training programs for students, faculty, and staff on the importance of renewable energy and energy conservation.
>
> **Purpose:** Foster a culture of sustainability and energy efficiency on campus.
>
> **Action:** Develop interactive programs, including lectures, seminars, and hands-on workshops with renewable energy experts.

4\. **Green Campus Initiatives**

> **Best Practice:** Promote green campus initiatives that encourage the use of renewable energy and sustainability practices in all areas.
>
> **Purpose:** Align the campus environment with eco-friendly principles, reducing environmental impact.
>
> **Action:** Encourage the use of solar-powered lights, energy-efficient appliances, and rainwater harvesting systems.

5\. **Collaboration with Industry and External Experts**

> **Best Practice:** Collaborate with industry leaders, government bodies, and external experts on renewable energy projects.
>
> **Purpose:** Stay updated on the latest developments in renewable energy technology and best practices.
>
> **Action:** Establish partnerships for research, knowledge sharing, and internships for students in renewable energy fields.

6\. **Monitoring and Reporting Energy Usage**

> **Best Practice:** Implement a system for continuous monitoring and reporting of energy consumption across campus.
>
> **Purpose:** Track the effectiveness of renewable energy systems and identify areas for improvement.
>
> **Action:** Use smart meters and energy management systems to collect data and create periodic reports for the administration.

7\. **Sustainable Campus Design**

> **Best Practice:** Promote energy-efficient building designs that incorporate passive solar heating, natural ventilation, and the use of sustainable materials.
>
> **Purpose:** Reduce overall energy consumption while ensuring the campus infrastructure is eco-friendly.
>
> **Action:** Work closely with architects and planners to integrate renewable energy solutions into new building projects.

8\. **Encouraging the Use of Electric Vehicles (EVs)**

> **Best Practice:** Set up electric vehicle charging stations and promote the use of electric vehicles on campus.
>
> **Purpose:** Encourage the use of sustainable transportation and reduce the carbon emissions from the institution's fleet.
>
> **Action:** Install EV charging stations at strategic locations across the campus and offer incentives for students and staff to use electric vehicles.

9\. **Solar Water Heating Systems**

> **Best Practice:** Install solar water heating systems in hostels, staff quarters, and other campus buildings.
>
> **Purpose:** Reduce the consumption of conventional energy for water heating, especially in large institutional settings.
>
> **Action:** Collaborate with solar energy vendors for the installation and maintenance of efficient solar water heaters.

10\. **Integrating Renewable Energy into Curriculum**

> **Best Practice:** Integrate renewable energy topics into the academic curriculum, particularly in engineering, environmental science, and related programs.
>
> **Purpose:** Equip students with the knowledge and skills to contribute to the renewable energy sector.
>
> **Action:** Develop courses, research projects, and internships focused on renewable energy technologies and sustainability practices.

11\. **Incentivizing Energy Conservation Efforts**

> **Best Practice:** Offer incentives such as awards or recognition for departments, students, and faculty who demonstrate energy conservation efforts or innovations in renewable energy.
>
> **Purpose:** Encourage active participation in renewable energy initiatives and energy conservation on campus.
>
> **Action:** Establish a reward system for energy-efficient practices, such as energy-efficient equipment use, reducing waste, and innovative renewable energy projects.

12\. **Establishing a Renewable Energy Fund**

> **Best Practice:** Set up a fund to support renewable energy projects and research on campus.
>
> **Purpose:** Ensure that renewable energy projects are adequately funded and can be sustained long-term.
>
> **Action:** Secure funding from alumni, government grants, and industry collaborations to support the development of renewable energy infrastructure.

13\. **Promoting Green Certifications**

> **Best Practice:** Pursue green certifications such as LEED (Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design) for campus buildings.
>
> **Purpose:** Showcase the institution's commitment to sustainability and renewable energy.
>
> **Action:** Work with certification bodies to achieve and maintain green building certifications for campus infrastructure.

14\. **Research and Innovation in Renewable Energy**

> **Best Practice:** Foster research and innovation in renewable energy technologies within the institution.
>
> **Purpose:** Contribute to the global body of knowledge on renewable energy and climate change mitigation.
>
> **Action:** Support faculty and students in renewable energy research through grants, collaboration with research organizations, and participation in innovation competitions.

15\. **Regular Review and Updates on Renewable Energy Goals**

> **Best Practice:** Review the institution's renewable energy goals and performance regularly and set new targets as needed.
>
> **Purpose:** Ensure that the institution remains on track to meet sustainability targets and adapts to new developments in renewable energy.
>
> **Action:** Organize annual reviews of renewable energy goals, with feedback from students, staff, and external stakeholders.

**30.14. Conclusion**

By implementing these best practices, the Renewable Energy Committee can create a significant impact on the institution's sustainability efforts. These practices not only promote the use of renewable energy but also foster an institutional culture of environmental responsibility and innovation.

**31. Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee**

**31.1. Purpose**

The Students Welfare Committee is established to ensure the holistic development, welfare, and support of students throughout their academic journey. It works proactively to create a safe, inclusive, and nurturing environment for students, addressing their academic, personal, and extracurricular needs.

**31.2. Key Objectives**

1\. Ensure student support services are effective and accessible.

2\. Facilitate the implementation of student-centric policies.

3\. Promote student engagement in co-curricular and extracurricular activities.

4\. Handle student grievances related to general welfare, infrastructure, and peer interactions.

5\. Coordinate with other student-related bodies (clubs, cells, grievance committees).

6\. Identify and assist students facing academic, financial, or psychological challenges.

**31.3. Functions of Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee**

The Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee plays a crucial role in addressing the needs of students belonging to Scheduled Tribes (ST), Scheduled Castes (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), and other marginalized communities within an institution. Its functions focus on promoting an inclusive environment, ensuring equal opportunities, and addressing any specific challenges faced by these students. Below are the key functions of this committee:

| **Function**                                       | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                            |
|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1\. Promote Equal Opportunities                    | Ensure that students from ST, SC, and OBC backgrounds have equal access to all academic, extracurricular, and administrative opportunities within the institution.                         |
| 2\. Addressing Grievances                          | Establish a grievance redressal mechanism for students belonging to ST, SC, and OBC categories, addressing any issues related to discrimination, harassment, or unequal treatment.         |
| 3\. Scholarships and Financial Assistance          | Oversee the distribution of government and institutional scholarships, fellowships, and financial aid to ST, SC, and OBC students, ensuring they are aware of available financial support. |
| 4\. Organizing Awareness Programs                  | Organize workshops, seminars, and awareness programs on the rights, privileges, and schemes available for ST, SC, and OBC students to empower them.                                        |
| 5\. Mentorship Counseling                          | Provide mentorship, career counseling, and psychological support to ST, SC, and OBC students, helping them overcome any academic or personal challenges.                                   |
| 6\. Academic Programs                              | Facilitate special academic support programs such as remedial coaching, tutorial sessions, and extra study hours for ST, SC, and OBC students who may need additional assistance.          |
| 7\. Promote Inclusivity                            | Organize cultural events, festivals, and celebrations that highlight the diversity and heritage of ST, SC, and OBC communities to foster inclusivity and unity.                            |
| 8\. Monitor Implementation of Reservation Policies | Ensure that reservation policies for admission, scholarships, and other institutional benefits are implemented in compliance with government regulations.                                  |
| 9\. Assist in Placement Support                    | Help ST, SC, and OBC students with placement opportunities, career fairs, and internships, ensuring they have the same access to career development resources.                             |
| 10\. Health and Well-being Support                 | Address the health and well-being concerns of ST, SC, and OBC students by ensuring access to health services, counseling, and other well-being programs.                                   |
| 11\. Identify and Support Underprivileged Students | Identify students who face socio-economic disadvantages and provide additional support, such as mentoring, financial aid, or personal counseling.                                          |
| 12\. Collaboration with External Bodies            | Liaise with government and non-governmental organizations to help ST, SC, and OBC students access schemes, resources, and support systems outside the institution.                         |
| 13\. Conduct Surveys and Feedback                  | Regularly collect feedback from ST, SC, and OBC students on the issues they face and evaluate the effectiveness of welfare programs, adjusting policies accordingly.                       |
| 14\. Encourage Leadership and Representation       | Promote leadership skills and representation among ST, SC, and OBC students through leadership training programs, student body representation, and other empowering activities.            |

**Additional Functions:**

> • Conducting Remedial Classes: Special focus on the academic improvement of ST, SC, and OBC students, especially those facing difficulties in mainstream education.
>
> • Fostering Networking Opportunities: Create networking opportunities with alumni, professionals, and industry leaders for ST, SC, and OBC students to enhance their career prospects.

**Key Goals:**

> • Equity in Education: Ensure that all students from ST, SC, and OBC backgrounds have access to equitable educational opportunities.
>
> • Inclusion and Social Justice: Build a culture of inclusion and social justice within the institution by addressing discrimination and fostering equal opportunities.
>
> • Empowerment: Empower students from marginalized backgrounds to overcome barriers and achieve academic and personal success.

**31.4. Roles and Responsibilities of Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee**

The Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee plays a vital role in ensuring the well-being and success of students belonging to Scheduled Tribes (ST), Scheduled Castes (SC), Other Backward Classes (OBC), and other marginalized communities within the institution. Its roles and responsibilities are geared towards promoting equal opportunities, addressing challenges, and providing support to these students. **Additional Key Responsibilities:**

2\. **Monitoring Implementation:** The committee monitors the proper implementation of the reservation policy, scholarships, and welfare programs.

3\. **Creating an Inclusive Environment:** It ensures that these students are welcomed into the mainstream educational activities without facing discrimination, fostering an inclusive academic and social environment.

4\. **Engagement with Authorities:** Collaborating with educational and governmental bodies to ensure students receive all the benefits entitled to them under various government schemes.

5\. **Advisory and Advocacy:** The committee plays an advisory role by suggesting improvements to institutional policies related to social equity and inclusion.

6\. **Promote Skill Development:** Beyond academic support, the committee is responsible for organizing skill development workshops and training sessions to improve employability among these students.

**Additional Roles:**

>
> • Encourage Social Engagement: Advocate for student participation in social service projects and initiatives that foster societal development.

By fulfilling these roles and responsibilities, the Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee helps create a supportive, inclusive, and equitable learning environment for all students, ensuring their success both academically and socially.

**31.10. Documentation Maintained by Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee**

The Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee is responsible for maintaining comprehensive documentation related to various activities, support systems, and records for the welfare of students, particularly those from marginalized backgrounds. | 9\. Skill Development Program Records                 | Documentation of skill development programs organized for ST, SC, and OBC students, including program outlines, facilitators, and attendance details.                         |

| 13\. Infrastructure and Facility Utilization Records  | Records related to the usage of infrastructure and facilities such as hostels, reading rooms, and resource materials available to marginalized students.                      |
| 14\. Discrimination Reports (Caste-based Incident)    | Reports documenting any incidents of caste-based discrimination, including investigation reports and actions taken by the committee to address the issue.                     |
| 15\. Faculty/Staff Training and Sensitization Records | Records of faculty and staff training programs focused on sensitizing them to the needs of ST, SC, and OBC students, including attendance and feedback.                       |
| 16\. Committee Meeting Minutes                        | Minutes of all committee meetings that document discussions on welfare issues, action plans, and decisions taken related to ST, SC, and OBC students.                         |
| 17\. Collaboration Agreements                         | Documentation of collaborations with government bodies, NGOs, and other organizations for financial aid, scholarship programs, and skill-building initiatives.                |
| 18\. Placement Records for ST/SC/OBC Students         | Records detailing the placement activities and outcomes for ST, SC, and OBC students, including companies, job roles, and placements.                                         |

| 22\. Event Planning and Execution Documents           | Detailed plans, invitations, schedules, and post-event reports for any event or activity organized by the committee for ST, SC, and OBC students.                             |
| 23\. Data on Academic Support Initiatives             | Documentation of remedial classes, academic support initiatives, and progress tracking for students who need additional help in their studies.                                |

**Key Documentation Aspects:**

1\. **Confidentiality:** Sensitive information related to students' caste, financial details, and personal background must be kept confidential and secure.

2\. **Transparency:** Proper records ensure that all processes related to scholarship distribution, grievance redressal, and welfare programs are transparent and fair.

3\. **Monitoring and Evaluation:** Regular records help monitor the progress of various initiatives and evaluate their effectiveness in meeting the needs of ST, SC, and OBC students.

4\. **Compliance:** Documentation ensures compliance with government policies, university guidelines, and institutional procedures related to student welfare.

5\. **Annual Review:** The documentation maintained provides a comprehensive review for the committee to assess past actions and plan future activities.

**31.13. Best Practices of the Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee**

The Best Practices of the Students Welfare/ST/SC/OBC Committee are key strategies and approaches that ensure the effective and smooth functioning of the committee while promoting the welfare of students from marginalized backgrounds. These best practices focus on inclusivity, support, empowerment, and continuous engagement. Below are some of the best practices followed by the committee:

| **Best Practice**                                      | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1\. Comprehensive Awareness Programs                   | Conduct regular awareness campaigns and workshops about the rights, scholarships, and opportunities available for ST, SC, and OBC students, ensuring they are well-informed.                                |
| 2\. Proactive Scholarship and Financial Aid Assistance | Ensure that all eligible students are well-informed about and have access to scholarships, fellowships, and other financial aid programs. Assist in the timely submission of applications.                  |
| 3\. Regular Feedback and Grievance Redressal           | Implement a transparent and efficient feedback mechanism where students can voice their concerns. Ensure that grievances, especially related to caste-based discrimination, are addressed swiftly.          |
| 4\. Academic Support and Remedial Classes              | Organize remedial classes, bridge programs, and academic counseling for ST, SC, and OBC students who may face learning challenges due to disparities in education or resources.                             |
| 5\. Mentorship and Peer Support Programs               | Set up mentorship programs with faculty members and alumni, as well as peer support systems, to guide and motivate ST, SC, and OBC students in their academic and personal growth.                          |
| 6\. Celebration of Diversity and Inclusivity           | Celebrate cultural diversity by organizing events like cultural nights, awareness days, and theme-based discussions that highlight the contributions of marginalized communities.                           |
| 7\. Active Collaboration with Government and NGOs      | Build partnerships with government bodies, NGOs, and other organizations to ensure access to funding, scholarships, internships, and employment opportunities for ST, SC, and OBC students.                 |
| 8\. Leadership Development Programs                    | Provide leadership training workshops and other platforms for ST, SC, and OBC students to develop leadership skills and represent their communities in various forums.                                      |
| 9\. Psychological Support and Counseling Services      | Offer regular counseling services, including stress management, career counseling, and personal guidance to help students cope with challenges they may face.                                               |
| 10\. Health and Wellness Support                       | Ensure access to health services for all students, and provide additional support for students from marginalized communities, such as mental health programs and wellness workshops.                        |
| 11\. Promote Student Participation in Decision-Making  | Actively involve ST, SC, and OBC students in the decision-making process at the departmental and institutional levels, ensuring they have a voice in policies affecting them.                               |
| 12\. Career Counseling and Placement Support           | Organize workshops on resume writing, interview techniques, and career planning tailored to the unique challenges faced by ST, SC, and OBC students, ensuring better placement opportunities.               |
| 13\. Inclusive Campus Environment                      | Foster an inclusive campus by addressing issues related to caste-based discrimination, and ensuring that all students, irrespective of their background, feel safe and valued.                              |
| 14\. Organize Skill Development Programs               | Offer skill development and employability enhancement programs that focus on practical training, certification courses, and industry collaboration to improve job readiness.                                |
| 15\. Continuous Monitoring and Data Collection         | Regularly collect data on the academic performance, feedback, and challenges of ST, SC, and OBC students, and use this data to improve support systems and services.                                        |
| 16\. Building a Strong Alumni Network                  | Create an active alumni network of ST, SC, and OBC students to provide networking, mentoring, and professional support to current students.                                                                 |
| 17\. Conduct Leadership and Entrepreneurship Programs  | Provide students with training in leadership and entrepreneurship, empowering them to become change-makers and job creators within their communities.                                                       |
| 18\. Accessible Infrastructure                         | Ensure that all infrastructure, including hostel facilities, libraries, and digital resources, is accessible to students from all socioeconomic backgrounds, including those from marginalized communities. |
| 19\. Sensitization of Faculty and Staff                | Organize regular faculty development programs and workshops to sensitize staff to the unique challenges faced by ST, SC, and OBC students, ensuring support and encouragement.                              |
| 20\. Establishment of Equal Opportunity Centers        | Create Equal Opportunity Centers that provide targeted services to ST, SC, and OBC students, addressing their academic, financial, social, and personal needs.                                              |

**Key Elements of Best Practices:**

1\. **Inclusivity and Representation:** Ensuring that marginalized communities are represented and included in all institutional activities, decision-making processes, and leadership roles.

2\. **Supportive Academic Environment:** Offering tailored academic support to help ST, SC, and OBC students overcome educational gaps or challenges.

3\. **Active Advocacy:** Advocating for the rights of ST, SC, and OBC students, both within the institution and in collaboration with external bodies such as government organizations and NGOs.

4\. **Resource Accessibility:** Ensuring that resources (scholarships, financial aid, academic materials, career counseling, etc.) are accessible to all students, with a particular focus on those from marginalized communities.

5\. **Awareness and Capacity Building:** Raising awareness about available programs, rights, and opportunities and building the capacity of ST, SC, and OBC students through skills development and empowerment programs.

6\. **Cultural and Social Inclusion:** Promoting social harmony by organizing activities that highlight and celebrate cultural diversity and inclusivity.

**Impact of Best Practices:**

> • **Empowered Students:** Students from ST, SC, and OBC backgrounds feel empowered to pursue their academic and career goals, leading to better outcomes.
>
> • **Reduced Discrimination:** By addressing grievances promptly and fostering an inclusive environment, instances of caste-based discrimination are minimized.
>
> • **Increased Placement Success:** With better career counseling and skill development opportunities, ST, SC, and OBC students experience improved job placement rates and career success.
>
> • **Stronger Support Systems:** The students benefit from a robust network of faculty, alumni, peers, and support services designed to cater to their unique needs.

**32. NSS/NCC Committee**

**32.1. Purpose**

The NSS/NCC Committee is constituted to coordinate and promote student participation in community service, nation-building activities, character development, and discipline through structured outreach, training, and service programs. It ensures students engage in social responsibility initiatives and defense preparedness programs, contributing to their holistic development.

**32.2. Objectives**

**NSS:**

> • Instill a sense of social responsibility and volunteerism.
>
> • Promote community engagement and nation-building activities.
>
> • Enhance personality through participation in social service.

**NCC:**

> • Develop discipline, leadership, and national service mindset.
>
> • Provide basic military training to students.
>
> • Create awareness about defense services and national security.

**32.3. Functions of the NSS/NCC Committee**

| **S.No** | **Function**                                     | **Description**                                                                                 |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1        | Planning and Coordination                        | Plan and schedule NSS/NCC activities throughout the academic year.                              |
| 2        | Student Enrollment                               | Mobilize and enroll students into NSS/NCC programs.                                             |
| 3        | Organizing Community Service Activities          | Conduct social outreach such as cleanliness drives, health camps, blood donation, etc.          |
| 4        | Conducting National and State Level Celebrations | Organize events for NSS Day, Independence Day, Republic Day, etc.                               |
| 5        | Training and Drills (NCC specific)               | Conduct regular parades, drills, and physical training sessions for cadets.                     |
| 6        | Awareness Programs                               | Arrange campaigns on drug abuse, gender equality, road safety, environment, etc.                |
| 7        | Camps and Adventure Activities                   | Facilitate participation in NSS Special Camps, NCC ATC, trekking, and adventure camps.          |
| 8        | Collaboration with External Agencies             | Coordinate with NGOs, civic bodies, hospitals, and defense units for meaningful engagement.     |
| 9        | Monitoring and Evaluation                        | Track participation, performance, and impact of activities; maintain reports and documentation. |
| 10       | Personality Development                          | Foster leadership, discipline, teamwork, and civic responsibility among student volunteers.     |

**32.4. Roles & Responsibilities of the Committee**

| **Function**             | **Description**                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Planning & Scheduling    | Prepare yearly action plans for NSS/NCC activities in line with institutional calendar.                                                                                                         |
| Coordination             | Collaborate with local NGOs, government agencies, and defense units for organizing activities and camps.                                                                                        |
| Monitoring Participation | Track and maintain records of student volunteers/cadets and their participation hours.                                                                                                          |
| Organizing Events        | Conduct awareness drives, blood donation camps, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, environmental campaigns, Republic/Independence Day parades, etc.                                                         |
| Student Development      | Facilitate annual special camps, leadership training, trekking, weapon training & camps, and certificate courses. Ensure participation in inter-collegiate/state/national level NCC/NSS events. |
| Recognition              | Recommend students for awards, certificates, or internal assessment credits where applicable.                                                                                                   |

**32.10. Documentation Maintained by NSS/NCC Committee**

*1. NSS/NCC Volunteer Registration Forms*

> • **Purpose:** To keep a record of all volunteers enrolled in the NSS/NCC programs.
>
> • **Details Included:** Personal details of the volunteers, their contact information, department, and year of study.
>
> • **Frequency:** Updated annually or as new students join the programs.

*2. Volunteer Attendance Records*

> • **Purpose:** To track attendance and participation in activities and events organized by the NSS/NCC.
>
> • **Details Included:** Date of activity, name of volunteer, hours of participation, and type of event (e.g., community service, camp, workshop).
>
> • **Frequency:** Maintained for every event or activity.

*3. Event/Activity Planning Documents*

> • **Purpose:** To document the planning and execution of each event, including details of objectives, expected outcomes, resources required, and the roles of volunteers.
>
> • **Details Included:** Event schedule, budget, location, assigned tasks, and contact information for external stakeholders (if any).
>
> • **Frequency:** Updated before and during each event.

*4. Budget and Financial Records*

> • **Purpose:** To track the financial expenditure for NSS/NCC activities.
>
> • **Details Included:** Details of funds received (if any), expenditure on various activities, and receipts for purchases made for events.
>
> • **Frequency:** Updated periodically or after each event.

*5. Event Feedback Forms*

> • **Purpose:** To gather feedback from participants and volunteers about the event's success and areas for improvement.
>
> • **Details Included:** Survey questions about event organization, volunteer engagement, and the impact of the activity.
>
> • **Frequency:** After each event or activity.

*6. Volunteer Certificates and Recognition Documents*

> • **Purpose:** To issue certificates for volunteers recognizing their participation and achievements.
>
> • **Details Included:** Name of the volunteer, event details, dates, hours of participation, and role in the event.
>
> • **Frequency:** Issued annually or at the completion of major activities.

*7. Reports on Community Service Activities*

> • **Purpose:** To document the outcomes of community service initiatives and outreach programs.
>
> • **Details Included:** Number of people reached, type of service provided, feedback from the community, and a summary of the activity's success.
>
> • **Frequency:** After each community service initiative.

*8. Volunteer Training and Development Documents*

> • **Purpose:** To maintain records of workshops, seminars, and training programs organized for volunteers.
>
> • **Details Included:** Details of training topics, attendees, trainer information, and outcomes of the training.
>
> • **Frequency:** Updated as training sessions are organized.

*9. Annual Reports*

> • **Purpose:** To summarize the activities, achievements, and challenges faced by the NSS/NCC during the academic year.
>
> • **Details Included:** Overview of all events and activities, financial summary, volunteer engagement data, and plans for the following year.
>
> • **Frequency:** Prepared at the end of each academic year.

*10. Permission/Approval Letters*

> • **Purpose:** To document the permissions granted for conducting events and activities from the administration, local authorities, or other relevant bodies.
>
> • **Details Included:** Official letters granting approval for community service, camps, and other major activities.
>
> • **Frequency:** Maintained for every significant activity requiring external permission.

*11. Event Photographs and Media Coverage*

> • **Purpose:** To document the visual history of events organized by the NSS/NCC, which can be used for promotional purposes, reports, and social media.
>
> • **Details Included:** High-quality photographs, video recordings (if any), media coverage (press clippings, social media mentions).
>
> • **Frequency:** Collected throughout each event or activity.

*12. List of Awarded Volunteers*

> • **Purpose:** To keep a record of students who have received awards, recognition, or certificates for their exceptional contributions.
>
> • **Details Included:** Names, award titles, event dates, and brief descriptions of why the volunteer was recognized.
>
> • **Frequency:** Updated annually or after major events.

*13. NSS/NCC Participation in Camps and National Activities*

> • **Purpose:** To track participation in state and national-level NSS/NCC camps, as well as other external activities.
>
> • **Details Included:** Dates of participation, camp locations, number of volunteers attending, and feedback on the camp's activities.
>
> • **Frequency:** Maintained throughout the year as volunteers attend different camps or national events.

*14. Communication Records (Emails, Notices, Memos)*

> • **Purpose:** To maintain records of official communications related to the NSS/NCC committee's activities.
>
> • **Details Included:** Emails to and from volunteers, faculty members, administration, and external partners.
>
> • **Frequency:** Ongoing, archived regularly.

*15. Legal and Regulatory Compliance Documents*

> • **Purpose:** To ensure the committee adheres to legal and regulatory requirements for organizing events and activities.
>
> • **Details Included:** Permissions from local authorities, guidelines for volunteer engagement, compliance with health and safety regulations, etc.
>
> • **Frequency:** Updated as needed based on the nature of activities.

**Importance of Documentation:**

1\. **Accountability:** Helps track volunteer contributions, activity participation, and overall program outcomes.

2\. **Transparency:** Facilitates transparency in the allocation of funds, planning of activities, and recognition of volunteers.

3\. **Compliance:** Ensures adherence to institutional policies, legal requirements, and government guidelines.

4\. **Continuous Improvement:** Serves as a reference for evaluating past activities, gathering feedback, and making informed decisions for future events.

5\. **Legacy and Record-Keeping:** Provides a historical record of NSS/NCC activities, which can be used for future reference and promotional purposes.

**32.12. Year Planner: NSS/NCC Committee**

1\. **January**

> o *Republic Day Celebrations* — **Responsible:** NSS/NCC Committee, Student Volunteers. Organize flag hoisting, cultural programs, and speeches.
>
> o *Winter Blood Donation Camp* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Red Cross Society.

2\. **February**

> o *Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Cleanliness Drive)* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Campus Maintenance Team. Organize campus-wide cleanliness campaigns.
>
> o *NCC Camp Preparation* — **Responsible:** NCC Cadets, NCC Instructors.

3\. **March**

> o *International Women's Day Celebration* — **Responsible:** NSS/NCC Committee, Women's Cell. Organize seminars, panel discussions, and cultural events to raise awareness.

4\. **April**

> o *Tree Plantation Drive* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Environment Committee. Encourage students to participate in planting trees on campus and in nearby areas.
>
> o *Blood Donation Drive* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Red Cross Society.

5\. **May**

> o *Summer Training Program for NSS Volunteers* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Medical Team, NSS Committee, External Trainers. Organize workshops and training sessions on leadership, community service, and social responsibility.
>
> o *NCC Annual Camp Participation* — **Responsible:** NCC Cadets, NCC Instructors.

6\. **June**

> o *Yoga Day Celebrations* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Yoga Instructor. Conduct yoga sessions for students and faculty to raise awareness of physical health and wellness.

7\. **July**

> o *NSS Orientation for New Volunteers* — **Responsible:** NSS/NCC Committee, Student Volunteers. Organize an induction session for freshers to inform them about NSS activities and goals.

8\. **August**

> o *Independence Day Celebrations* — Flag hoisting, cultural performances, and patriotic events.
>
> o *Health & Hygiene Awareness Campaign* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Health Committee.

9\. **September**

> o *NSS Day Celebrations* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Senior NSS Volunteers, NSS Committee, Student Volunteers. Organize a series of activities and programs to celebrate NSS's contribution to social welfare.

10\. **October**

> o *NCC Orientation for New Cadets* — **Responsible:** NCC Cadets, NCC Instructors. Conduct an orientation session for fresh NCC cadets.
>
> o *Disaster Management Awareness Program* — **Responsible:** NSS Volunteers, Local Disaster Management Authority.

11\. **November**

> o *National Integration Camp* — **Responsible:** NCC Officers, New NCC Cadets, NSS Volunteers, Campus Cultural Committee. Conduct programs focusing on national integration and unity.

12\. **December**

> o *Annual NSS/NCC Awards Ceremony* — **Responsible:** NSS/NCC Committee, Administration. Recognize the contributions of outstanding NSS and NCC volunteers in various activities.
>
> o *Winter Camp for NCC Cadets* — **Responsible:** NCC Officers, NCC Cadets. Organize a winter camp for training, learning, and physical fitness.

**Key Events and Activities Overview:**

> • **Community Service Projects:** Regular community service activities such as blood donation drives, cleanliness drives, tree plantation, and health awareness campaigns.
>
> • **Special Days & Celebrations:** NSS/NCC Day, Republic Day, Independence Day, National Integration Day, etc., are key occasions for organizing campus and community events.
>
> • **Workshops & Trainings:** NSS and NCC conduct orientation, leadership, and skill-building programs to empower volunteers.
>
> • **Health and Environment Initiatives:** Awareness campaigns on health, hygiene, wellness, and the environment, along with programs like yoga and blood donation camps.
>
> • **Volunteer Recognition:** Regular recognition of outstanding volunteers who contribute significantly to various NSS/NCC initiatives.

**32.14. Best Practices for NSS/NCC Committee**

1\. **Regular Engagement with Students**

> o Ensure frequent communication with students through workshops, meetings, and orientation programs.
>
> o Provide continuous guidance and mentorship to NSS/NCC volunteers.
>
> o Organize regular check-ins to keep track of volunteer engagement and participation.

2\. **Focused Community Service Projects**

> o Organize community service initiatives that address real-world issues such as sanitation, health, education, and environment, thereby enhancing student involvement and social responsibility.
>
> o Partner with local NGOs, government bodies, and community leaders to implement these projects.

3\. **Inclusive and Diverse Activities**

> o Conduct events and activities that are inclusive, allowing all students, regardless of background, to participate and contribute.
>
> o Ensure activities cater to a diverse student base, allowing for cultural, environmental, educational, and social initiatives.

4\. **Celebration of National Days**

> o Ensure active participation in the celebration of national days like Republic Day, Independence Day, and Gandhi Jayanti through flag hoisting, cultural events, and awareness campaigns.
>
> o Organize activities that highlight national values, patriotism, and civic responsibility.

5\. **Leadership Development Programs**

> o Conduct leadership development workshops, soft-skill training, and team-building exercises to help volunteers grow.
>
> o Assign leadership roles to students in various projects to enhance their organizational and leadership skills.

6\. **Health and Hygiene Awareness Campaigns**

> o Organize health camps, blood donation drives, health check-ups, and vaccination awareness programs, particularly focusing on issues relevant to the local community.
>
> o Foster awareness on hygiene and sanitation through campus-wide campaigns and community outreach.

7\. **Collaboration with Government Initiatives**

> o Engage in government schemes like Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, Digital India, and various awareness programs initiated by the government.
>
> o Collaborate with local administration for conducting disaster management workshops and community service projects.

8\. **Participation in National and State-Level Camps**

> o Encourage volunteers to participate in national and state-level NSS/NCC camps to foster a sense of unity and national pride.
>
> o Offer pre-camp preparation sessions to prepare students for these larger events and ensure their smooth participation.

9\. **Awareness and Advocacy Programs**

> o Promote social causes such as gender equality, environmental protection, child rights, and education through advocacy and awareness programs.
>
> o Utilize platforms like seminars, workshops, and discussions to spread knowledge about important social issues.

10\. **Recognition and Rewards**

> o Regularly recognize and reward volunteers for their commitment and contributions through awards, certificates, and public acknowledgment.
>
> o Organize an Annual Volunteer Recognition Day to celebrate the efforts of the most active and impactful volunteers.

11\. **Integration with Academic Curriculum**

> o Incorporate NSS/NCC activities into the academic curriculum where possible, offering students credits or recognition for their involvement.
>
> o Encourage faculty to collaborate with NSS/NCC for academic and extra-curricular projects.

12\. **Green Initiatives**

> o Promote environmental sustainability by organizing tree plantation drives, e-waste collection drives, and recycling campaigns.
>
> o Foster a culture of environmental consciousness through regular awareness sessions on reducing carbon footprints and conserving natural resources.

13\. **Alumni Engagement**

> o Involve alumni who have previously been part of the NSS/NCC programs in mentoring current volunteers and providing guidance on career and community service.
>
> o Organize alumni interaction sessions to share experiences, learnings, and success stories.

14\. **Cultural Integration and Social Harmony**

> o Organize inter-departmental cultural events, sports activities, and competitions to encourage teamwork, social integration, and interaction across disciplines.
>
> o Focus on promoting social harmony, unity in diversity, and fostering national integrity among students from different backgrounds.

**Benefits of these Best Practices:**

> • **Increased Volunteer Engagement:** By creating a well-rounded program with diverse activities, students are more likely to remain committed and engaged in the NSS/NCC programs.
>
> • **Enhanced Community Impact:** Focused community service activities lead to tangible positive outcomes for the local population.
>
> • **Leadership and Skill Development:** Volunteers develop valuable leadership and interpersonal skills that benefit them both in personal growth and future career opportunities.
>
> • **Promoting Civic Responsibility:** The initiatives foster a sense of social responsibility and national pride among students, contributing to a positive societal impact.

**33. General Maintenance Committee**

**33.1. Purpose**

The General Maintenance Committee ensures that all physical infrastructure—such as buildings, classrooms, laboratories, furniture, electrical systems, water supply, and sanitation facilities—is maintained efficiently and consistently. A well-maintained campus supports a conducive learning environment, which is a key component in NBA and NAAC accreditation criteria.

**33.2. Objectives**

> • To ensure safety, cleanliness, and functionality of the institutional infrastructure.
>
> • To conduct periodic inspection and prompt maintenance of all campus assets and utilities.
>
> • To establish a preventive maintenance schedule for critical infrastructure and equipment.
>
> • To ensure all facilities are user-friendly, inclusive, and accessible to stakeholders.
>
> • To support institutional functions, academics, and research by providing reliable physical infrastructure.

**33.3. Roles & Responsibilities**

| **Responsibility**         | **Description**                                                                                                        |
|----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Routine Maintenance        | Oversee daily upkeep of classrooms, labs, washrooms, common areas, and corridors.                                      |
| Infrastructure Repairs     | Coordinate repair of furniture, fixtures, plumbing, electrical faults, and equipment.                                  |
| Preventive Maintenance     | Schedule periodic checks of lab equipment, generators, UPS, lifts, HVAC, water tanks, etc.                             |
| Civil and Electrical Works | Attend to structural repairs, painting, lighting, wiring, and electrical load management.                              |
| Complaint Resolution       | Maintain a register or digital portal for staff/student complaints and resolve within a defined TAT (Turnaround Time). |
| Vendor Coordination        | Liaise with external agencies for AMC (Annual Maintenance Contracts) and special repair work.                          |
| Documentation              | Maintain records of maintenance schedules, expenses, vendor bills, and Budget audits.                                  |
| Emergency Response         | Immediate action during breakdowns, power failures, plumbing blockages, etc.                                           |
| Compliance                 | Ensure building safety, sanitation, and fire safety norms are followed.                                                |

**33.4. Committee Composition**

| **Designation**                  | **Role**               |
|----------------------------------|------------------------|
| Principal / Dean                 | Chairperson            |
| Senior Faculty                   | Coordinator / Convenor |
| Estate Officer / Admin In-Charge | Member Secretary       |
| Heads of Departments             | Representatives        |

> • Technical/Support Staff: Maintenance Supervisor, Electrician, Plumber, Lab Assistants
>
> • Student Nominee (optional): Feedback and suggestions

**33.5. Maintenance Areas Covered:**

> • Classrooms & Laboratories
>
> • Restrooms & Washrooms
>
> • Electrical and Electronics Systems
>
> • Internet, Wi-Fi & Networking Infrastructure
>
> • Water Supply & Drainage Systems
>
> • Roads, Parking, Pathways
>
> • Canteen, Auditorium, Library
>
> • Hostels, Guest Houses (if applicable)
>
> • Fire extinguishers & emergency exits
>
> • Lifts and Generators

**33.6. Relevance to NBA**

| **NBA Criterion**                                                       | **How the Committee Supports It**                                                                                                                               |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Criterion 6 – Governance, Institutional Support and Financial Resources | Ensures the availability and maintenance of physical facilities.                                                                                                |
| Criterion 7 – Continuous Improvement                                    | Demonstrates planned maintenance through policy and execution. Supports hygiene, safety, and sustainability (e.g., water conservation, green campus practices). |

**33.7. Relevance to NAAC**

> • Criterion 4 – Infrastructure and Learning Resources
>
> • Criterion 6 – Leadership and Management
>
> • Criterion 7 – Institutional Values and Best Practices

**33.8. Essential Documentation for NBA/NAAC**

> • Logbook of maintenance activities (manual or ECAP/digital).
>
> • Complaint Register / Maintenance Portal Screenshots.
>
> • AMC contracts and maintenance invoices.
>

>

**33.9. Sample Maintenance Reporting Cycle**

**1. Complaint Raised** → By Faculty/Student through register/portal.

**2. Complaint Forwarded** → To concerned technician/vendor.

**3. Issue Resolved** → Within 24–48 hours for minor issues.

**4. Resolution Updated** → In register or system for transparency.

**5. Feedback (Optional)** → Collected periodically for service improvement.

**33.10. Best Practices**

> • Use of QR code-based issue reporting on campus.
>
> • Energy audits and water conservation checks.
>
> • Establish Green Protocols for eco-friendly maintenance.
>
> • Regular campus cleaning drives involving students and staff.

**34. Canteen, Housekeeping, Hygiene & Sanitation Committee**

**34.1. Purpose of the Canteen, Housekeeping, Hygiene & Sanitation Committee**

This committee ensures a clean, hygienic, and healthy environment in the institution by managing canteen services, campus cleanliness, and sanitation facilities. It contributes directly to the health, well-being, and productivity of students and staff, which is essential for both academic excellence and compliance with NBA/NAAC quality parameters.

**34.2. Objectives of the Canteen, Housekeeping, Hygiene & Sanitation Committee**

> • To ensure the availability of hygienic and nutritious food in the college canteen.
>
> • To maintain cleanliness across all academic, administrative, and residential spaces.
>
> • To monitor the quality and safety of sanitation facilities including drinking water, restrooms, and waste disposal.
>
> • To promote awareness of personal hygiene and environmental cleanliness.
>
> • To provide feedback-based improvements and support green and sustainable campus practices.

**34.3. Functions of the Canteen, Housekeeping, Hygiene & Sanitation Committee**

*1. Canteen Management and Oversight*

> • **Objective:** To ensure the smooth and hygienic operation of the campus canteen(s) and food outlets.

**Functions:**

> o Regular monitoring of food quality, cleanliness, and hygiene standards in the canteen.
>
> o Ensuring food is prepared and served in a safe, clean environment.
>
> o Coordinating with the canteen contractor to ensure compliance with health and safety guidelines.
>
> o Organizing periodic food quality assessments to ensure that food provided meets nutritional standards and hygiene regulations.
>
> o Addressing student and staff complaints related to food quality, pricing, and cleanliness.

*2. Health and Hygiene Inspections*

> • **Objective:** To ensure that the campus is maintained in a hygienic and sanitized condition.

**Functions:**

> o Regular inspection of the campus facilities, including classrooms, restrooms, corridors, and common areas to ensure cleanliness.
>
> o Ensuring the proper disposal of waste in a timely and efficient manner.
>
> o Overseeing the availability and cleanliness of hygiene facilities (toilets, drinking water, etc.) on campus.
>
> o Ensuring that waste management practices, such as recycling, composting, and proper waste segregation, are followed.
>
> o Supervising pest control and maintaining cleanliness in food preparation and storage areas.

*3. Promoting Health and Safety Standards*

> • **Objective:** To uphold a safe and healthy environment for students, faculty, and staff.

**Functions:**

> o Developing and enforcing health and safety protocols on the campus, including the use of sanitizers, face masks (if required), and social distancing (if applicable).
>
> o Coordinating with local health authorities to ensure compliance with public health guidelines and policies.
>
> o Organizing health and hygiene awareness programs and workshops for students and staff to promote a culture of cleanliness and health.
>
> o Ensuring regular deep cleaning of high-touch surfaces like doorknobs, elevators, and desks.

*4. Waste Management and Sustainability Initiatives*

> • **Objective:** To implement eco-friendly practices and reduce the environmental impact of waste.

**Functions:**

> o Developing and implementing waste management strategies that include waste segregation (wet, dry, and hazardous waste).
>
> o Promoting recycling initiatives on campus and coordinating the recycling of paper, plastic, and other materials.
>
> o Organizing awareness campaigns about reducing single-use plastics and promoting the use of reusable containers and bags.
>
> o Ensuring the proper disposal of food waste from the canteen and other areas.
>
> o Collaborating with external agencies or vendors for sustainable waste disposal practices.

*5. Monitoring and Evaluating Housekeeping Services*

> • **Objective:** To ensure efficient and effective housekeeping services across the campus.

**Functions:**

> o Supervision and evaluation of housekeeping staff to ensure that cleaning and maintenance tasks are carried out regularly and effectively.
>
> o Ensuring the proper maintenance of cleanliness in administrative offices, classrooms, hostels, corridors, and other public areas.
>
> o Regular inspection of cleaning equipment and supplies, ensuring that they are in good condition and safe to use.
>
> o Coordinating with housekeeping vendors and ensuring adherence to the institution's quality standards.

*6. Catering Services and Nutritional Awareness*

> • **Objective:** To promote healthy eating habits among students and faculty.

**Functions:**

> o Ensuring that the canteen offers balanced, nutritious, and safe food options.
>
> o Organizing awareness programs on healthy eating and nutrition.
>
> o Providing dietary recommendations and alternatives for students with specific dietary needs (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, etc.).
>
> o Encouraging the canteen to provide fresh fruits, vegetables, and other healthy food options, reducing processed or unhealthy food items.

*7. Emergency and Safety Protocols*

> • **Objective:** To ensure the safety of individuals in the event of a hygiene-related emergency (e.g., foodborne illness outbreaks).

**Functions:**

> o Establishing and communicating emergency protocols for food safety issues, accidents, or sanitation-related concerns.
>
> o Ensuring that the staff and vendors working in food service areas are trained in emergency first-aid and food safety protocols.
>
> o Immediate response to any sanitation emergencies or hygiene-related complaints, such as reports of foodborne illnesses or unsanitary conditions.

*8. Collaboration with Local Authorities and Health Experts*

> • **Objective:** To ensure compliance with local health regulations and leverage expert advice on sanitation and hygiene matters.

**Functions:**

> o Coordinating with local health departments for regular inspections and audits of the campus's canteen, health facilities, and overall hygiene practices.
>
> o Consulting with nutritionists, sanitation experts, and other professionals to maintain high health standards across the campus.
>
> o Collaborating with local health authorities to perform periodic inspections of food handling and cleanliness practices in the canteen.

*9. Feedback Mechanism*

> • **Objective:** To address student and staff concerns regarding cleanliness and hygiene.

**Functions:**

> o Creating a system for students and staff to submit feedback or complaints regarding cleanliness, food quality, sanitation, or housekeeping services.
>
> o Acting on feedback promptly and ensuring that any recurring issues are addressed in a timely manner.

*10. Regular Health and Sanitation Audits*

> • **Objective:** To monitor and maintain ongoing hygiene and sanitation standards across the campus.

**Functions:**

> o Scheduling regular audits of health and sanitation practices, both in the canteen and across other campus areas like dorms and classrooms.
>
> o Publishing a "Hygiene Report" with suggestions and action plans to maintain or improve cleanliness standards.
>
> o Conducting periodic surveys or feedback sessions with students to assess the effectiveness of sanitation and hygiene practices on campus.

| Sanitation & Waste Management  | Ensure waste bins are placed and emptied regularly, maintain drainage systems, promote segregation of waste, and coordinate with municipal bodies. |
| Drinking Water Facilities      | Regular inspection and maintenance of water coolers, RO units, and ensure water potability through periodic lab tests.                             |
| Restroom Hygiene               | Ensure availability of water, soaps, cleaning supplies, exhaust systems, and proper lighting in restrooms.                                         |
| Awareness Campaigns            | Organize cleanliness drives, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan programs, and health awareness workshops.                                                       |
| Complaint & Feedback Mechanism | Maintain registers or digital portals for grievances related to hygiene or canteen, and resolve issues timely.                                     |

**4. Quarterly Reporting** → Submit health and hygiene status report to Principal/Administration.

**34.11. Events / Activities Organized by Canteen, Housekeeping, Hygiene & Sanitation Committee**

*1. Hygiene and Sanitation Awareness Campaigns*

> • **Objective:** To educate students, staff, and faculty about the importance of maintaining hygiene and sanitation on campus.

**Activities:**

> o Organizing workshops and seminars on topics like hand hygiene, personal cleanliness, waste segregation, and maintaining clean surroundings.
>
> o Distributing pamphlets and posters that promote hygiene practices, such as proper handwashing techniques and maintaining cleanliness in the canteen and other common areas.
>
> o Inviting guest speakers or experts in public health and hygiene to deliver talks on sanitation practices.

*2. Campus Cleanliness Drives*

> • **Objective:** To ensure the campus remains clean and waste is managed efficiently.

**Activities:**

> o Organizing cleanliness drives where students and staff work together to clean various parts of the campus, including classrooms, hostels, and outdoor spaces.
>
> o Collaborating with local organizations or environmental groups to encourage sustainable practices such as recycling and reducing waste.
>
> o Holding competitions between departments or student clubs to see who can collect the most recyclable waste or clean a designated area the best.

*3. Canteen Health & Hygiene Inspections*

> • **Objective:** To maintain a high standard of hygiene and food safety in the campus canteen.

**Activities:**

> o Conducting surprise inspections of the canteen and food service areas to ensure compliance with hygiene and safety standards.
>
> o Organizing workshops for canteen staff on food safety, handling, and hygiene protocols.
>
> o Introducing student feedback surveys to gather input on food quality, cleanliness, and overall satisfaction.

*4. Waste Management & Sustainability Workshops*

> • **Objective:** To promote waste segregation and environmentally friendly practices on campus.

**Activities:**

> o Hosting workshops on waste management techniques, such as composting, recycling, and reducing plastic use.
>
> o Setting up recycling stations around the campus and educating students and staff on how to use them correctly.
>
> o Conducting seminars on the importance of sustainability and reducing waste, focusing on practices such as reusing, reducing, and recycling.
>
> o Organizing a "Green Campus" initiative where students contribute to sustainable practices and receive recognition.

*5. Health and Hygiene Awareness Weeks*

> • **Objective:** To raise awareness about health, cleanliness, and hygiene.

**Activities:**

> o Celebrating Health and Hygiene Week with daily activities like free health checkups, sanitation workshops, and fitness sessions.
>
> o Partnering with local health organizations or hospitals to offer free medical camps or health screenings for students and staff.
>
> o Organizing talks on mental health, physical health, and overall well-being.
>
> o Distributing free hygiene kits (including sanitizers, masks, etc.) during the awareness week.

*6. "Healthy Campus" Programs*

> • **Objective:** To promote the importance of a healthy lifestyle through clean and safe campus practices.

**Activities:**

> o Organizing fitness programs or yoga sessions for students and faculty, focusing on stress relief and wellness.
>
> o Creating campaigns on healthy eating habits, encouraging nutritious meals in the campus canteen.
>
> o Hosting workshops on mental health awareness and its connection to maintaining a clean and safe environment.
>
> o Introducing initiatives like "No Trash Day" or "Plant a Tree Day" to raise environmental consciousness.

*7. Canteen and Housekeeping Staff Training Programs*

> • **Objective:** To ensure the campus staff (canteen workers, housekeeping staff) are well-trained in hygiene and food safety practices.

**Activities:**

> o Organizing periodic training sessions for canteen staff on food hygiene, cleanliness, and customer service.
>
> o Providing workshops for housekeeping staff on efficient cleaning techniques, use of cleaning equipment, and safe handling of cleaning chemicals.
>
> o Offering awareness sessions for staff about the importance of their role in maintaining a safe and hygienic campus.

*8. Student Participation in Hygiene Initiatives*

> • **Objective:** To encourage student involvement in maintaining a clean and hygienic campus.

**Activities:**

> o Engaging students in organizing and participating in cleanliness campaigns and environmental sustainability initiatives.
>
> o Creating student-led teams to monitor and maintain cleanliness in high-traffic areas like libraries, cafeterias, and hostels.
>
> o Running competitions for the most innovative waste disposal solutions or the best-decorated and cleanest campus spaces.

*9. Medical and Sanitation Workshops*

> • **Objective:** To ensure that the campus community understands the importance of sanitation in health and wellness.

**Activities:**

> o Hosting workshops with local health experts on topics like preventing infections, sanitizing food preparation areas, and maintaining sanitary conditions in hostels and dormitories.
>
> o Offering first-aid training sessions for students and staff, emphasizing the importance of immediate response in hygiene-related emergencies.

*10. Regular Health and Sanitation Audits*

> • **Objective:** To monitor and maintain ongoing hygiene and sanitation standards across the campus.

>
> • Campus-wide Swachh Bharat activities and green campaigns.

**35. Purchase and Store Committee**

**35.1. Purpose**

The Purchase and Store Committee ensures that all purchases of goods, equipment, lab consumables, software, and infrastructure for academic and administrative needs are made in a transparent, efficient, and cost-effective manner, in compliance with institutional procurement policies and financial norms. It also oversees proper inventory management, storage, and asset verification, which are essential for NBA/NAAC accreditation.

**35.2. Objectives**

> • To ensure transparent procurement through quotations, tenders, or e-procurement platforms.
>
> • To maintain accurate records of purchases and stock registers.
>
> • To monitor inventory usage, stock depletion, and replenishment.
>
> • To ensure quality assurance in procured items and timely delivery.
>
> • To ensure budget adherence and documentation as per auditing requirements.
>
> • To facilitate periodic stock verification and disposal of obsolete items.

**35.3. Roles & Responsibilities**

| **Area**                    | **Responsibility**                                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Indent Review               | Verify and approve requisitions from departments with appropriate justifications.                                                                   |
| Vendor Selection            | Shortlist and finalize vendors based on quotations/tenders following purchase norms (e.g., DGS&D/GeM rules).                                        |
| Purchase Process            | Float quotations, process tenders, approve comparative statements, negotiate if needed.                                                             |
| Order Placement             | Issue purchase orders with terms and conditions, delivery dates, and warranty clauses.                                                              |
| Receiving & Inspection      | Physically inspect received goods for quality and quantity before acceptance.                                                                       |
| Stock Entry & Asset Tagging | Update the stock register and allocate inventory to the concerned department. Tag equipment/assets with unique IDs for tracking and audit purposes. |
| Annual Stock Verification   | Conduct internal audits and submit stock verification reports.                                                                                      |
| Write-Off Process           | Identify and recommend disposal of non-functional or outdated items following institutional norms.                                                  |

**35.4. Committee Composition**

| **Designation**                      | **Role**                                  |
|--------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| Principal / Director                 | Chairperson                               |
| Vice Principal / Dean                | Member                                    |
| HoD (of Indenting Department)        | Member                                    |
| Senior Faculty (Non-Indenting Dept.) | Member                                    |
| Purchase Officer / Admin Officer     | Member Secretary                          |
| Accounts Officer                     | Member                                    |
| Store In-Charge                      | Member                                    |
| Internal Auditor                     | Invitee (for verification and compliance) |

**35.5. Types of Purchases Handled**

> • Laboratory Equipment & Instruments
>
> • Computers, Software & IT Infrastructure
>
> • Books, Journals, Subscriptions
>
> • Furniture and Fixtures
>
> • Consumables and Stationery
>
> • Civil, Electrical, Plumbing Materials
>
> • AMC (Annual Maintenance Contracts)

>
> • e-Procurement platform or GeM (Government e-Marketplace) integration.
>
> • Barcode-based inventory for labs and classrooms.
>
