**40.13. Best Practices**

1\. **1. Active Industry and Alumni Engagement:**

> o **Practice:** The IIC establishes strong ties with industry professionals and alumni entrepreneurs to serve as mentors, advisors, and partners for students working on innovative ideas and startups.
>
> o **Benefit:** Students gain real-world insights, practical advice, and potential opportunities for internships, investments, or collaboration with industry experts.

2\. **2. Regular Hackathons and Innovation Challenges:**

> o **Practice:** Organizing themed hackathons, idea competitions, and innovation challenges regularly to encourage students to think outside the box and develop creative solutions to societal or technical problems.
>
> o **Benefit:** These competitions foster creativity, collaboration, and problem-solving skills among students, while also identifying viable ideas for potential startups.

3\. **3. Innovation Clubs and Student-Initiated Startups:**

> o **Practice:** Establishing dedicated innovation clubs within departments to facilitate student-driven innovation and entrepreneurship activities. These clubs act as incubators for entrepreneurial ideas.
>
> o **Benefit:** Provides students with the resources and support to convert ideas into real startups and encourages a culture of innovation throughout the campus.

4\. **4. Collaboration with External Innovation Hubs and Incubators:**

> o **Practice:** Partnering with government and private incubation centers, accelerators, and innovation hubs to offer students access to funding, mentorship, and resources for startup development.
>
> o **Benefit:** Provides students with a platform to take their innovations to the next level and connect with investors, mentors, and startup ecosystem partners.

5\. **5. Intellectual Property (IP) Awareness and Protection:**

> o **Practice:** Promoting awareness of intellectual property rights (IPRs) through workshops, seminars, and collaborations with IPR cells. Encouraging students to patent their innovative ideas and products.
>
> o **Benefit:** Ensures that students' innovations are protected, encouraging more students to engage in research and entrepreneurial ventures while safeguarding their intellectual property.

6\. **6. Establishing a Structured Mentorship Program:**

> o **Practice:** The IIC sets up a structured mentorship program, where students are paired with industry professionals, successful entrepreneurs, or faculty members who can guide them in their innovation and startup journey.
>
> o **Benefit:** Helps students receive personalized guidance on overcoming challenges and refining their ideas, improving their chances of success in their ventures.

7\. **7. Innovation Portals and Online Platforms:**

> o **Practice:** Developing an innovation portal or online platform where students and faculty can showcase their projects, inventions, and innovations. This portal can also serve as a hub for networking, collaboration, and sharing ideas.
>
> o **Benefit:** Provides visibility to the innovations created within the institution and fosters collaboration among students, faculty, and external stakeholders.

8\. **8. Organizing Entrepreneurial Skill Development Programs:**

> o **Practice:** Offering short-term certificate courses, workshops, and seminars focused on developing entrepreneurial skills such as business planning, marketing, financial management, and pitching ideas.
>
> o **Benefit:** Equips students with the necessary skills to transform their ideas into successful businesses, providing a well-rounded education that goes beyond academic learning.

9\. **9. Encouraging Cross-Disciplinary Collaboration:**

> o **Practice:** Encouraging students from different disciplines (engineering, management, arts, etc.) to collaborate on innovative projects and startups. Cross-disciplinary teams often generate more diverse and unique solutions.
>
> o **Benefit:** Fosters a culture of collaboration and diversity, leading to innovative and well-rounded solutions that might not have emerged in a more siloed academic environment.

10\. **10. Recognizing and Rewarding Innovations:**

> o **Practice:** Establishing recognition programs such as awards, certificates, and scholarships for students who show exceptional innovation and entrepreneurship.
>
> o **Benefit:** Provides motivation for students to engage more in innovation and entrepreneurship, and acknowledges the hard work and creativity of students, further promoting a culture of innovation.

11\. **11. Providing Access to Funding Opportunities:**

> o **Practice:** Assisting students and faculty in finding grants, funding competitions, and investment opportunities through government schemes, private organizations, and venture capitalists.
>
> o **Benefit:** Provides essential financial support for early-stage startups, enabling students to take their ideas from concept to reality.

12\. **12. Building Innovation and Entrepreneurship Curriculum:**

> o **Practice:** Offering specialized courses and electives related to innovation, entrepreneurship, and intellectual property rights (IPR) as part of the curriculum.
>
> o **Benefit:** Instills an entrepreneurial mindset in students from the beginning, making them more likely to engage in innovation during their studies and beyond.

**40.14. Conclusion**

The Institution's Innovation Cell Committee plays a crucial role in developing an innovation-driven culture within the institution. By providing resources, support, and guidance, it helps students and faculty members to transform their creative ideas into practical solutions and entrepreneurial ventures. The committee facilitates collaboration, research, and development, empowering the institution to contribute to the broader innovation ecosystem.

**41. Anti-Drug Committee**

**41.1. Introduction**

The Anti-Drug Committee is constituted in accordance with UGC/AICTE guidelines and government directives to create a drug-free campus environment. It aims to prevent, monitor, and address drug abuse issues among students and staff, and to promote awareness through education and counseling.

**41.2. Objectives of the Anti-Drug Committee**

1\. **Prevent Drug Abuse** among students by creating awareness and instilling discipline.

2\. **Monitor and Report** suspicious activities related to substance abuse within the campus.

3\. **Organize Awareness Programs** in collaboration with law enforcement agencies and NGOs.

4\. **Counsel Students** who may be vulnerable or showing signs of addiction.

5\. **Build a Safe and Healthy Campus** environment free from substance abuse.

6\. **Ensure Implementation** of UGC/AICTE/State directives regarding anti-drug measures.

**41.3. Core Functions of the Anti-Drug Committee**

1\. **1. Awareness and Sensitization**

> o Conduct seminars, rallies, and workshops to educate students and staff about the harmful effects of drugs.
>
> o Promote anti-drug messages through posters, pamphlets, slogans, and social media.

2\. **2. Surveillance and Monitoring**

> o Keep vigilant watch in and around the campus, hostels, and nearby areas for any suspicious activity.
>
> o Conduct random checks (in coordination with law enforcement if needed).

3\. **3. Prevention and Early Detection**

> o Identify early signs of drug use or addiction among students through observation and peer feedback.
>
> o Set up a confidential mechanism to report drug-related concerns anonymously.

4\. **4. Counseling and Rehabilitation Support**

> o Facilitate access to psychological counseling and rehabilitation services for students in need.
>
> o Maintain collaboration with medical experts and local de-addiction centers.

5\. **5. Law Enforcement Liaison**

> o Coordinate with local police and Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) for periodic checks and expert sessions.
>
> o Report any serious or criminal offenses involving drugs for necessary action.

6\. **6. Policy Implementation**

> o Ensure that institutional policies regarding anti-drug measures are properly implemented.
>
> o Suggest revisions or improvements to policies based on evolving trends and feedback.

7\. **7. Student Engagement**

> o Involve students in peer education programs, awareness campaigns, and leadership roles within the committee.
>
> o Encourage formation of student clubs to advocate for a drug-free lifestyle.

8\. **8. Documentation and Reporting**

> o Maintain records of activities, incidents, and actions taken.
>
> o Submit regular reports to college authorities and external agencies when required.

**41.4. Committee Composition**

| **S.No** | **Designation**                                   | **Role in Committee**       |
|----------|---------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| 1        | Principal / Head of Institution                   | Chairperson                 |
| 2        | Senior Faculty Member / Dean Student Welfare      | Coordinator / Convener      |
| 3        | One Faculty Member from Each Department           | Members                     |
| 4        | Medical Officer / College Health Centre In-Charge | Health Advisory Member      |
| 5        | Hostel Wardens (Boys & Girls)                     | Member Representatives      |
| 6        | NSS/NCC Program Officer                           | Awareness & Outreach Member |
| 7        | One Parent Representative (optional)              | Community Liaison           |
| 8        | One Legal Expert or Counselor (optional)          | External Advisory Member    |
| 9        | Two Student Representatives (UG & PG)             | Student Members             |
| 10       | Local Police Department Representative (optional) | Liaison / Advisory Member   |

**41.5. Roles and Responsibilities of the Anti-Drug Committee**

1\. **1. Policy Formulation & Implementation**

> o Develop and implement a zero-tolerance policy towards drug use on campus.
>
> o Ensure alignment with government anti-drug laws and UGC/AICTE/State directives.

2\. **2. Awareness & Education**

> o Conduct awareness programs, seminars, and workshops on the harmful effects of drug abuse.
>
> o Collaborate with NSS, NCC, NGOs, and health departments for campaigns and outreach activities.
>
> o Observe Anti-Drug Day (June 26) and other national awareness initiatives.

3\. **3. Monitoring and Surveillance**

> o Maintain strict vigilance in hostels, canteens, and vulnerable areas.
>
> o Establish a watchdog mechanism with support from faculty and student representatives.
>
> o Encourage students to report drug-related incidents anonymously and safely.

4\. **4. Counseling & Rehabilitation Support**

> o Facilitate counseling services for students with drug-related issues through trained professionals.
>
> o Refer students to rehabilitation centers or medical facilities when required.
>
> o Conduct empathy-based orientation sessions for peer support and rehabilitation.

5\. **5. Coordination with Authorities**

> o Work with local law enforcement agencies for training and action when required.
>
> o Ensure legal compliance and documentation for any disciplinary or legal measures.
>
> o Act as a bridge between institutional administration and external agencies.

6\. **6. Student Engagement and Peer Involvement**

> o Promote student participation in the committee for peer education and monitoring.
>
> o Encourage formation of student anti-drug clubs or task forces.

7\. **7. Reporting & Documentation**

> o Maintain records of activities, awareness sessions, complaints, and interventions.
>
> o Submit periodic reports to the institution and affiliating university/authority.

**41.6. Events / Activities by the Anti-Drug Committee**

1\. **1. Anti-Drug Awareness Week**

> o Series of events including guest lectures, awareness rallies, poster competitions, and street plays.
>
> o Organized in collaboration with NGOs or local law enforcement.

2\. **2. Guest Lectures & Expert Talks**

> o Sessions by psychologists, de-addiction specialists, and police officials on the impact of drug abuse.
>
> o Focus on legal consequences, mental health effects, and rehabilitation.

3\. **3. Poster & Slogan Writing Competitions**

> o Thematic contests to spread awareness and encourage student creativity on anti-drug messages.
>
> o Display of winning posters around campus.

4\. **4. Awareness Rally / Walkathon**

> o Organized with students and staff marching through nearby communities carrying banners and placards.
>
> o Promotes a strong visual message against drug use.

5\. **5. Short Film / Skit Competitions**

> o Students create short films or perform skits dramatizing the consequences of drug addiction.
>
> o Screened across campus and shared on institutional social media platforms.

6\. **6. One-to-One Counseling Sessions**

> o Confidential counseling made available for students dealing with peer pressure or substance use issues.
>
> o Led by trained counselors and supported by psychology departments or external professionals.

7\. **7. Pledge Ceremony**

> o Mass participation in taking a pledge to stay drug-free.
>
> o Often conducted on International Day Against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking (June 26).

8\. **8. Collaboration with Police Department**

> o Conduct mock drills or interactive sessions on identifying and handling drug abuse.
>
> o Facilitate real-life case discussions and role-plays.

9\. **9. Awareness Campaign in Hostels**

> o Special sessions or posters in hostel common areas to ensure constant reminders of a drug-free campus.
>
> o Peer-led initiatives for support and awareness.

10\. **10. Quiz and Debate Competitions**

> o Topics focused on the dangers of drugs, mental health, and legal aspects.
>
> o Encourages informed discourse among students.

**41.8. Documentation Maintained by Anti-Drug Committee**

The Anti-Drug Committee in an educational institution should maintain a variety of documents to ensure proper management of its activities, track progress, and adhere to legal and policy requirements. Below is a list of key documents typically maintained by the committee:

1\. **1. Committee Structure and Documentation**

> o **Constitution of the Committee:** Documentation outlining the formation, composition, roles, and responsibilities of the Anti-Drug Committee members.
>
> o **Minutes of Meetings:** Records of meetings, decisions made, and action points discussed by the committee. This includes both formal and informal meetings.
>
> o **Committee Membership Details:** List of current members, their roles, and contact information.

2\. **2. Policy and Guidelines Documents**

> o **Anti-Drug Policy:** The official policy of the institution regarding drug abuse prevention, including rules, regulations, and sanctions.
>
> o **Code of Conduct:** Specific code of conduct for students and staff related to drug use and abuse prevention.
>
> o **Zero Tolerance Policy:** Documentation clarifying the institution's stand on drug use and the consequences of violations.

3\. **3. Event and Activity Documentation**

> o **Event Planning Documents:** Detailed records for events organized by the Anti-Drug Committee, including event objectives, planned activities, participant lists, budgets, and feedback forms.
>
> o **Workshops/Seminars/Guest Lecture Records:** Documentation for educational and awareness events, including speaker details, attendees, and event outcomes.
>
> o **Reports of Awareness Campaigns:** Reports summarizing the goals, activities, and feedback from campaigns such as posters, social media drives, and community outreach programs.

4\. **4. Counseling and Support Services**

> o **Counseling Records:** Confidential records of students or staff who seek counseling services related to drug abuse. These may include individual counseling sessions, follow-ups, and treatment plans (maintained as per privacy laws).
>
> o **Support Group Records:** Documentation of peer support groups, including meeting schedules, agendas, participant details, and any actions taken.

5\. **5. Data Collection and Surveys**

> o **Drug Use Survey Data:** Surveys or questionnaires distributed to students and staff to gauge the extent of drug use, awareness levels, and satisfaction with anti-drug initiatives.
>
> o **Survey Results & Analysis:** Reports that summarize the findings from surveys, including trends, concerns, and actionable insights.
>
> o **Feedback Forms:** Forms collected from participants of awareness campaigns, workshops, and events for quality improvement.

6\. **6. Legal and Compliance Documentation**

> o **Compliance Reports:** Records ensuring that the institution is in compliance with local and national drug abuse prevention laws and regulations.
>
> o **Incident Reports:** Documentation related to drug-related incidents within the institution, including investigations, resolutions, and follow-up actions.
>
> o **Confidentiality Agreements:** Agreements that ensure privacy for students receiving counseling or participating in support programs.

7\. **7. Collaboration and Partnership Documents**

> o **Partnership Agreements:** Documents related to collaborations with external organizations such as health agencies, law enforcement, or rehabilitation centers.
>
> o **Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs):** Any formal agreements made with external bodies for awareness programs, counseling services, or joint initiatives.

8\. **8. Annual Reports**

> o **Annual Activity Report:** A comprehensive report summarizing all anti-drug activities, campaigns, and initiatives carried out throughout the year. This may include participation data, outcomes, and recommendations for the future.
>
> o **Annual Budget Report:** Financial records detailing the budget allocation and spending on anti-drug activities, events, and resources.

9\. **9. Promotional and Informational Materials**

> o **Brochures and Flyers:** Printed or digital materials used for awareness campaigns, detailing the dangers of drug abuse and available resources.
>
> o **Social Media Posts and Campaigns:** Documentation of social media activities, including posts, videos, and ads aimed at spreading anti-drug messages.

10\. **10. Monitoring and Evaluation**

> o **Progress Reports:** Regular reports on the progress of ongoing initiatives, including the status of awareness campaigns, student participation, and behavioral changes.
>
> o **Evaluation Forms:** Forms used to assess the effectiveness of programs, workshops, or campaigns, collected from participants after each event.

11\. **11. Financial Documentation**

> o **Expense Records:** Documentation of any expenses incurred during anti-drug events, including receipts and payment records.
>
> o **Sponsorship or Grant Documents:** Records of any funding received for anti-drug programs, including sponsorship agreements or grant applications.

**General Guidelines for Documentation:**

> • **Confidentiality:** All counseling records and personal data must be handled with the utmost confidentiality and in compliance with relevant privacy laws (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA).
>
> • **Archiving:** Keep documents organized and archived for easy access during audits, evaluations, or assessments.
>
> • **Regular Updates:** Documentation should be updated regularly to reflect new activities, changes in policies, or feedback from events and surveys.

**41.9. Best Practices of the Anti-Drug Committee**

The Anti-Drug Committee plays a crucial role in creating awareness, preventing substance abuse, and providing support for affected individuals in the institution. Below are some best practices that can be implemented by the committee for maximum effectiveness:

1\. **1. Awareness Campaigns**

> o **Regular Campaigns:** Organize frequent awareness campaigns to educate students, faculty, and staff about the dangers of drug abuse. These campaigns can include poster distributions, seminars, webinars, and workshops.
>
> o **Use of Social Media:** Leverage social media platforms to spread anti-drug messages and reach a wider audience.
>
> o **Guest Speakers & Experts:** Invite experts from mental health, addiction counseling, and law enforcement to give talks on the harmful effects of drugs.

2\. **2. Counseling and Support Services**

> o **Counseling Sessions:** Establish a confidential counseling service for students who may be struggling with drug-related issues. Ensure that these services are accessible and sensitive to the needs of the students.
>
> o **Peer Support Groups:** Develop peer support groups where students can share experiences and help each other stay accountable and drug-free.
>
> o **Hotline for Assistance:** Set up a 24/7 helpline where students can anonymously seek help or advice about drug abuse issues.

3\. **3. Collaboration with External Organizations**

> o **Partnership with Local Health Organizations:** Collaborate with local health organizations, mental health professionals, and rehabilitation centers to provide additional resources and support.
>
> o **Engagement with Law Enforcement:** Work closely with local law enforcement to ensure that the institution is complying with anti-drug policies and regulations and to address any drug-related incidents on campus.

4\. **4. Organizing Drug-Free Events**

> o **Sports & Fitness Events:** Organize sports tournaments, fitness challenges, or other recreational activities that emphasize the importance of a healthy, drug-free lifestyle.
>
> o **Creative Workshops:** Conduct art, drama, or music workshops where students can express their emotions and thoughts about the dangers of drug use.
>
> o **Anti-Drug Awareness Days/Weeks:** Establish a drug-free awareness week with events like rallies, exhibitions, and guest lectures.

5\. **5. Building a Stronger Network within the Institution**

> o **Student Volunteers:** Involve students in the committee's initiatives by forming volunteer groups who can lead awareness efforts and act as role models for their peers.
>
> o **Training Faculty and Staff:** Provide training to faculty and staff on how to identify signs of drug abuse and how to effectively intervene or refer students to proper support services.

6\. **6. Prevention through Education**

> o **Incorporating Anti-Drug Messages in Curricula:** Integrate anti-drug education into existing academic programs and workshops to emphasize prevention from an early stage.
>
> o **Life Skills and Stress Management:** Offer workshops on stress management, healthy coping mechanisms, and building resilience to prevent students from turning to drugs as a means of escape.

7\. **7. Regular Monitoring and Feedback**

> o **Survey on Drug Usage:** Conduct regular anonymous surveys to track the prevalence of drug use among students, assess awareness levels, and gather feedback for improvement.
>
> o **Review of Campaign Effectiveness:** Analyze the effectiveness of previous awareness campaigns and make adjustments to ensure they continue to meet student needs.

8\. **8. Empowering Parents and Families**

> o **Parent Awareness Programs:** Conduct programs to engage parents and families in the fight against drug abuse. These programs can help parents recognize signs of drug use and learn ways to talk to their children about the dangers of drugs.
>
> o **Parent-Teacher Conferences:** Include drug abuse awareness discussions during parent-teacher meetings to raise awareness and build a community effort in tackling the issue.

9\. **9. Zero Tolerance Policy**

> o **Strict Policy Implementation:** Implement a zero-tolerance policy towards drugs and substance abuse on campus. Ensure that the policies are communicated clearly and enforced consistently.
>
> o **Clear Consequences:** Establish clear and transparent consequences for students found violating the anti-drug policies.

10\. **10. Annual Awareness Day and Celebrations**

> o **National Anti-Drug Day:** Celebrate days such as National Anti-Drug Day (June 26) by organizing special events, guest lectures, and activities that focus on combating drug abuse.
>
> o **Recognition Programs:** Recognize and reward students who demonstrate leadership in promoting a drug-free lifestyle within the campus.

**Impact of Best Practices:**

> • **Enhanced Awareness:** Regular awareness activities lead to a better understanding of the harmful consequences of drug abuse.
>
> • **Supportive Environment:** Students, faculty, and staff are equipped with the tools to support those in need of help, ensuring no one suffers in silence.
>
> • **Healthier Campus Community:** By promoting a drug-free environment, the institution fosters the overall well-being and success of its students.
>
> • **Sustained Engagement:** Involving students and parents in the anti-drug efforts ensures long-term success and community involvement in tackling the issue.

**42. Anti-Ragging Committee**

**42.1. Objective**

To ensure a ragging-free environment on the campus by implementing preventive measures, sensitization programs, monitoring, and prompt redressal of complaints, as per the guidelines of UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009.

**42.2. Constitution of the Committee**

The Anti-Ragging Committee is constituted under the leadership of the Head of the Institution and comprises faculty members, administrative staff, representatives from students (senior and fresher categories), and external representatives (NGOs, legal experts, etc.).

**Composition:**

> • Chairperson: Principal / Head of the Institution
>
> • Coordinator: Senior Faculty Member
>
> • Faculty Members (from various departments)
>
> • Administrative Officer / Hostel Warden
>
> • Student Representatives (UG/PG – Senior & Fresher)
>
> • Parent Representative
>
> • Local NGO / Civil Society Representative (optional)
>
> • Legal Expert / Advocate (optional)

**42.3. Anti-Ragging Committee Objectives**

> • **Creating a ragging-free atmosphere:** Ensure that there is no ragging, both inside and outside the campus.
>
> • **Awareness creation:** Educate students about the acts and punishments associated with ragging activities.
>
> • **Promoting cordial relations:** Foster harmonious relationships among students to achieve the institution's mission and objectives.
>
> • **Self-confidence and national interest:** Raise awareness about how an individual's self-confidence can positively influence national interests.
>
> • **Implementation of UGC regulations:** Ensure the effective implementation of the provisions laid out in the UGC regulations aimed at curbing ragging.
>
> • **Regulation and punishment:** Identify and discipline students involved in ragging as per the UGC regulation, 2009.

**42.4. Definition of Ragging and Punishable ingredients of Ragging**

In exercise of the power conferred by Clause (g) of Sub-Section (1) of Section 26 of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, the University Grants Commission hereby makes the following Regulations, namely

**"Ragging" means** any disorderly conduct whether by words spoken or written or by an act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness any other student, indulging in rowdy or undisciplined activities which causes or is likely to cause annoyance, hardship or psychological harm or to raise fear or apprehension thereof in a fresher or a junior student or asking the students to do any act or perform something which such student will not in the ordinary course and which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of shame or embarrassment so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of a fresher or a junior student.

**Punishable ingredients of Ragging:**

> • Abetment to ragging;
>
> • Criminal conspiracy to rag;
>
> • Unlawful assembly and rioting while ragging;
>
> • Public nuisance created during ragging;
>
> • Violation of decency and morals through ragging;
>
> • Injury to body, causing hurt or grievous hurt;
>
> • Wrongful restraint;
>
> • Wrongful confinement;
>
> • Use of criminal force;
>
> • Assault as well as sexual offences or even unnatural offences;
>
> • Extortion;
>
> • Criminal trespass;
>
> • Offences against property;
>
> • Criminal intimidation;
>
> • Attempts to commit any or all of the above-mentioned offences against the victim(s);
>
> • All other offences following from the definition of "Ragging".

**42.5. What Constitutes Ragging?**

Ragging includes any of the following actions:

> • **Teasing or handling with rudeness:** Any conduct by a student or students, whether through spoken or written words or acts, that teases, treats, or handles a fresher or another student in a rude manner.
>
> • **Rowdy or undisciplined behavior:** Engaging in activities that cause or are likely to cause annoyance, hardship, physical or psychological harm, or raise fear or apprehension in a fresher or another student.
>
> • **Coercion to perform acts:** Forcing a student to perform actions they would not typically do, resulting in fear, shame, torment, or embarrassment, which affects the student's physical or psychological well-being.
>
> • **Disruption of academic activities:** Any action by a senior student that prevents, disrupts, or disturbs the regular academic activities of a fresher or another student.
>
> • **Exploitation of students:** Using the services of a fresher or any other student to complete academic tasks meant for an individual or group of students.
>
> • **Financial extortion:** Any act of extorting money or forcing a fresher or any other student to bear unnecessary expenses for the benefit of the students involved in ragging.
>
> • **Physical abuse:** This includes all forms of physical abuse such as sexual abuse, homosexual assaults, stripping, forcing obscene or lewd acts, bodily harm, or any other actions that endanger health or safety.
>
> • **Verbal and written abuse:** Any verbal or written abuse, such as insults, obscene gestures, or public humiliation, including deriving sadistic pleasure from the discomfort of a fresher or any other student.
>
> • **Mental harassment:** Any act that negatively impacts the mental health or self-confidence of a fresher or any other student, with or without the intent of deriving sadistic pleasure, or demonstrating power, authority, or superiority over them.

**42.6. Functions of the Anti-Ragging Committee**

1\. **1. Complaint Handling and Enquiry:**

> o To consider complaints received from students, conduct inquiries, and submit reports to the Anti-Ragging Committee along with recommendations for punishment for the offenders.

2\. **2. Overseeing Undertakings:**

> o To oversee the process of obtaining undertakings from students as per the established provisions and regulations.

3\. **3. Workshops and Orientation:**

> o To conduct workshops and awareness sessions regarding the menace of ragging and to orient students on its prevention.

4\. **4. Providing Contact Information:**

> o To provide students with contact information, including addresses and phone numbers of individuals designated to receive complaints or distress calls related to ragging.

5\. **5. Raising Awareness:**

> o To create awareness among students about the anti-ragging rules, regulations, and the importance of maintaining a ragging-free environment.

6\. **6. Prevention of Ragging:**

> o To take necessary measures for the prevention of ragging within the campus and hostels, ensuring a safe and supportive environment for all students.

**42.7. Anti-Ragging Committee – Roles & Responsibilities**

In compliance with UGC Regulations, the Institute has constituted the Anti-Ragging Committee under the leadership of the Head of the Institution to ensure the implementation of effective mechanisms for the prevention of ragging and for taking appropriate actions against students involved in or abetting such activities.

**Coordinator – Roles and Responsibilities**

The Anti-Ragging Coordinator is entrusted with the following duties:

1\. **1. Conduct Surprise Raids**

> Carry out surprise inspections at locations prone to ragging or with potential for ragging incidents.

2\. **2. Immediate Enquiry and Reporting**

> Conduct on-the-spot inquiries into any reported incident of ragging referred by faculty, students, parents, or guardians, and submit a detailed report with recommendations to the Head of the Institution for immediate action.

3\. **3. Ensure Regular Vigilance**

> Oversee the functioning of the Anti-Ragging Squad and ensure they make frequent rounds to monitor student behavior across the campus.

4\. **4. Establish a Suggestion/Complaint Box**

> Set up a complaint/suggestion box on campus to enable students to report issues or grievances anonymously.

5\. **5. Timely Disciplinary Action**

> Take swift and appropriate action against students violating anti-ragging policies, in coordination with institutional authorities.

6\. **6. Compliance with Regulations**

> Address complaints and incidents of ragging in line with government and university regulations and procedures.

7\. **7. Documentation and Reporting**

> Maintain detailed records of all anti-ragging activities, actions taken, and reports filed. Submit periodic updates to the Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC).

**42.8. Provision of Punishment for Ragging at the Institution (As per UGC Guidelines)**

In accordance with the University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulations on curbing the menace of ragging in higher educational institutions, the following punitive actions may be taken against students found guilty of ragging. The severity of punishment shall depend upon the nature and gravity of the offence as determined by the Institution's Anti-Ragging Committee.

**Possible Punishments:**

1\. **1. Cancellation of Admission**

> Permanent revocation of the student's admission to the institution.

2\. **2. Suspension from Attending Classes**

> Temporary prohibition from attending lectures and academic sessions.

3\. **3. Withholding or Withdrawal of Scholarships/Fellowships and Other Benefits**

> Stoppage of financial support or institutional incentives.

4\. **4. Debarment from Appearing in Examinations or Evaluations**

> Prevention from sitting for any test, exam, or assessment process.

5\. **5. Withholding of Results**

> Temporary or permanent withholding of academic results.

6\. **6. Debarment from Institutional Representation**

> Prohibition from representing the college at regional, national, or international events (e.g., sports, festivals, conferences).

7\. **7. Suspension or Expulsion from Hostel**

> Temporary or permanent eviction from institutional accommodation.

8\. **8. Rustication from the Institution**

> Temporary expulsion for a period ranging from one to four semesters.

9\. **9. Permanent Expulsion from the Institution**

> Complete removal from the rolls of the institution with a ban on admission to any other institution.

10\. **10. Monetary Fine**

> Imposition of a fine up to ₹25,000.

11\. **11. Collective Punishment**

> In cases where the specific individuals involved in ragging are not identified, the institution may impose punishment on a group of students as a deterrent measure to ensure community accountability.

**42.9. Functions of the Anti-Ragging Squad**

The Anti-Ragging Squad operates under the directive of the principal and plays a vital role in preventing and addressing ragging incidents within the institution. The squad functions as a vigilant and proactive body to maintain a safe and student-friendly environment.

**Composition:**

> • The Squad shall include a Nodal Officer, nominated by the principal, who will serve as the key coordinator for anti-ragging measures.
>
> • The Nodal Officer will be supported by a team of teaching and non-teaching staff from various departments and administrative sections, also nominated by the principal.

**Key Functions:**

1\. **1. Vigilance and Patrolling:**

> o Conduct regular patrols and inspections in identified ragging-prone zones such as classrooms, hostels, canteens, parking areas, common rooms, and campus corners.
>
> o Maintain a strong presence in hotspots and areas of student congregation, particularly during early weeks of the academic session.

2\. **2. Surprise Inspections:**

> o Organize unannounced visits to hostels and other sensitive areas to detect and deter any potential ragging activity.

3\. **3. Oversight and Monitoring:**

> o Keep continuous oversight on student behavior in high-risk zones and report any suspicious activity immediately to the Anti-Ragging Committee.

4\. **4. Investigation and Reporting:**

> o In the event of a complaint or observed incident, the Squad is empowered to conduct preliminary investigations.
>
> o Gather facts and testimonies, document evidence, and submit detailed findings and recommendations to the Anti-Ragging Committee for further action.

**42.10. Members – Anti-Ragging Squad**

Members of the Anti-Ragging Squad shall:

> • Keep continuous vigil and take preventive action against incidents of ragging.
>
> • Monitor student activities in key areas of student congregation such as: Classrooms, Laboratories, Libraries, Canteens, Common Rooms, Buses, Playgrounds, and Hostels.
>
> • Report any suspicious behavior or ragging incidents immediately to the coordinator.
>
> • Assist in conducting awareness programs and maintaining a supportive environment for new students.

**42.11. Affidavit by Student**

In order to ensure strict compliance and monitoring of anti-ragging measures and make students aware of the prohibition of ragging and the punishment, the college has prescribed, an affidavit to be signed by the student to the effect that he/she will not indulge in the act of ragging, and will be severely punished if found indulging in such activity, both under penal as well as under UGC Regulations and also affirm to the effect that he/she has not been expelled and/or debarred by any Institution and further confirms that he/she would not indulge, actively or passively, in the act or abet the act of ragging and if found guilty of ragging and/or abating ragging, shall be liable to be proceeded under the regulations and/or under any Penal Law or any other Law for the time being in force. The college shall obtain the affidavit from students duly signed in by them, while seeking admission to the college in every academic year. Apart from filling in the affidavit by the freshers, the seniors will also sign in the undertaking, declaring that they shall not indulge in the ragging both in and outside the college premises.

**42.12. Affidavit by Parents**

In order to achieve the objective & as laid down in the UGC Regulations, for curbing the menace of ragging, the college shall obtain affidavit from parents/guardians of students also, duly signed by the concerned parents/guardians of the applicant to the effect that he/she has read and understood the provisions of these regulations with same effect as laid down in the affidavit by students.

**42.13. Display of names and contact numbers of members of Anti Ragging Squad**

The names and contact numbers of Members of the Anti-Ragging Squad shall be uploaded on the college website and displayed at various visible points, also at the entry passage which is conspicuous to all students. The members of anti-ragging squad shall be deployed at all vulnerable areas to monitor any activity which calls on for ragging.

**42.14. Complaint Box**

For registering complaints against ragging or other grievances, a Complaint Box shall be placed at prominent areas of the college where any student can write and drop his/her complaint or can give any suggestion regarding ragging, if any. The Complaint Boxes shall be locked and can be accessed by the Nodal Officer of the Anti-Ragging Squad, once in a week. In case the Nodal Officer is not present on the campus, then a person nominated by the nodal officer shall be permitted to open the complaint box, the report of which shall be submitted by him/her to the Anti-Ragging Committee. Upon getting any grievance related to ragging, the nodal officer shall be empowered to investigate the case and report the same to the Anti-Ragging Committee, which shall be further dealt strictly, as per the UGC Regulations.

**42.15. Online Anti-Ragging Feedback Mechanism**

The College shall be collecting online feedbacks from the freshers during July to September, so that the students could be given a fair platform to register their complaints against ragging. The feedback report shall be submitted to the Anti-Ragging Committee for further analysis of complaints found, (if any) and taking appropriate action against those found guilty as per the UGC Regulation.

**42.16. Complaint Redressal Procedure**

In order to deal with the complaints against ragging and help students in distress, the UGC has introduced National Anti-ragging helpline 1800-180-5522 (24 x 7 Toll Free). The grievances related to ragging can also be registered through email at helpline & antiragging.in for bringing the matter to public attention. For any further information regarding ragging, the students can visit the UGC website i.e. www.ugc.ac.in and www.antiragging.in or can also contact UGC Monitoring Agency i.e Aman Satya Kachroo Trust on following No. 09871170303, 09818400116 (only in case of emergency).

**42.20. Anti-Ragging Campaign**

The senior students in all the programmes are hereby instructed not to resort to any acts towards their juniors, which may be construed as ragging. Ragging of any kind is prohibited by law. Students indulging in acts of ragging, either directly or indirectly, are punishable for varying period of imprisonment, as per law, as well as the minimum punishment that will be inflicted by the college will be rustication from the college.

The college has already constituted an Anti-Ragging Committee consisting of teachers and the junior students have been provided with the mobile phone numbers of all the members of the Anti-Ragging Committee. Any complaint by a junior student against a senior student, who might resort to ragging, will be viewed seriously and immediate action will be initiated. The details as to what amounts to ragging as per Law and the punishment prescribed are prominently displayed on Special Notice Boards on the Campus.

Therefore, senior students are hereby instructed to behave decently with their juniors and never give scope for the junior to feel that they are being ragged.

The Heads of the Departments are therefore requested to ensure that this information is brought to the notice of all the senior year students of their respective departments.

**42.21. Anti-Ragging Measures**

This is to inform all the 1st year students that all necessary steps are taken to ensure ragging free environment on the college campus which include the following. The college has constituted Anti-Ragging Committee for this purpose. For easy access to the students, the names, departments and mobile phone numbers of the Chairman, Convener and Members of the Anti-Ragging Committee have been already circulated/distributed.

Further, the Anti-Ragging Squads have been constituted and the members are posted at various locations in the Campus and Hostels under separate jurisdictions for the purpose of observing, preventing and taking suitable actions.

The lists have already been circulated to all departments, and being given wide publicity through repeated announcements and bulletining at prominent places.

The students are hereby advised that they need not hesitate to report to any Member of the Anti-Ragging Committee or Squad any grievances arising due to any kind of misbehavior by a senior student. It is assured that once such an incident is established, severe action will be taken by the authorities against those responsible. All steps are being taken to restrain the seniors from resorting to any acts which may be construed as ragging so that the juniors can move freely in the college campus.

Students may feel free to contact any authority of this college in case of any grievance or threat of ragging.

The Heads of the Departments are therefore requested to ensure that this information is brought to the notice of all the first-year students of their respective departments.

**42.22. Best Practices of the Anti-Ragging Committee**

1\. **1. Proactive Induction and Orientation Programs**

> o Conduct detailed induction sessions for freshers and parents explaining anti-ragging mechanisms, UGC norms, and institutional support.
>
> o Include interaction with senior students in a moderated, friendly environment to build trust and confidence.

2\. **2. Robust Monitoring and Surveillance Mechanisms**

> o Installation of CCTV cameras in key locations like corridors, canteens, hostels, and isolated areas.
>
> o Regular rounds by the Anti-Ragging Squad in classrooms, buses, hostel corridors, and campus hotspots.

3\. **3. Digital Grievance Redressal System**

> o Establish an online anonymous complaint portal for students to report incidents without fear.
>
> o Ensure confidentiality and prompt redressal within a specified time frame.

4\. **4. Dedicated Helpline and Publicized Contact Details**

> o Display 24x7 helpline numbers, nodal officer contact information, and complaint procedures at visible locations throughout the campus.
>
> o Ensure the same information is included in student handbooks and on the college website.

5\. **5. Involvement of Multiple Stakeholders**

> o Include faculty, non-teaching staff, hostel wardens, and student representatives in both the Anti-Ragging Committee and Squad.
>
> o Engage alumni and external legal/psychological experts for awareness and redressal sessions.

6\. **6. Structured Documentation and Reporting**

> o Maintain detailed records of: Undertakings submitted by students and parents (as per UGC norms); Minutes of Anti-Ragging meetings; Reports of inspections and surprise raids; Actions taken on complaints and follow-up measures; Annual activity reports submitted to IQAC and affiliating university.

7\. **7. Organizing Regular Awareness Programs**

> o Conduct seminars, workshops, and role-plays on human rights, legal literacy, and consequences of ragging.
>
> o Organize essay writing, poster-making, and drama competitions on anti-ragging themes.

8\. **8. Installation of Suggestion / Complaint Drop Boxes**

> o Provide easily accessible drop boxes for anonymous complaints or suggestions.
>
> o Regularly check and take action based on inputs received.

9\. **9. Sensitization of Senior Students**

> o Conduct pre-semester workshops for senior students on leadership, mentorship, and responsible behavior.
>
> o Introduce mentorship programs where seniors guide juniors in academics and career planning.

10\. **10. Zero Tolerance Policy with Transparent Punishment Framework**

> • Clearly communicate the consequences of ragging to all stakeholders.
>
> • Implement disciplinary actions as per UGC guidelines and publish outcomes (without disclosing student identities) to deter future violations.

**43. College Academic Committee**

**43.1. Introduction**

The College Academic Committee (CAC) is a strategic body constituted at the institutional level to oversee, plan, monitor, and enhance the academic activities and standards of the college. It plays a pivotal role in aligning academic practices with institutional vision, regulatory guidelines, and accreditation requirements.

**43.2. Objectives of the College Academic Committee**

**1. Ensure Academic Excellence**

To uphold and enhance the quality of academic standards through continuous monitoring, review, and guidance.

**2. Promote Effective Curriculum Delivery**

To ensure timely and effective implementation of curriculum, academic schedules, and teaching plans.

**3. Facilitate Faculty and Student Development**

To encourage professional growth of faculty and holistic development of students through academic, co-curricular, and skill-based activities.

**4. Monitor Academic Progress**

To regularly assess and review student performance, attendance, and academic outcomes for continuous improvement.

**5. Plan Institutional Academic Growth**

To formulate and implement short-term and long-term academic strategies aligned with the Vision and Mission of the institution.

**6. Support Quality Assurance and Accreditation**

To contribute actively towards maintaining quality benchmarks and ensuring readiness for accreditation and assessment processes.

**7. Encourage Innovation in Teaching and Learning**

To adopt innovative teaching methodologies and integrate technology for enhanced learning experiences.

**8. Promote Academic Discipline and Integrity**

To maintain academic discipline, monitor examination practices, and promote ethical behavior among students and faculty.

**9. Create a Student-Centric Academic Environment**

To ensure that academic activities are inclusive, student-focused, and geared toward enhancing employability and research aptitude.

**43.3. Composition of College Academic Committee (CAC)**

The College Academic Committee (CAC) is constituted to oversee and ensure the effective implementation of academic policies, curriculum planning, teaching-learning processes, and student performance improvement. It acts as an advisory and regulatory body for all academic matters at the institutional level.

**1. Chairperson**

|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Role/Responsibility** | Presides over the meetings and provides strategic direction for academic planning and execution. |

**Members (2)**

| **Vice Principal (if applicable)**        | Assists in coordinating academic processes                      |
|-------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| **All Heads of Departments (HoDs)**       | Represent departmental academic concerns and planning           |
| **Controller of Examinations**            | Coordinates examination schedules, evaluation, results          |
| **Academic Coordinator / Dean Academics** | Monitors academic calendar, syllabus coverage, mentoring        |
| **Senior Faculty Members (2-3)**          | Provide insights on curriculum delivery and student performance |

| **Placement Officer (optional)**          | Shares industry needs and inputs for skill alignment            |

**Functions of the College Academic Committee**

> • Prepare academic calendar and monitor adherence.
>
> • Approve departmental academic plans, time-tables, and assessment schedules.
>
> • Suggest curriculum enrichment based on industry and student feedback.
>
> • Monitor student performance, attendance, and remedial actions.
>
> • Coordinate internal examinations and Continuous Internal Evaluation (CIE).
>
> • Recommend best practices for teaching-learning improvements.

**43.4. Functions of the College Academic Committee**

1\. **1. Policy and Direction Setting**

2\. **2. Academic Performance Review**

> o Periodically review academic programs, teaching methodologies, and student performance across all departments.

3\. **3. Faculty and Student Development**

> o Evaluate and support faculty development initiatives such as training, FDPs, workshops, and conferences.
>
> o Review student development programs including seminars, skill development, internships, and mentoring.

4\. **4. Institutional Growth and Planning**

> o Formulate long-term academic and institutional development plans aligned with the Vision and Mission of the college.

5\. **5. Academic Calendar and Time Table Management**

> o Prepare, approve, and review the Academic Calendar and Class Schedules for smooth academic delivery.

6\. **6. Quality Assurance and Accreditation Readiness**

> o Plan and implement measures for maintaining and improving the quality of education.
>
> o Monitor compliance with quality benchmarks related to NAAC, NBA, and other accreditation bodies.

7\. **7. Monitoring Teaching and Learning Discipline**

> o Keep strict vigilance on faculty attendance and punctuality in conducting classes.
>
> o Ensure classes are conducted as per schedule and syllabus coverage is tracked.

8\. **8. Student Attendance and Examination Ethics**

> o Review students' attendance records and take appropriate actions in case of deficiencies.
>
> o Monitor and address issues related to malpractices in examinations.

9\. **9. Other Academic Excellence Initiatives**

> o Recommend and oversee any additional academic initiatives to enhance the overall educational standards and learning environment.
